**R846 -- VIRTUA COP'S GUNS FROM MISTER'S STICKS AND MOUSE, THE CROSSHAIRS,
AND WHY THE ATTRACT IS IN JAPANESE.** (Route 1 of R841; Ben, 2026-10-15:
joystick and mouse only, GunCon / SNAC stays documented. M2_VCOP_GUN, now ON
by default.)

*Believed (R839 / R841):* the core's mapping (rtl/io/m2_vcop_guns.sv, never
built) scales the stick and a mouse to MAME's ranges; MiSTer's mouse path
might carry an absolute gun position ("TO BE CHECKED"); the crosshair draws
on the game's aim point; a gun's trigger reaches the core as a joystick
button.

*Now known -- VERIFIED:*
  1. HOW MISTER CORES TAKE A GUN (read, not run; shallow clones): System 32
     (meathax/s32 512b547, s32_lightgun.sv: JTFRAME's contract), PSX
     (PSX_MiSTer cd17b5a, GunCon / Justifier), MegaDrive, SNES, NES
     lightgun / zapper, and Main_MiSTer 13f1de9 (input.cpp, user_io.cpp).
     System 24's core is published as an .rbf only (no source found).
       - Aim: every core takes joystick_l_analog_N as an ABSOLUTE screen
         position, u = a + 128, pos = u * dim >> 8 (S32, PSX; MD / SNES /
         NES the same up to scale). P1 = analog_0, P2 = analog_1.
       - Main: a USB gun (Sinden, GUN4IR, GunCon 3, OpenFIRE, ...;
         QUIRK_LIGHTGUN) sends its ABS axes to the left stick, calibrated by
         MiSTer's F10 screen to -127..+127 edge to edge (-128 only for PSX),
         saturating off the screen; no deadzone. Its BUTTONS go to the MOUSE
         buttons (ps2_mouse[2:0]), not the joystick's. There is NO absolute
         mouse channel: ps2_mouse is relative deltas of all mice merged, and
         a gun's axes never become mouse motion. So R841's "absolute mouse"
         does not exist; a mouse aims by accumulation, and only one player
         can have it.
       - Mouse: accumulated per packet toggle, 1:1 (S32 halves it), y -= dy,
         clamped to the screen. Trigger from ps2_mouse[0] (S32 ORs it into
         P1's trigger always).
       - Off-screen: full deflection at an edge is off-screen (PSX, MD,
         SNES, NES); reload is a button that forces off-screen and fires
         (PSX Triangle; MD / SNES Justifier B).
       - Cursor: drawn in the native pixel domain before the scaler; a small
         '+' (3x3 / 7x7) or JTFRAME's 8x8 white-on-black sight; hidden off
         the screen; per-player colours (PSX: P1 blue, P2 yellow).
  2. THE GAME'S OWN AIM POINT (MAME 0.289, sim/io/mame_m2_vcop_marks.lua):
     Virtua Cop's test menu has GUN SETTING -> GUN MARK CHECK, which draws
     each player's mark (P1 cyan, P2 pink) where the game puts the gun, and
     prints the calibration it uses: AD1 X 0x083-0x276, Y 0x024-0x1a9; AD2
     X 0x080-0x273, Y 0x027-0x1a9 -- MAME's PORT_MINMAX are the game's own
     default calibration. With the coordinates forced at the I/O board
     (24 points, both guns, 43 unclipped marks; sim/io/vcop_marks.py) the
     mark's centroid sits on pixel floor((v - min) * dim / span) -- MAME's
     crosshair pixel (PORT_CROSSHAIR scale 1.0 over the 496 x 384 visible
     area) -- with residual x +0.13 +- 0.32 px, y 0.00 +- 0.32 px, at most
     0.7 px. So "MAME's crosshair" and "where the game shoots" are the same
     pixel, measured, not assumed.
  3. THE MAPPING (m2_vcop_guns, rewritten): stick -> pixel u * 496 >> 8,
     u * 384 >> 8; pixel -> the smallest game unit on that pixel, v - min =
     ceil(px * span / dim): X px + (px>0) + (px>=166) + (px>=331); Y1 py +
     (py>0) + (py>=77) + (py>=154) + (py>=231) + (py>=308); Y2 py + (py>0) +
     (py>=193). The mouse (OSD "Mouse": Gun 1 trigger [default], Gun 1
     aim+trigger, Gun 2 trigger, Gun 2 aim+trigger) aims one gun when told
     to; its left / right buttons are ALWAYS that gun's Trigger / Reload, so
     a USB gun on player 1 works with the defaults (aim on analog_0, trigger
     on the mouse button). Joystick bits 4 Trigger, 5 Reload, 6 Start, 7
     Coin, 8 Test, 9 Service (P1); the Virtua Cop MRA names them (Daytona's
     J1 unchanged). IN0 / IN1 as MAME's vcop map. Off-screen: MAME
     model1io2 fpga_r's 5% border on the game units (a calibrated gun at
     +-127 lands inside it). RELOAD holds the gun at the off-screen corner
     at once and pulls the trigger 1-2 ticks later (tick = 2^17 clk_sys =
     1.64 ms), and keeps the corner ~3 ticks after release: the I/O board
     reads IN1 and the coordinates at different moments of its 1 kHz scan,
     so a simultaneous change could be read as a shot on the screen. "Gun
     reload: Auto" is DSW1 bit 0 (MAME "Reloading"), as R839 wired it.
     Every stage registered (hps_io inputs; pixels; units; off-screen):
     nothing longer than an adder and a compare on clk_sys (R843); the
     mouse arithmetic is plain concatenations, no signed casts (R662).
  4. THE CROSSHAIRS (rtl/video/m2_vcop_xhair.sv, clk_mem): a '+' per gun,
     arms 5 (Small) / 9 (Large), in the game's own player colours (P1 69FFFF
     cyan, P2 FF90A4 pink, from its GUN MARK CHECK) with a 1-px black
     outline, P1 over P2, hidden when the gun is off the screen, "Off" in
     the OSD for real guns. x is vid_x_d (the column the picture shows,
     R779); y is vcnt, or at 15 kHz interlaced the field row compared as
     line {row, cy[0]}, so the horizontal arm shows in BOTH fields (lines
     cy & ~1, cy | 1) rather than flickering at 30 Hz. R839's draft compared
     the field row with the 0..383 line (wrong in interlace: it drew at
     2x the height, in one field) and inverted the picture (invisible on
     mid grey); both replaced. Pipeline: dy per line, dx per pixel, the
     range tests, the colour -- three clk_mem cycles, inside the 6.25-cycle
     (24 kHz) / ~9.7-cycle (15 kHz) pixel.
  5. BENCHES:
       - test_m2_vcop_guns: every stick value of both axes of both guns
         (against the edges and centre): crosshair pixel, units inside
         MAME's range, units on the SAME pixel by the game's floor rule;
         every pixel 0..495 / 0..383 walked through the mouse for both guns
         by the same rule; 200,000 random mouse packets (deltas to +-255) in
         all four OSD modes against an accumulate-and-clamp model; 100,000
         random button sets against MAME's IN0 / IN1; 2,000,000 cycles of
         random reloads (joystick and mouse right button): 0 cycles with the
         trigger on the screen, the corner always leads the trigger by >= 1
         tick and outlasts it by >= 1 tick; a gun at +-127 reads off-screen;
         en low hides the crosshair. 417,523 checks, 0 failures. Planted
         faults caught: a threshold off by one (166 -> 167; Y2's 193 term
         dropped), the mouse's y sign, a border constant, the mouse buttons
         on both guns, Start / Coin swapped, the reload's trigger delay
         removed, the corner released early.
       - test_m2_vcop_xhair: m2_vcop_xhair in the real m2_video_timing with
         Model2.sv's ce_pix accumulator and vid_x_d, the picture being its
         own coordinates, sampled at ce_pix as the framework does: every
         visible pixel of a whole frame classified and compared with the
         expected cross, 18 cases (24 kHz and 15 kHz 273/274 interlaced;
         Small, Large, Off; corners; overlapping crosses; hidden guns;
         random): 0 wrong pixels, the aim pixel itself P1's colour in each,
         and every pixel not under a cross exactly the picture's (nothing
         moved). Planted: the interlace line rule, dx off by one, three
         extra cycles of latency -- caught; ONE extra cycle passes (that is
         the margin).
       - Daytona / Desert Tank identity: the guns' in0 / in1 reach m2_ioz80
         only through the unchanged `vc_gun ? vc_in0 : iob_in0` (vc_gun =
         game ID 1), the crosshair draws only with c_on (en = vc_gun) and
         Size != Off, and the bench shows the picture untouched with the
         crosses off; everything else new is inside generate blocks
         (VCOP_GUN). With M2_NO_VCOP_GUN the RTL is the pre-R846 core:
         quartus_map below.
       - lint_top clean with the guns on and off; lint_idx the same 147
         lines as 05e371c (only CONF_STR's text differs); quartus_map
         --analyze_file 0 errors (Model2.sv, m2_vcop_guns, m2_vcop_xhair).
  6. AREA, quartus_map 17.0, whole design:

       build                              ALMs est.  ALUTs   registers  block bits  DSP
       05e371c (R845, 77f69df's RTL)        40,181   57,379    48,780   4,379,775   90
       this, M2_NO_VCOP_GUN=1               40,181   57,379    48,780   4,379,775   90
       this, as committed (guns on)         40,468   57,778    49,166   4,379,775   90

     So the guns cost +287 ALM estimated (+399 ALUT, +386 registers), no
     block memory, no DSP. By entity: m2_vcop_guns 279 ALUT / 194 registers,
     m2_vcop_xhair 141 / 160, hps_io +42 / +55 (joystick_1, analog_1 and
     the mouse outputs now read, and the longer CONF_STR). OFF IS THE
     PRE-R846 CORE EXACTLY in all five numbers. A first version that kept
     separate crosshair registers in m2_vcop_guns measured +362 ALM; they
     now read the pixel registers. R836's ratio (+135 est -> +91 placed)
     suggests ~+200 placed on s1126's 41,267 of 41,910 -- ~41,470 (99%).
     The guns are ON by default (Ben: "if the area is modest"); it is the
     smallest piece of Virtua Cop so far, but the chip is nearly full and
     clk_sys has been missing on most seeds, so if a fit fails to place or
     close because of it, M2_NO_VCOP_GUN=1 in the QSF is the switch.

  7. TIMING RISK: the gun logic is four register stages on clk_sys, each one
     small adder or compare deep, and reads hps_io only through its own
     input registers (R842 / R843's lesson). The crosshair is on clk_mem
     (100 MHz): an 11-bit subtract, then 4-bit range tests, then a 4-way
     colour mux, each registered; its inputs from clk_sys are quasi-static
     and cross by two flops (sys_top's clock groups make clk_sys / clk_mem
     asynchronous, so they are not timed). What it adds to clk_sys is
     placement pressure at ~41,270 / 41,910 ALM.
  8. THE JAPANESE TEXT IS THE SET, NOT THE CORE. MAME 0.289 vcopa on a fresh
     NVRAM shows the same Japanese tutorial at 45-60 s. The language follows
     the COUNTRY in backup RAM byte 0x1b (CPU 0x01d0001b; 0 USA, 1 JPN, 2
     EXP -- the strings at program 0x29d20; the boot's WARNING routine at
     0x3a60 runs only when it reads 1, 0x1d40). A fresh backup RAM is filled
     from the data ROM at 0x2831ba0 (pc 0x2cf58-0x2cf68), which puts 1
     (Japan) there: the default of this ROM set, as MAME's model2.cpp notes
     for other sets ("Default country is USA / Japan"). Holding the byte at
     0 in MAME (sim/io/mame_m2_vcop_country.lua) gives the English tutorial
     ("The Lock-on Sight automatically targets enemies", "When your supply
     of bullets is depleted, aim the gun outside the screen") and the US
     attract (the EPA "Recycle it" screen, no WARNING). The core's I/O
     EEPROM and DSWs play no part. Not changed: the core matches MAME. A
     country switch would be a backup-RAM patch, a design decision for Ben.

*INFERRED (each with what settles it):*
  a. On the board a stick's crosshair sits on the game's aim: the board's
     GUN MARK CHECK (TEST -> GUN SETTING) with the stick and Crosshair
     Small should show each mark inside its cross, and AD1 / AD2 reading
     83 / 24 / 276 / 1a9 and 80 / 27 / 273 / 1a9 (a gun adjustment done in
     the game's own menu would move the marks off the crosses; DEFAULT
     ADJUSTMENT restores it).
  b. A USB gun calibrated in MiSTer (F10) aims where it points, its trigger
     arriving on the mouse button (default Mouse = Gun 1 trigger); aiming
     off the screen and pulling reloads. Untested: no gun here.
  c. The 1.64 ms reload lead is enough: the I/O handler's scan is ~1 ms
     (R839: 1,010 / s); the board will show a reload, not a shot.
  d. The build still fits and closes at the area above (a fit).

**R847 -- clk_sys AT 80 MHz: FIVE RECURRING PATHS, ONE COMMIT EACH.**
e252aa0 (Daytona + Desert Tank + Virtua Cop's type-2 I/O board and i960
forms, ~41,300 / 41,910 ALM, M10K 533/553) failed clk_sys on six of six
seeds (s1126-s1131: -0.558 .. -1.233). Reseeding does not close it; the same
groups recur. Read post-fit from four seeds' databases (s1129, s1131 re-timed
in sm2-builds/sm2-tim-sta with -detail full_path), each fixed on its own
commit on a3dd42f so they can be taken separately. Renderer, geometry and
sound worked in the releases and fail now from fullness; the I/O board is new.

*Now known -- VERIFIED (what each path really was, and the change):*
  1. THE Z80's FIRMWARE / WORK RAM -> tv80s di_reg (worst group on s1126,
     s1127, s1130; to -0.856). The RAMs are read on the NEGEDGE, so this is
     a HALF-cycle path (6.25 ns), and di_reg is in the wrapper, outside
     R590/R762's core-only exception. di_reg is NOT loaded on cen (tv80s
     loads it every clk of T2), so R590's argument does not reach it by
     itself; the argument that does is written in Model2.sdc: nothing but
     the core reads di_reg, every core register loads only on cen (busrq_n
     is tied, so ClkEn = cen), cen is never closer than 8 clks at 80 MHz
     (type 1 one in 20, type 2 6144 / (80 x 625) = one in 8.14), and the
     RAM output changes only half a clk after a cen edge (A moves only
     there) or after a write strobe ends in a write cycle (di_reg not
     loading). Type 2's f_op (the RETI watch) is the same shape -- loaded
     through a fetch strobe, read only after it ends -- and was next
     (post-map +0.685). Commit 2914d83: R847's two-cycle exception, RAMs ->
     {di_reg, g_t2.f_op}. Checked by simulation, not just argument: the
     ioz80 benches rebuilt at the REAL pacing (TICK 4/80, T2 6144) with the
     RAM data held back by exactly the two cycles the exception allows
     (fw_q / ram_q through two posedge registers), and separately with all
     of di held back two cycles into di_reg and the core's dinst: type 1
     hash 7606a0e5ca41b432, type 2 hash 699238baabf0fc75 (every M1 address
     and DPRAM write with its clk), 5,047 DPRAM writes, 7,445 interrupts,
     identical in all three. test_m2_ioz80_t2 (MAME) and _t1same pass.
  2. m2_raster_fill det_r (s1127-s1131, to -0.547, up to 422 paths;
     pf_st.S_PF_N -> det_r, pr_ax / pr_o1 -> det_r, pr_o1 -> nxo).
     *Believed:* R727's registers had taken the plane fit off the critical
     list. *Now known:* Quartus RESOURCE-SHARES det's multipliers with nxo's
     (ax*by - bx*ay and o1*by - o2*ay share by and ay; different states),
     so the path is pr_* -> an operand mux selected by the state register
     -> DSP Mult9 -> DSP Mult10's adder -> det_r: 0.5 + 2.5 routing + 3.9
     + 1.7 + 2.25 ns. S_PF_N appears as the SOURCE because it drives the
     mux select. Commit 9043cd5: dp_ab / dp_ba = the two products,
     registered every cycle (no reset, no enable: unshareable), det_r =
     dp_ab - dp_ba in S_PF_D; S_PF_DW waits two cycles (dw_2, cleared at
     quad accept), one more per pass, two or three a quad. Four frames,
     core configuration (MIP on, mode 1): every pixel identical (c3857662
     6d8e0e69 e04fb93e 1f325f0f); draw +0.44 / +0.02 / +0.41 / +0.51%
     (f2000 687,834 -> 690,834); fetch lists 0..4 of ~200,000 different
     (texel-cache timing, as R727). test_m2_raster_fill 152,373 / 0, _mip
     1,989,828 / 0, test_m2_raster3d 40 / 0.
  3. m2_span_tex iss_ooz -> d0_e (s1129 -0.702, 106 paths). Not distance:
     top_bit()'s loop with `n == 0` in its condition became an 11-cell
     priority chain. Commit 26e37f7: each byte encodes its own top bit,
     the highest non-zero byte picks. All 2^32 inputs against the old
     function: 0 differ. Four frames: pixels, fetch lists and draw cycles
     identical. test_m2_span_tex 7,214 / 0, _ftb 17 / 0, _mip 7,222 / 0.
  4. m2_geo_engine tx_c / xl_raw -> g_raw (s1129 -1.078 / -0.771, 110
     paths). gam()'s constant multiply landed in a DSP at X86 (the engine
     sits near X40) and g_raw packed into the NEXT DSP's input register
     (tslope's, X32): two long DSP routes in one cycle. Commit c96ca76: the
     curve as two 256-entry tables in logic (generated from the formula,
     all 1,024 inputs checked: 0 differ) and its select registered (g_sel:
     tx_c is set entering E_XL, xl_go is first high the cycle after E_XL's
     first mem_go). No ROM inferred (block bits unchanged), one DSP fewer.
     geodiff on w2300 / w5000 / w9000 (textured polygons take curve 0):
     quads, colours and cycles identical (822,322 / 868,855 / 624,572).
     test_m2_geo_engine 70 / 0, test_m2_geometry 438 / 0, _mipz 444 / 0.
  5. fx68k aob -> m2_multipcm_dual key_wait / s_active (s1130 -0.518, 233
     paths; s1131). aob -> the address decode -> the slot select (fanout
     149) -> the 64-way demux -> the enables. A multicycle would need aob
     never to move while AS is asserted, which is a claim about fx68k's
     microcode, not provable here; so a register. Commit 900760d: select,
     strobe, address and data registered together before the engine (one
     clk later, same order; nothing reads the chips back). Sound board in
     the core's configuration (PCM_SHARED, YM_STUB, TICK_DEN 80, 30 M
     cycles, 5,399 MultiPCM writes): output hash 27b719043c354a31 (every
     chip sample every cycle) and the cpu / pcm / mix hashes identical; at
     TICK_DEN 50 likewise (08146a194550d7c3).
  6. POST-MAP (quartus_map + quartus_sta --post_map, slow model, a3dd42f ->
     900760d), worst slack per path:
       S_PF_N / pf_st -> det_r     +3.230 -> +9.995
       iss_ooz -> d0_e             -1.171 -> +8.318
       tx_c -> g_raw                +5.343 -> (no path)
       xl_raw -> g_raw              +6.607 -> +8.539
       aob -> key_wait / s_active   -6.388 / -6.272 -> (no path; aob ends
                                    at the new registers)
       Z80 RAMs -> di_reg / f_op    +0.685 -> +13.185 (two cycles); di_reg's
                                    worst is now IR -> its enable, +1.158
  7. POST-MAP IS NOT PESSIMISTIC FOR DSP-ROUTED PATHS. R825 calibrated it
     at 2.3-4 ns pessimistic on carry chains. Here det_r was +3.23 post-map
     and -0.55 post-fit, g_raw +5.34 and -1.08: post-map leaves out the
     route to a DSP column, which is most of these paths. A path that runs
     DSP to DSP needs a post-fit reading; a good post-map number says
     nothing about it.
  8. AREA (map estimate): 40,500 -> 40,498 ALM, ALUT 57,838 -> 57,827,
     registers 49,170 -> 49,218, DSP 90 -> 88, block bits 4,379,775
     unchanged. By entity (ALUT / registers / DSP): m2_raster_fill
     5,225 -> 5,213 / +33 / 39 -> 38; m2_span_tex -16 / 0; m2_geo_engine
     +37 / +2 / 3 -> 2; m2_sound_board +3 / +13.

*NOT addressed (each seen post-fit, each its own cause):*
  - m2_geo_clip kst / cs -> the pool's round-robin grant -> m2_geo_engine st
    (s1131 -0.833, s1130 cs -> kst / mul_a_q -0.53): R727's "by design"
    combinational grant; post-map -3.28 before and after. The next
    candidate.
  - qoz -> oz_n / oz_emax (s1130 -0.476, s1127 -0.146): the vertex mux,
    kd_e's subtract and oz_norm's shift into a DSP input register; a
    different cause from the determinant. Taking kd_e a cycle early (the
    first vertex's in oz_pre from oz_emax_q) would keep S_OZ's cycles.
  - det_r -> its zero test -> the numerators' enables (post-map -0.90;
    not seen post-fit): a det_z = (dp_ab == dp_ba) register beside det_r
    would be exact.
  - ldr_top -> sw_burst (s1130 -0.225), m2_texel_cdc s_wp_g2 -> s_rp
    (-0.445), m2_eng_ra idx_q -> s_fill, raster3d pst -> the store's RAM,
    m2_geo_view sm_r -> a_right: once each.
  - sys_top gp_outr -> PhaseInc (s1131 -1.233, its worst): the framework's
    HPS config write, not ours.

*INFERRED (what settles it):* a. the five groups are gone post-fit and
clk_sys closes with margin on most seeds; the geometry pool grant is then
the worst left -- a seed sweep of 900760d. b. none of the five changes is
visible on the board: Daytona, Desert Tank and Virtua Cop as before.

*R847 addendum -- a3dd42f (the guns) and area.* s1132-s1134 (a3dd42f,
41,416-41,471 ALM, 99%): clk_sys -1.291 / -1.352 / -1.224, and s1134's groups
are NOT e252aa0's: m2_raster_div d_mag -> rem (507), the TGP's mb86233_alu
opr_add_b -> fp_add (29), hps_io cmd / byte_cnt -> status (24), MultiPCM v ->
pos_zero (4), the Z80's di_reg (2). So at 99% the failure moves with
placement; removing one recurring path exposes the next.
  * The divider's group is fixed like the others (db879d7). *Believed
    first:* the d + 2d add in front of each radix-4 step was the cost, so
    3 x |den| was registered at load -- and post-map got WORSE (-3.19 ->
    -4.07): the add was not on the worst path at all. *Now known:* written
    as `>=` then `-`, Quartus built each compare as an 8-level LUT tree and
    put the subtract's carry chain after it. Each compare is now its own
    subtract's borrow (three 35-bit differences side by side), with 3d
    registered: post-map d_mag -> rem -3.190 -> +1.032, any -> rem -3.240
    -> +0.658, -37 ALM estimated. The step against the old one on 117 M
    inputs (every rem and d below 2048, 100 M random): 0 differ. Four

**R849 -- THE CROSSHAIRS ONLY IN PLAY: THE GAME'S OWN STATE, SNOOPED ON THE
i960's WRITES.** Board, s1134 (a3dd42f): the guns work with joystick and
mouse (Ben). Two changes asked: a crosshair only IN GAME (not attract,
title, menus / test, continue, game over), and player 2's only while player
2 is playing. (M2_VCOP_GUN; game ID 1 only.)

*Believed (R846):* a crosshair shows whenever the guns are built, the game
is Virtua Cop and the gun is on the screen. That draws one over the attract
-- whose tutorial plays a 1P demo with its own revolver, hearts and lock-on
sights, so it looks like a game -- and over every menu, and player 2's
whenever a stick or mouse is near the middle.

*Now known -- VERIFIED (MAME 0.289 vcopa, sim/io/mame_m2_vcop_play.lua:
coins, starts, triggers and Test by schedule, the guns swept at the I/O
board, work RAM 0x500000-0x51ffff dumped every 0.1-0.5 s, snapshots every
0.25-2 s; then every write to the bytes found, with its IP):*
  1. THE ADDRESSES (work RAM, byte 0 of each word; the game writes them
     with st, whole words, mask ffffffff):
       0x5016d4  the game's MODE. 0 boot / the reboot after test mode (IP
                 0x267c, 0x20e8, ...), 1 attract (0xa2f0, 0x11f40, ...), 2
                 credited start (0x6ddd0), 3 / 4 / 6 into and out of STAGE
                 SELECT (0x6df9c, 0x59b60, 0x59e7c), 7 PLAYING (0xa4f0), 0x0c
                 the continue countdown when no player is left (0x99f8 /
                 0x9acc), 0x0d game over (0xacf4).
       0x50ee30  PLAYER 1: 0 out, 1 in play (0x20e0 at a start, 0xad48 at a
                 join or a continue taken), 2 its continue countdown (0x99d8
                 / 0x9a44), 3 its own game over while the other plays on
                 (seen for P2, 0x524a0), then 0 (0xacbc, 0x52518).
       0x50ee34  PLAYER 2: the same (0x221c / 0xae78 join, 0x9aac / 0x9b18
                 continue).
     Found by separating dumps: across scenario A (a 1P game to game over,
     then a 2P-start with one credit, P2 alone, to game over), 0x5016d4 was
     the one byte whose in-game values ({7}) never occur in the attract,
     continue or game-over phases (6 candidates; the other five are scroll
     / timer counters with overlapping ranges); 0x50ee30 / 0x50ee34 are the
     ones that are 1 exactly while that player plays. In the attract the
     words are rewritten every frame (IP 0x2144 / 0x224c, all 0; the mode
     stays 1); in a game only on a change.
  2. THE TIMELINES (state every 0.5 s; snapshots agree):
       A: attract 15-41 s (mode 1, demo with hearts and sights), start 41.5
          (2, P1 = 1), stage select 44.5 (4), PLAYING 45.5-76.5 (7, P1 1),
          continue 76.5 (0x0c, P1 2), game over 81 (0x0d, P1 0), attract
          87; P2 alone: 91.5 (2, P2 1) ... 7 at 112.5, 0x0c at 133, 0x0d at
          153.5.
       B: P2 joins at 56.5 (mode stays 7, P2 1); P1's continue 74.5-77.5
          (P1 2, mode 7 -- P2 still playing; the continue taken: P1 1); P2's
          continue 80-101 (P2 2), P2's game over 101-104 (P2 3), P2 0; P1
          dies at 108.5: mode 0x0c, 0x0d at 113.5.
       C: No Enemies, both play 45-150 s through SCENE 1 / 2 / 4 RESULTS
          (mode 7 throughout); Test at 150 and 170.
       D: Test in the attract (20 s, 23 s), then a game, Test in the game
          (80 s, 95 s).
       E: P2 starts alone (41.5), P1 joins at 61.5, P2's continue and own
          game over (76.5, 84.5), P1 dies: 0x0c at 89, 0x0d at 94.
  3. TEST MODE IN A GAME (D, C): the test menu is on the screen from the
     press (snapshots 60.3 s on: TEST MODE, then EXIT TEST MODE) while all
     three words still read 7 / 1 for ~3 s; leaving it reboots the game,
     whose first act is a write of 0 to the mode word (IP 0x267c). No other
     byte marks the test screens: the 140 separating candidates are the
     test program's own scratch and an input latch (0x50156c holds the IN0
     edge, 4 = Test) that also carries 1 / 0x10 for coin / start. In the
     attract the mode is already 1. So the RULE is: in play = mode 7 and
     player byte 1 and no Test press since the last write of the mode word.

*The core (rtl/io/m2_vcop_state.sv, clk_i960, inside g_vcgun):* a completed
i960 write (bus_req & bus_we & bus_ack & be[0]) to 0x5016d4 / 0x50ee30 /
0x50ee34 is decoded on the bus and five flops take the answers (which word,
lane 0 == 7, lane 0 == 1); three flops keep in-game / P1 / P2, one the test
latch (joystick 0 bit 8, the MRA's Test); play = en & in-game & ~test &
player, registered, into m2_vcop_guns (one more flop on clk_sys; clk_i960 is
an exact / 2), where c_on = en & play & on-screen. Nothing reads work RAM;
nothing is on clk_sys's paths but that flop. Stage select (mode 3 / 4 / 6)
is a menu, so no crosshairs there either ("shoot to select" has three large
panels); the SCENE RESULTS between scenes keep mode 7 and show them.

     and the tags) -> another client's grant -> SIX levels of m2_geo_engine's
     one-hot next-state chain (Quartus builds a shared hold term, so a grant
     used in E_LUMM / E_LUMA reached st.E_DONE, E_NORM, E_LINK, E_CC). Three

     requests are registers, set on every move into K_TEST / K_CLIP with the
     operation cs names there and dropped on their own grant. Tried and

commit, the TGP adder's alignment before its operand register (7ce9926,
~+117 ALUT), is reverted (9ecb403), as R848 advised; the other seven stay.
test_tgp's mb86233_regs failures (46,966) predate this work (R848 found them
on c545187 too) -- open, not yet looked at. Next: s1147-s1149 of 9ecb403.

**s1147-s1149 = b5f0c4d (R848 less the TGP adder): WORSE THAN c545187 --
R848's RTL IS WITHDRAWN.** clk_sys -1.060 / -1.582 / -1.385 (s1149 also
misses general[0] -0.048 and general[3] -0.264) at 41,453-41,476 ALM, none
closing -- against c545187 (R847 only), 2 of 3 closing (clk_sys +0.204 /

path margin with no cycle added, so more seeds close. *Now known:* at 99%

**R851 -- AFTER THE RELEASE (Model2_20261016, merged f7c41ad): BEN'S
ANSWERS, AND THE TGP REGISTER BENCH.**
  * Virtua Cop is PLAYABLE past its first stage on the board (Ben); R849's
    "MAME never got past stage 1" no longer limits what is known to work.
  * Virtua Cop's country (R846: a fresh backup RAM starts as Japan) is the
    game's own setting -- its test menu, or a ROM set from another region.
    Nothing for the core to do; no option will be added.
  * GunCon on SNAC (R841 route 2): noted for later, not being worked on.
  * test_mb86233_regs' 46,966 failures (R848 found them on c545187) were the
    BENCH, not the RTL. tb_mb86233_regs.cpp came from Model 1 with register
    0x21 as plain storage; on Model 2, rf 1 (0x21) is the input FIFO's pop
    and 0x22 the output FIFO's push (R112, 0e49c54, model2.cpp's
    copro_tgp_rf_map), which the RTL has implemented since 31 August -- every
    failure was a read of 0x21 expecting a stored value and getting the
    harness's FIFO input (0). The bench now drives rf_fifo_rdata with a fresh
    value each cycle, expects it on 0x21, and checks rf_fifo_rd (0x21 reads)
    and rf_fifo_wr (0x22 writes): 3,000,000 checks, 0 failures. No RTL
    change. All three games run on the board, as they did.

**R872 -- OPEN ON THIS CORE: TEXTURED COLOUR IS DAYTONA'S LUMA MODEL, AND
VIRTUA COP AND DESERT TANK ARE WRONG.** (Recorded on main from the Model 2A
branch's R867; numbered clear of that branch's entries.)
*Believed (R784):* textured colour can be taken from a fixed model of the
luma RAM -- row 0 a ramp (i/2), row 1 its inverse (63 - i/2), any other row
as row 0 -- and a colour table that is a straight line, read once at luma 32.
That is Daytona's data, and Daytona is right with it.
*Found (model2a R867, tb_m2_raster3d on MAME's own display lists):* the luma
rows and the colour table are the GAME's data. Virtua Cop draws row 16 as row
0 here (mean error 164 / 255, every pixel over 32) and its row 1 is 42 - i/3
(error 53); Desert Tank's row 11 is off by 51. On the 2A games the same model
inverted VF2's row-1 polygons outright (the "checkerboard" on heads).
*Fix (to be ported):* model2a 526ef64 / 47dd93c -- per texel, MAME's
L = min(63, lumaram[row][t >> 1] * luma >> 8), then the colour table and the
output curve, from on-chip copies (the luma rows a game uses, the 3D palette,
the colour table) filled from the CPU's SDRAM writes. ~9 M10K on this core
(533 / 553 at s1142). Behind a switch; Daytona's frames must stay
byte-identical with it off and match MAME with it on.

**R890 -- OPEN ON THIS CORE: VIRTUA COP'S AMMO DISPLAY NEVER UPDATES.**
(Recorded on main, numbered clear of the Model 2A branch's entries.) Ben,
2026-10-20: the HUD's bullets always look full. Suspected: run-time texture
updates (texture RAM written by the i960) not reaching what the renderer
samples -- a stale cache or copy. The 2A branch's Virtua Cop 2 shows no
bullets at all (model2a R889); whatever that finds should be checked here.
---

## MODEL 2A-CRX (branch model2a)

This section is the Model 2A-CRX core's. It lives only on branch `model2a`,
which is never merged into main (HANDOFF, 476fd6f / fa0b883): the 2A core is
headed for its own repository, its releases (RBF, MRAs, README) go into
releases/ on that branch only, and fixes that belong to both cores are made on
main/headroom and merged INTO model2a, never the other way. R832 (MODEL 2A-CRX)
is the board's description; the entries below are the bring-up.

**R852 -- MODEL 2A-CRX: THE BRANCH, THE BRING-UP GAME (VIRTUA FIGHTER 2), THE
2A BOARD BEHIND ONE SWITCH, AND VF2 IN THE WHOLE-CORE BENCH. NOT FITTED, NOT
ON A BOARD.**

*The branch rule.* `model2a` (from main 4b81d89; 476fd6f, fa0b883) is the
Model 2A-CRX core and is never merged into main: not code, not files. Its
releases go into releases/ on this branch only; fixes shared with the
original core are made on main/headroom and merged into model2a. The core
calls itself Model2A (CONF_STR) and its MRAs say `<rbf>Model2A</rbf>`.

*The bring-up ROM: Virtua Fighter 2, Version 2.1 (MAME `vf2`).* Chosen from
R832's 2A list because it is the plain board and nothing else (MAME 0.289,
GAME lines 7636-7639):
  * machine config `model2a` itself -- no drive board, no analog inputs, no
    light guns, no protection chip (not model2a_0229 / model2a_5881);
  * MAME flags 0 (works); Hanguk Pro Yagu 98 shares the config but is
    MACHINE_NOT_WORKING;
  * inputs: a digital stick and three buttons a player (INPUT_PORTS(vf2)
    over model2crx).
Next: Virtua Cop 2 (`vcop2`, flags 0): the same board plus light guns read
through the 315-5649's serial channel 2 (lightgun_mux_r / _w). Not Sega Rally
(`srallyc`, all sets MACHINE_NOT_WORKING in MAME, and the drive board), not
Sky Target / Manx TT (MACHINE_NOT_WORKING).

*What changed in the core (Model2.sv; with M2_NO_2A the original core):*
  1. SWITCHES. `M2_2A` (default on here; VERILOG_MACRO "M2_NO_2A=1" off) and
     two new switches for the original board's parts, both following it:
     M2_M1SOUND (the Model 1 sound board: fx68k, MultiPCM, YM3438, the ROM
     scan -- the scan stays at the top level and idles, see 9) and M2_IOZ80
     (the I/O board: Z80, MB8421, firmware, m2_cab_inputs). With M2_2A the
     M2_VCOP_* default off. With M2_NO_2A every switch is main's default.
  2. THE 2A MAP (MAME model2a_crx_mem): the bridge's BOARD_2A (it existed,
     unused) -- 256 KB RAM at 0x200000-0x23ffff, no program mirror -- at
     SDRAM word 0x12a0000; the 315-5649 at 0x01c00000-0x01c0001f
     (m2_315_5649: ports A-G, direction, mode, the RS-422 and analog
     registers as MAME's device answers them; umask32 0x00ff00ff, so device
     offset n is lane 0 / 2 of dword n >> 1) with the 93C46 on port A
     (m2_93c46, eepromser.cpp's 93Cxx: streaming reads, output on the falling
     clock, locked at power-on, no reset pin); 0x01c00040 and the boot ROM's
     other 0x01c000xx writes go nowhere and read 0, as in MAME.
  3. THE TIMERS (m2_timers, 0x00f00000): VF2 uses them and the original core
     has none (R835 measured Desert Tank's profiler harmless). VF2's interrupt
     enable is 0x21 -- vblank and TIMER 3 -- and its timer 3 handler starts
     the sound UART's byte chain; timer 2 is a stopwatch it busy-waits on
     (8.7 M reads in 90 s; 76% of the bench's instructions in its first 30 M
     are those loops). 25 MHz real time, expiry raises bit timer + 2.
  4. THE SOUND SIDE, SILENT (m2_2a_snd_stub). VF2 NEVER READS THE i8251
     (MAME, five runs: boot, attract, play, second boot); it sends 312 bytes
     in 90 s of attract from the interrupt-10 handler (31.25 kbaud, TxRDY
     idle-high), and boots, attracts and plays a round identically with the
     sound 68000 suspended from power-on AND with interrupt 10 stripped from
     every enable write. So the stand-in takes every byte and answers none.
  5. THE 2A ROM LAYOUT (mra/Virtua Fighter 2 (Version 2.1).mra, + [15kHz
     CRT]; image 0x2D40000 bytes): program 512 KB whole at 0 (no second half
     elsewhere -- the original core's prog_ext is off), main_data 16 MB at
     0x80000, textures 8 MB at 0x1080000 (MAME's 0-4 MB and 8-12 MB, the hole
     collapsed as on the original board), polygons 12 MB at 0x1880000, TGP
     tables at 0x2480000, 68000 program at 0x24C0000, samples 8 MB at
     0x2540000 moved by the loader's XTRA to SDRAM byte 0x3400000 (below
     ST_BASE). No copro data: vf2's region is ROMREGION_ERASE00 and the TGP's
     reads of it answer 0. The 1/x and 1/sqrt tables and the 2A video
     board's mpr-16310..16312 are unused by MAME and not loaded. VERIFIED:
     tools/rom_csum.py builds it; tools/mra_vs_mame.py --layout=2a (new)
     matches all eight slots against ROM_START(vf2) by CRC; a swapped
     polygon interleave is caught. vf2.zip holds MODEL2_CPU_BOARD's and
     MODEL2A_VID_BOARD's ROMs.
  6. THE TGP: VF2 DOES NOT RUN DAYTONA'S PROGRAM. Its upload is 3,802 words
     (crc32 fd8d0383; Daytona and Desert Tank: 2,024, d6d611dd), one upload
     at 0.204 s, and MAME's program map is 0x000-0xfff: the core's 2,048-word
     RAM could not hold it (replay: desync at the 4th io write, 437 of 465
     outputs wrong). PROG_WORDS 4096 with M2A (+8 M10K inferred). With it the
     replay of a 31-frame attract window (frames 1500-1531: 83,494 FIFO words
     in, 28,787 out, 81,637 io reads, 82,114 io writes; 53% of retired TGP
     instructions above 0x7ff) left 152 outputs wrong: MAME subnormal
     (8003ceda ...), RTL zero -- VF2's TGP program carries small integers as
     subnormal floats through fmul / fadd (pc 0xb31-0xb43). fp_mul and fp_add
     now take SUBNORM (on with M2A): the replay is BIT-EXACT against MAME,
     unimplemented-opcode flag 0 cycles. Daytona's race replay stays PASS at
     2048 and at 4096 + SUBNORM (its 15 differences are NaN encoding, as
     before). INFERRED: the MB86234 keeps subnormals as MAME's host floats do
     -- VF2's code depends on them, which it could not on a part that
     flushed.
  7. THE 3D's CRTC OFFSETS come from the game on the 2A board: MAME's
     horizontal_sync_w / vertical_sync_w (the tilemap chip's xhout / xvout at
     0x01040000 / 0x01060000: 84 + x, 130 + y). Daytona writes 0 / 128, the
     constants the core had; VF2 writes y = 127. Measured with the geometry
     differential (MAME 0.289 + p14 dumps, walks 1500 and 4600):
     m2_geo_view with the constant put 467 of 523 polygons 1.0-1.1 px low;
     LIVE (2A) -- walk 1500 523 of 523 equal, walk 4600 760 of 762 (one
     screen-edge clip vertex 1.4 px, one 5-vertex clip split differently);
     u/v, sort z and texture parameters equal on both; no hang (M2GD_HANG).
  8. CHAR RAM IS ZEROED AT BOOT ON THE 2A BOARD (the buffer-RAM sweep, 512 KB
     more). VF2 leaves parts of its glyphs unwritten and relies on MAME's
     zeroed RAM: in the bench at the WARNING screen tile RAM and palette
     equal MAME's (32,768 and 4,096 words, 0 differ) and the CPU's 190,432
     char writes equal MAME's stream, but 166,432 char words read 0xFFFF
     where MAME has 0 -- rows of every glyph missing ("GAME" read "GAML").
  9. THE ORIGINAL CORE IS UNCHANGED WITH M2_NO_2A: lint_top clean in both;
     test_m2_boot (Daytona, 3 M instructions) output byte-identical to main;
     Daytona's TGP replay PASS; quartus_map 17.0 against main (4b81d89):
     registers 49,291 -> 49,292 (+1: the TGP upload address is 12 bits),
     block memory bits and DSP equal, combinational ALUTs 57,774 -> 57,782
     (+8, spread +-1..10 over modules the change does not touch -- synthesis
     perturbation, as R839's +13), ALMs needed 40,416 -> 40,463. Found on the
     way: wrapping the sound board's ROM scan in a generate block mapped to
     30 fewer registers and ~100 more ALUTs with every switch at main's value
     (bisected over five maps); the scan stays at the top level and idles
     when M2_M1SOUND is 0.

*Benches added:* test_m2_315_5649 (the 315-5649 and 93C46 against a

0 wrong; six planted faults caught, one -- the denormalising sticky bit -- an
equivalent mutation); test_fp_mul_subnorm (4.0 M products, 1.28 M with a
subnormal) and test_fp_add_subnorm (2.0 M, 0.55 M), 0 wrong against host

m2_boot_harness A2=1: the 2A map, the 315-5649, the timers, the i8251 with
the silent end, Model2.sv's interrupt controller).

*Area, quartus_map 17.0 (Model2, ALMs needed is the map's estimate):*

    build                         ALMs est.  comb. ALUT  registers  block bits   DSP
    main 4b81d89                    40,416      57,774     49,291   4,379,775    88
    this, M2_NO_2A                  40,463      57,782     49,292   4,379,775    88
    this, 2A                        35,823      50,940     44,623   4,019,640    86

*The SCSP -- what the freed room has to take (assessment only, not built):*
  * Source: MiSTer-devel/Saturn_MiSTer @ a23bbb2 (2026-09-16) now carries the
    SCSP itself (rtl/Saturn/SCSP/SCSP.sv 3,141 lines + SCSP_pkg.sv 671).
    CORRECTION to §5.3's table: "MiSTer-devel/Saturn_MiSTer -- SCSP RTL
    present: no" is out of date; it is newer than srg320/Saturn's copy (89.7
    against 77.5 KB). STILL NO LICENCE: no LICENSE file, no header in either
    SCSP file, GitHub reports none -- §5.3's position (read it, do not adapt
    it; ask srg320) stands.
  * Measured, quartus_map 17.0, the SCSP alone (virtual pins): 2,577 ALMs
    est., 3,604 ALUT, 2,022 registers, 21,920 block bits in 24 tiny RAMs
    (~25 M10K, ~9% full each), 5 DSP. The 2023 copy: 2,073 -- the study's
    2,030 was that code. With fx68k (2,134 ALM fitted, R60-era; already
    vendored here) the sound side is ~4,700 ALMs against 4,593 freed: the 2A
    core would land where main does (40,416 est.), at ~98-99%.
  * Features: 32 slots, the effects DSP, DMA, timers and interrupts are in
    it. MIDI IS NOT -- and on Model 2A MIDI is the i960's only channel to the
    sound CPU; CR2 / CR3 are plain registers, no FIFOs, no status, no
    interrupt. Its sound-RAM port has fixed timing and no stall (RAM_RDY
    unused): an access every 4 SCSP clocks, data sampled ~265 ns later --
    the Saturn gives it a time slot of its own SDRAM. This core's 13-port
    round-robin m2_sdram cannot promise 265 ns.
  * The SCSP sees only its 512 KB of sound RAM (as MAME's scsp_map): the
    68000 must move samples from the 8 MB ROM into it, and its program ROM
    (0x600000) and sample ROM windows (0x800000-0xffffff, banked by 0x400000
    bit 5) come from SDRAM with DTACK stalls, as m2_sound_board does.
  So the SCSP is: a licence (or a from-scratch SCSP against MAME's BSD-3
  scsp.cpp, §5.3), MIDI added, a deterministic sound-RAM port, ~25 M10K (or
  MLAB), and ~4,700 ALMs with its 68000.

*THE WHOLE-CORE BENCH (make test_m2_boot_2a; M2_A2=1, the 2A image from
rom_csum.py, M2_MAXFRAMES=1300): VF2 REACHES ITS 3D ATTRACT, silent.*
87.8 M i960 instructions, 1,300 video frames, no trap, PASS; ~29 min on this
PC. Against MAME 0.289 (fresh NVRAM both):

    event                                   MAME frame   bench frame
    BACKUP RAM IS BROKEN / SOUND INITIALIZE     6           ~20
    WARNING screen                             ~85         ~170
    grey, SEGA logo, the first polygons        727          805
    3D attract (sky, landscape, fighters)      988         1070

The bench runs 78-90 frames behind from the boot screen on and the gap
holds, so the difference is the boot's speed (the bench's i960 at 24 MHz
against MAME's idealised timing), not a stall. From frame 1070: 1,000-1,800
polygons a frame out of the geometry engine; over the run 1,183 walks,
14,241 objects, 248,078 textured polygons (198 texture states), 1.45 M
texture words uploaded by the CPU, the walker's opcodes all known (unknown
0), no projection abandoned, the TGP never reads copro data (0 reads -- the
2A zero gate is never exercised by VF2). The bench has no rasteriser: its
frames show the 2D only -- at frame 1200 the attract's sky and mountains,
"INSERT COIN(S)", "CREDIT 0/2", "(c) SEGA 1994". 21 bytes went to the sound
side by frame 1300; intena 0x21 throughout.

Found and fixed on the way (each recorded above or in its commit):
  a. TGP program RAM too small (6), subnormals (6), CRTC offsets (7), char
     RAM never zeroed (8).
  b. A BENCH FAULT, NOT THE CORE'S: the bench served the TGP's buffer-RAM
     reads and writes at word 0x16d0000 while the harness's bridge puts the
     CPU's at 0x16f0000 (R257 moved one, not the other). VF2's TGP reads what
     the CPU writes there; on the reset pattern it ran off to pc 0x3233 and

     words in) was bit-exact, which put it in the bench. The 2A bench now

*Not explained, recorded:* the geometry engine refused 4,023 polygons as
non-finite (an Inf / NaN input) over the bench's ~230 3D frames (~1.6%);
the geodiff of MAME's own walks 1500 and 4600 refuses none. So the bench's

upstream state. Settles it: a geodiff of a BENCH walk (dump the bench's
buffer RAM at a walk) against the MAME walk of the same frame, or the
board.

**R854 -- VF2 AT 28.75 FPS: THE GAME LOCKS ITSELF TO TWO VBLANKS WHENEVER
ITS FOREGROUND OVERRUNS ONE. MAME's VF2 NEVER OVERRUNS; OURS DOES EVERY
FRAME. NOT THE DRAW, NOT THE WALK. NO FIX YET; s1160 MEASURES IT ON THE
BOARD.**

*What was believed.* s1150 on the board: m2-fps.py reads 28.7-29.0 in the
attract and in play (79 readings over 25 min, mean 29.5, four higher ones
at screen changes); Ben: it feels slow. MAME's render_mode_w comment lists
30 Hz games (skytargt, desert, vstriker, vcop) without vf2. The original
core's Daytona was CPU/TGP-bound until R815-R817.

*MAME's target (0.289, vf2, sim/io/mame_m2_vf2_boot.lua, traces with
sim/io/mame_m2_trace_window.lua TW_CPU).*
  * render_mode_w 0x00000004 at frame 3 (60 Hz mode); videoctl 0 (geo_parse
    every vblank). Flips (0x803008) 57-58 a second from frame 11 on, in the
    boot, the attract and a fight: ONE NEW LIST EVERY VBLANK, 57.5 fps.
  * i960 a frame: attract foreground 33.0 k instructions (32.3-33.4 k, 18
    frames), the rest of the frame a background decompression coroutine
    (resumed at 0x4aeac, saved at 0x4add0-0x4aea8; 110-167 k); fight 39.1 k
    busy plus 56 k in the vblank spin at 0x10f98. FP forms 5% of the
    foreground (mulr 537, addr 581, cmpr 304 a frame).
  * TGP 67.6 k (fight) / 68.6 k (attract) instructions a frame; FIFO in
    ~2,700 words a frame, out ~930. Polygons a rendered list: attract mean
    888 (max 1,598), fight 1,500-1,650.
  * Code: 34.9 KB distinct a fight frame; line-change misses a frame 3,016
    (8 KB direct), 2,113 (16 KB), 1,192 (32 KB) -- the size of Daytona's race.

*The mechanism (MAME dasm, verified in the bench).* 0x500000 is a vblank
counter the IRQ raises; the frame loop clears it at 0x10fc8. When the
foreground ends it calls 0x4bcd4: counter 0 (done inside the vblank) ->
mode byte 0x50006d = 0 and the background runs; counter != 0 (OVERRAN) ->
mode 2 (0x4bce0) and no background. At 0x10f74 mode 2 waits at
0x10f90/0x10f98 for the counter to CHANGE -- the next vblank. So a
foreground of 1.0-2.0 vblanks gives exactly two vblanks a frame, 28.75 fps,
and the game logic steps once a frame: half speed, which is what Ben feels.
Mode 0 with the counter at 1 goes on at once; counter >= 2 bumps 0x500018
(the game's own "CPU_FAIL" meter beside "CPU_POWER" / "CPU_WORST").

*Not the 3D (simulation).*

**R855 -- THE i960 WAS HELD BY THE GEOMETRIZER'S PUSH QUEUE, NOT BY ITS
MEMORY: R638's HOLD WINDOW DOES NOT FIT VF2's LISTS. FIXED FOR 2A
(m2_geo LIST_WIN); THE TGP's PORTS JOIN THE SDRAM CLASS.**

*What was believed (R854 on the board).* The i960 waits on memory ~78% of
every vblank, about half instruction fetch and half data, the TGP ~10% and
the geometry push 5.3-5.7%: "far worse than Daytona's tuned path", so the
fix would be the i960's memory path for VF2's code and data.

*What is now known.*
  1. VF2's DISPLAY LISTS (MAME 0.289, M2JMP_OUT, 4,315 walks, coin at 26 s):
     four buffers 8,192 dwords apart -- walks start at dword 0x0000 /
     0x2000 / 0x4000 / 0x6000 in turn -- every game list jumps inside its own
     buffer (3,322 walks with jumps; jump targets and ends <= 3,033 dwords
     from the start; only the boot's first ten walks run off empty memory).
     Daytona's are two buffers 16,384 apart with no jumps (R638).
  2. R638 holds a pushed word while a walk runs if it lands in [w_ip,
     w_ip + 12,288) -- and EVERY word once the walk has jumped. For VF2 the
     next list (8,192 ahead) is inside the window and every walk jumps, so
     everything the game pushes while the previous list is walked is held:
     the 128-word queue fills and push_stall holds the i960 (s1160's K), and
     push_busy stays high, so every store the i960 makes into buffer RAM
     waits for the walk's end too (R697's gate) -- in the bench that shows as
     fetch wait (5.9-6.3 cycles an instruction against 1.5-2.2 without it),
     the bridge holding the store while the i-cache's fill waits behind it.
  3. FIX: m2_geo LIST_WIN (default 0 = R638 unchanged; Model2.sv sets 4096
     with M2A). A word is held only inside [start, start + LIST_WIN) of the
     list being walked: at or past w_ip, or anywhere in it once the walk has
     jumped. 4,096 is half VF2's buffer spacing and 1.35x its longest list;
     Daytona's other buffer (16,384 away) was already outside R638's window
     and its lists never reach 4,096, so the original core's behaviour is the
     same with either rule (the original core keeps 0).
  4. ALSO FOR 2A, NOT MEASURED ON A BENCH THAT CAN SHOW IT: the TGP's read
     ports (8 tables, 9 its banked window -- buffer RAM for VF2, ~1,300
     external reads a frame in MAME's TGP trace) join m2_sdram's priority
     class behind the i960, texel port 2, the glyph fetch and the walker
     (SDR_PRI). The TGP waits on each read with one outstanding and was
     behind the whole class. s1160's K (TGP holds ~10%) is the measure.

**R856 -- THE MODEL 2A SOUND BOARD: WHAT FOUR 2A GAMES ASK OF THE SCSP, ITS
DSP AND ITS 68000 (MEASURED IN MAME), AND OUR OWN SCSP DESIGNED TO THAT,
SMALLER THAN THE SATURN CORE'S. DESIGN ONLY -- NOTHING BUILT IN THIS ENTRY.**
(Ben: we write our own Model 2A sound board and make it smaller than the
Saturn core's SCSP, 2,577 ALMs est. / ~25 M10K / 5 DSP (R852), so that the
room the 2A board frees (~4,600 ALMs) takes it with margin; sound before the
visual bugs.)

*The reference and its licence -- VERIFIED (headers read, MAME 0.289):*
src/devices/sound/scsp.cpp, scsp.h, scspdsp.cpp, scspdsp.h: `license:
BSD-3-Clause`, `copyright-holders: ElSemi, R. Belmont` (scsp.cpp also
`thanks-to: kingshriek`). In 0.289 the LFO is inside scsp.cpp (there is no
scsplfo.hxx). src/mame/sega/model2.cpp: BSD-3-Clause, R. Belmont, Olivier
Galibert, ElSemi, Angelo Salese, Matthew Daniels. Everything below derives
from BSD-3 sources only (THIRD_PARTY.md). The Saturn core's SCSP (no
licence) was not read; only its measured size (R852) is used.

*The method.* A patch (sim/sound/mame_p16_scsp.sh, applied to a private copy
of the MAME tree; inert without M2SCSP_OUT) logs every 68000 write and read
of the SCSP's registers and every 68000 write to sound RAM, each against the
sample it lands before (MAME brings the stream up to date on every register
access, so writes land between samples); MAME's mix per sample before the
clamp; every key-on with the slot's sixteen registers; the DSP program at
each start; MIDI bytes in; interrupt-line calls; the 68000's accesses by
region; MAME's derived tables. sim/sound/mame_m2_2a_snd.lua plays any 2A
game headless for 300 s (coins at 40, 110, 200 s, Start pulsed, every
digital player field on a fixed pseudo-random sequence, analog fields
walked for vcop2 / srallyc); sim/sound/scsp_usage.py summarises.
THE MEASUREMENT IS CHECKED, NOT TRUSTED: sim/sound/scsp_ref.h is scsp.cpp +
scspdsp.cpp ported standalone (BSD-3; the timers, interrupts, MIDI, DMA and
stream framework left out -- none reaches the mix), and scsp_replay drives
it with the logged writes. MAME's derived tables: identical. The mix:

    game      samples (300 s)  non-zero    differ from MAME's mix
    vf2         13,230,649     12,622,991     0
    vcop2       13,230,649     13,212,559     0
    srallyc     13,230,649     12,448,595     0
    zeroguna    13,230,649     12,386,880     0

So the logs are complete for the output, writes at sample boundaries are
MAME's semantics, and scsp_ref.h is a bit-exact golden model for the RTL.
(zeroguna is model2a_5881 with init_zerogun's patch, as MAME runs it;
srallyc is MACHINE_NOT_WORKING in MAME but plays attract and races with
sound -- and never loads a DSP program.)

*Measured usage (MAME 0.289, 300 s each; slot-sample = one active slot for
one sample):*

All four DSP programs use only MRD MWT IWT TWT EWT XSEL BSEL ZERO NXADR,
YSEL 0 / 1 and SHIFT 0 / 1 -- never TABLE, ADREB, ADRL, FRCL, YRL, NEGB or
NOFL. Not one game uses FM, PCM16, a reverse or ping-pong loop, noise,
SBCTL, SDIR, STWINH, EGHOLD, LPSLNK, DMA or MIDI out. Every one uses all 32
slots, the pitch LFO (triangle; zeroguna excepted) and timers A and B; Sega
Rally alone has no DSP program; Virtua Cop 2 alone touches the amplitude
LFO (26 slot-samples in 300 s) and timer C. EVERY 4 KB PAGE OF SOUND RAM IS
WRITTEN BY THE 68000: the samples are STREAMED -- the sound program copies
them from the 8 MB ROM into looping windows in sound RAM and refills behind
the playing position, polling CA (the position, 4 KB granularity) 3,000-
11,500 times a second.

*Sound-RAM bandwidth (scsp_replay's cache models on MAME's own access
stream):* slots read 26-38 bytes a sample; 256 direct-mapped 8-byte lines
(one SDRAM burst) miss 6.5-10.8%: 1.6-4.1 line fetches a sample. DSP reads
into 64 x 4-word lines miss 1.1% (vcop2) to 27% (zeroguna): 0.25-3.5
fetches a sample; DSP writes 4-10 single words a sample. The 68000: ~5 RAM
reads and ~8 RAM writes a sample, 26-35 program words a sample (a cache's
job). Worst case ~25 SDRAM transactions a sample, 1.1 M/s -- the order of
the Model 1 board's two MultiPCMs and uncached 68000 that the 2A build
removed.

*THE DESIGN (rtl/sound/scsp/, behind M2_2A; the original core unaffected):*
  1. ONE SLOT ENGINE, TIME-MULTIPLEXED, IN MAME's ORDER: 32 slots a sample
     in slot order, then the DSP, then the effect returns and the mix --
     DoMasterSamples' order, so a replay can be bit-exact. Per slot: the
     registers from a 512 x 16 M10K (also the 68000's view); state
     (position, next position, envelope volume / state / rate indices / DL /
     hold, LFO phases, active, backwards; ~160 bits) in M10K; ONE 27 x 27
     multiplier shared by the pitch LFO, the interpolation (p1 x 4096 +
     (p2 - p1) x f -- MAME's sum exactly), the amplitude LFO, the envelope
     and the three level products. MAME's tables as ROMs: EG_TABLE (1,024 x
     13), PSCALES and ASCALES (8 x 256), AR / DR (64), LFO steps (32).
  2. THE LEVEL WORD WITHOUT THE 64 K TABLE. MAME's LPAN / RPANTABLE[TL |
     PAN << 8 | SDL << 13] is FIX(4.0f x LPAN x TL x fSDL) in single
     precision. VERIFIED (sim/sound/scsp_level_check.cpp): two 24-bit
     mantissa products, each rounded to nearest-even as a float multiply
     rounds, from 256 + 16 + 8 factor entries, then x 2^14 and truncated,
     equal MAME's table in all 131,072 entries. A small serial evaluator
     recomputes a slot's five words (direct L / R, DSP send, effect L / R)
     when TL, SDIR, IMXL, DISDL, DIPAN, EFSDL or EFPAN is written (~700
     slot writes a second); the engine reads the stored words.
  3. THE DSP AS A SEQUENCED UNIT: MPRO (128 x 64) and TEMP (128 x 24) in
     M10K, MEMS / MIXS / COEF / MADRS / EFREG in MLAB, one 24 x 13 MAC, a
     step every ~2 clocks, MAME's semantics including its quirks (memory only
     on odd steps; LastStep from the 0xBF0 start; MIXS accumulating while
     stopped; DEC). All instruction fields are built -- they are cheap -- and
     the unused ones are benched with random programs against scsp_ref.h.
  4. SOUND RAM IN SDRAM, DECOUPLED RATHER THAN FIXED-LATENCY. 512 KB is ~410
     M10K, and the ring buffer alone (64 KB) is ~52 of the ~68 the 2A build
     leaves (s1164: 485 / 553). So it lives in SDRAM at byte 0x2580000 (the
     2A layout's unloaded hole, after the board RAM), on the three ports the
     2A build freed: 5 the 68000 (program ROM, sample ROM, sound RAM), 6 the
     slots' line fills, 7 the DSP (line fills and writes). No arbiter change.
     This SDRAM cannot promise the Saturn's fixed slot (R852), so the engine
     does what R821's MultiPCM does on this board: it runs ahead of real time
     into a small output FIFO, stalls on a miss, and the FIFO drains at
     exactly 44,100 Hz (22.5792 MHz / 512). Pitch, envelopes, LFOs and the
     timers count samples, so they stay exact; the engine needs ~1,000 of
     the 1,814 clk_sys a sample has at 80 MHz. Caches: slots 256 x 8 bytes,
     DSP 64 x 4 words (a DSP write patches a present line); the 68000's
     writes are snooped and invalidate either.
  5. TIMERS, INTERRUPTS, MIDI AS MAME HAS THEM: timers A / B / C count
     output samples ((255 - count) x prescale); SCIEB / SCIPD / SCIRE (with
     MAME's re-pend of an expired timer) / SCILV and the per-level line
     calls; the 32-byte MIDI-in FIFO fed from m2_sound_link's far end, MIBUF
     reads popping it; MSLC / CA / SGC / EG latched each sample.
     NOT BUILT (unused by all four; each would come back as a parameter and
     its bench): FM (MDL / MDXSL / MDYSL and the 64-entry ring), reverse and
     ping-pong loops, noise (SSCTL 1, LFO waveform 3 -- MAME's own is
     machine().rand()), DMA, MIDI out, the main-CPU interrupt (MCIEB / MCIPD
     stored, not wired; MAME binds no main_irq on Model 2).
  6. THE 68000 (fx68k, vendored) at 11.2896 MHz from clk_sys by a phase
     accumulator (enPhi at 22.5792 MHz), MAME's model2_snd map: 0x000000 RAM
     512 KB, 0x100000 SCSP, 0x400000 the bank latch (no 2A set has more than
     8 MB of samples, so it never banks), 0x600000 program ROM 512 KB,
     0x800000-0xffffff the sample ROM, linear. Autovectored interrupts at the
     SCSP's levels. Reset copies the 16-byte vector table from ROM to RAM, as
     MAME's reset_model2_scsp does. A 2 KB read cache on the ROM windows.

*Area target (quartus_map 17.0, ALMs needed est. -- the measure the Saturn
core's 2,577 is in):* the SCSP alone <= 1,800 ALMs est., <= 20 M10K, <= 3
DSP (Saturn: 2,577 / ~25 / 5); with fx68k and the board's glue <= 4,000
ALMs est. against the 4,593 the 2A build freed. INFERRED split: slot engine
~550, level evaluator ~120, DSP ~350, registers / timers / IRQ / MIDI /
monitor ~200, caches and three ports ~250, FIFO and output ~60, 68000 glue
~150; fx68k ~2,100. Measured block by block as each is built.

*Benches:* every block against scsp_ref.h driven by MAME's own captures --
bit-exact, since nothing any game uses is non-deterministic: the level
evaluator exhaustively; the slot engine per slot and the mix, replayed with
writes at sample boundaries; the DSP on the three games' programs and on
random programs; then the whole board (fx68k on the real sound ROM, MIDI
from MAME's bytes at MAME's times) at latency sweeps an order of magnitude
past the SDRAM's, for underruns and for level and timing against MAME's
mix (free-running, the 68000's writes land mid-sample, so not bit-exact --
R821's case).

**R858 -- THE 2A SCSP REDESIGNED: A MICROCODED SLOT ENGINE AND A SERIALISED
DSP. 2,720 -> 1,868 ALMs est., BIT-EXACT ON EVERY BENCH. NOT THE 1,300 BEN
ASKED FOR, NOR R857's 1,450-1,500 -- WHY, BLOCK BY BLOCK.**
(Ben, after R857: a stripped SCSP larger than srg320's complete one (2,577)
means the architecture is wrong; rebuild it narrow and sequenced, target
~1,300, the engine alone under ~700. Then, on the engine's numbers: go on
to the projection of R857's option 1.)

*THE DESIGN (rtl/sound/scsp/):*
  1. m2_scsp -- THE SLOT ENGINE IS A MICROCODED DATAPATH. One 32-bit ALU,
     the one 27 x 18 multiplier, a 16-entry register file in M10K (two
     copies, one per read port), all per-slot state in one M10K: eight
     32-bit rows a slot (CUR, NXT, the two LFO phases, ~EGST + VOL, the AR /
     D1R / D2R / RR rate rows -- the state row of eg_pre is read directly).
     A microinstruction is fetched into F (its reads: two registers, one
     state row, a slot-register word on each of two ports, one level word;
     its next address) and executes in E the clock after (one ALU result, a
     multiply, flags, latches, two side effects). The two halves are two
     ROMs (256 x 41, 256 x 66), the E one addressed a clock later; a hold
     (DISPATCH, WAIT) keeps a microinstruction in F and feeds E bubbles, so
     nothing ever stalls in E. sim/sound/scsp_uasm.py is the assembler, the
     program and a pipeline checker (register, product, table, flag and
     ring latencies on every execution path), and writes the include the
     RTL takes its field layout from. A slot is 23 microinstructions (26
     with the amplitude LFO, 30 with FM, 33 both); SSCTL 3 skips at the
     fourth. The effect returns, the output (DAC, MVOL, the 0x408 monitor),
     MAME's key-on sweep and the word-5 rates are microprograms too. The
     LFO waves are baked into one 16 K x 9 ROM (PSCALES / ASCALES read
     flat, as MAME's pointers do), the AR / DR rates into a 128 x 27 one.
  2. m2_scsp_regs -- the common registers as the 68000 wrote them in an
     MLAB (MAME's udata), only the bits read live in flops; the timers on
     one shared sample counter, each timer holding the count its callback
     falls due at; the interrupt lines as clear / set masks; MIDI in / out.
  3. m2_scsp_dsp -- SERIALISED: five clocks a step and one multiplier for
     X x Y, PACK's shift (x 2^e) and UNPACK's (x 2^(11-e), >> 11); B is
     never registered (ACC = (X Y >> 12) +- B at ph 4, every write of the
     step from the old ACC's SHIFTED then); MAME's all-at-once EFREG / MIXS
     clears are sixteen writes each (before / after a run); a go taken
     during the reset's clears is held.
  4. m2_scsp_level -- the final shift of a level word through its own
     multiplier ((m x 2^(24-s)) >> 24); the third factor read where it is
     used. 54 clocks a slot's six words.
  5. The fetch: one pick, from the cache's lookup only (a miss fills, then
     looks again).

*BENCHES (all unchanged; every one bit-exact against scsp_ref.h):*
  * tb_m2_scsp on MAME's 300 s captures of VF2, VCop2, Sega Rally and
    Zero Gunner (d81cfb6, SDRAM latency 6-40): 0 samples differ from the
    reference or from MAME's mix, the IPL right on every sample, 846 M
    slot-samples checked, 0 wrong.
  * The 40 random captures (FM, PCM16, the noise LFO, SSCTL 2 / 3, MOBUF,
    timers / interrupts / MIDI in; every third at latency 20-400): 40 PASS
    (and again on R859's timing changes, 517a535).
  * tb_m2_scsp_dsp: random programs at latency 6-40 and 1-400 (1,000,000
    runs) and the three games' programs, 30 s each: 0 EFREG / RAM words
    wrong. tb_m2_scsp_level: all 393,216 words.
  The benches found, in the redesign: a cleared state RAM reading as
  ATTACK (MAME's slots start in RELEASE -- key-ons ignored; the row now
  keeps ~EGST); the FM offset taken from the 32-bit-wrapped product (MAME's
  own steps never wrap; the slice is now of the full product); MON2 under
  a predicate that was false when MVOL = 15 (side effect 2 is never
  predicated now); a DSP go lost in the reset's clears.

*AREA (quartus_map 17.0, sim/sound/scsp_area_top.sv, all switches on):*

      no select in the ALU                          1,896

    block (final)                          ALUT   regs   ~ALMs

      the 68000's accesses)                1,188    561    ~900

    slot cache                                65     94     ~50
    DSP (+ its 64-line cache)             629+64 310+64    ~530

    M10K: ~45 (the LFO ROM 18, microcode 4, caches 8, the rest one or two
    each) against the 68 the 2A build leaves -- the LFO ROM is the first to
    compute in logic if block RAM gets tight (+~40 ALUT for the waves).
    Engine clocks a sample at SDRAM latency 6-40, 300 s (mean / max of
    the 1,814 a sample has at 80 MHz): VF2 1,092 / 2,087, VCop2 1,119 /
    2,056, Sega Rally 622 / 1,615, Zero Gunner 1,351 / 2,275. The peaks
    pass 1,814 and the output FIFO (eight samples) carries them; a random
    capture at latency 20-400 peaks at 5,192 with its mean at 1,284.

*WHAT R856 AND R857 GOT WRONG:*
  * R856's split (engine ~550, DSP ~350, registers ~200) was a guess and
    wrong by 2x; R857 recorded it.
  * R857's projection for the remaining work (DSP ~585 -> ~300, timers -70,
    level -40, engine -100: ~1,450-1,500 total) was too optimistic by
    ~400. Measured: the DSP's serialisation gave -47 ALMs, not -285 -- its
    shifters were ~120 ALMs, the rest is spread over ten muxes and adders of
    20-30 ALMs each (inputs, X, Y, B, SHIFTED, the address, the EFREG and
    MIXS adds, the 68000's read-back) and ~310 flops (ACC, MEMVAL, FRC,
    Y_REG, ADRS, DEC, the write and read addresses), all of which a
    five-clock step still needs. The timers could not go onto one
    decrementer: tb_m2_scsp checks the IPL the clock after tick44, so the
    three timers must count in that clock (the shared counter instead gave
    -34). The ALU-mux merges (PASSA / PASSB into the adder, RING / EFREG on
    one input, LFOI / RATE on one) measured +27 -- inside quartus_map's
    noise -- and were reverted.
  * Measured costs of what the engine is (variants, one piece removed):
    the A operand mux 92 ALMs, B 66, the ALU's result mux 102, FM (ring,
    MDL, the 68000's 0x600 window) 74, the envelope 40, the product slices
    30; ~560 flops (fetch addresses and samples, the latched register
    fields, 32 active bits, the 68000's access, the outputs, the monitor).

*WHY NOT 1,300.* The arithmetic is cheap; the cost is per-bit muxing and
flops of datapaths that must keep MAME's exact 32-bit int arithmetic, and
there have to be two of them: one sequenced datapath for slots and DSP
together would need ~770 clocks (32 slots) + ~1,000-1,300 (the DSP in
microcode) of the 1,814 a sample has, and running the DSP beside the next
sample's slots needs it to have its own datapath -- which is what costs.
The register block has to act in the clock tick44 or a MIDI byte arrives
(MAME's order, which the IPL bench checks) and so cannot be sequenced.
Against srg320's complete SCSP (2,577 est., ~25 M10K, 5 DSP): 1,868 est.,
~45 M10K, 3 DSP -- 28% fewer ALMs, more block RAM.

**R862 -- THE OTHER THREE 2A GAMES: SEGA RALLY, VIRTUA COP 2, ZERO GUNNER.
MRAs, GAME IDs 0x10-0x12, A LAYOUT EXTENSION, PER-GAME INPUTS. ZERO
GUNNER'S 315-5881 ASSESSED, NOT BUILT; VIRTUA COP 2'S GUN AIM SPECIFIED, NOT
BUILT. NOTHING FITTED, NOTHING ON A BOARD.**
(Ben: finish the mapping and MRAs for the other three 2A games; no 15 kHz
MRAs; static work -- MRA image checks, MAME source and short MAME runs, unit
benches; no whole-core simulation. NOTE: commit 88a02f1 on model2a, made in
parallel, also names R862 in its message (the 2A telemetry); this entry is
the games.)

*Believed (R852):* Sega Rally is out ("all sets MACHINE_NOT_WORKING in MAME,
and the drive board"); every 2A set fits VF2's layout; the 315-5649's analog
channel is cleared by a machine reset.

*THE LAYOUT -- VF2's slots do not move; an EXTENSION is appended (VERIFIED by
the tools; the SDRAM side by bench).* The three sets do not fit VF2's image:
  * program: VF2 512 KB; Sega Rally and Zero Gunner 1 MB (two 512 KB EPROMs
    interleaved), Virtua Cop 2 2 MB (CPU 0x000000-0x1fffff, four EPROMs);
  * copro data: VF2 none (ERASE00); Sega Rally 4 MB (mpr-17754 / 17755, the
    TGP's terrain data -- MAME's region 8 MB, the top 4 empty);
  * smaller regions (data 12 MB, textures / samples 4 MB, polygons 4-8 MB,
    a 256 KB sound program) are zero-padded to the slot, as MAME's unloaded
    space reads 0.
  The extension follows VF2's 0x2D40000-byte image: MRA 0x2D40000 the
  program from 512 KB (1.5 MB slot, CPU 0x080000-0x1fffff), MRA 0x2EC0000
  the copro data (4 MB). The first remap (XTRA, the samples) already sends
  everything past 0x2540000 to SDRAM byte 0x3400000, which would put the
  copro data across ST_BASE (0x3E00000, written after the load) and past 64
  MB; so m2_rom_loader has a SECOND remap (XTRA2_FROM / XTRA2_TO, default
  off -- main's core unchanged): bytes from 0x2D40000 go to SDRAM word
  0x1300000, the 2A hole between the sound RAM and GAME_WORK (program slot
  0x1300000, GAME_COPRO_2A 0x13C0000, ending 0x15C0000 < 0x1620000).
  Images: Sega Rally 0x32C0000, Virtua Cop 2 and Zero Gunner 0x2EC0000 (Zero
  Gunner's program slot padded whole, so 0x100000-0x1fffff reads 0 as in
  MAME), VF2 0x2D40000 (unchanged; the same tools PASS).
  The bridge (BOARD_2A): prog_ext now sends CPU 0x080000-0x1fffff to
  base_progx + the CPU's word (base_progx = slot - 0x40000 words); without
  prog_ext (VF2, game 0) the program reads linearly as before. Port 9 (copro
  data) reads GAME_COPRO_2A, and R852's zero gate opens only for Sega Rally
  (a2_copro_rom); for the others those reads stay 0.
  Checks: tools/rom_csum.py (now applies <patch>) builds each image;
  tools/mra_vs_mame.py --layout=2a (now: ROM_COPY, the GAME line's init
  patches applied to MAME's side, the two extension slots required wherever
  MAME's region has data there) -- PASS for all four sets, every slot equal
  to ROM_START by CRC (srallyc 10 slots, vcop2 / zeroguna 9, vf2 8).
  tb_m2_rom_xtra2a (new: the two remaps as Model2.sv sets them, the last
  byte of Sega Rally's image included, 9 / 0) and tb_m2_rom_xtra (7 / 0);
  tb_m2_cpu_bridge on the 2A decode (new build, BOARD_2A: 0x80010, 0x100020,
  0x1FFFF8 from the extension, 0x40030 / 0x7FFF0 from the slot, 0x80040
  linear with prog_ext clear -- 927 / 0) and on main's (925 / 0).
  INFERRED: polygon and texture addresses past each set's ROM read the
  slot's padding (zeros) or the next slot where MAME reads 0 or wraps (a
  4 MB texture region masks to 4 MB in MAME); copro reads at 4-8 MB wrap
  into 0-4 MB here (a 20-bit dword index) where MAME reads 0. None of the
  three is known to read there.

*GAME IDs (index 4):* 0x10 Sega Rally, 0x11 Virtua Cop 2, 0x12 Zero Gunner
(2A games from 0x10, clear of the original core's 1 / 2; VF2 stays 0).
Model2.sv: is_srally / is_vcop2 / is_zerogun (M2A only), prog_ext for all
three.

*INPUTS -- rtl/io/m2_2a_inputs.sv (new), from MAME 0.289's INPUT_PORTS; the
joystick bits follow each MRA's <buttons names>:*
  * VF2: R852's expressions moved here unchanged.
  * Sega Rally (srallyc + gears): IN0 0x01 coin, 0x04 test, 0x08 service,
    0x20 VR (view), 0x40 start; IN1 6:4 the shifter, ACTIVE HIGH,
    daytona_gearbox_r's {0,2,1,6,5} for N,1,2,3,4 (Gear Up / Down step it);
    IN2 PEDAL3 (hand brake): 0x00 rest, 0xFF held; analog channels 0-2
    STEER / ACCEL / BRAKE. The analog side and the shifter are Daytona's
    m2_cab_inputs, unchanged, with its four OSD lines (Pedals, Steering,
    Steering smoothing, Right stick) now in the 2A CONF_STR behind "h2"
    (status_menumask bit 2 = Sega Rally), on main's status bits. Behind the
    switch M2_2A_RALLY (default on; M2_NO_2A_RALLY leaves the block and the
    lines out). The MRA's buttons are Daytona's J1 order (Coin, Start,
    Test, Service, View, Hand Brake, Accel, Brake, Gear Up, Gear Down) so
    m2_cab_inputs reads the bits it always did.
    THE RANGE, MEASURED IN MAME 0.289 (headless, coin + start, auto-picked
    menus, a race held 120 s at fixed analog values, PNG every 5 s, md5
    compared): accelerator 0x00 = 0x20 = 0x30 (rest) and 0xC0 = 0xE0 =
    0xFF (full); steering 0x00 = 0x20 and 0xE0 = 0xFF (0x40 differs: the
    control); brake 0x20 / 0x30 = 0x00 at full throttle. So Daytona's
    0x20..0xE0 is full travel for Sega Rally too. The game has no
    calibration screen (GAME ASSIGNMENTS: advertise sound, country, cabinet,
    link, difficulty, mode); its INPUT TEST shows HANDLE / ACCEL / BRAKE raw.
  * Virtua Cop 2 (vcop2): IN0 model2's (coins, test, service, starts); IN1
    0x01 P1 trigger, 0x02 P2 trigger (both on IN1); IN2 0xFF. MRA buttons
    Trigger, Start, Coin, Test, Service; player 2 on joystick 2.
  * Zero Gunner (zerogun): model2crx with IN1 / IN2 0x0c unused; the stick
    and two buttons a player (the game's I/O CHECK calls them SW1 / SW2;
    the MRA says Button 1 / Button 2); SW3 0xFF (bit 0 low = its debug menu).
  THE 315-5649 now reads analog channels 0-2 from the cabinet (0xFF for a
  game with none, MAME's unbound default), 3-7 0xFF. CORRECTION to R852:
  MAME's device_reset sets only the direction and the mode -- the analog
  channel is 0 at construction and survives a machine reset; here it was
  cleared on the game reset (invisible while every channel read 0xFF). It
  now starts at power-on only.
  Benches: tb_m2_2a_inputs (new, in `make test`): 20 M cycles, the game
  switched at random, 120 M checks, 0 wrong -- VF2 against Model2.sv's
  expressions at 9fb631d bit for bit; Sega Rally against a model of MAME's
  ports (the gear table from daytona_gearbox_r; 45,857 shifter moves, every

*SEGA RALLY: WHY MAME SAYS MACHINE_NOT_WORKING, AND WHETHER IT MATTERS.*
model2.cpp's own TODO: "srallyc: initial enemy car placement seems to be
slightly incorrect for a few cars, seems to be affected by i960 clock speed,
may need wait state emulation to fix". MAME's February 2026 cleanup
(5aa8d67f35, "tentatively promoted some games to working": Virtua Cop 1 / 2,
Zero Gunner, Pilot Kids, Virtua Striker) left every srallyc set flagged, and
it still is on MAME master; the drive board (force feedback, 838-11661) is
hooked up but does nothing. In MAME 0.289 the game boots, attracts, takes
coins and races (above). For this core it does not matter: a start-grid

states, closer to the board), and the drive board's outputs are ignored here

*ZERO GUNNER'S PATCH (init_zerogun: maincpu 0x700 = 0x08000004), CHECKED.*
0x700 is `st g14,(g5)` inside the boot's clear of work RAM 0x500000-
0x53ffff (loop 0x6fc-0x718; g14 is 0). Before it the boot copies the PRCB
from ROM (0xb0) to RAM 0x5000b0 and reinitialises the processor on it with
an IAC (synmovq to 0xff000010 at 0x63c / 0x660); the clear then zeroes that
PRCB, whose +20 is the interrupt table pointer (0xae0 in ROM's copy). MAME's
i960 re-reads PRCB+20 on every interrupt (i960.cpp, three places) and so does
this core's (i960_top.sv T_INTR: boot_addr <= prcb_reg + 20 in every mode),
so both vector through a zeroed table; the board does not, so the 80960KB
must keep the pointers it read at the reinitialisation (INFERRED -- the only
reading under which the unpatched program runs on silicon). 0x08000004 is
`b` to the next word: the store is skipped, the PRCB survives. The MRA
carries it as <patch offset="0x700">04 00 00 08</patch>, and mra_vs_mame
applies MAME's init to MAME's side: PASS. The silicon-faithful alternative
-- latch PRCB+20 / +24 at reset and at an IAC reinitialise -- would drop the
patch and change every game's interrupt path; not done.

*ZERO GUNNER'S 315-5881 -- MEASURED, ASSESSED, NOT BUILT.*
MAME 0.289 (sim/prot/mame_m2_zg_5881.lua, 200 s: attract, two credits,
play):
  * the game writes 96 halves (192 bytes, offsets 0x00-0xbf) into the RAM at
    0x01d80000 once, at 0.97 s, and never reads it (all 152 reads are the
    chip's); it then runs 19 CHECKS: write the address (16 six-word entries,
    0x00-0x5a) and the subkey -- a 16-entry table in the program at 0x27a44,
    one per entry -- read the status (0), the dummy word and FOUR words;
  * every header is 0x00700 (plain, 8 x 1): the decompressor is never used;
  * WITH THE DECRYPT READS FORCED TO 0 (what this core does now) MAME plays
    the first credit with small differences from t = 40 s and then stays on
    a black screen from the end of that game (t = 110 s on); the real run
    goes on to the second credit. So Zero Gunner needs the chip.
  sim/prot/m2_5881_ref.h (new: MAME's 315-5881_crypt.cpp standalone, BSD-3,
  THIRD_PARTY.md) and sim/prot/zg_5881_replay.cpp replay the capture: 19
  sessions, 95 decrypt reads, 0 differ from MAME -- the oracle an RTL chip
  would be benched against.
  WHAT A BUILD NEEDS (ESTIMATED, not mapped):
    a. the RAM: 64 KB in MAME's map, 192 bytes used -- a 256-byte MLAB /
       one M10K at 0x01d80000 (written by the i960, read by the chip), ~10
       ALMs;
    b. the block cipher: two 4-round Feistel networks, 32 six-in / two-out
       s-boxes (64 LUTs), the key schedule (the game key a per-game
       constant -- 0x042c0d13 is MAME's ROM_PARAMETER; the sequence key
       latched at the subkey write; the middle result per word), the
       counter, the 2-bit dec_hist splice and the header parse: ~250-350
       ALMs pipelined over a few clocks at 80 MHz;
    c. the decompressor (two 512-byte line buffers, nine Huffman trees):
       ~200-300 ALMs + 1-2 M10K -- NOT NEEDED by Zero Gunner;
    d. the bridge side: the read of 0x01d9000c must wait for its word
       (m2_cpu_bridge has io_stall), plus the 0x01d8 / 0x01d9 decode.
  So a Zero-Gunner-only chip (a + b + d) is ~300-400 ALMs and 1 M10K behind
  a switch -- not small against the 2A build's margin with the sound board
  (R857 / R858). Stopped here for Ben's decision. A table of the 16
  answers would be ~30 ALMs but is ROM-derived data in the RTL (rule 4):
  not an option.
  [R873: NOT NEEDED. The chip is only a check -- nothing it decrypts is
  used -- and eleven one-byte MRA patches bypass it, 0 ALM. "So Zero
  Gunner needs the chip" above is wrong.]

*VIRTUA COP 2'S GUNS -- WHAT THE AIM PATH NEEDS (MAME 0.289), NOT BUILT.*
  * vcop2's machine config binds the 315-5649's RS-422 channel 2: a write of
    offset 0x0a (dword 5, the low lane) is lightgun_mux_w (m_lightgun_mux =
    data); a read of offset 0x0c (dword 6, the low lane) is lightgun_mux_r.
    The status at 0x0d stays MAME's HACK 0x0c. Today the core drops 0x0a
    and reads 0x0c as 0x00.
  * lightgun_mux_r: mux < 8 -> lightgun_data_r(mux) = port[mux >> 1], the
    high byte when mux bit 0 is set, of four 10-bit ports in the order
    P1_Y, P1_X, P2_Y, P2_X; mux >= 8 -> lightgun_offscreen_r(0): 0xFC | P1
    off-screen (bit 0) | P2 off-screen (bit 1).
  * ranges: P1_X 137..630 (default 0x17f), P2_X 134..627 (0x17c), both Y
    36..425 (0x0e6); off-screen within 5% of an end, as ints: X 24, Y 19.
    The reload is a shot with the gun off-screen and the trigger (IN1 bit
    0 / 1, mapped now).
  * so: an 8-bit mux register and a byte read mux in m2_315_5649 (~30
    ALMs); positions from MiSTer's sticks / mouse -- R846's m2_vcop_guns
    gives screen coordinates, rescaled to the ranges above (X ~ pixel +
    137, Y ~ line + 36 over 496 x 384: INFERRED; the game's own gun
    adjustment in its test menu settles it); its crosshairs (m2_vcop_xhair)
    and VCop 1's OSD lines under the vcop2 game ID. R852 measured the guns
    and crosshairs at ~420 ALUT on the original core.
