**R863 -- LINK PLAY OVER TCP/IP (Ben: "not for now", but for BOTH cores):
NOTED, NOT PLANNED YET.** Ben's Daytona recomp
(github.com/alphanu1/daytona-arcade-recomp) links cabinets over TCP:
src/runtime/comm_board.{h,cpp} transplants MAME's m2comm in its
M2COMM_SIMULATION mode (BSD-3, Ariane Fugmann; the board's Z80 program
EPR-16726 is not run, its protocol is): a 16 KB shared RAM the game maps at
0x01a00000, the CN / FG registers, a ring of cabinets (each sends to the
next), a numbering token from the master, then each frame's race-data block
(frame offset 0x1c0) passed on, and a vsync token; the host supplies a
non-blocking transport (TCP). Shape for MiSTer, small in the FPGA: the core
exposes only the shared RAM (in DDR3 rather than 13+ M10K -- main sits at
~529-533 of 553 M10K, 2A at ~539) and the CN/FG registers through the HPS
bridge, and a small Linux helper on the MiSTer (like MidiLink) runs the
ring protocol and the TCP sockets; estimated ~100-200 ALM in the core. A
UART path is too slow (a frame's block x 57.5 Hz is tens of KB/s against
115,200 baud). Applies to the original core (Daytona Revision A's link
board) and to 2A games with a link (Sega Rally among them). Behind its own
compile-time switch when it is built.
R863 addendum (Ben, agreed plan): THE ROUTE IS A HELPER PROGRAM ON MiSTer's
OWN LINUX, NO KERNEL CHANGE. On the DE10-Nano the Ethernet PHY is wired to
the HPS's EMAC, not the FPGA, so the core cannot reach the network directly
(the debug UART also ends in Linux, as /dev/ttyS1). Plan: the core puts the
comm board's 16 KB shared RAM in DDR3 and its CN/FG registers behind the HPS
bridge (~100-200 ALM, own switch); an ordinary userspace program, started
from Scripts or at boot like MidiLink, runs the ring protocol (the recomp's
comm_board.cpp, BSD-3 from MAME's m2comm) and the TCP sockets over Ethernet
or Wi-Fi. Rejected for now: a user-port Ethernet module with hardware TCP/IP
(e.g. WIZnet W5500 over SPI, ~150-250 ALM, no Linux) -- it needs an add-on
board for every player. Not scheduled.

**R859 -- THE 2A SOUND BOARD: THE 68000, THE SCSP AND THEIR RAM IN SDRAM,
IN Model2.sv BEHIND M2_2A_SOUND. 4,421 ALMs EST. FOR THE WHOLE BOARD.**

*THE BOARD (rtl/sound/m2_2a_sound.sv), as MAME 0.289's model2.cpp has it:*
  * fx68k at 11.2896 MHz (enPhi from an 882 / 3125 accumulator of 80 MHz;
    Model2.sv passes 225792 / SYS_MHZ x 10000), model2_snd_map: RAM
    000000-07ffff, SCSP 100000-100fff, program ROM 600000-67ffff, samples
    800000-ffffff, the bank latch at 400000 ignored (no 2A set has more
    than 8 MB of samples, so MAME's banks are linear).
  * reset_model2_scsp: the program's first 16 bytes copied into RAM before
    the 68000 leaves reset (it boots from RAM). Its interrupts are the
    SCSP's levels, autovectored (VPA on the acknowledge).
  * EVERYTHING IN SDRAM on ports 5, 6, 7 (the Model 1 board's, free on 2A):
    the 68000 (program and samples through a 128-line x 4-word cache, read-
    only so never invalidated; RAM uncached, every RAM write snooped by the
    SCSP's caches), the SCSP's slot fills, its DSP. Sound RAM at word
    0x12C0000 (byte 0x2580000), the 2A layout's unloaded hole after the
    board RAM. ROM_SWAP: the loader stores a word little end first.
  * The SCSP runs ahead into an eight-sample FIFO (MLAB) drained at 44,100
    Hz; tick44 also counts its timers.
  * Model2.sv: `M2_2A_SOUND` (1 on the 2A build; 0 is R852's silent
    stand-in). Reset is the stand-in's: cpu_rst_n & mem_rst_n & cp_done.
  * Area (quartus_map 17.0, the board alone): 4,421 ALMs est., 5,850 ALUT,
    3,196 registers, 3 DSP blocks, 323 Kbit of block RAM.

*BENCHES:*
  * tb_m2_2a_sound (make test_m2_2a_sound SND_IMG=build/snd2a/<game>
    SCSP_CAP=build/scsp/<game>; the images from sim/sound/snd_img.py): the
    board free-running on VF2's real sound program at 80 MHz against three
    SDRAM ports of random latency 6-40, with MAME's MIDI bytes at MAME's
    times. Not bit-exact by design (the 68000's accesses land when its own
    timing puts them, R821's case): the SCSP write stream is compared with
    MAME's in order (an LCS over a window; SND_FROM / SND_OFS move it).
    First 1.5 s: all 1,405 writes in MAME's order (100%), 0 stray writes,
    the FIFO never empty. VF2 20 s with MAME's MIDI: every byte taken, 98.2%
    of writes in MAME's order, the level against MAME's second by second
    from 13 s: 902/919, 1,867/1,927, 1,272/1,414, 1,869/1,937, 2,240/2,324,
    2,816/3,163, 2,709/2,720. VCop2 17 s: 2,716/2,716 from 3 s; Zero Gunner
    6 s: 65/74, 154/178; Sega Rally 19 s: 247/240, 198/203, 237/238 (the
    shortfall is the later boot). The bench first read the output port as
    unsigned -- a small negative sample showed as full scale; fixed.
  * The comparison first said 16-67%: MAME's capture holds a byte write's
    data on both bytes (the 68000 drives both halves); the bench now masks
    MAME's data with its byte mask too. A bench fault, not the board's.
  * THE 68000 BOOTS ~57 ms LATER THAN MAME'S (its first SCSP write at 0.456
    s against 0.399 s, 14% later; the offset constant after): the boot's
    RAM loop goes uncached to SDRAM and each access waits for it. MAME's
    model2_snd gives RAM and SCSP accesses ONE wait state ("the same
    waitstate weights as Saturn", before_delay 1) and the ROM none; ours
    take as many as the SDRAM port's latency costs. Sound is timed by the
    SCSP's timers, not the 68000, so this moves when the program gets
    there, not its tempo. Not changed.
  * MAME's sample map is three windows (800000 the first 2 MB, a00000
    bank4 = samples + 0x200000, e00000 bank5 = + 0x600000) that are LINEAR
    as reset leaves them; model2snd_ctrl moves the banks only for a region
    over 8 MB, which no 2A set has. So the board's linear 800000-ffffff
    window is MAME's, and the 400000 latch is ignored.
  * test_m2_boot_2as (new; the harness's A2_SOUND, the board on the i8251
    as Model2.sv has it, SDRAM ports at latency 12 with m2_sdram_cdc's held
    acknowledge): VF2 to frame 1,300 with the same picture as without sound
    -- once two faults were found (below).

*AREA AND TIMING -- WHAT quartus_map COULD NOT SAY.* The board alone:
4,421 ALMs est. The whole 2A core with it: 39,699 est., 40,9xx-41,0xx of
41,910 fitted (98%), M10K 539 / 553. The first build (s1170-s1172) failed
by -1.86 / -1.94 / -2.69 ns, every path in the SCSP engine: E started from
block-RAM outputs read unregistered (~3.3 ns of the 12.5 before any logic)
and ran operand mux, 32-bit adder, the envelope's clamp compares and the
result mux in one clock (q -> q alone was -0.49). Fixed (517a535) without
changing the microcode's meaning: OP_EG adds in E and clamps / writes /
loads EGV's address the clock after (the checker forbids a state write or a
Q use in the clock after an EG); the E microword read with F's and
registered (a bubble in its place on a hold); FETCH / TADR / output
captures from the sum or the operand, not the result mux (the checker
asserts their operations); the common registers decode from a registered
address; the level shift a clock after its rounding. Second build
(s1173-s1175): the engine's paths gone, clk_sys -0.85 / -0.38 / -0.003 on
one path left -- a timer written in the clock tick44 fires, through the
due adder; tested directly (count 254, prescale 0 is the only case,
bab8ea6). Third build (s1176-s1178): clk_sys +0.363 / +0.058; what fails is
m2_sdram's arbiter on clk_mem (-0.22, live since ports 5-7 are) and the
HDMI scaler -- seed territory at 98%; s1178 did not route. The whole SCSP
now 1,926 ALMs est. (+58), every bench bit-exact.

*TWO FAULTS THE BOOT BENCH FOUND (on its 48 MHz clock):*
  * THE 68000's FIFTH WRITE WAS LOST (9fb631d, R861): m2_scsp acknowledged
    every write into a four-entry queue with no full check, and the queue
    drains only in the engine's operation windows. VF2's RBP / RBL write was
    lost; the DSP ring landed at word 0, on the vectors; the 68000 took an
    illegal instruction at frame 175 and an address-error storm with its
    stack in the SCSP's registers at 649, writing MOBUF on the way -- the
    "MIDI byte back". The SCSP bench never saw it: it waits for the engine
    to go quiet after every write ("the 68000 is never faster than this" --
    false on the board). A write that finds the queue full now waits, and
    its DTACK with it.
  * The i960 stalled its command burst once a byte came back: Model2.sv
    raised IRQ 10 on a rising edge of TXRDY | RXRDY (R860, the parent's
    fix: MAME asserts while either is high).

*s1176 / s1190 ON THE BOARD: SILENT.* The 68000 runs, bytes arrive, voices
are programmed, no underruns -- and the board's output is 0 in every record
while the bench at the same RTL plays. Exact zero is MVOL = 0 (the output
is T0 x mvol_gain(0) >> 16); in sim the driver writes MVOL at 3.03 s after
its RAM phase, with the timers, then scans 0x408 at ~80,000 writes a
second -- the board shows no such scan. So the driver's init diverges on
the hardware. 3c609bd checks the sound RAM through port 5 before the 68000
runs (4 K words, the byte enables too) and clears all 512 KB to zero as
MAME's starts; 86dc162's 'U' record reports the check, MVOL and the writes
to 0x400 / 0x418 -- the next board run decides between the SDRAM path and
power-up content.

*NOT DONE:* the 68000's wait states measured against a real board; the
SDRAM latency the board sees on ports 5-7 under load (the engine needs it
low: at 20-400 clocks its mean is ~3,300 a sample, past real time).

**R865 -- SEGA RALLY AND ZERO GUNNER BLACK AT 0 FPS (s1192): BOTH TRAP ON
flushreg IN THEIR FIRST INSTRUCTIONS. flushreg ALONE (i960_top FR) NOW LIVE
FOR THE THREE 2A GAMES (M2_2A_FPU). NOT YET FITTED.**
(Board, s1192 = model2a 6f55e59: VF2 and Virtua Cop 2 run at 57.5 fps --
so R862's program extension and bridge window work; Sega Rally and Zero
Gunner black, 0 fps, for 2 minutes. MRA parts checked against the zips.)

*Believed (R862):* the three games need only their MRA, inputs and layout;
the i960 forms were not re-checked for them -- R852's form check was VF2's.

*Found (MAME 0.289, static scan + breakpoints; no simulation):*
  1. sim/io/vf2_formscan.py over each program: Sega Rally holds 372
     candidates of 23 forms this core traps on in the 2A build (VCOP_FPU is
     0 there), Zero Gunner 151 of 16, Virtua Cop 2 36 of 9 (none executed --
     it runs).
  2. sim/io/mame_m2_bphits.lua with a breakpoint on every candidate:
     FLUSHREG IS EXECUTED AT 0x005C0 BY SEGA RALLY (frame 4) AND AT 0x00670
     BY ZERO GUNNER (frame 0) -- the boot. On this core that is a trap and a
     halted i960: a black screen at 0 fps, exactly R844's Virtua Cop 1 fault.
     flushreg is one of i960_top's VC forms (R844), in the original core for
     Virtua Cop and left out of the 2A build with the rest of VCOP_FPU (R852:
     the trig microcode, 172 ALUT + 24,576 bits).
     Over the whole session (220 s each: boot, attract, coins at 60 s and
     150 s, starts, play -- Sega Rally with the accelerator held and the
     wheel swept) NO OTHER CANDIDATE IS EVER HIT: flushreg once per game,
     nothing else of the 372 / 151 (calls, cvtilr, atanr, logr, sinr, the rl
     transcendentals, cvtzril, cpysre, movre ...). INFERRED for code those
     runs never reached (later stages, test mode).
  3. Ruled out on the way:
     * MiSTer's <patch> (Main_MiSTer support/arcade/mra_loader.cpp): the
       whole <rom> is assembled in one buffer (rom_checksz reallocs) and
       rom_patch memcpys at the offset from its start once the parts are in
       -- our 0x700 in the image, little-endian bytes 04 00 00 08 = MAME's
       ROM[0x700/4] = 0x08000004. Right as written.
     * Sega Rally's copro data: its TGP reads none at boot (0 copro-data
       reads in the first 3 s); the TGP program is not even uploaded until
       frame 81 (1,665 words) -- frames 12-81 are a frame-count delay polling
       videoctl (0x98000c), not 0x980004. The two TGP windows replayed
       through m2_copro (4096 words, SUBNORM): Zero Gunner frames 12-102 (204
       in, 44 out, 104 io reads) and Sega Rally 81-171 / 83-143 -- PASS,
       bit-exact against MAME.
     * The comm board: Sega Rally reads 0x01a14000 once and writes it twice;
       it does not wait on it. The drive board is write-only from the i960
       (port E). Backup RAM stays inside 0x01d00000-0x01d03fff.
     * The EEPROM: Sega Rally reads 18 words (all 0xFFFF fresh), writes its
       defaults and polls ready after each write; Zero Gunner likewise. The
       93C46 is benched against MAME's device (R852) including that polling.
     * Zero Gunner's 315-5881 reads 0 here, as in R862's zeroed MAME run
       (which boots and plays a credit). The i8251: Zero Gunner polls status
       for TxRDY (0x81 / 0x85) before each byte, never reads data.

*FIX:* i960_top has a new parameter FR -- flushreg's dispatch live while
vc_en, without the rest of VC (no transcendental microcode, no M10K; the
register file has always done the work, R844). Model2.sv: M2_2A_FPU
(default 1) builds VC = VCOP_FPU (0 on 2A) and FR = FPU2A, vc_en =
(VCOP_FPU & is_vcop) | (FPU2A & (is_srally | is_vcop2 | is_zerogun)). VF2
(game 0) keeps vc_en low: its core is as before. A first cut turned on the

showed flushreg is all either game needs. Cost now: one AND-OR in the
dispatch, two flops of sync; not mapped.
Bench: test_i960_top_fr (new: the whole-CPU lockstep on an FR=1, VC=0 build
with vc_en high, the reference's flushreg live -- 200 programs, 0

**R867 -- "SOME TEXTURES GET A CHECKERBOARD" (Ben, VF2 on s1164 / s1192: a
character's head): NOT THE CHECKER BIT. R784'S TEXTURED-COLOUR MODEL ASSUMES
DAYTONA'S LUMA RAM AND COLOUR TABLE, AND VF2'S ARE NEITHER. FIXED ON THE 2A
BUILD BY COLOURING EVERY TEXEL THROUGH THE GAME'S OWN TABLES (TEXLUT). MAIN
UNCHANGED -- BUT MAIN'S VIRTUA COP AND DESERT TANK HAVE THE SAME FAULT.**

*Believed (the task, and R784):* either hdr0[15] (MAME's `checker`, the
stipple) reaches polygons MAME does not flag, or the pattern is sampling
(nibble order, banks, bilinear, mip). R784 recorded "lumaram rows other than
0 and 1 (taken as row 0)" as NOT VERIFIED and built the textured colour as
min(255, A + slope * lum(t) / 32), lum = t/4 for row 0 and 63 - t/4 for row
1 -- Daytona's two rows -- with the slope read from the colour table at luma
32, which is exact only for a table that is a pedestal plus a straight line.

*Measured (MAME 0.289 vf2, M2DIFF / M2MIP dumps of attract lists 100-3800;
tb_m2_raster3d in Model2.sv's m2_raster3d configuration, MAME's lists, MAME's
curve, every textured pixel MAME drew):*
  1. THE CHECKER BIT IS INNOCENT. MAME's VF2 lists carry 40 checker polygons
     in 110 s of attract (4 in some lists, a stage effect), none on a
     character. geodiff_2a on MAME's walks 1500 / 4600 (the current RTL):
     texture parameters, the checker bit included, 532 / 767 quads, 0 differ.
  2. VF2's LUMA RAM: row 0 = floor((i+1)/3) (0..42), row 1 = 49 + i/8 (a
     bright, nearly flat ramp), rows 2 and 3 = i/2. Its polygons use rows 0-3
     only (30,623 / 8,399 / 30,032 / 8,311 over 50 lists). Every row-1
     polygon was drawn with R784's INVERSE ramp: full-contrast and
     inverted -- Shun Di's white beard black, Akira's dark brows and eyes
     white, the temple floor white for teal, its walls white for brown.
  3. VF2's COLOUR TABLE has a second ramp above luma 48 (c5 = 8: 64, 71 ..
     143 for luma 4..44, then 64, 140, 185, 203 for 48..60). Row-1 polygons
     always land there (their luma is >= 224, so L = 48..62); 28% of rows
     2-3 pixels do too. No single slope can follow it.
  4. THE SAMPLING IS FINE: MAME's own texel and luma per pixel (colour.txt)
     through R784's colour model give the same error as the whole RTL (f400:
     row 1 mean 139 / 255 against the RTL's 138, row 0 34 against 45); MAME's
     formula on the same inputs gives 0.
  The board's own screenshot (s1150, Shun Di from behind) shows exactly this:
  his head black with skin-coloured texels through it, the floor white.

*The fix (TEXLUT, M2_2A only -- Model2.sv R3D_TEXLUT = M2A):* m2_span_tex
colours a textured pixel as model2rd.ipp does,
    L = min(63, lumaram[row][t >> 1] * luma >> 8)
    colour = gamma(colortable[ch][palette3d[colorbase].c5[ch]][L])
from three shadows written where the CPU's writes land in SDRAM (bridge port
1, Model2.sv): eight luma RAM rows (1 M10K), the 3D palette's 1,024 entries
(2 M10K) and the colour table at luma 0-63 (3 x 2 M10K). Five stages after
the retire instead of one (luma read; L; three table reads; v - bias; x K),
all moving together on the output's handshake; a skipped last texel can free
its span's parameter set while earlier pixels are still in them, so y and
the stipple ride by value. The curve is m2_geo_engine's gam(): 0 at or below
the bias, (v - bias) x K >> 16 clamped (MAME 64 / 87496, Mild 32 / 74941,
Off identity) -- exact against the GAM_B64/B32 tables by construction.
m2_geo_engine (TEXLUT) hands a textured polygon's colour base on instead of
the slope (no palette or table read, no cache entry); textures Off colours
it flat and clears its textured bit there. The quad carries {luma, colour
base} in the store's colour field (17 raw bits, RAWCOL), the slot in the
texture word (TXW 26) and one bit beside the vertices (VX) -- every bit the
store's M10K already had spare (att 30 of 30, uvt 195 of 195, vtx 105 of
105): 0 M10K there. The OSD's texture brightness (R239) does not apply.
THE EIGHT ROWS ARE PER GAME (MAME 0.289, every polygon of 50 attract lists):
VF2 0-3, Virtua Cop 2 0, 1, 16, Sega Rally 0, 1 -> slots {row[4], row[1:0]}
(rows 0-3, 16-19); Zero Gunner 0-5, 9, 100 -> its own map (is_zerogun). A
row outside its game's eight takes the slot it aliases. Zero Gunner's map is
from its rows only; its pictures are NOT benched.

*Before / after (mean max-channel error of 255 / share over 32):*
    list                         R784 model        TEXLUT
    VF2  f2620 Akira close-up    24.22 / 20.20%    1.33 / 0.37%
    VF2  f100  Shun Di, temple  100.66 / 79.63%    4.02 / 0.77%
    VF2  f400                   108.74 / 80.83%    3.71 / 1.39%
    VF2  f520 / f900 / f1000     45.2 / 82.2 / 74.1  3.34 / 5.95 / 4.09
    VF2  f1480 / f1500 / f3000   79.6 / 58.5 / 53.0  5.83 / 5.76 / 4.99
    VF2  f3800                   60.58 / 63.72%    4.63 / 1.35%
    VCop2 v300 / v3200 / v4800   80.8 / 38.0 / 25.2  3.68 / 0.87 / 4.18
  (what is left is sampling -- bilinear, mip, the quarter-pixel fit.) Draw
  time +1-2% (f1500 703,451 -> 711,053 core cycles; v4800 1,071,907 ->
  1,084,390): the five stages are latency, not throughput.

*Main is unchanged:* at TEXLUT 0 the raster bench paints byte-identical

**R866 -- AREA FOR THE 2A BUILD: THE REDUCED FPU IS IMPOSSIBLE (SEGA RALLY AND
ZERO GUNNER RUN LONG-REAL CODE FROM WORK RAM); THREE FLIP-FLOP ARRAYS MOVED
TO MLAB, EXACT, -896 ALMs ESTIMATED. AND R865 IS INCOMPLETE: BOTH GAMES STILL
TRAP.**
(Goal, Ben: room in the 2A build -- 98%, 41,034 ALM in s1192 -- for Zero
Gunner's 315-5881 and more; every change exact, benched against the old
RTL.)

*Believed (R818 c, R865):* a single-precision i960 FPU (FP_EXT 0, ~-1,000..
-1,250 placed) might serve the 2A games; R865's breakpoints said Sega Rally
and Zero Gunner run flushreg and nothing else the 2A core lacks. FP_EXT does
not exist in the RTL: R818 named it as a requirement, never built.

*Now known (VERIFIED, MAME 0.289):*
  1. SEGA RALLY AND ZERO GUNNER RUN FROM A COPY IN WORK RAM. A trace at 30 s
     shows Sega Rally at PC 0x5cxxxx; dumps of 0x500000-0x5fffff at 5 / 15 /
     40 / 80 s (sim/io/mame_m2_ramdump.lua) match the program ROM: Sega
     Rally RAM 0x5a0000-0x5fd7ff = ROM 0x1000-0x5e7ff, Zero Gunner RAM
     0x540000-0x5cebff = ROM 0x40000-0xcebff, unchanged from 15 s on. A ROM
     breakpoint never fires for that code, so R865's "no other candidate is
     ever hit" saw only the boot. VF2 and Virtua Cop 2 run from ROM.
  2. Every FP-class word of each program tagged RL (long-real / extended
     form), FPR (a single form naming fp0-fp3) or SGL (sim/io/
     i960_fpext_scan.py), breakpointed at its ROM address and at its RAM
     copy, one-shot (mame_m2_bphits.lua BP_ONCE), coins and play inputs
     (BP_MASH). Forms executed (distinct PCs, first time):
       VF2 (420 s): addr subr mulr divr cmpr cvtri cvtzri cvtir -- SGL only.
       Virtua Cop 2 (420 s): the same set plus sqrtr (122.9 s) -- SGL only.
       Zero Gunner (420 s): movr/movrl/addrl/subrl/mulrl/cmprl from 1.57 s,
         divrl 26.5 s, fp0-fp3 throughout, and CPYSRE AT 39.95 s.
       Sega Rally (97 s): movr/movrl/divrl/mulrl/addrl and fp0-fp3 from
         0.089 s, CVTZRIL AT 0.123 s, then at 23.54 s cmprl, ATANR, REMR,
         CPYSRE, and SINR at 46.37 s.
     Traces confirm each: 0x5a2dc4 cvtzril fp0,g4 (0.10-0.13 s);
     0x5465f0 cpysre fp0,+0.0,fp0 (Zero Gunner, 39.93 s); 0x5ddd40 atanr
     g6,g7,g6 and 0x5ddd54 remr r11,g6,g5 (Sega Rally, 23.53 s).
  3. So FP_EXT 0 IS NOT POSSIBLE on a core that runs Sega Rally or Zero
     Gunner: both live in long-real arithmetic and fp0-fp3 from boot. Not
     built. The full double datapath stays.
  4. R865'S BUILD STILL TRAPS. On the 2A core (VC 0, FR 1) cvtzril and
     cpysre trap (VC forms); atanr, remr and sinr have no RTL at all
     (vf2_formscan RTL_LACKS). Sega Rally halts at its 0.123 s cvtzril --
     black, as before flushreg was fixed; Zero Gunner at ~40 s. Needed:
     cvtzril and cpysre live under FR-like gating (they are VC's own forms,
     no microcode); atanr / sinr as the single forms of R845's sequencer
     (MAME: atan2 / sin on the widened double, rounded to float -- so the
     VC microcode, ~+241 ALM, 4 M10K); remr (fmod, exact) is new: an
     iterative remainder. NOT DONE HERE.

*Changed (each exact; quartus_map 17.0, whole design, 2A build):*

     + TGP rf in MLAB                          39,267   56,210  47,124  1,654
     + geometry xform matrix in MLAB           39,110   56,046  46,740  1,718

**R870 -- VIRTUA COP 2'S GUNS: VIRTUA COP'S DRIVER ON THE 315-5649'S SERIAL
CHANNEL 2. M2_2A_VCOP2_GUN, ON BY DEFAULT IN THE 2A BUILD. +289 ALMs
ESTIMATED. NOTHING FITTED, NOTHING ON A BOARD.**
(Ben: "Virtua Cop 2 has no gun driver for joypad or mouse. It should use the
same as Virtua Cop." The last open item of R862's Virtua Cop 2 section.)

*Believed (R862):* channel 2 is the gun board (lightgun_mux_w / _r, read from
model2.cpp, not run); "X ~ pixel + 137, Y ~ line + 36 over 496 x 384"
(INFERRED); the guns, crosshairs and VCop 1's OSD lines go across under the
vcop2 game ID; R849's in-play rule (mode word, player words, a Test latch)
would carry over with new addresses.

*Now known -- VERIFIED (MAME 0.289, sim/io/mame_m2_vcop2_play.lua; five runs,
one MAME at a time, -video none):*
  1. HOW THE GAME READS ITS GUNS. A write tap on CPU 0x01c00014 (device
     offset 0x0a, lane 0) and a read tap on 0x01c00018 (offset 0x0c, lane 0):
     after a boot handshake in the first 0.07 s (the mux written with
     0x00..0xff, 0x7d, 0xfc, 0xfd ... -- MAME answers all >= 8 with the
     off-screen byte), the game writes the mux 0, 1, ..., 8 and reads each
     value TWICE (pc 0x373b8 / 0x373e4 write, 0x373cc / 0x373e0 and 0x373f8 /
     0x3740c read; 0x37330 / 0x37344 for mux 8), once a frame: 114-116 reads
     of each mux value a second in every second of 200 s. Defaults read
     e6 00 7f 01 e6 00 7c 01 fc: P1_Y 0x0e6, P1_X 0x17f, P2_Y 0x0e6, P2_X
     0x17c, LOW BYTE AT THE EVEN MUX, the off-screen byte 0xfc. Every byte
     equals lightgun_mux_r recomputed in Lua from MAME's ports: 0 mismatches.
  2. THE GAME USES WHAT IT READS. Coordinates forced at the tap (60-61 s P1
     (200,100) P2 (500,300); 61-62 s (137,36) (627,425); then (383,230)
     (380,230)) appear as 16-bit words at 0x507204 / 08 / 0c / 10 (P1_X,
     P1_Y, P2_X, P2_Y; copies at +0x10 / +0x20) in the RAM dumps at 61 / 62 /
     63 s, and nowhere else with that sequence.
  3. THE GAME'S CALIBRATION IS MAME'S RANGES, AND ITS AIM IS MAME'S LINEAR
     MAP. TEST -> GUN SETTING -> GUN MARK CHECK (the test menu opens on EXIT:
     Service x9 to GUN SETTING, Test, Service x1, Test) prints AD1 XMIN 137
     YMIN 36 XMAX 630 YMAX 425, AD2 134 / 36 / 627 / 425 -- exactly
     INPUT_PORTS_START(vcop2)'s PORT_MINMAX -- and draws each player's mark
     in Virtua Cop's own colours (P1 69FFFF, P2 FF90A4: m2_vcop_xhair's
     colours are right for this game too). At five forced points per gun the
     mark's centroid sits at floor((v - min) * 496 / span) + (-0.49, -1.62)
     px, the SAME offset at all nine unobstructed marks (spread 0.00): the
     game's aim is MAME's crosshair map; the constant is the splash sprite's
     own centroid against its anchor (INFERRED: it does not move with the
     coordinates). R846 measured +0.13 / 0.00 on Virtua Cop's marks.
  4. VCOP2'S RANGES AGAINST VCOP'S: X spans 493 (vcop 499), Y 389 for BOTH
     guns (vcop P1 389, P2 386); P1_X min 137 (vcop 131), P2_X 134 (128).
     Off-screen by int(span * 0.05f): X 24, Y 19 (as vcop) -- P1 X <= 161 or
     >= 606, P2 X <= 158 or >= 603, Y <= 55 or >= 406. Pixel to unit, the
     smallest unit on the pixel (R846's rule): v - min = ceil(px * 493 / 496)
     = px - (px>=166) - (px>=331), Virtua Cop's two X thresholds subtracted
     instead of added; Y is Virtua Cop's P1_Y rule for both. 493 units over
     496 pixels leave pixels 165, 330 and 495 without a unit (MAME's
     crosshair skips them); they take the next pixel's. The bottom line, 383,
     is unit 424, not 425 (425 is MAME's pixel 384) -- Virtua Cop's Y alike.
  5. WHO IS IN PLAY (RAM dumps every 1 s, then write taps -- NOTE: a tap kept
     in a Lua local is garbage-collected and silently stops; run 2's write
     log has only the boot clear. The taps are globals now):
       0x500034 word  the main mode, ONE-HOT, written whole EVERY frame (pc
                      0x273c): 0x02 boot, 0x20 / 0x80 the two attract
                      sequences, 0x100 a game, 0x2000 / 0x4000 / 0x8000 /
                      0x04 / 0x10 results and the way back to the attract.
       0x500038 byte  the step in the mode (0x500039 holds a copy, written as
                      its own byte): in a game 2 start, 3-7 stage select and
                      the way in, 8 play, 9 continue with nobody left, 0x0a
                      game over. TEST MODE WRITES 0 HERE on entry (pc 0x1ffc)
                      and stops the mode writer.
       0x502088 word  P1: 0 out, 1 in play, 2 its continue countdown; in the
                      attract the demo player toggles it 1 / 0 every frame.
       0x50208c word  P2: 1 at a start or join (pc 0x5fdc, 0x305c alone), 2
                      at its countdown (0x6280), 0 at game over (0x5f10).
     Run 3 (P1 starts 44 s, P2 joins 56 s, P1 continues 69.6 s, P2 77.7 s,
     both out 88 s, game over 94 s; P2 alone 160 s, Test in play 175 s, out
     190 s): every in-game change is one write; the mode word stays 0x100
     through Test (written one more frame after the press, at 175.022, then
     the test entry writes step 0 at 175.040). So R849's Test latch -- held
     until the next mode write -- would clear one frame later and show P2's
     crosshair over the test menu. V2's rule: a player is in play when the
     mode is 0x100, the step is not 0 and its word is 1. P2's crosshair then
     shows from P2's start (its stage select included when P2 starts: it
     aims at the panels) to its countdown or game over, and never in test.
     (Virtua Cop hides P2's in stage select; here it is kept, by choice:
     a P2 who starts alone selects the stage, and later stages' steps are
     unseen -- see c below.)

**R868 -- M2_PROBE: A TELEMETRY BUILD THAT FITS.** M2_WHY with M2_DEBUG_LITE
needed 4,192-4,211 LABs of 4,191 (s1194-s1199), so the board could not be
asked anything. M2_PROBE (Model2.sv g_nodbg, with M2_NO_DEBUG, without
M2_DEBUG_LITE) is one m2_dbg_stream fed one record every third prof_tick
(2.46 ms), no 'G': 'C' the i960's IP, 'S' / 'T' / 'U' the 2A sound board's
records (R862 / R864), and from R871 'Q' the TGP's queue counts, with the
TGP's pc in 'C' in place of the sequencer and bridge fields. Decoder:
tools/decode_why.py. s1203 (c4c4306 + M2_PROBE + M2_NO_2A_RALLY): 41,130 ALM,
539 M10K, setup -0.689 ns on clk_mem and -0.637 ns on clk_sys -- good enough
to read the board (VF2 at 57.5 fps as on s1201); s1204 did not fit.

**R871 -- VF2 SILENT ON THE BOARD: THE BYTE ENABLES DO NOT REACH THE SDRAM, AND
THE 2A SOUND BOARD TRUSTED THEM. ITS BYTE WRITES ARE NOW READ-MERGE-WRITE.
ALSO: VF2'S ATTRACT LOCKUP IS THE TGP NOT ANSWERING.**

*Believed (R859, R864):* the RTL plays VF2 at MAME's level in simulation, so
the board's silence is a start-up fault (MVOL never written); the sound-RAM
clear before boot (c3ee7d2) might cure it. s1201 (c3ee7d2): still silent.

*Measured (s1203, M2_PROBE, VF2 attract, 75 s from load):* the 68000 RUNS
(96 M bus cycles), takes the i960's MIDI (138 bytes), writes the SCSP 37,092
times and timer A 39,606, and MVOL IS 15 -- the program starts. The output
peak is 0 in all 7,523 T records. The pre-boot check reads 4,088 OF 4,096
WORDS WRONG.

*Why 8 right:* the check writes a pattern word-wide, then one byte of each
word alone, then reads back. If the byte write lands in BOTH lanes (or is
lost, or the word comes back byte-swapped) the only words still right are
those whose expected high and low bytes are equal -- for this pattern that is
exactly 8 even words and no odd one. The word-wide writes land.

*Cause:* R82 found on this board, for the i960, that "the byte enables are
LOST between source and silicon -- a byte store landed in all four lanes";
m2_cpu_bridge has done byte stores as read-modify-write since (R729). The 2A
sound board (R859) wrote the 68000's byte stores with a_be and trusted the
mask: every simulation (tb_m2_2a_sound's memory, the controller bench, which
only ever wrote on port 0) honours it. On the board each 68000 byte write to
sound RAM overwrote its neighbour byte; the SCSP plays only from sound RAM
(MAME scsp_map), where the program builds its data, so the output is silence.
Ruled out on the way: the controller with ports 5 and 7 writing (new
M2_SDRAM_W57=1 in tb_m2_sdram, 13-port 2A configuration: 2,277,631 checks,
0 fails), the CDC (s_ack drops with s_req), DQM wiring (be[1] -> DQMH),
the port 5-7 mux, the loader's byte order and the SDRAM map.

*Fix:* m2_2a_sound: a 68000 byte write to RAM is B_RMR (read the line) then
B_RMW (the byte merged, the whole word written, the SCSP's caches snooped);
the check's V_TB does the same in two phases. tb_m2_2a_sound's memory now
writes the whole word whatever be says (as the board; SND_BE_HONOUR=1 for the
old model) and FAILS on any masked write. Bench: the old RTL on the new
model reads 4,088 wrong -- THE BOARD'S NUMBER; the new RTL 0 wrong, 0 masked
writes of 1,772,621, SCSP writes 98.2% in MAME's order, PASS (6 s).
*What the board must show:* the check 0 wrong, and VF2's sound.
*ON THE BOARD (s1205 = f7c5a0d + M2_PROBE + M2_NO_2A_RALLY; 40,997 ALM, 539
M10K, clk_sys -0.243 ns): THE CHECK READS 0 WRONG; the output peak reaches
14,854 (non-zero in 695 of 4,075 T records in 50 s from load); VF2 at 57.5
fps. Ben: "we have sound!" -- CONFIRMED.*
*BUT (Ben, same build): "I don't think it's right" and the sound effects are
"at a very low volume", "like 1% compared to music". The music plays; the
effects are heard, ~40 dB down. R859's bench compared music levels only --
no effect was ever compared with MAME. Open: R874.*

*The lockup (same capture session, s1203):* VF2 froze in attract (Lau's
close-up, 0 fps). Over 12 s every C record was IP 0x00007dc4 with the TGP
holding the CPU: 0x7dc0 is a ret, 0x7dc4-0x7dcc three ldq (g11)[g12] -- the
routine that reads 12 result words from the TGP's output FIFO. The TGP never
produced them. The sound board kept running. M2_PROBE now carries the TGP's
pc and its queue counts ('Q') so the next lockup says where the TGP is.

**R869 -- THE 2A GAMES' i960 FORMS, COMPLETE, FROM A FORM LOG IN MAME'S OWN
i960 (NOT BREAKPOINTS). ZERO GUNNER'S FIRST TRAP IS cvtzril AT 2.57 s, NOT
cpysre AT 40 s. i960_top F2A: cvtzril, cpysre, atanr, sinr AND AN EXACT remr,
LIVE FOR THE THREE 2A GAMES. +354 ALMs ESTIMATED, 4 M10K. NOT FITTED.**
(Ben: establish the complete set of forms Sega Rally, Zero Gunner and Virtua
Cop 2 execute that the 2A core traps on, then implement exactly that set.
Limits: one MAME at a time, one Verilator build at a time, no fits, no board,
whole-core simulations under ~10 minutes.)

*Believed (R866):* Sega Rally traps on cvtzril at 0.123 s, then atanr, remr,
cpysre at 23.5 s and sinr at 46.4 s; Zero Gunner's first trap is cpysre at
39.95 s; atanr / sinr need R845's sequencer; remr needs an exact iterative
fmod. Found by one-shot breakpoints on every candidate word of the program,
at its ROM address and at its copy in work RAM.

*THE METHOD (sim/io/mame_i960_formlog.patch, a patch to MAME 0.289's
i960.cpp; a tool, not the core).* R866 showed that a ROM breakpoint cannot
see code run from RAM; a candidate list cannot see code it does not list.
So the log sits in execute_run, ahead of execute_op: every distinct FORM the
CPU executes -- REG op.op2, MEM op + mode bits 13:10, ret by its frame type,
CTRL / COBR op -- with its first PC, instruction word and time, and a count
of each at exit; and, for the REG forms i960_top lacked (vf2_formscan.py
RTL_LACKS), every new PC and every distinct operand tuple with MAME's result.
Wherever the code lives. Then:
  * sim/io/i960_formcheck.cpp steps the lockstep's whole-CPU reference
    (sim/i960/i960_cpu_ref.h, whose traps the lockstep holds the module to,
    R836) once on each form's first word, in the 2A core as it was (FR 1, VC
    0), as it is now (F2A 1) and in the main core (VC 1);
  * sim/io/mame_i960_formlog.py checks every logged operand tuple against
    what the module computes (fmod exactly; atanr / sinr through R845's own
    microcode interpreter, tools/i960_fptrans.py, then narrowed; cvtzril as
    cvtzri sign-extended; cpysre);
  * sim/io/mame_m2_2a_play.lua plays the game (a fresh NVRAM each run).

*Found (VERIFIED, MAME 0.289, headless, one run at a time):*
  1. SEGA RALLY, 600 s (attract; credits at 30 / 220 / 410 s; the gear lever
     stepped 1-2-3-4, accelerator held 18 s in 20, the wheel swept +-0x60,
     brake, hand brake, VR; three races driven badly but at speed): 150
     forms. The old 2A core traps on FIVE, and on nothing else:
        cvtzril  0.144 s  0x5a2dc4   105,064 executions, 10 PCs
        atanr   23.57 s   0x5ddd40    74,957, 6 PCs (to 93.1 s)
        remr    23.57 s   0x5ddd54    38,014, 1 PC
        cpysre  23.57 s   0x5d0910    52,375, 3 PCs
        sinr    36.36 s   0x5e27ac         3, 1 PC
     (sinr at 36.4 s here, 46.4 s in R866's run: input-dependent.) A
     second run, 330 s -- attract only to 240 s (its demo races later stages
     at speed), then the test menu walked (CRT test and on): 145 forms, the
     same traps but sinr, nothing new; every operand tuple again equal.
  2. ZERO GUNNER, 600 s (attract; credits at 60 / 230 / 400 s, button 1
     held, button 2 every 5 s, the stick on a walk; mission 1 played): 153
     forms. The old 2A core traps on TWO:
        CVTZRIL  2.573 s  0x554590    68,680, 3 PCs (0x55762c / 0x557644 at 5.23 s)
        cpysre  39.99 s   0x5465f0   107,160, 8 PCs (to 74.8 s)
     So Zero Gunner halts at 2.57 s on the R865 core -- before its first
     picture (MAME: the Psikyo logo at ~5 s, 3D attract by 15 s), which is
     the board's "black from the first seconds". R866 RECORDED cpysre AT
     39.95 s AS THE FIRST, AND THAT WAS WRONG: the ROM word at 0x54590 is
     0x6c801980 (cvtzril fp0, g0), copied to 0x554590 as R866's own map
     says, so it was a candidate; why the one-shot breakpoint run did not
     report it is not established (one candidate: BP_ONCE disables
     breakpoint n by the list's numbering, which is MAME's only if nothing
     else ever set one). The form log needs no candidate list.
  3. VIRTUA COP 2, 600 s (attract; credits at 30 / 200 / 370 s, the gun
     swept and fired, reloads off-screen, play to game over and the
     continues): 203 forms; the 2A core traps on NONE (it runs no flushreg
     either). It runs from ROM (R866), so this agrees with R866's
     breakpoints; it now holds for every form, not only the FP candidates.
  4. EVERY EXECUTED INSTANCE, CHECKED (the log keeps every distinct operand
     tuple; distinct / executions): Sega Rally atanr 50,868 / 74,957, remr
     23,189 / 38,014, cvtzril 58,218 / 105,064, cpysre 35,240 / 52,375, sinr
     1 / 3; Zero Gunner cvtzril 92 / 68,680, cpysre 16,842 / 107,160. The
     module's result equals MAME's on every one. Operand classes:
       * remr: register singles in, register out. The divisor is ALWAYS
         0x40c90fdb (2 pi as a single, 6.2831855); dividends -6.355..6.607,
         so |x / y| <= 1.052 and the exponent difference is 0 or less: one
         quotient bit. No zero, infinity, NaN or subnormal. Sega Rally needs
         fmod only over that range; the unit below is exact everywhere
         anyway (it is what MAME computes, and its cost is the subtractor and
         two counters, not the range).
       * atanr: register singles, or a literal src1 (1.0: atan2(y, 1));
         register out; src1 -277..369; no specials.
       * sinr: three executions, one argument (0.2468), register in and out.
       * cvtzril: always fp0-fp3 (doubles) into a register pair; Sega Rally
         -0.72..4,095.9, Zero Gunner -16,384..16,384 -- inside the module's
         exact range (|x| < 2^31, R839).
       * cpysre: fp0 / fp1 / fp3 with a literal src2 (0.0 or 1.0: the sign
         always positive), into the same fp register.
  5. The main core (VC 1) would trap on Sega Rally's atanr, remr and sinr
     (VC has the rl transcendentals, not these single forms) -- recorded,
     irrelevant: the main core does not load the 2A games.

*BUILT -- i960_top F2A (Model2.sv: F2A = FPU2A, the M2_2A_FPU switch, live
by vc_en for game IDs 0x10-0x12 as FR is):*
  a. cvtzril and cpysre: VC's own decode, gated (vc_on || ta_on). No new
     logic beyond the gate.
  b. atanr (0x68.0, entry 3) and sinr (0x68.c, entry 0): R845's sequencer,
     now built when VC || F2A (TRB), started from the single forms' T_EXEC
     path (not T_RLLO); its operands are the widened single (fp_a_wide /
     fp_b_wide) or fp0-fp3; the result narrows through u_cvt_a into a
     register or stays whole in fp0-fp3 -- MAME's set_rif(atan2(t2f, t1f)) /
     set_rif(sin(t1f)) on the widened double. The rl transcendentals and
     sqrtrl stay VC-only (neither game runs them).
  c. remr (0x68.3): rtl/cpu/i960/i960_fprem.sv, new. Restoring division of
     the significands, a quotient bit a cycle, keeping only the remainder;
     then normalised a bit a cycle (the exponent counts down from y's).
     Exact: nothing rounds (fmod's remainder is always representable). C99
     F.9.7.1 for the specials; the units' flush for subnormals (§8.1). Up to
     ex - ey + 53 cycles (2,048 measured over doubles; Sega Rally's take
     ~3). Its operands are held on fp_b / fp_a through T_FP, as the
     sequencer's are; the result is read in done's cycle (no 64-bit result
     register: 192 ALUT / 71 registers, against 297 / 144 with one).
  Everything new is gated by F2A (a parameter) and ta_on (F2A && vc_en):
  with F2A 0 every new term is a constant 0 -- the main core's i960 (VC 1,
  FR 0, F2A 0) is the logic it was; with vc_en low (VF2, game 0) none of it
  can start.

*BENCHES:*

    whole exponent range (differences to 2,046), widened singles, exact
    multiples k*y and their neighbours, |x| next to |y|, the largest ratio
    (DBL_MAX by the smallest normals) -- 0 mismatches; max 2,048 cycles.
    Seven planted faults: five caught (thousands of mismatches each), two
    equivalent and proved so (an early exit when ex == ey and mx < my;

**R874 -- "SFX AT ~1% OF THE MUSIC, DRUMS MISSING" (Ben, s1205, VF2): NOT
REPRODUCED IN SIMULATION. THE SCSP AND THE 68000'S STREAMING GIVE MAME'S
SOUND EFFECTS AND DRUMS; THE FAULT IS IN SOMETHING THE BENCHES DO NOT MODEL.
NO RTL CHANGE.**

*Believed (the task):* a gross attenuation (~40 dB) on one SCSP path that
only sound effects use -- the effect send, the DSP's MIXS / EFREG scaling,
EFSDL, MVOL -- never seen because R859 compared music levels only.

*Measured (MAME 0.289 vf2 capture, keyon.txt / regs.bin / ramw.bin, 300 s):*
  1. EVERY VF2 VOICE IS THE SAME KIND. All 9,967 key-ons: PCM8B, LPCTL 1,
     SA = 0x10000 + slot x 0x2000 (a fixed 8 KB ring per slot, LSA 0, LEA
     0x1fff), DISDL 3, ISEL 0, MDL 0, SDIR 0, SSCTL 0, slots handed out
     round-robin. The 68000 copies every sample from ROM into its slot's
     ring (word writes only: 220 K words/s, 1 ROM read per RAM write; the
     first 512 words land 16 samples BEFORE the key-on, the whole ring in
     ~30 ms). There is no separate SFX path: the direct send, the DSP send
     and the effect returns are the music's.
  2. THE SOUND EFFECTS are MIDI channel 14 note-ons (9e nn vv; first at
     19.78 s). They and the music's drums share, and no melodic voice has:
     word 8 = 0x7800 (OCT -1, FNS 0: unpitched, 22,050 Hz) with word 4 =
     0x001f (AR 31, D1R 0, D2R 0) and RR 31, KRS 0. SFX: TL 4, DL 0, word
     9 0x5100; drums: TL 0x15-0x1e, DL 0 or 31, word 9 0x5300. Melodic
     voices have FNS != 0 and D2R != 0.
  3. THE SCSP RTL IS ALREADY PROVEN ON EXACTLY THESE: tb_m2_scsp replays this
     capture's register AND sound-RAM writes for all 300 s bit-exact against
     scsp_ref.h and MAME's mix (R857/R858: 194,928,084 slot-samples, 0
     wrong) -- every SFX and drum included. So level, pan, the DSP and the EG
     are MAME's for these voices in simulation.
  4. THE 68000 SIDE (tb_m2_2a_sound, new SND_SHIFT=9: MAME's MIDI from 5 s
     moved 9 s earlier, so the music starts at 4.77 s and the first SFX at
     10.79 s in an 11.6 s run, 48 MHz, ~9 min):
     * our sound RAM against MAME's (rebuilt from ramw.bin) at the music's
       start: rings 0-21 equal word for word where both have filled them;
     * the first SFX: keyed on with TL 4 as MAME's; its ring holds MAME's
       sample bytes, 3,840 of 4,096 words equal (the rest our refill, later
       in time), the decaying envelope of the effect the same block by block;
     * output RMS in 50 ms windows against MAME's out.bin across the SFX:
       ratio 0.76-1.37, mean ~1.07 -- no 40 dB loss; at the music's start
       (drums keyed at 4.78 / 4.89 s) 0.64-1.12.
  5. LONGER LATENCY (LAT_A_LO / LAT_A_HI new, the 68000's port alone): at
     100-400 clocks the boot (pre-boot check, clear, the RAM loop) takes
     past 5 s and the driver is not running yet; at 30-200 on all ports at
     48 MHz the engine starves (273 FIFO empties). Neither is the board
     (no underruns, the driver running). Not a reproduction.
  6. Ruled out on the way: the 0x400000 bank latch (VF2's 8 MB is linear,
     model2snd_ctrl banks only past 8 MB), the sample MRA order (program and
     samples both ROM_LOAD16_WORD_SWAP, both map="12"), the 2A SDRAM layout
     (samples at byte 0x3400000-0x3BFFFFF, nothing else there), m2_sdram's
     write acknowledge (given after the WRITE command, not posted: the slot
     cache's snoop cannot be outrun), the OSD volume stage, the MIDI FIFO
     (32 entries, MAME's), FM / MIDI_OUT (same on the board and benches).

*What is left (the board is the oracle):* the bench reproduces MAME for these
voices, so the board differs in something it does not model: (a) s1205 fails
clk_sys setup by -0.243 ns (TNS -0.436) -- which path is not in the saved
report; quartus_sta on the s1205 database names it, and an SCSP engine path
(the envelope or the step multiplier) would fit a fault confined to one
envelope / pitch shape; (b) the real i960's MIDI (the SFX only -- the drums
are sequenced by the 68000, no MIDI during the music); (c) the board's
SDRAM latency on ports 5-7 under load, never measured. Next: name the
failing path; an M2_PROBE record of one slot's words 4-8 and its EG level
after an SFX key-on on the board.

*R874 addendum -- s1205's failing paths (quartus_sta on its database):*
all 40 worst clk_sys setup paths are inside m2_scsp: prod[41] / prod[24] /
prod[30..43] / ue[10] -> the register file's write data (rfb_rtl_0
porta_datain_reg4 / reg5; also rfa, st), worst -0.243 ns (data 11.84 ns,
skew -0.82 ns): the multiply result through the PSL shift, the A mux and the
ALU into rf. The level / envelope datapath, failing on silicon only for the
data that exercises it, is the leading explanation for a fault no simulation
shows. R875: the path is being cut; s1207 / s1208 (other placement) test it
on the board meanwhile.


**R873 -- ZERO GUNNER'S 315-5881 IS ONLY A CHECK: NOTHING IT DECRYPTS IS
USED. ELEVEN ONE-BYTE MRA PATCHES REPLACE IT, 0 ALM. PROVED IN MAME 0.289
OVER FOUR TWO-PLAYER CREDITS (840 s).**
(Ben: try to patch out the decryption checks before building the chip.)

*Believed (R862):* with the decrypt reads at 0 MAME plays the first credit
"with small differences from t = 40 s", then stays black; "so Zero Gunner
needs the chip" -- ~300-400 ALMs and 1 M10K (R862 a + b + d).

*Found (MAME 0.289, read / write taps with the i960's IP and registers,
MAME's disassembly of the work-RAM copy -- R866: RAM 0x540000-0x5cebff is
program 0x40000-0xcebff, the code runs there):*
  1. ONE ROUTINE TALKS TO THE CHIP, 0x56b8d0 (program 0x6b8d0): address / 2
     to 0x01d90008, the subkey to 0x01d9000c, a dummy read, the status at
     0x01d90000 polled until bit 0 clears, then (length - 4) / 2 halves from
     0x01d9000e, byte-swapped, stored to the buffer in g0. The boot (program
     0x810 / 0x860) copies 192 bytes from 0x56de40 to the chip's RAM with
     0x56b820 -- the only use of 0x01d80000.
  2. ELEVEN CALLERS, ALL THE SAME SEQUENCE: r4 = random(16) (0x54b430);
     subkey 0x27a44[r4], length 0x27a24[r4] (12), address 0x27a64[r4];
     decrypt 8 bytes to 0x40(fp); ldl the double at 0x279a4[r4 * 8], cmprl it
     with the decrypted double; on a mismatch 0x513000 += 1; return. Every
     one of the eleven functions returns straight after its compare: the
     decrypted bytes are never read again.
  3. THE COUNTER 0x513000: zeroed at boot (0x54b1e0), read only by the
     eleven checks and by the main loop at 0x54b2e4 (a read tap over 840 s
     saw no other reader): once it passes 10 the loop adds 1 a frame and
     skips the game's state machine (the dispatch at 0x54b310); after 3600
     frames it calls 0x54b560 (a reseed) and sets 11 again -- for good.
  4. THE CORE TODAY (run B below, reads 0, unpatched): 1 at the boot check,
     7 by 47.7 s (one per check of the first credit), 10 at 160 s, 11 at
     179.45 s; from then the 3D background still scrolls but with no HUD,
     no enemies, coins ignored, and MAME itself stopped at 241 s ("I960:
     84051000: Unhandled 00") a second after the next coin. R862's black
     screen at 110 s is this lockout on its schedule.
  5. R862'S "SMALL DIFFERENCES FROM 40 s" ARE NOT DATA: B's frames part
     from A's at the first credit's checks (40 s) while C -- the same zeros,
     the increment not taken -- matches A to 83.55 s. INFERRED: the cycles
     of the taken increment path shift the game's timing (MAME's i960
     counts cycles; the seed below mixes [0x5021d6] / [0x5021d8]).
  6. THE RANDOM NUMBER GENERATOR READS THE PROGRAM: 0x54b430 (and 0x54b560)
     do seed += ROM[seed & 0xffffc] + 0x2b67 + [0x5021d6] + [0x5021d8] +
     [0x5000cc]. So ANY patched program word changes the random sequence
     when the seed lands on it -- MAME's own init_zerogun at 0x700 does,
     against the board. In run A the seed lands on two of the eleven site
     words in 840 s: 0x55cd4 at 83.550078 s and 0x475e8 at 657.795779 s
     (data reads with IP 0x54b470, the ld at 0x54b46c).

*THE PATCH (Zero Gunner (Export, Model 2A).mra):* each check's "be" past the
increment becomes "b" -- opcode 0x12 -> 0x08, the displacement kept -- so a
check never counts and 0x513000 stays 0, as with the chip. Program offsets
(= MRA image offsets: all below 0x80000); RAM copy at +0x500000:
     0x443c8 12000028 -> 08000028   <patch>28 00 00 08</patch>
     0x446e0 0x449bc 0x44bac 0x44e14 0x474dc 0x475e8 0x477f4 0x4cc34
     0x55cd4 0x56204: 12000018 -> 08000018   <patch>18 00 00 08</patch>
Three sites (0x474dc, 0x449bc, 0x44e14) never ran in 840 s; same sequence,
patched anyway. The boot's copy carries the patch (read back at 5 s).
Alternative not taken: one word, the main loop's test at 0x4b2ec
(cmpibge 10,g5 -> b 0x54b310, 24 00 00 08) -- one RNG-visible word instead
of eleven, but the counter then climbs with every check and RAM no longer
matches the chip's; not run.
tools/mra_vs_mame.py: a CORE_PATCHES table applies these to MAME's side
(checking each was MAME's be): --layout=2a PASS.

*PROOF (sim/prot/mame_m2_zg_patch.lua, sim/prot/zg_patch_cmp.py; MAME
0.289, fresh nvram each run; 840 s: credits at 40 / 240 / 440 / 640 s --
two coins, 1P and 2P start, both players weave and fire until game over
(~90 s), attract between; per second the counter and FNV hashes of work RAM
0x500000-0x53ffff, RAM 0x200000-0x23ffff, buffer RAM 0x900000-0x91ffff, the
code copy every 30 s; 420 snapshots; RAM dumps every 60 s):*
     A   real chip, MAME's program            39 checks, all pass
     AL  A again (with the ROM-read log)      == A in everything
     B   reads 0, unpatched (the core today)  lockout 179.45 s, crash 241 s
     C   reads 0, the MRA's program (rom_csum image loaded over maincpu, 11
         words differ)                        counter 0 all run; 4 games to
                                              game over, attract between;
                                              39 checks at A's times to 83 s
     D   real chip, the MRA's program         == C: every hash, 420 / 420
                                              snapshots, 28 / 28 dumps
     CF  as C, the RNG's reads of the 11 words given MAME's original
                                              == A: 420 / 420 snapshots, all
                                              hashes all 840 s; dumps differ
                                              only in the 11 patched words
  D == C bit for bit means the chip's answers have NO effect once the checks
  are bypassed: nothing decrypted is consumed. CF == A means the patch
  changes nothing else -- the only difference left between C and A is the
  random sequence parting at the seed's reads of patched words (A vs C
  first differs at 84 s, the second after the 83.55 s read).

*What the board must show:* Zero Gunner, once it runs past R866's FP forms
(cpysre at ~40 s traps on the 2A build; another change), plays credit after
credit: no lockout after the first game, coins and starts answered. The
0x01d8 / 0x01d9 traffic is unchanged (the boot upload, the subkey writes,
the status read as 0 ends the poll). Its board black screen at boot is a
separate fault. NOT VERIFIED on the board; not run on the core in
simulation.
*Cost:* 0 ALM, 0 M10K -- R862's chip (a + b + d) is not needed for Zero
Gunner. The other 315-5881 sets in MAME (keys 2c2a4a93, 042e2dc1; not 2A
games) are not assessed.

**R875 -- THE SCSP's FAILING clk_sys PATH (s1205, -0.243 ns) IS THE DAC's
SATURATION, NOT THE ENVELOPE: P's SHIFT TAKEN A CLOCK EARLY AND THE DAC FED
FROM THE REGISTER PORT. NO MICROCODE CHANGE; BIT-EXACT; ~+0.8 ns ESTIMATED.**

*Believed (R874's lead (a)):* s1205's only clk_sys failure, -0.243 ns, all
40 worst paths inside the SCSP from `prod` (and `ue[10]`, the PSL select,
and the state RAM) to the register file's and state RAM's data inputs -- the
level / envelope multiply, which would plausibly corrupt only voices held at
full level (VF2's effects and drums).

*Measured (quartus_sta on s1205's own database, full paths; nothing refit):*
every path at or below +0.4 ns goes through `dac()` -- OP_DAC's saturation
compare (x~11, x~7, Equal34). The worst: the DSP block's output register
prod[41] (tco 0.89 + 0.73 ns) -> the PSL shift mux (FM: prod >>> 17 gives
a_v[24]) -> the A mux (2 LUTs) -> the DAC's 17-bit sign check (2 LUTs) ->
the result mux (4 LUTs) -> rfb datain[4]: 9 LUT levels, 11.84 ns, skew
-0.82 ns. The same compare closes the state-RAM path (st q -> A mux -> DAC
-> rf, +0.012) and the ue[10] / ue[6] select paths (+0.158 / +0.382). Only
the output microprogram uses OP_DAC, both times on a = RA (SMPL, SMPR), so
the path from P to the DAC is one the microcode never takes -- but it is a
structural path, and it was the one that failed. The same netlist with the
DAC excluded: prod -> adder -> scmp -> f3 / f4 +0.685, prod -> adder -> rf
+0.757, rfb -> adder -> scmp -> f3 / f4 +0.837, state RAM -> adder -> f4
+0.921, -> rf +0.966. So the effect-path theory of R874 (a) is not
supported by the timing report: the failing logic is the output DAC, every
sample, every voice alike (of the 6,000 worst SCSP paths, every engine
path below +0.685 ns passes through it).

*The microcode (sim/sound/scsp_uasm.py; P from E(k+2)):* of the 17 product
uses, 15 are at exactly k+2 -- pitch -> plfo multiply (#2 -> #4), plfo
(#4 -> #6), fm, frac (#11 -> #13, FM #18 -> #20), alfo, eg, the four level
products l0 / l1 / l2 / l5 back to back, e3 / e4 in each effect return,
ol / or in the output; only pitch's PASSA (#5) and FM's (k+4, k+5) have
slack. A register stage on P with no microcode change (option a) is
impossible; re-scheduling for P at k+3 (option c) costs ~5-6
microinstructions a slot (23 -> ~29) and one per effect return, ~+25% on
an engine already peaking past its 1,814-clock budget (VF2 max 2,087,
R858). Not done.

*The change (option b, retiming; rtl/sound/scsp/m2_scsp.sv):*
  1. P's shift a clock early: psl_v is now a REGISTER, the shift (S6 / S12
     / S16 / FM) applied to mul_a x mul_b as it leaves the DSP block, with
     the select of the microinstruction about to enter E (ue_f[PSL]; a
     bubble enters as NOP, which reads no P) and PCM16 as E will see it
     (w0l, or sqb when this clock latches word 0). E starts from flops; the
     DSP block's output is no longer registered there (prod stays, in
     logic, for the ring and MIXS slices). MA_PSL feeds mul_a from psl_v.
  2. OP_DAC takes ra_q, the register file's port A, not the A mux; the
     assembler now refuses a DAC with a != RA. ROMs unchanged (assembled:
     identical hex).
  A sim-only check (`SCSP_CHK`) compares, every clock E is not a bubble,
  the early shift with the late one and the DAC's operand with A's; a
  mutant with the select forced fired it 25 M times in 16 s of VF2 (and
  failed the bench); a mutant without the PCM16 look-ahead does not fire
  -- no microinstruction reading P follows a word-0 latch, so the
  look-ahead is exact but never exercised.

*Benches (all with SCSP_CHK: 0 mismatches):*
  * tb_m2_scsp, MAME's VF2 capture, the first 65 s (2,866,500 samples;
    drums from the music's start at ~13.8 s, the first SFX at 19.8 s):
    0 differ from the reference, 0 from MAME's mix, 28,662,188 slot-samples
    0 wrong, IPL and 68000 reads 0 wrong (14.5 min wall; the full 300 s is
    ~65 min, past this session's limit -- NOT RUN); also 34 s and the plain
    (no SCSP_CHK) build 10 s: PASS.
  * the 40 random captures (FM, PCM16, noise LFO, SSCTL 2 / 3, timers,
    MIDI; every third at latency 20-400): 40 PASS, 254,766,194
    slot-samples 0 wrong, 0 differ from the reference or MAME's mix. (A
    first pass said 40 FAIL with the RTL equal to MAME's mix and the
    REFERENCE wrong: `make test_m2_scsp` copies SCSP_HEX, which lacks
    scsp_lfonoise.hex, so the reference ran without MAME's noise table;
    randrun.sh copies *.hex. A bench-setup trap, not the RTL.)
  * tb_m2_scsp_dsp 4,000,000 random runs, tb_m2_scsp_level all 393,216
    words: PASS (files unchanged).
  * tb_m2_2a_sound VF2 6 s: PASS, as R871 (sound-RAM check 0 wrong, 98.2%
    of writes in MAME's order, 0 masked writes).
  * lint_top (2A): clean; lint_idx: nothing new; quartus_map
    --analyze_file: 0 errors.

*Area (quartus_map, the whole 2A build, default switches):* m2_scsp 2,418
ALUT (1,211 own), 1,615 registers (749 own), 3 DSP blocks, 273,780 bits;
s1205's map (M2_PROBE, M2_NO_2A_RALLY): 2,426 (1,217), 1,603 (737), 3,
273,780. -8 ALUT, +12 registers. Whole design 39,906 ALMs est. (default
switches; s1205's configuration 39,753 -- not comparable).

*Expected timing -- AN ESTIMATE FROM s1205's NETLIST, NOT A FIT:*
  * the DAC: rfa q -> saturation (2) -> result mux (4) -> rf / st: 6
    levels; the same path through the A mux was +1.006 (rfa) and +0.012
    (st); without the A mux's two levels, ~+1.5-2 ns. The st, prod, ue
    -> DAC paths no longer exist.
  * P's users: from a flop instead of the DSP output register through the
    shift mux: the +0.685 / +0.757 adder paths gain ~1.5-2.5 ns.
  * the new multiply cycle: DSP input registers -> 27 x 18 multiply
    (output unregistered) -> one 4:1 LUT -> psl_v: ~6-7.5 ns of 12.5.
  * so the engine's worst becomes paths this change does not touch:
    rfb -> B mux -> adder -> scmp -> f3 / f4 at +0.837, state RAM ->
    adder at +0.92-0.97 -- ~+0.8 ns, subject to the next fit's placement
    (+-0.3 ns seed to seed is usual at 98%).
  * STILL NEAR THE LIMIT IN THE SCSP (unchanged here): m2_scsp_dsp, MPRO's
    q -> MADRS + DEC + ADRS + 1 (three chained adders) -> addr_w <
    0x40000 -> pk_go -> mul_a at +0.447 (memval +0.637, mul_b +0.659).
    addr_w holds through a step (k, DEC, ADRS change at ph 4 / FIN), so
    pk_go's compare could be registered at ph 2 -- a candidate, not done.
    Outside the SCSP, s1205's next clk_sys path is m2_raster_fill xah ->
    s1_valid at +0.278, and pll_hdmi fails by -0.184.

*What the board must show:* the next 2A build closes clk_sys (SCSP paths
>= ~+0.4 ns); then whether VF2's effects and drums come back to MAME's
level. If they do not, R874 (b) / (c) stand and the timing failure was not
the cause -- the failing path was the output DAC, which every voice passes,
so a fault confined to the effects was never a good fit for it.

**R878 -- s1207 ON THE BOARD (model2a af10f15 + M2_PROBE + M2_NO_2A_RALLY;
41,437 ALM, 553 / 553 M10K, clk_sys -0.217 (m2_fb_wcomb), clk_mem -0.027;
no SCSP path among the 40 worst). Ben, 2026-10-18:**

20,000,000 cycles, 120,000,000 checks, 0 mismatches; tb_m2_vcop2_guns

**R877 -- "DRUMS A TINNY HISS, EFFECTS GONE UNDER THE MUSIC" (VF2, s1205 /
s1207) AND ZERO GUNNER SILENT: THE SOUND BOARD IS NOT STARVED OF SDRAM ON THE
BOARD. THE HYPOTHESIS IS RULED OUT BY THE BOARD'S OWN 68000 RATES AGAINST
BENCHES AT KNOWN LATENCY. ZERO GUNNER'S CAPTURE IS A HUNG GAME (THE TGP), NOT
A SOUND FAULT. TOOLS BUILT; TWO DEFENSIVE CHANGES (POSTED 68000 WRITES ON,
AN ARBITER AGE ESCALATION OFF BY DEFAULT); A PROBE RECORD 'L'.**

*Believed (the task):* ports 5 / 6 / 7 sit outside m2_sdram's class (R639 /
R702 / R766 / R789 / R854); under video load the 68000 (blocking, its RAM
uncached) and the SCSP (waits on misses) fall behind -- the rings stale
(drums -> hiss), effects keyed late, Zero Gunner's 538 underruns. "On VF2 the
68000 writes the SCSP only ~6-26 K/s during the music where MAME writes ~88
K/s."

*Measured:*
  1. THE DEMAND (MAME 0.289's 300 s captures, bus.txt / dspstats.txt, per
     second): VF2 -- 68000 RAM reads 218 K, RAM writes 270 K (all uncached:
     each one an SDRAM transaction on port 5), program fetches 1.23 M and
     sample reads 226 K (through the 1 KB line cache), SCSP 9 K reads / 40 K
     writes; DSP memory reads 573 K and writes 176 K. Zero Gunner -- RAM 229 K
     / 354 K, program 1.39 M, samples 267 K, DSP 571 K / 176 K. In the bench
     (tb_m2_2a_sound's new demand counters, VF2 SND_SHIFT=9, 11.6 s at 80
     MHz, latency 6-40) the three ports ask, over the run (music from 4.8
     s): port 5 252 K reads + 290 K writes /s, port 6 30 K reads /s, port 7
     137 K reads + 168 K writes /s; worst 10 ms windows 3,205 (port 7) and
     2,609 (port 6) transactions (port 5's, 33,430, is the pre-boot clear).
     The 68000 waits on port 5 15.6% of all clocks at a mean of 23 clk.
  2. WHAT m2_sdram GIVES THEM (tb_m2_sdram_load, new: the 2A build's 13
     ports and class, a synthetic 57.5 Hz frame whose render phase (75%) has
     every class port re-requesting after a short random think time, the
     sound ports at the demand above; clk_mem cycles, request to acknowledge;
     x0.8 + ~4 for clk_sys through m2_sdram_cdc):
       load                            port 5 p50 / p90 / p99 / max
       moderate (think 160, 55% busy)       20 /  39 /  88 / 212
       heavy (think 40, render saturated)   89 / 243 / 330 / 437
       pathological (think 10)             146 / 385 / 461 / 579
     Ports 6 and 7 alike. Outside the class a sound request waits for the
     round-robin slot (one in three grants while the class is busy) to
     reach it -- up to ~36 transactions.
  3. THE BENCH AT THOSE LATENCIES (tb_m2_2a_sound LAT_TRACE, new: each
     request takes the latency the load bench gave a request at the same
     point of its frame). The 68000's bus cycles a second and SCSP writes a
     second in the scan before the music and during it:
       run                         before music       during music
       bench, latency 6-40         2.12 M / 83 K      1.85-1.90 M / 20-49 K
       bench, heavy trace          1.47 M / 54 K      (later boot)
       bench, latency 20-150       1.65 M / 63 K      1.16-1.23 M / 8-19 K, 142 underruns
       THE BOARD, s1207 VF2        2.17 M / 86 K      1.80-1.99 M / 17-49 K, 0 underruns
       MAME (its capture, the
       same stretch, SND_SHIFT)        --              ~35-45 K
     THE BOARD SITS ON THE LIGHT-LATENCY BENCH, NOT THE LOADED ONE -- before
     the music it is even a little faster. Its port 5 therefore waits about
     what the 6-40 model gives (mean ~23 clk_sys) in VF2's attract; ports 6
     and 7 share the arbiter's treatment. And the drop during the music is
     not a board symptom: the bench at 6-40 drops the same way, and so does
     MAME (the task's "88 K/s" is the scan before the music; MAME writes
     ~35-45 K/s during it). The 0 underruns of s1205 agree.
  4. ZERO GUNNER (s1207 capture, 1,220 records): the i960's IP is
     0x00560c38 and the TGP's pc 0x0857 in EVERY record, copro_stall set in
     every one; no MIDI byte reaches the sound board in the whole capture
     (324 -> 324) and the underrun count does not move (538 -> 538: they
     happened before it). The game is hung on the TGP; the sound board, given
     nothing to play, plays its idle level (peak 290-521). Not a sound fault
     -- R871's VF2 lockup has a second instance.
  So the hypothesis is RULED OUT for VF2's attract (the capture Ben listened
  to) and does not apply to Zero Gunner's capture. VF2's drums / effects
  stay open: R874 (b) the real i960's MIDI, and anything the bench's MAME
  MIDI replay cannot reach.

*Built:*
  a. tb_m2_sdram_load (make test_m2_sdram_load): the latency table above, and
     LOAD_TRACE writes each sound port's (issue, latency) for b.
     UNEXPLAINED: its shadow check reports ~1.5% of port 7's reads with a
     word pair shifted (data written at an odd address read at the even one
     below), with or without b's AGE, with or without eight-word bursts;
     tb_m2_sdram's own W57 / AGE suites read 0 fails over 2.15-2.28 M checks.
     Most likely this bench's stimulus (it reissues on the cycle after an
     acknowledge, as no m2_sdram_cdc port can), but the DSP writes on port 7
     on the board, so it is RECORDED, NOT DISMISSED.
  b. m2_sdram AGE / AGE_T: a port in AGE ready for AGE_T clk_mem cycles is
     taken into the class and to its top until granted; the aged bits are
     registers, so the class masks stay register AND register. Heavy load,
     AGE 5-7 at 48: port 5 p50 / p99 / max 78 / 124 / 156 (from 89 / 330 /
     437); the cost falls on the texel ports at saturation (port 12 p99 395
     -> 613). Model2.sv: M2_2A_SND_AGE, OFF by default (the board does not
     need it, item 3; the arbiter is on clk_mem, which failed by -0.22 to
     -0.69 ns in s1176-s1203). test_m2_sdram13 gains the AGE case with ports
     5 and 7 writing: 2,151,281 checks, 0 fails, 0 violations; the four old
     cases unchanged (AGE 0 is the controller as it was).
  c. m2_2a_sound POST_WR (Model2.sv M2_2A_SND_POST, ON): a 68000 word write
     to RAM, and the write half of a byte write's merge, is acknowledged at
     once and completes behind the 68000; the next RAM access or cache fill
     and any SCSP access wait for it, the snoop goes out when it lands -- so
     every later read and the SCSP see the writes in the 68000's order. MAME
     gives RAM one wait state; ours waited for the SDRAM. On the heavy trace
     it lifts the 68000's scan rate 1.47 M -> 1.64 M (AGE as well: 1.88 M).
     POST_WR 0 restores the old acknowledge (B_WPW).
  d. M2_PROBE 'L' (pb_sel 5; records now turn C S T U Q L, each every ~14.8
     ms): the longest wait on ports 5, 6, 7 since the last L (clk_sys, 10
     bits saturating), clocks/16 port 5 had a request outstanding, and the
     port 6 / 7 requests that waited 256 or more. tools/decode_why.py prints
     them. A board run settles item 3 directly: waits of ~20-75 clk_sys say
     the ports are served (expected); ~250+ would revive the hypothesis for
     that scene, and M2_2A_SND_AGE=1 is the change.
  e. tb_m2_2a_sound: per-port demand (reads / writes a second, the worst 10
     ms window, mean / max latency, the 68000's share of time waiting) and
     LAT_TRACE / LAT_CDC.

*Bench before / after (VF2 SND_SHIFT=9, 11.6 s, 80 MHz; FIFO underruns,
the 68000's share of clocks waiting on port 5, its bus cycles a second in
the music):*
       RTL / latency                  underruns  68000 waits  music rate
       old, 6-40                          0         15.6%      1.85-1.90 M
       old, heavy trace                 198         39.1%      1.22-1.28 M
       POST_WR, heavy trace             135         42.1%      1.37-1.41 M
       POST_WR + AGE, heavy trace         0         32.2%      1.65-1.68 M
       POST_WR, 6-40                      0         16.8%      2.01-2.17 M
  (The SND_SHIFT runs all FAIL the bench's 90% write-order test, the old RTL
  at 6-40 included -- the shift moves MAME's writes, not ours; the same RTL
  without the shift, VF2 6 s: PASS, 98.1% of writes in MAME's order, 0
  underruns, sound-RAM check 0 wrong, 0 masked writes -- R871 / R875's
  98.2%.) The levels second by second are within a few percent across all
  five; the bench's level comparison cannot hear drums or effects.

*Not done / open:* Zero Gunner's 538 underruns (before its
capture -- the SCSP's FM engine against its 1,814-clock budget, R857's max
1,830, is a candidate that does not need SDRAM at all); Sega Rally silent,

**R880 -- THE PROBE CAPTURES THE i960'S MIDI.** Every bench feeds the sound
board MAME's MIDI bytes; the board's come from our i960 through the i8251
and m2_sound_link. VF2's effects are MIDI note-ons from the i960 (channel 14,
R874) and its music's channels are set up by MIDI, so a difference there
would explain both symptoms and no bench could show it. M2_PROBE's 'M'
record: each byte the sound board takes from the link goes into 16 places;
a record slot with bytes waiting sends up to four instead of its turn (the
turn waits one slot), with a running count so a lost record shows. The
decoder rebuilds the stream (decode_why.py <capture> 80 <out>) for a byte-
for-byte comparison with MAME's midi.txt.


**R876 -- ZERO GUNNER'S LOCKUP IS `rep rpc`: A REGISTER-COUNTED rep READ b0,
MODEL 1'S FIXED FAULT, NEVER PORTED. AND SEGA RALLY RUNS 1,348 WORDS AHEAD OF
THE TGP INTO A 128-WORD QUEUE THAT DROPPED THEM: A FULL INPUT FIFO NOW HOLDS
THE i960. NEITHER EXPLAINS VF2's 0x7dc4. NOT FITTED.**

*The board (s1207 = af10f15 + M2_PROBE, decode_why):* Zero Gunner locks within
1-2 s of play; for 15 s every C record is i960 IP 0x00560c38, copro_stall,
TGP pc 0x0857, no unimplemented op, no input or output word dropped.

*What the probe's pc is:* m2_tgp dbg_pc = retire_pc, the last instruction
RETIRED -- an address in the game's uploaded program (Zero Gunner uploads
2,856 words, 0xb28; there is no microcode in front of it). A `rep` body
retires at its own pc each iteration, so 0x857 is the body below.

*What 0x857 is (Zero Gunner's TGP program, dumped by the capture; a Python
port of MAME's mb86233d.cpp read it):* the dispatcher at 0x04f takes a command
word's exponent field (the function-port code) and jumps through the table at
0x055. Codes 0x37 / 0x38 -> 0x84f: `mov rf1, $0x40` (N). Code 0x39 -> 0x851:
`ldi #0x41, x1; d = $0x40 << 2; mov d, rpc; rep rpc; mov rf1, (bx1+1)` --
pop 4N words into data RAM. Code 0x3a -> 0x859: the same count, pushed out.
The i960 at 0x560c38 is in a different routine: `st 0x2b2b` to the function
port 0x8802b0 (command 0x2b), three argument pushes, then `ld (g6)` x3 -- the
three results. So the TGP was still popping inside command 0x39 while the
i960 had moved on and was waiting for command 0x2b's answer: the TGP believed
it was owed more words than the i960 sent.

*Why (MAME 0.289, mb86233.cpp case 0x0f sub 2):* `u8 r = opcode & 0x8000 ?
read_reg(opcode) : opcode;` -- read_reg masks the index to opcode & 0x3f,
0x34 = rpc. mb86233_core loaded the register-file read address for a
register-sourced rep with 6'd0: b0. R737 says so in as many words ("Model 1's
deb6642 reads opcode[5:0] there (MAME), not ported (R732)"), and
tb_mb86233_core's generator pinned the register form to index 0 "because this
core still reads b0". Model 1's mb86233_core.sv (reference 0b5d04f, current
with its local repository) has the fix and describes this exact failure: "a
transfer that runs too many times waits on an input FIFO that will never
fill". Zero Gunner's b0 is 0 (`ldi #0x0, b0` at 0x043), so every `rep rpc`
ran 256 times; the first command 0x39 hangs. Only Zero Gunner uses the form:
`rep <register>` occurs at 0x856 and 0x85e of its program and nowhere in
VF2's (3,802 words), Sega Rally's (1,665), Daytona's or Desert Tank's.

*Reproduced (MAME 0.289 + sim/tgp/tgp_capture_2a.lua, new: tgp_capture.lua
with its Daytona inputs off, over mame_m2_2a_play.lua's Zero Gunner session;
coin at 20 s, window frames 1300-3700 = 41.7 s, play from ~30 s; 4,200,104
words in, 1,511,470 out, 1,133,471 io reads, 728,897 io writes, no upload in
the window; the first 0x38 / 0x39 at frame 1769, 6,102 of each in the
window). tgp_replay TGP_PROG=4096 on af10f15's RTL: FAIL -- "no retire for
2M cycles at pc 0857 state S_SRC", after 140,748 input pops, 48,586 outputs,
46,768 io reads, all bit-exact against MAME. The last commands: 0x38 with N
= 2, 0x39, eight words; MAME took eight and went on to command 0x05, the RTL
took 28 and waited. Board and bench agree on the pc and on the direction of
the wait.

*FIX (mb86233_core.sv, Model 1's rule):* rd_addr_q for a register-sourced
rep (rep group, sub 2, opcode[15]) is opcode[5:0]; rd_hold carries it to
S_RETIRE as before. No state, no cycle; one more term in a 6-bit mux. The
replay of the whole window: PASS, bit-exact -- 1,511,470 outputs, 4,200,104
pops, 1,133,471 io reads and 728,897 writes, 0 mismatches, unimplemented 0;
52.0 M TGP instructions, 4.04 s of TGP time at 80 MHz in 41.7 s.

*SEGA RALLY -- A DIFFERENT CAUSE, FOUND ON THE WAY (the same capture in a
race: srallyc, mame_m2_2a_play.lua's rally session, frames 1300-3720).*
Its TGP is bit-exact over the whole window with the plain replay (706,456
outputs, 4,240,743 pops, 2,096,663 io reads, 4,755,136 io writes, 452,091
buffer-RAM reads served from the capture, 0 mismatches). But the i960 runs
ahead: between two output reads it pushes up to 1,348 words (1,482 runs over
1,024 words, 3,042 over 128 in 40 s; the first at frame 1516), and MAME's
input FIFO sits above its 8 words for 2.56 M of the 4.24 M pushes -- its
generic_fifo HALTS the i960 then (model2.cpp:197, on_fifo_full_post_sync).
m2_copro never held a write: its queue is 128 and a push into it full was
dropped (dbg_in_dropped), on R133-era reasoning ("the queue is 128 deep and the
counter says if it was ever too small"). The TGP spends ~150 clk_sys cycles
a word in Rally's window; an i960 storing a word every ~20 cycles is 128
ahead within ~150 words of a 1,000-word run. Every word past that was lost
and the command stream slipped -- the 3D dropping out and the crash Ben saw
fit it. The other games never come near: longest run Daytona 28, Desert
Tank 56, VF2 34, Zero Gunner 38.
RESULT BENCH (tb_tgp_replay --board-push, new: pushes offered whatever the
FIFO holds, completing unless m2_copro stalls them, as the board's bridge;
--gap 40, the i960 0..40 cycles between accesses; frames 1300-1530):
  * the old m2_copro (the rep fix in): the first word dropped at feed
    frame 1515 -- the first long run -- after 40,297 bit-exact pops; then
    3,233 of 43,728 pops, 1,089 of 2,328 outputs wrong, 4,494 words dropped
    by the cap of 300 M cycles, and the TGP off the end of its program (pc
    0xe09b). On the board that is a command stream slipping on every long
    run.
*FIX (m2_copro.sv):* a FIFO-port or function-port write into a full input
queue raises `stall` (push_hold) while the TGP runs, and lands on the first
cycle a slot frees; the bridge already holds a stalled write in S_IOW
(io_sel re-asserted, one push on completion). A halted or uploading TGP
keeps the old outcome (it cannot drain). Every original-board game measured
stays below 128, so the original core never stalls on it.
  * with it, the same run: PASS, bit-exact (6,019 outputs, 71,433 pops,
    21,860 io reads, 80,889 io writes), 0 dropped; the i960 held on the full
    queue 2.35 M cycles (29 ms at 80 MHz over 230 frames).
  * the whole race window with board-like timing (--board-push --gap 40
    --jitter 40): PASS, bit-exact (706,456 outputs, 4,240,743 pops,
    2,096,663 io reads, 4,755,136 io writes), 0 dropped. Zero Gunner's
    window the same way (--gap 60 --jitter 40): PASS, bit-exact, the hold
    never fires.
  * WHAT IT COSTS, AN ESTIMATE: in that run the i960 model sat on the full
    queue for 470 M of 888 M cycles, and the TGP was busy 11.1 s of TGP time
    at 80 MHz (CPI 9.0 with the jitter) across 2,420 frames (42 s). The
    bench's i960 offers a word every ~20 cycles, faster than the board's, so
    this overstates the hold -- but Sega Rally is TGP-bound on this core
    where the other games are not, and if it runs below MAME's frame rate on
    the board the TGP's speed (R771-R778) is the place to look, not this.

*VF2's 0x7dc4 (s1203, minutes of attract) is NEITHER.* VF2's program has no
register-counted rep, and its longest run ahead is 34 words. Its TGP is
bit-exact under board-like timing too: tb_tgp_replay --gap 60 --jitter 40
(new: memory answers lat + 0..40 cycles, seeded) on the three VF2 windows
(frames 20-760, 700-760, 1500-1531: 83,494 words in at 1500), Sega Rally's
two boot windows and Zero Gunner's: PASS, bit-exact, 0 dropped. So the
TGP's own arithmetic, sequencing and memory handshakes under variable
latency are cleared for the code those windows run. Open, with what settles
it: the next VF2 lockup on a probe build now reports the TGP's pc; if it is
the dispatch wait (0x035 region, input empty) the i960 / bridge lost a word
or a command; if it is in a handler, a capture of that handler's window.
A candidate not tested: VF2's TGP reads buffer RAM the i960 has just written
(R852 b); on the board those reads go through m2_sdram port 9 while the
i960's stores go through the bridge -- a read that overtakes a posted store
reads stale data, and a stale count can steer a TGP loop.

*R880 ON THE BOARD (s1213 = 626fd21 + M2_PROBE + M2_NO_2A_RALLY; 41,438 ALM,
553 / 553 M10K, clk_sys -0.229, clk_mem -0.131): VF2 from load, 100 s, 89 M
