**R881 -- R877's PORT-7 "WORD PAIR SHIFTED" IS A BENCH ARTIFACT (VERILATOR
DOES NOT MASK A C++ INPUT), NOT m2_sdram. THE 2A SDRAM PATH WITH THE REAL
CROSSING AND THE REAL SOUND BOARD RETURNS EVERY WORD RIGHT: 0 FAILS IN 57 M
TRANSACTIONS. NO RTL CHANGE.**

*Believed (R877 a):* ~1.5% of tb_m2_sdram_load's port 7 reads came back with
a word pair shifted (data written at an odd address read at the even one
below), "most likely this bench reissuing on the cycle after an acknowledge,
as no m2_sdram_cdc port can" -- recorded, not dismissed, because the DSP
writes on port 7 on the board and the drums are a hiss there.

*Established:* the bench's addresses were `bank << 23`, which sets bit 24 for
banks 2 and 3 -- a 25-bit value written into the harness's 24-bit p*_addr
inputs. Verilator does not mask a value written from C++, and the harness
packs the thirteen inputs into one vector; the generated code is
`p_addr[7] = (p7_addr << 8) | (p6_addr >> 16)`, so port 6's bit 24 (bank 2,
always set) became port 7's bit 0. A watch on every WRITE the controller
issued showed every port 7 write at address | 1 (issued 9c0008, written
9c0009). Reads were shifted the same way, so only a write at an odd address
was visible -- read back one word low, exactly R877's pattern; port 2 (from
port 1) and port 6 (from port 5) were hit too, unseen against unwritten zeros.
The reissue explanation was wrong: m2_sdram takes that stimulus correctly.
Fix (bench): tb_m2_sdram.cpp's Harness masks every address to the port width
before driving it. tb_m2_sdram_load now reads 0 fails of 2,870,487 checks
(AGE: 0 of 2,744,998); 60 frames at think 8: 0 of 27,338,942; AGE, think 40:
0 of 30,446,933. tb_m2_sdram, the four test_m2_sdram13 cases (AGE case
2,151,281 checks, R877's number), 128 MB and test_m2_sdram_cdc (also at 80 /
100 MHz, jitter 1.5 ns) unchanged and green.

*The real path, built (tb_m2_sdram_cdc_load, make test_m2_sdram_cdc_load):*
m2_sdram_cdc (FAST 2, 3, 10, 11, 12) + m2_sdram (2A class, PRI_TOP 3,
eight-word reads on 2 / 10-12, COL_BITS 10) + the device model, clk_sys 80 and
clk_mem 100 MHz driven independently (phase, drift, jitter). Ports 5-7 are the
REAL m2_2a_sound -- bus FSM, line cache, R871's read-merge-write, R877's posted
writes and snoops, its boot check and clear -- with stand-ins only for the
68000 (bus cycles from the C++) and the SCSP core (its two SDRAM clients
copied, around the REAL m2_scsp_cache: the slot fetch's look / fill / look
again, the DSP's R_LOOK / R_FILL / R_AGAIN and w_pend / w_out / gap). A video
load on 1-4, 8-12 and the write port (the i960 writing on 1). sdram_model gains
DEFAULT_HASH (unwritten words read a hash of their address, off by default),
so a word from the wrong address, port or burst slot cannot pass as zero.
Checks: every read word on every port at the clock its requester took the
acknowledge, against the set of values legal for its request-to-acknowledge
window (exact, from every write's own window -- not a tolerance); the 68000's
program / sample reads and its own RAM exactly (posted writes and merges seen
by its later reads); every slot-cache hit and DSP read against memory as it
stood 32 clk_sys earlier (a lost snoop would leave a line stale); the
request contract (held unchanged until acknowledged, never dropped early, no
slow-port acknowledge without a request, one first half per eight-word read,
200 us watchdog); after a drain the device's READ / WRITE counts equal what
was asked (nothing lost or doubled); the boot check; device violations.
Mutations it catches (3 ms runs): s_ack not gated by s_req 71,301 fails; no
68000 snoop into the slot cache 18; B_LOOK filling without waiting for a
posted write 24,961; port 7's captured address | 1 (R877's pattern on the real
path) 3,214.

*Result (each run: the boot check reads 0 wrong; 0 device violations; READs
and WRITEs served = asked):*
  run (think clk_mem, clock)            transactions   words checked   68000 checks  fails
  3 s, think 20, drift +1 ps            21,713,910     113,024,781     1,538,305      0
  1.5 s, think 8, ratio exact, phase 0  11,025,071      52,830,797       631,935      0
  1.5 s, think 160, drift -3, jit 400    10,210,797      68,641,321     2,920,512      0
  1 s, think 40, phase 1250 fixed         7,237,999      41,250,587       666,775      0
  1 s, think 40, phase 7777 fixed         7,238,940      41,146,443       668,047      0
In the 3 s run ports 5 / 6 / 7 made 944 K / 931 K / 927 K transactions
(3.55 M slot lookups, 685 K DSP reads checked). Not run (stopped for time):
the AGE and POST_WR=0 builds' sweeps, BOOT_FULL, jitter 1.5 ns.

*Analysis, for what simulation cannot show:* a slow port's s_ack is gated by
s_req and its edge term lasts one slow cycle, so an acknowledge cannot be
taken for the next request; m2_sdram writes p_dout only for the delivering
port, and the slow side reads it >= 2 clk_sys after the toggle. The address
and read-data buses cross unconstrained (asynchronous groups) with ~20-35 ns
of slack -- routing would have to be grossly long to matter. The one-clk_sys
low between a posted write's acknowledge and the next request (12.5 ns) is
always seen by a 10 ns clk_mem.

*So:* the SDRAM path does NOT explain "drums a tinny hiss, effects gone under
the music". Open as before: the SCSP datapath that fails timing on silicon
(R874 addendum / R875), and whatever else no bench models.

**R882 -- ARE THE SOUND ROMS IN SDRAM WHAT THE ZIP HOLDS?** Every link of the
board's sound path is now proven but one: the MIDI equals MAME's (R880), the
SCSP and the sound program equal MAME's in simulation (R857 / R874), the
real SDRAM crossing under load reads 0 wrong (R881). Every bench loads the
sample ROMs straight from the zip; on the board they come through Main's MRA
loader, m2_rom_loader and the relocation to SDRAM byte 0x3400000 (R852 /
R862). A wrong or missing 2 MB part would leave the voices whose samples
live there playing garbage -- VF2's drums as hiss -- and the rest right.
m2_2a_sound CHKSUM (on with M2_PROBE): before the 68000 starts, V_SUM reads
the program (256 K words) and the samples (4 M words) through port 5 and
sums each region's 68000-order words; M2_PROBE's 'R' record (in Q's place,
R876 having fixed the TGP) carries one region a record. Bench (VF2 images
from the zip): program dc60fe32, samples 2c87d546 f6039863 33a13138
346ebe9e -- equal to the same sums computed in Python from vf2.zip
(epr-17574.30; mpr-17573.31, -17572.32, -17571.36, -17570.37).



**R883 -- "THE BENCH'S PITCHES KEEP GOING UP AND DOWN" (Ben, listening to the
VF2 bench clip against MAME's): THE CLIP WAS A 48 MHz RUN WHOSE ENGINE FELL
BEHIND REAL TIME. SEPARATELY, AT THE BOARD'S 80 MHz, OUR TIMERS RAN 1.3% FAST
AND THE MUSIC WITH THEM: A TIMER STARTS AT ITS WRITE, NOT AT THE SAMPLE THE
WRITE LANDS IN (MAME). FIXED, +21 ALMs est.; THE REPLAY BENCHES UNCHANGED.**

*Believed (the task):* the register-visible play state (CA through MSLC, the
timers' interrupts) runs ahead of the timers by a varying 0-8 samples (the
output FIFO), so the driver's streaming sees position and time disagree and
the pitch wavers. The RMS / brightness checks used so far cannot hear pitch.

*Measured (sim/sound/tb_m2_2a_sound, VF2, SND_SHIFT=9, 11.6 s, latency 6-40,
against MAME 0.289's capture -- regs.bin, out.bin, keyon.txt):*
  1. THE CLIP BEN HEARD WAS RUN AT 48 MHz (R874's run: 511,764 output values
     for 11.6 s -- the bench read the output every CLK / 44,100 = 1,088
     clocks, 44,117.6 a second). At 48 MHz the engine has 1,088 clocks a
     sample, below its need in VF2's dense passages: 972 output-FIFO
     underruns, and the playback rate (samples generated per 100 ms of
     drained time / 4,410) fell to 0.958-0.998 in bursts at 8.6-9.0,
     10.2-10.5 and 11.2-11.4 s -- up to 4.2% (74 cents) flat for 100 ms at
     a time, then back to 1.000: the pitches "going up and down". The same
     run at 80 MHz, the board's clock: 0 underruns, the rate 0.9998-1.0002
     in every 100 ms; the board reported 0 underruns (R877). So the wobble
     was the bench's clock, not the RTL and not the board.
  2. THE PITCH REGISTERS ARE MAME's. Word 8 (OCT / FNS) and word 9 (the LFO)
     are written with MAME's values in MAME's order (5-11 s: 191 / 191; all
     85 of 7.5-10.5 s matched by value in order); the driver does no software
     vibrato. The output's spectral peaks match MAME's window by window
     (e.g. 444 / 440 Hz, the FFT's 4 Hz bins). Pitch is not where it differs.
  3. THE TIMERS DO NOT. VF2's driver re-arms timer A in its handler (0x418 =
     206: 49 samples, prescale 0) and timer B (0x41a = 0x3c0: 504 samples).
     Write-to-write intervals, 5-11 s: MAME 49.890 / 505.134 samples, ours
     49.253 / 504.622 -- timer A 1.28% fast. Against MAME's out.bin (best
     lag per 0.25 s window) the bench drifts +3,600 samples in 6.75 s
     (+1.2%), and key-ons paired with MAME's drift -0.95%: the whole music
     ran ~1.2% fast, so no fixed alignment with MAME holds past ~0.3 s.
  CAUSE: MAME's timers are scheduler timers adjusted from the writing CPU's
  local time (scsp.cpp UpdateReg 0x18-0x1d: m_timerA->adjust(attotime::
  from_ticks(512, clock / pris / (255 - count)))), so a timer re-armed by its
  handler a latency d after the interrupt falls due P + d after the previous
  expiry (d ~0.9 sample in MAME's capture). Ours counted P drained ticks from
  the sample the write landed in, so d was dropped: the period was P (P + 1
  when d crossed a tick). R857's "the timers count output samples ... a
  fraction of a sample late at most" is right for one period; the fraction
  is lost on EVERY re-arm, and VF2 re-arms 900 times a second.
  NOT THE TASK'S HYPOTHESIS: at 80 MHz the FIFO keeps the engine a near-
  constant 6-7 samples ahead (it refills within ~900 of each sample's 1,814
  clocks); a constant lead is a latency, not a rate, and cannot change pitch.
  Ticking the timers on generated samples instead would have tied them to
  the engine's jitter and left them as fast as before.

*The fix (rtl/sound/scsp/m2_scsp_regs.sv, m2_scsp.sv, m2_2a_sound.sv):* each
timer keeps its write's phase within the drained sample -- tph, the 44.1 kHz
accumulator's top six bits (1/49 of a sample at 80 MHz, 1/59 at 48) -- and,
once its count is due at a tick, fires in the clock the phase reaches it (or
at the next tick). A write in the tick's own clock counts as on it. `exact`
= !step_mode: tb_m2_scsp and the random captures apply writes at sample
boundaries and fire on the tick as before. Area (quartus_map,
sim/sound/scsp_area_top.sv): 1,922 -> 1,943 ALMs est., +33 ALUT, +21
registers, no block RAM. (A clock-exact 11-bit phase cost +47 ALMs and gave
the same timing: timer A 49.944 against 49.931.) tb_m2_2a_sound now reads its
output once per drained sample on the board's own accumulator.

*Bench, before / after (VF2 SND_SHIFT=9, 11.6 s, 80 MHz, latency 6-40):*
                                     before (0d18683)   after      MAME
  timer A interval, samples              49.253         49.931    49.890
  timer B interval, samples             504.622        505.240   505.134
  0x418 writes, 5-11 s                    5,372          5,299     5,304
  key-ons 4.5-11.6 s                        851            850       850
  drift against MAME (key-ons)           -0.95%         +0.064%
  output against out.bin, the lag held at the 4.6 s window's (+-2.3 ms),
  waveform correlation per 0.5 s from 4.6 s:
    48 MHz (the clip Ben heard)  0.52 0.30 0.04 0.18 0.06 0.11 0.06 0.14 0.12 0.31 0.06 0.11 0.10
    80 MHz before                0.10 0.10 0.08 0.13 0.07 0.06 0.04 0.06 0.10 0.11 0.09 0.09 0.11
    80 MHz after                 0.63 0.58 0.53 0.73 0.36 0.46 0.39 0.56 0.11 0.14 0.12 0.09 0.08
  after, low-passed (< ~150 Hz) / 5 ms RMS envelope, 4.6-8.6 s: 0.79-0.94 /

The offset at which the bench meets MAME is -78 samples (-1.8 ms) from

picked. The music starts with its MIDI, so the 68000's later start (the
pre-boot check, ~222 ms, R871) does not move it.

THE LEAD IS NOT IT -- TESTED: the same run with the engine held to one
sample ahead (o_ready at f_n < 1, a scratch copy of m2_2a_sound, not
committed) gives a BYTE-IDENTICAL SCSP write stream, times included, and

the 6 samples of lead. What is left is the 68000's own pace: its RAM and
SCSP accesses wait on SDRAM where MAME's take one wait state (R859), so its
background scan reaches each slot at other moments than MAME's. Free-running
by design (R821's case); not changed here.

**R884 -- "STILL A FAST WOBBLE OR FAST POPPING" (Ben, R883's clip against
MAME's): NOT THE 68000'S PACE. NO RING IS READ STALE; A ZERO-LATENCY 68000
AND A MAME-TIMED ONE MATCH MAME NO BETTER THAN TODAY'S. THE 68000 NOW RUNS
ON MAME'S WAIT STATES, ITS CLOCK STOPPED WHILE SDRAM ANSWERS (EXACT, +18
ALMs est.). WHAT IS LEFT OF ITS TIMING AGAINST MAME IS THE CPU CORE: fx68k
TAKES AN INTERRUPT ONE INSTRUCTION LATER THAN MAME'S 68000.**

*Believed (the task):* VF2's driver streams every voice through an 8 KB ring
"only ~16 samples ahead" of the play position (R874); our 68000 waits on
SDRAM where MAME's takes one wait state (R859), so in places it falls behind
and the SCSP plays last lap's data -- a fast wobble or popping, worse with
more voices. Ben's clip correlates with MAME's ~0.53 in the drum intro.

*Measured (tb_m2_2a_sound, VF2, SND_SHIFT=9, 11.6 s, 80 MHz, latency 6-40
unless said; an instrumented copy of the bench -- PACE -- reading the
engine's fetches, the 68000's bus and the sound RAM's writes; MAME 0.289's
capture, and its debugger on the sound CPU):*
  1. NO STALE READS. Every slot fetch from a ring checked against the
     68000's last write to that word: a word read at the start of a new lap
     not rewritten since its previous lap's read -- 0 of 812,765 (today's
     RTL), 0 of 807,180 (latency 1), 0 of 797,823 (EXACT, below). At note
     starts (a voice's first 2,048 samples, a word not written since 4,000
     samples before its key-on): 172 reads in 2 of 214 voices; MAME's own
     capture, positions rebuilt from keyon.txt and word 8, 7 of 219 voices.
  2. THE RING IS A LAP AHEAD, NOT 16 SAMPLES. MAME's 68000 writes each ring
     word 1 K-4 K samples ahead of the play position (27% of 1.5 M writes)
     or 4 K-8 K (68%); under 64 samples ahead 0.009%. Ours: 35% / 55%,
     under 64 0.45% -- more near the pointer, never late (item 1). R874's "16
     samples" is the first 512 words landing just before a key-on, not the
     streaming margin; at 22 kHz a lap is 0.37 s of slack.
  3. PACE DOES NOT MOVE THE MATCH. 10 ms windows against out.bin, each
     fine-aligned +-3 samples around one lag (Ben's measure), drum intro
     4.6-6.6 s / 4.6-11.6 s: today 0.573 / 0.234; latency 1 (the 68000 never
     waits) 0.424 / 0.168; EXACT 0.354 / 0.137. The fixed-lag figure falls
     with each because each runs at a slightly different tempo (item 5); with
     the lag followed in 0.25 s steps the three are the same: 0.672 / 0.665
     / 0.674 in the intro, 0.400 / 0.428 / 0.390 overall.
  4. THE 68000'S BUS AGAINST MAME'S (half-clocks with AS low; MAME's model2_snd:
     ROM and samples 5, RAM and SCSP 7 -- before_delay(1) is one clock):
       today   program hit 5, fill 10.2 (4.6% of 12.2 M fetches); samples
               hit 5, fill 10.2 (23%); RAM read 9.93; RAM write 5.70 (posted:
               74% at 5, faster than MAME); byte write 12.2; SCSP read 6.28,
               write 5.93
       EXACT   every ROM / sample cycle 5, every RAM / SCSP cycle 7
  5. WHERE THE 68000 STILL DIFFERS FROM MAME: THE INTERRUPT. Timer A's
     period is 49 samples plus the handler's latency to its re-arm (R883).
     MAME (debugger on audiocpu, totalcycles at the handler 601f16 and the
     re-arm 601f1a, 13.6-16.6 s): 12,770.2 clocks (49.884 samples), latency
     226.2 (sd 19.3); entry to re-arm always 138 (MOVEM.L of 13 registers,
     26 one-wait writes). Ours: today 49.931, EXACT 49.967 (12,789 clocks;
     IRQ to iack 51.4, iack to re-arm 195.9 -- the handler identical, entry
     to the re-arm write 157 from the first fetch). All of EXACT's 20 clocks
     are IRQ to handler entry: MAME 75.2 (sd 19.3, nothing past ~175), ours
     ~93 (sd 40, a tail to 220). fx68k latches the pending interrupt at the
     START of an instruction (grp1LatchEn & enT3, "interrupt pending on T2")
     and takes it at that instruction's end; MAME's m68000 decides at the
     END (m_next_state = m_int_next_state at the IRD load, the last
     microword). An IRQ that arrives inside VF2's copy loop -- MOVEM.L
     (A1)+,D0-D7 / MOVEM.L D0-D7,(A2) / ADDA.W #$20,A2, sixteen times (the
     interrupted PC is there 22% of the time in MAME, 29% in ours) -- waits through
     the next MOVEM (88 clocks) on fx68k only. NOT CHANGED: fx68k is
     upstream byte for byte (THIRD_PARTY.md), and which core is the silicon
     is not established here -- a MAME cycle count is not a hardware fact.
     Today's RTL sat nearer MAME's tempo (49.931) only because its posted
     writes were a wait state faster than MAME's and offset part of it.

*Built (rtl/sound/m2_2a_sound.sv EXACT, Model2.sv M2_2A_SND_EXACT, both 1):*
each bus cycle has exactly MAME's wait states in the 68000's own clocks --
DTACK held off past the first DTACK sample of a RAM / SCSP cycle (fx68k
samples DTACK on PHI2: the second after AS decides zero waits, the third
one) -- and where the answer is not there by the sample that must see it,
the 68000's CLOCK STOPS instead of a wait state going in. Half-clocks fall
due at 2 x 11.2896 MHz as before into a credit; one issues when there is
credit, the 68000 is not stopped and none issued the clock before (fx68k:
never two enables in a row), so after a stop it catches up at up to clk / 2
(1.77 x at 80 MHz); never ahead of real time, at most 511 half-clocks (~1
sample) behind before time is dropped. SDRAM time costs real time, not 68000
time, so the board's video load stops moving the sound program's timeline
-- while the catch-up keeps up. EXACT 0 is the clock as before.
  * Bench (6-40): behind real time mean 0.71 half-clocks, max 67 (3 us),
    never at the cap. The unshifted 6 s run: PASS, 98.9% of writes in MAME's
    order (98.2% before), 0 underruns, the check 0 wrong; the matched writes

  * Area (quartus_map 17.0, m2_2a_sound alone): 4,827 -> 4,845 ALMs est.,

*What this predicts for the board:* nothing new to hear from this change --
the bench says the pace was not the fault and EXACT sounds like today
(item 3). What it changes is that the board's 68000 now keeps the bench's
timeline whatever the video does, while its SDRAM answers about as the 6-40
model does (VF2 attract, R877); under saturation it falls back toward the
old behaviour, still ahead of it. So a board clip and the bench clip should
now differ only where the board's SDRAM truly starves the 68000 or the SCSP

**R885 -- THE DIFFERENTIAL SPLIT: THE FREE-RUNNING SCSP COMPUTES MAME'S
MIX FROM WHAT IT IS GIVEN (REPLAYED THROUGH scsp_ref.h, EVERY SAMPLE
ACCOUNTED FOR). WHAT IT WAS GIVEN WAS WRONG BECAUSE OF WHAT IT TOLD THE
68000: THE 0x408 MONITOR WAS LATCHED IN THE ENGINE'S TIME, AND 11% OF
VF2's READS SAW ANOTHER SLOT'S CA -- THE DRIVER REFILLED ITS STREAMING
RINGS EARLY, OVERWRITING DATA NOT YET PLAYED. THE MONITOR NOW LATCHES IN
THE 68000's OWN TIME, AS MAME's: THE BENCH NOW WRITES MAME's STREAM, AND
MATCHES MAME 0.725 OVER 4.6-11.6 s (WAS 0.390). -15 ALMs EST., NO BLOCK RAM.**

*Believed (the task):* Ben hears the bench's VF2 clip as "a fast wobble or
fast popping"; R883 / R884 ruled out the timers, the 68000's pace, stale
ring reads, the pitch registers, SDRAM, MIDI and the ROMs. tb_m2_scsp is
bit-exact only in step mode; the free-running engine applies a write at a
slot boundary, runs ahead into the FIFO, and its register-visible state can
be ~7 samples ahead. Split it: replay OUR run's accesses through the
reference at the places the engine applied them. Equal -> the 68000 is fed
something different; not equal -> the engine departs from MAME.

*Built to split it (sim only; nothing synthesised changes for it):*
  * M2_SND_TRACE (m2_scsp.sv, m2_2a_sound.sv, `ifdef): +sndtrace=<file>
    logs, in the ENGINE's time, every 68000 register access as the engine
    applies it (the sample it lands in, and where: before slot 0..31, after
    the slots, or inside a slot for a RAM write), every sound-RAM write as it
    lands (68000 and DSP), every sample made (raw L / R), and the drained
    sample count. make obj_snd2a_tr/Vm2_2a_sound SCSP_SFX=_tr
    SCSP_DEFS=-DM2_SND_TRACE.
  * sim/sound/scsp_split.cpp (make obj_scsp_split/scsp_split): scsp_ref.h
    (MAME's scsp.cpp, ported) given the trace's accesses at the same sample
    and slot (scsp_ref.h gained a per-slot hook, nothing else), its mix
    compared with the engine's sample for sample, and its reads checked.
    It also counts (a) 0x408 reads whose latch was made for another slot
    than MSLC selects, and (b) slot reads of a word the 68000 wrote TWICE
    since the slot last read it -- a later lap of a streamed ring played
    early. (R884 item 1 checked only the opposite, a word NOT rewritten.)
  * sim/sound/scsp_cap2tr.py: MAME's own capture in the same format. It
    replays EQUAL to MAME's out.bin (20.6 s, 0 samples differ) -- the tool
    and the reference agree with MAME before they judge the RTL.

*Measured -- THE SPLIT (VF2, SND_SHIFT=9, 11.6 s, 80 MHz, latency 6-40,
0c90017's RTL):*
  1. THE ENGINE IS THE REFERENCE. 511,566 samples: 68 differ with RAM writes
     that land inside a slot's microprogram counted after that slot, 124
     with them counted before -- and NO sample differs under both (the trace
     cannot tell whether such a write beat the slot's fetch; 432,676 of
     3,692,473 RAM writes land inside a slot). 398,075 register writes,
     32,537 slot-register / 0x408 reads 0 wrong. Every access applied before
     slot 0 instead (MAME's "between samples") differs everywhere by 15-30%
     RMS -- one-sample shifts of a voice, inaudible, but it shows the split
     placement is needed to see equality. So the free-running engine, mid-
     sample writes and run-ahead included, computes MAME's mix from what it
     is given. R821's departure is not the fault.
  2. WHAT IT IS GIVEN DIFFERS FROM MAME'S BECAUSE OF THE MONITOR. 3,438 of
     32,229 0x408 reads (10.67%) returned a latch made for another slot
     than MSLC selected; 454 of them a different CA bit 7 than the selected
     slot's own. MAME's: none on the delayed path, by its update rule (b)
     -- inferred, not counted: the capture keeps no order within a sample.
  THE CHAIN (sound program disassembled at 602242-60266a):
     a. The driver's background loop walks 32 voice records. At the end of
        each it writes MSLC (move.b $16(a0),$408(a5)); in the next it burns
        ~300 68000 clocks (ten ror.l #8 -- longer than a sample's 256) and
        tests CA bit 0 (btst #7,$409(a5)): which half of the voice's ring is
        playing. When it flips, it copies the next 512 bytes of the stream
        into the other half (sixteen MOVEM.L pairs, 6022e4-6024b2) and counts
        the stream down ($a(a0) -= 0x200); at the stream's end (6024be, no
        delay) it clears LPCTL and writes LEA so the voice plays out.
     b. MAME: sound_stream::update() runs to the CPU's LOCAL time and makes
        samples up to and including the current one; the monitor is latched
        at the end of each update that made a sample, for the MSLC then. So
        a sample boundary of the 68000's own time always falls inside the
        ~300-clock wait, and the read sees its slot.
     c. Ours: the monitor was latched by the engine's output microcode at
        the end of each sample it MADE. The engine makes a sample when the
        FIFO drains one, but not evenly: a slow DSP pass or SDRAM waits hold
        a sample past the next drain. Of the stale reads, 2,834 had two
        drained samples between the MSLC write and the read with the engine
        still in the same sample (the read waiting at the DSP window).
     d. A wrong CA bit -> a copy into the half being played -> the voice
        plays a later block early, or skips one: a discontinuity a block at a
        time. The stream is used up faster: our 68000 wrote 20-30% more
        sound RAM than MAME's in 5-8.5 s and ~2x in 8.6-11.6 s (4.6-11.6 s:
        2,937,152 words, MAME 1,893,845), and 86% of the slot reads of a
        freshly written word read one written twice (MAME 34% -- the
        driver's normal pattern; the excess is the fault). The streams end
        early -- the end-of-stream writes (word 0 low byte 0x11-0x14, word 3
        LEA) land 150-290 ms before MAME's
        (slot 2 4.959 / 5.117 s, slot 0 4.989 / 5.173, slot 11 5.100 /
        5.391) -- and the voices freed early move the driver's slot
        allocation: R883's "slot 19 for MAME's 20 at 5.84 s" and the missing
        TL rewrites at 8.54 s are downstream of this, not of the run-ahead.
     R883's test (the engine held to one sample ahead: byte-identical
     writes) is consistent: the lead was never the fault; the latch's
     timing against the 68000's clock was.

*The fix (rtl/sound/scsp/m2_scsp.sv, m2_2a_sound.sv, the microcode):* free-
running, the monitor is latched in the 68000's time. m2_2a_sound counts
the 68000's issued half-clocks (512 a sample: 2 x 11.2896 MHz / 44,100) and
pulses cpu_tick at each wrap. m2_scsp snoops MSLC at the 68000's bus write
(mslc_c), and at cpu_tick takes that slot and asks for a latch; the engine
serves it at its next operation window (dispatch between slots, the DSP
wait, idle -- a few clocks) with a three-word microcode call (UA_MON:
MON1, MON3, RET; the sweep's call mechanism). A 0x408 read no longer goes
through the operation queue: it is answered from the latch as soon as no
latch is pending -- EXACT stops the 68000's clock meanwhile, so the wait
is real time, not 68000 time. Content: the slot's state where the engine
is (~7 samples ahead; R883 showed that lead does not matter). Step mode
(tb_m2_scsp) keeps the per-sample latch and is unchanged.

  0x408 reads for another slot            3,438 of 32,229   0 of 68,101  0 (b)
    with the wrong CA bit                 454               0
  68000 sound-RAM writes, 4.6-11.6 s      2,937,152         1,893,277  1,893,845

    word written twice                    806,462 / 692,794 1,118,769 / 383,837

The 8-20 Hz excess -- half as much again as MAME's envelope modulation -- is
the measurable "fast wobble"; its strongest lines are now MAME's (4.2, 8.5,
1.7, 3.2 Hz: the music's beat). The residual against MAME has no periodic
line of its own before or after (its peaks are the beat): the wrong reads
came ~65 a second but at irregular moments, so the pops were irregular too.
Clicks by |2nd difference| > 4000 tell nothing (ours 19 / 18, MAME 28 / 25).
The writes left unmatched after the fix are pairs 2-9 ms apart in order (8.6-
10.6 s: 817 of 823 matched, the six are word-5 / key-off writes in swapped
order). What remains of the sample-level difference is the tempo: the
followed lag walks from -20 to -251 samples over 7 s (~0.07% slow), R884
item 5's fx68k interrupt latch, and the 0.25 s tracking itself.

  2. WHERE EACH COMES FROM, 20-120 s (VF2 20-80): VF2 direct 893, DSP return
     2,095 (the direct path 15% of the power); Rally direct 362, return 0
     (100%); Zero Gunner direct 519, return 221 (85%); Virtua Cop 2 direct 319,
     return 2,717 (all of it the DC).
  3. WHY (keyon.txt, all key-ons): DISDL is 3 on every VF2 and Rally voice
     (9,967 / 11,319), 3 on 96% of Zero Gunner's (2 and 4 the rest) -- -24 dB,
     so one full-scale 8-bit voice peaks at ~2,000 directly. VF2's music sends
     to the DSP (IMXL 2-5 on 28% of key-ons) and its returns come back at
     EFSDL 6-7 (-6 / 0 dB); its effects are TL 4, ISEL 0, IMXL 0, word 11
     0x6000 (DISDL 3, no effect send). Rally: IMXL 0 and EFSDL 0 on every
     key-on, TL mostly 0x2a-0x3c (-16 to -22 dB on top of DISDL 3). The 0x400
     writes are the same in both (DAC18B 1, MVOL 15) and MAME's 18-bit DAC
     path has the 16-bit one's scale (put_int_clamp(smpl, 131072) against
     (smpl >> 2, 32768)); ours (m2_scsp dac()) the same.
  4. VF2's EFFECTS AGAINST THE REST, IN MAME (47-75 s, a two-player fight,
     84 channel-14 note-ons): the effect voices' RMS over 0-150 ms after each
     note-on, median 507, peak 1,826; the rest of the mix over the same
     windows 2,489, peak 9,260: -12.9 dB. On the whole mix the 50-150 ms
     after a note-on is -0.1 dB from the 200 ms before (median): in MAME a hit
     does not rise above the music.

*Ours (tb_m2_2a_sound, 80 MHz, latency 6-40, the trace build; new
SND_MIDI_DROP=1 drops MAME's MIDI in [SND_SHIFT_AFTER - SND_SHIFT,
SND_SHIFT_AFTER) as the writes are, so a later game reaches the driver at the
boot's end: SND_SHIFT=41 SND_SHIFT_AFTER=43 puts VF2's second game -- MIDI
43.0 s on -- at 2 s, the fight's first hits at 6 s; 10 s, ~15 min wall,
PASS, 0 underruns). The run's trace through scsp_split: 34 of 441,007 samples
differ (mid-slot RAM writes, R885's ambiguity; residual 0.000 in every 0.5 s).*
                                      ours            MAME
  8 hits, 47-51 s: effects RMS        474 (median)    475
    rest of the mix                   2,938           2,963
    effects / rest                    -15.8 dB        -15.9 dB
    effects peak / rest peak          1,731 / 10,806  1,731 / 10,719
  over 47-51 s: effects / drums /
    music / DSP return / total        301/575/763/2,176/2,916   300/580/763/2,178/2,920
  the DAC output (WAV), 50-150 ms

The OSD volume (Model2.sv, 80% default) is one gain on both channels after
the DAC: it changes no balance. Nothing between the DAC and AUDIO_L
saturates: VF2's p99.9 is 7,000-15,000, no sample of MAME's mix reaches the
16-bit clamp in 300 s.

*Conclusion:* the board does what MAME does, and so -- given R880's MIDI
and R885's split -- does the bench: Ben's two ratios (effects ~-13 dB under
VF2's music, Rally ~-15 dB under VF2) are MAME 0.289's own. The shared
"path" is real but it is in the games' register values, not in our RTL: every
voice's direct send is DISDL 3, and only what a driver routes through the DSP
comes back loud. Changing it would depart from MAME, the reference for what
the silicon computes (the project rules), with nothing here to say MAME is wrong --
its SDL table (-36 .. 0 dB, 6 dB steps) and its DSP path are self-consistent
(one full-scale voice at SDL 7 reaches 16-bit full scale directly or through a
unity DSP program). NOT CHANGED.
*What would settle it (a study-level question for Ben):* a recording of a
real 2A board -- a VF2 fight (hit against music) or Rally against VF2 at one
amplifier setting. If the hardware's effects stand ~13 dB higher, the direct
send (or the DSP input / return scaling) is where MAME is wrong, and one
constant in the level unit's SDL table or the DSP's MIXS / EFREG scaling would
move it; the clip vf2_fight_OURS_direct_plus12dB_left_mono.wav (the bench's
split, direct sends x4) is what that would sound like. Until then, a per-game
OSD "sound boost" is a gain, not a balance, and fixes only Rally / Zero
Gunner's overall level.

TARGET NEEDS A LAYOUT EXTENSION, MANX TT RUNS AS IT IS (AN MRA, AND tanr).
THE INPUT PROFILES. THE 315-5881 AND 317-0229 ARE CHECKS ONLY (PATCHES
PROVED IN MAME). NOTHING FITTED, NOTHING ON A BOARD.**
(Ben, through the coordinator: bring these up cheapest first and give MRAs
to test; input profiles so games do not each add mapping logic; the chip is
full -- prefer zero-logic answers. Limits: one MAME, one Verilator build,
quartus_map only, no board, no run over ~15 min.)

*Believed:* each new 2A set is an MRA on R852 / R862's layout plus its
traps, its protection and its controls -- the four released games' pattern.

*THE FINDING THAT DECIDES MOST OF IT: FIVE OF THE SEVEN DO NOT FIT THE
SDRAM.* Nobody had counted the new sets' ROM against the 2A layout. From
MAME 0.289's ROM_STARTs (every chip scanned in 256 KB blocks for blank
space: all full but motoraid's third polygon pair, 2.5 of 4 MB used):

  set        prog  data          tex (MAME layout)   poly   copro  smp  ROM MB
  2A slots   0.5+1.5  16         8 {0-4, 8-12 MB}    12     4      8
  vf2        0.5   16            4+4 split           12     -      8   41
  manxtt     0.5   12+1 (x4)     4                   12     4      8   43.4
  skytargt   0.5   16+1 (x16)    8 contiguous        16     4      8   54.3
  pltkidsa   1     8             16                  32     -      8   65.5
  hpyagu98   2     32            8 contiguous        16     -      8   66.4
  motoraid   1     24+1 (x8)     8 contiguous        24*    2      8   68
  doaab      1     24+4 (x2)     8 contiguous        24     -      8   69.5
  dynamcop   2     32            16                  32     -      8   90.5
  ("x n": MAME's ROM_COPY mirrors of the last pair. Add the 68000 program,
  the TGP tables and ~5.5 MB of the core's RAMs in SDRAM.)

The controller addresses 64 MB (R19: 1,024 columns; an eleventh column bit
aliases). So MANX TT fits the 2A layout as it stands; SKY TARGET fits 64 MB
but not the layout; the other FIVE need more than 64 MB of ROM before one
RAM is placed -- no MRA can load them on this core, whatever their traps.
Measured on the way (taps on the data windows, 240 s each): hpyagu98,
motoraid and skytargt read main_data above 16 MB through MAME's 0x06000000
window (main_data + 0x1000000), which the bridge maps linearly into the
texture slot today; skytargt reads its 1 MB pair there at mirrored
addresses (0x0640xxxx-0x064dxxxx).

A SECOND GENERAL FACT, THE TEXTURE-COORDINATE ROM: every set built from 4 MB
texture chips (skytargt, hpyagu98, motoraid, doaab: 8 MB at MAME 0-8 MB;
pltkidsa, dynamcop: 16 MB) addresses that ROM's bit 21, which R671's
packing {a[22], a[20:0]} drops: half their u/v and texture headers would
read the other half's. INFERRED fix for the 8 MB sets, ~1 LUT in
m2_geo_engine behind a parameter: {a[22] | a[21], a[20:0]} -- the 2 MB-chip
games never set a[21] (R671: it "would land in the gap, which nothing
addresses"), the 4 MB-chip 8 MB games never set a[22] (MAME's region is
empty there). NOT BUILT: no set that needs it can load yet.

*PROTECTION (MAME taps on 0x01d80000-0x01d9ffff with the IP; MAME's own
disassembly of the program; PL_ZERO runs where the 315-5881's decrypt reads
answer 0, as this core's empty window does; PL_PATCH runs with the patch
words written into the program region before the boot):*
  * PILOT KIDS (315-5881): ONE session, at boot (1.99 s): 12 bytes to the
    chip RAM, subkey 0x7140, 8 bytes decrypted ("98-PILOT") by 0x15750 into
    0x40(fp) and compared byte by byte (0x51900-0x51970) with the program's
    own copy at 0x5518c8; on a mismatch 1 -> 0x5092d4. That flag's four
    readers (0x158b0, 0x6d9c4, 0x6e474, 0x6e848) quietly corrupt the game
    (zero object entries and play state). Zeroed reads: the game runs but
    diverges (credits / score differ at every 30 s snapshot). PATCH: program
    0x51900 3dad0074 (cmpibne) -> 08000080 (b 0x51980), <patch>80 00 00
    08</patch> -- plus MAME's init_pltkids 0x730 = 08000004. PROOF: zeroed
    reads + the patch: the flag 0 for all 229 s, and every snapshot
    (30..240 s) byte-identical to the real-chip run's.
  * DYNAMITE COP (315-5881): FOUR sessions (4.4, 5.1, 24.7, 108 s), two
    checkers: 0x66ac0 (subkey 0x7700, "UCHIDA MOMOKA   ", against 0xbc800)
    and 0x66a00 (subkey 0x1326, 16 binary bytes, against 0xbc7f0); the
    decrypted buffers (0x513f20 / 0x513f40) have no other reference in the
    program. A mismatch stores 2 in 0x51f4b4 and calls 0xa3a00 / 0xa3a50.
    ZEROED READS: MAME HALTS AT 4.36 s ("I960: 0: Unhandled 00") -- the
    first check's penalty. PATCH: the six compare branches cmpibe -> b, same
    displacement: 0x66a50 0x66a68 0x66a80 0x66a98 (3aad0010 -> 08000010) and
    0x66b14 0x66b54 (3aad0038 -> 08000038). PROOF: zeroed reads + the six
    words: 240 s, all four sessions at the real run's times, 0x51f4b4 0x68
    throughout, every snapshot byte-identical to the real-chip run's.
  * DEAD OR ALIVE (317-0229) -- ASSESSED AS ASKED, STOPPED THERE: MAME does
    not emulate DOA's use either (HACK_MODE_DOA hands back a fixed string).
    The boot (0x760) probes the chip -- up to 9,999 polls of 0x01d8400c for
    0xfff0 (MAME's doa_unk_r toggles it) -- then 0x2bd0 uploads 24 + 128
    words of tables, a source, and reads 48 bytes back into 0x54b390,
    compared with a string; 1 / 0 -> 0x54fabc (three readers). The chip
    produces that string and nothing else. Without the chip the probe times
    out (the flag 0, no hang: the timed-out branch skips the poll-forever
    routine). PATCH: 0x760 and 0x778 (the two calls) -> 5c801e01 (mov 1,g0),
    so the flag is 1 and the window is never touched. MAME: 0x54fabc 1 from
    the first second as with the chip (113 / 114 samples, both runs); frames
    differ from the real run's (the skipped polls move the boot), which is
    expected and not an equivalence proof. COST: 0 ALM, 2 MRA words, against
    a chip (Huffman tree + dictionary decompressor) at ~300-500 ALM -- and
    DOA also needs movre (above) and does not fit the SDRAM (69.5 MB).

**R888 -- SEGA RALLY'S "COUPLE OF SLOWDOWNS" (s1220) ARE OURS, NOT THE
ORIGINAL'S: OUR TGP TOOK 1.54x MAME'S TIME FOR RALLY'S WORK, 27% OF IT HELD
ON BUFFER-RAM WRITES. POSTED WRITES AND AN EARLY ALU LAUNCH BRING IT TO
0.97x, BIT-EXACT. NOT FITTED.**

*What was believed (R876).* "Sega Rally is TGP-bound on this core": in the
board-like replay the i960 model sat on the full input FIFO 470 M of 888 M
cycles, and "if it runs below MAME's frame rate on the board the TGP's speed
(R771-R778) is the place to look".

*What the real board does -- hints, none of them a hardware fact.*
  * The clock. MAME 0.289 model2a: `MB86234(config, m_copro_tgp,
    50_MHz_XTAL)`, and mb86233.h `execute_clocks_to_cycles` = clocks / 3:
    16.67 M instruction cycles a second. mb86233.cpp charges one cycle an
    instruction (a stalled one re-runs) and one more for a floating-point
    ALU op whose result alu_post_2 writes (lab and ld/mov, not the 0x0f
    group). Model 1's notes read the part the same way (tools/model1-ref
    docs/00-decisions.md: "three input clocks per instruction cycle ... FP
    ops take a further cycle"). Sega Retro lists the TGP as "16 MHz, 16
    MFLOPS" -- the same ~16 M instruction cycles a second. Nothing on this
    machine (docs/, Model 1's, MAME's) gives the real chip's wait states on
    its table, data-ROM or buffer-RAM accesses; MAME charges none. So the
    real TGP's time is taken here as MAME's model of it: ~60 ns an
    instruction, 120 ns for a written FP op.
  * Rally's TGP work against that model. tb_tgp_replay now counts MAME's
    cycles for the very instruction stream the RTL retires (new FRAME
    BUDGET block). Rally's race window: 119.6 M MAME cycles, 7.17 s over
    2,420 vblanks (42.1 s); a vblank's TGP work p50 3.12 ms, p90 4.20, max
    5.05 of 17.39. On MAME's model of the part the TGP has 3.4x headroom in
    every frame of the race. MAME's own game rate over the same scripted
    race (sim/tgp/mame_flips_2a.lua, new: the 0x803008 frame-start writes,
    R637's flips.lua, counted per vblank): 2,419 flips in 2,420 vblanks --
    57.5 fps, one 2-vblank frame in 42 s.
  * No report was found of the arcade game slowing down (a web search; not
    proof either way).

*Ours, measured.* The Rally capture regenerated (make tgp_capture_2a
CAP2A_SET=srallyc CAP2A_GAME=rally: frames 1300-3720, the same 4,240,743 words
in / 706,456 out as R876 -- the session is deterministic). tb_tgp_replay
TGP_PROG=4096 --board-push --gap 40 --jitter 40 (lat 6: a table, ROM or
buffer-RAM access answered in 6..46 clk_sys), model2a 8751702's RTL: PASS,
bit-exact; 887.5 M cycles, 98.26 M instructions, CPI 9.03; TGP busy (all but
the empty-input wait) 11.02 s at 80 MHz = 1.54x MAME's model; a vblank's work
p50 4.99 ms, p90 6.32, max 7.49. Where it went:
  * pc 0x15b, `mov (data) -> io` under a rep, buffer-RAM stores ~12 words a
    call, 4,047,804 of them (1,672 a vblank): 60 cycles each, 243 M = 27.4%
    of the TGP's time. Each 32-bit store is two 16-bit transactions on the
    shared write port, and the TGP waited for both (R133's design). MAME: one
    instruction cycle.
  * io waits 290 M: buffer-RAM writes 238.0 M, data ROM 23.8 M (950 k
    reads), tables 17.3 M (694 k), buffer-RAM reads 11.3 M (452 k).
  * S_ALU 156.7 M (17.7%): an FP op waited its five pipeline stages after
    the transfer's states, never under them; S_DECODE 11.1% (one a retire).
  * The SDRAM latency the bench's lat/jitter stands for (tb_m2_sdram_load,
    the 2A class, ports 8 / 9): idle p50 15 clk_mem; at 49% bus load p50 18,
    p90 38; at 78-80% p50 44-81, p90 78-184. With the request / acknowledge
    registers and the CDC that is ~19 clk_sys idle and ~25-40 typical -- R876's
    6 + 0..40 (mean 26) sits inside it.
Zero Gunner (gap 60, jitter 40): 1.10x MAME's model; Daytona's race (lat 6,
infinitely fast i960): 0.93x -- neither stores much buffer RAM. VF2's attract
(gap 60, jitter 40): 1.49x -- it does (below).

*FIX 1 -- POSTED BUFFER-RAM WRITES (m2_tgp BUFW_Q; Model2.sv: 32 with M2A, 0
otherwise).* A buffer-RAM store is queued (m2_fifo_m10k, 32 x 47 in MLAB, 33
deep with its head) and acknowledged a cycle later; the queue drains through
bufw_* with exactly the old handshake (request, acknowledge, drop, re-raise --
halves and entries never closer than one idle cycle) and in order, so every
reader sees the TGP's stores in the order it made them. What waits on it
(`wq_busy`: a word in the array, the read in flight, the head, or a request
out): the TGP's own buffer-RAM reads (they go out on port 9 and could
overtake) that fall inside the span of addresses queued since the queue was
last empty -- every queued address is inside [wq_lo, wq_hi], so a read outside
cannot alias one (waiting for the whole queue instead cost 163 M cycles in the
slow-memory run below); and the i960's read of a result word (m2_copro holds
the read, `stall`, until the queue is empty) -- the i960 learns that a command is
done from the output FIFO, so everything the TGP stored before that has
landed when the read completes. Data-ROM reads do not wait (nothing writes
the ROM); a read's `dat_half` is now 0 always (wr_hi can be 1 while a ROM
read goes out). A TGP reset (halt, upload) drops an unwritten word; the queue
drains in well under a microsecond and the i960 halts the TGP only around an
upload.

*FIX 2 -- THE ALU UNDER THE TRANSFER (mb86233_core EARLY_ALU; Model2.sv: 1
with M2A).* alu_pre's operands are the S_DECODE snapshot (pre_a/b/d/p) and
alu_op_r, both fixed on the edge into S_SRC, so a lab / ld-mov's op starts in
S_SRC's first cycle and runs its five stages under the source and destination
accesses. Its result is still written only after the transfer (alu_post_ok:
S_ALU, MAME's alu_pre / transfer / alu_post order); a result that lands
before the FSM gets there (the transfer waited on io or the input FIFO) is
dropped unwritten and S_ALU launches the op again from the same snapshot -- the
old timing, never worse. A lab whose op is still in flight when its B read
completes writes A and B first and takes the result in S_LAB_WA / S_LAB_WB
(the op reads the snapshot, never A or B, and writes only D, P, ST). Not
launched early: fdvd (the divider's busy handshake), and a ld/mov whose
transfer writes D (the write-priority rule takes the transfer's value at
launch) or SFT (the shifts read SFT live; launching after the transfer is
the old behaviour and is kept). Model 1's core (reference 0b5d04f) has the
same snapshot and no early launch.

*Measured, the same Rally run (board-like, as above), every result stream
IDENTICAL to 8751702's (15,678,320 words) and bit-exact against MAME:*

                         cycles     CPI   TGP busy  x MAME   vblank p50 / max   i960 held (full FIFO)
  8751702                887.5 M   9.03   11.02 s   1.54     4.99 / 7.49 ms     469.8 M
  + EARLY_ALU only       792.5 M   8.07    9.82 s   1.37     4.47 / 6.63        --
  + posted writes only   659.4 M   6.71    8.14 s   1.13     3.55 / 5.73        --
  both (the 2A build)    564.6 M   5.75    6.94 s   0.97     3.03 / 4.87        232.6 M

pc 0x15b: 60 -> 7 cycles a store; buffer-RAM write wait 238.0 M -> 4.4 M; the
buffer-RAM reads that now wait for the queue 11.3 M -> 14.6 M; S_ALU 156.7 M
-> 60.7 M. The bench's i960 is held on the full input FIFO half as long.
(The final RTL, with the read span: 562.7 M cycles, 0.96x, vblank p50 3.02 /
max 4.83 ms.) With slower memory (--lat 24 --wlat 24 --jitter 60, seed 7:
24..84 clk_sys an access): 8751702 1,193.1 M cycles, 2.07x MAME, vblank max
9.92 ms; the 2A build 732.1 M, 1.24x, max 6.16 ms, IDENTICAL. There the
queue fills (33 pending at most) and the stores' wait is 103 M: the drain,
not the TGP, sets the pace of the copy loop.
Zero Gunner's play window (gap 60, jitter 40): 410.2 M -> 359.0 M cycles,
1.10x -> 0.93x MAME, IDENTICAL (it stores no buffer RAM; all EARLY_ALU).
Daytona's race on the 2A TGP: 9.73 M -> 8.81 M (lat 6), IDENTICAL. VF2 (a new
capture, attract frames 1500-1800: 814,468 words in, 272,424 out, 782,648 io
writes -- VF2 stores buffer RAM heavily too): with the board-like i960 (gap

7.64 -> 5.32 ms; with the plain feed (lat 6) 138.6 M -> 110.1 M, 1.14x ->
0.88x; IDENTICAL both ways. R855's "the TGP hold is now the largest single

The original core (both parameters 0): Daytona's race cycle-for-cycle as
before (9,726,730 cycles; 12,287,990 board-like) -- main's games unchanged.

*Area (quartus_map 17.0 of m2_copro alone at the 2A parameters):* 2,992 ALM
estimated -> 2,999 with EARLY_ALU (+3 registers) -> 3,045 with the queue and
its span (+146 registers: the head, the read register, the span; the 32 x 47

*Levers measured and NOT taken:*

*THE STORE ORDER, CHECKED.* The replay serves a buffer-RAM read from MAME's

tracks every store from its acknowledge to its high half's bufw acknowledge

**R891 -- THE MiSTer 128 MB MODULE IS TWO 64 MB CHIPS ON ONE CHIP-SELECT LINE,
WITH EACH CHIP'S BYTE MASK ON A11/A12. m2_sdram DRIVES IT (DUAL, MASK_ON_A); THE
2A BUILD ADDRESSES 128 MB. R19'S ALIASING AND R82 / R871'S LOST BYTE ENABLES ARE
THE SAME WIRING, REPRODUCED ON THE BENCH. A POWER-UP TEST FOR THE BOARD
(M2_MEMTEST). NOT FITTED, NOT ON A BOARD.**
(Ben, through the coordinator: Ben's board has a MiSTer 128 MB module, two
64 MB chips; extend m2_sdram for it behind a parameter, keep 64 MB working
for the released games, model the module in the bench, wire the 2A build,
and a board memory test. Limits: one Verilator build at a time, quartus_map
only, no fit, no board, no run over ~15 min.)

*Believed (R18, R19, R82, R871, R887):* a 128 MB module on the connector's 13
address and 2 bank pins must be one chip of 4 x 8192 x 2048 (R18), and R19
measured that eleventh column bit aliasing -- "64 MB is what this controller
can address" (R19), "whether a dual-chip 128 MB module can be addressed at all
is a board question" (R887). Separately, the board drops byte enables (R82:
a byte store lands in all four lanes; R871: the 2A sound board's 68000 bytes
smeared), so every byte write is read-modify-write (R729, R871) and source
and silicon were said to "disagree".

*Now known (from the reference; INFERRED for this board until the test below
runs):* MiSTer-devel/PSX_MiSTer rtl/sdram.sv, a working core written for
these modules (GPL-3.0-or-later; read, not copied):
  * `assign SDRAM_nCS = chip;` with `chip <= addr[26]` -- byte address bit 26,
    the 64 MB boundary. The module inverts the one chip-select line onto the
    second chip, so nCS low selects the lower 64 MB and high the upper.
  * `assign {SDRAM_DQMH,SDRAM_DQML} = SDRAM_A[12:11];` and the CAS word
    `{cas_addr[12:9],SDRAM_BA,SDRAM_A,cas_addr[8:0]} <= {~be[1:0], rnw,
    addr[25:1]}`: each chip's DQM is wired to A11/A12, so the byte mask
    travels on A[12:11] in the column phase (columns are A0-A9, A10 is
    auto-precharge).
  * Start-up runs precharge-all / two refreshes / MRS to chip 0, then to
    chip 1; each refresh interval issues AUTO REFRESH to chip 0, then chip 1.
So R19's eleventh column bit drove a column bit on A11 -- the chips' DQM --
which is why it aliased; and R82 / R871's lost masks are this controller
putting the mask on the connector's DQM pins, which this module does not use
as masks. Both are the bench's findings now (mutations r19_col11, mask_off
below); the board test is what settles them.

*BUILT:*
  * rtl/mem/m2_sdram.sv, DUAL (default 0): a word-address bit above the 64 MB
    decode (AW + 1, at the TOP, so the lower 64 MB decode exactly as the one
    chip did) drives sd_cs_n per transaction (a register, cs_sel, set in
    S_DISPATCH before a transaction's first command); row state for eight
    banks ({chip, bank}: bank_open, bank_row, ras_cnt, rd_bank_cnt, ras_ok,
    rd_ok); the bring-up's precharge-all, eight refreshes and MRS each go to
    chip 0 and a cycle later to chip 1 (per chip the spacing is unchanged);
    each refresh is precharge-all chip 0, chip 1 (S_PRE1), tRP, REFRESH chip
    0, chip 1 (S_REF1), tRC -- one row of each chip per T_REFI. MASK_ON_A
    (default 0): a WRITE carries ~be on A[12:11] (COL_BITS <= 10 checked at
    elaboration), a READ 00. A NOP needs no chip select (it is a NOP or a
    deselect to both chips), so cs_sel has no reset and packs in the pin.
  * Model2.sv, the 2A build: SDR_AW 26 (SDR_DUAL = M2A), DUAL and MASK_ON_A
    on, the DQM pins = SDRAM_A[12:11] (PSX's assign; m2_sdram's own sd_dqm
    differs from A[12:11] only at ACTIVATE, where DQM does nothing at CL 2 --
    a DQM masks read data two edges later, which is the READ's own data only
    when the READ itself carries it). Every GAME_* constant keeps its value
    (no released layout moves; the loader's ioctl_addr[26:1] already covers
    128 MB). T_REFI 770 on 2A (below). The original core (M2_NO_2A): SDR_AW
    25, DUAL / MASK_ON_A off, its DQM pins from sd_dqm, T_REFI 781 -- the
    logic as it was.
  * A 64 MB MODULE STILL WORKS (bench, below): the controller's chip-1
    commands are deselects to a single chip, every released game is below
    64 MB, and a module whose chip takes DQM from the DQM pins sees the same
    mask there.
  * sim/mem/sdram_model.sv: DQM_FROM_A (the chip's mask from A[12:11]),
    RD_DQM (DQM masks read data two edges later; a masked read byte is a
    violation), CHECK_RET (RETENTION: a row with data not restored by
    ACTIVATE / PRECHARGE or by the REFRESH its own row counter reaches,
    within T_RET = 64 ms at 100 MHz, loses its data -- V_DECAY, code 14),
    CHECK_INIT (no access unless the LAST MRS had a precharge-all, two
    refreshes and a BL1 / sequential / CL word -- V_INIT, code 15; the last
    one, because the controller's cmd reads 0000, an MRS, before its
    synchronous reset lands). All default off: every earlier harness checks
    what it did. New module sdram_module: CHIPS (2: the 128 MB module, chip
    1 on ~cs_n; 1: the 64 MB module), each chip a full sdram_model, DQ shared,
    two chips driving DQ a fight.
  * m2_sdram_harness: DUAL, MASK_ON_A, MODULE (1: sdram_module), CHIPS,
    T_REFI_C; the module's chips are 10 column bits whatever the controller
    says, so a controller that misdrives the chip select or the column
    aliases here as on the board. tb_m2_sdram.cpp: TB_DUAL / TB_LOWER, pick_addr
    over {chip, bank}, a chip phase (the same word address in both halves,
    write port and port 0 byte writes, every row/column bit walked, then
    read back) and a retention phase (TB_RET idle cycles, then rows in every
    bank of both chips read back).
  * rtl/mem/m2_memtest.sv (M2_MEMTEST=1 with M2_PROBE=1): the board test,
    below.

*BENCH (Verilator 5.052):*
  * The existing suites, default parameters, OUTPUT IDENTICAL LINE FOR LINE
    to daca25b (results, latencies, throughput, telemetry): test_m2_sdram
    (2,111,407 checks), test_m2_sdram13 (five configurations), test_m2_sdram128
    (1,626,207), test_m2_sdram_cdc (93,651), test_m2_sdram_cdc_load (four
    runs). test_m2_rom_xtra2a at SDR_AW 26 (Model2.sv's value now) PASS.
  * make test_m2_sdram128d (13 ports, the 2A class, T_REFI 770, the module
    with every check on, TB_RET 14,000,000 idle cycles = 2.2 x T_RET):
      128 MB module             1,896,367 checks, 0 fails, 0 violations;
                                chip phase 8,192 / 0; retention 512 rows in
                                all 8 banks, 2,048 / 0, 0 rows decayed
      + 8-word texel reads,     2,119,444 checks, 0 / 0
        ports 5 / 7 byte writes
      64 MB module, < 64 MB     2,108,258 checks, 0 / 0; retention 256 rows,

    DUAL's own cost, against the same harness at DUAL 0 (10 columns): the

  * MUTATIONS, each caught (the 2A dual configuration, ports 5 / 7 writing):
      no_ref1   chip 1 never refreshed     chip-1 V_REFRESH; retention 1,024
                                           fails, 256 rows decayed
      no_pre1   no chip-1 precharge-all    V_REF_OPEN (108,929)

      cs_stuck  chip select not driven     13,982 data fails
      mask_off  MASK_ON_A 0 (the mask on   518 byte-write fails, ZERO
                the DQM pins only)         violations -- R82 / R871's board
                                           signature, now in simulation

                                           decayed -- see below
      r19_col11 COL_BITS 11, no DUAL (R18) 998,679 fails, and READ DATA MASKED
                                           (839,824 violations): A11 is a
                                           column bit at the READ, so the
                                           chips' DQM drop its data -- R19's
                                           aliasing, reproduced
  * m2_memtest (make test_m2_memtest; one clock, port 1 of m2_sdram, the
    module): the 2A controller -- four passes, the last three after 8 M, 16 M
    and 32 M idle cycles (each > T_RET), all 0 errors, the loader released
    172,800 cycles after ready; MASK_ON_A 0 -- 2,048 MASK errors, 128 in every
    region, 0 data; a 64 MB controller on the module -- 368 data errors, 46
    in each of regions 0-7 (the 46 fixed samples; the random ones differ per
    region), each reading its region+8 twin's data, which the decoder names;
    no_ref1 -- pass 1 clean, passes 2-4 2,048 data errors, all 256 in each of

*A FINDING: T_REFI 781 IS PAST THE PART'S 64 ms.* ref_cnt runs 0..T_REFI, so a
refresh comes every T_REFI + 1 cycles; 782 x 8,192 rows = 6,406,144 cycles,
64.06 ms at 100 MHz. sdram_module's retention check flags every row
(refi781). The 2A build takes 770 (771 x 8,192 = 63.2 ms). The original core
keeps 781 -- harmless in practice at room temperature, out of specification
all the same -- Ben's decision for main. ALSO FOR MAIN (not changed): its byte
mask is on the DQM pins only; on this module those masks are lost (main's
bridge does RMW since R729, so the i960 is safe; any other byte writer is not).

*THE BOARD TEST (M2_MEMTEST, rtl/mem/m2_memtest.sv).* At power-up, before any
download, on port 1 (the i960's, in reset until a game is loaded): sixteen
regions of 8 MB ({chip, bank, row MSB}), 256 samples each -- offset 0, all
ones, every offset bit set alone and clear alone (row and column, high and
low), then 210 LFSR offsets -- 4,096 words, all WRITTEN BEFORE ANY IS READ,
each word's data naming its sample ({~s[3:0], s}); one in four has its low
byte, one in four its high byte, rewritten with a masked write. Read back at
once (pass 1, CL+2 as the game uses), then -- while nothing is downloaded --
re-read after ~0.84 s, ~3.4 s and ~13.4 s idle (80 MHz clk_sys; only the
refresh touches the memory then) and every ~13.4 s after. The loader waits
for pass 1 (1.7 ms on the bench's single 100 MHz clock; a few ms through the
crossing); a download parks the test. Results: probe records 'B'
(a region: data errors, mask errors, the first bad sample and word) and 'b'
(passes; hps_io's sdram_sz; totals), in every probe slot until a game is
loaded, then one slot in sixteen.
  HOW TO RUN: Model2.qsf already sets VERILOG_MACRO "M2_NO_DEBUG=1"; add
  "M2_PROBE=1" and "M2_MEMTEST=1" (and "M2_NO_2A_RALLY=1" if the probe
  build needs the room, as s1205 did). Copy the .rbf to
  /media/fat/_Arcade/cores/ under a name of its own, and load the CORE
  ALONE, not an MRA: `echo "load_core /media/fat/_Arcade/cores/<rbf>" >
  /dev/MiSTer_cmd` (a download parks the test after pass 1 -- an MRA load
  gives pass 1 only). The records repeat until a game is loaded, so the
  capture may start after the load: `python3 /tmp/uartcap.py 60 /tmp/uart.txt`
  (tools/uart_capture.py, as board-capture.sh copies it) covers passes 1-5;
  then `tools/decode_why.py <capture>`.
  WHAT EACH RESULT MEANS:
    * every pass 0 / 0: the module is addressed as two chips, every row and
      column line works on both, the masks reach the chips, and both are
      refreshed. The 2A build can use 128 MB.
    * mask errors in every region, no data errors: the mask is not reaching
      the chips on A12:A11 (or is not this module's wiring) -- R82 again.
    * data errors in regions 0-7 only, each first bad word reading as a
      sample of region r+8: the upper chip is not being selected (chip
      select inversion absent: a single 64 MB chip, or the module wired
      otherwise); the decoder names the twin byte address.
    * errors in one half only on passes 2-4, pass 1 clean: that chip is not
      refreshed (its refresh, or its precharge before it, does not reach it).
    * a few errors in every region, the words reading as walking samples
      (k 2-23: offset bit k-2 set alone; k 24-45: bit k-24 clear alone): an
      address line (a row or column bit) stuck or shorted -- the sample a
      word reads as names the bit.
    * sdram_sz in the 'b' record: what MiSTer believes (8003 = 128 MB set);
      information only -- nothing in the core uses it.

**R889 -- VIRTUA COP 2'S AMMO DISPLAY: NOT A TEXTURE. THE REVOLVER IS A LATER
WINDOW THAN THE STREET AND THIS CORE SORTED BY z ALONE, SO THE STREET HID
IT. FIXED ON THE 2A BUILD: THE WINDOW IS THE TOP OF THE SORT KEY (WINKEY).
MAIN UNCHANGED.**
(Ben, s1220: "there are no bullet textures, so you can't see how many
bullets you have.")

*Believed:* run-time texture RAM writes (the i960 redrawing the bullets per
shot) not reaching what the renderer samples, or a texture path R867's
tables do not cover. And R641 (Daytona attract): "ONE window a frame,
always: window ORDER is not a cause" -- true there, never re-checked for
another game.

*Measured (MAME 0.289 vcop2, sim/io/mame_m2_vcop2_play.lua with a write tap
on 0x12000000-0x1281ffff, M2GEO walks at 51.5-54.5 / 58 / 63 / 64.2 s,
M2DIFF lists 2300 and 2910):*
  1. THE AMMO DISPLAY IS A 3D REVOLVER CYLINDER, bottom left: 12 or 13
     polygons from the POLYGON ROM, one object per bullet count (oba
     0x805af4 six, 0x805d59, 0x80594e ..., 0x805bc7 empty; tha moves with
     it), drawn after the list's fourth window_data, focal 1200, rotated per
     shot. Sides h0 0x4009 (64x64, opaque), front face 0x6009 (translucent,
     the empty chambers), and ONE more translucent quad for the loaded
     rounds (h 6009,7001,1900,3f40: luma row 1, sheet bit set, texture
     (0,128)). No direct_data, no texture_data, no 2D layer: nothing the
     i960 writes per shot except the display list itself. Texture RAM writes
     happen only at scene loads (the tap: none between shots).
  2. MAME DRAWS WINDOW BY WINDOW. render_polygons runs `for (window =
     cur_window; window >= 0; window--)`, z buckets inside each, with the
     fill map (first write wins): a later window is in FRONT of an earlier
     one whatever their z. Virtua Cop 2's lists: window 1 the street (z
     buckets 18,151-46,166), window 2 the crosshair ring (~20,155), window 4
     the revolver (45,635). By z alone the revolver is behind almost the
     whole street and the ring behind its near walls.
  3. THIS CORE'S KEY WAS z ALONE (m2_geometry.sv:1012 `.in_z({16'd0,
     hzkey})`, m2_quad_store.sv:521 key = in_z[15:0]); m2_geo counted
     windows (win_cnt, R642) but never per walk and nothing read it.
     tb_m2_raster3d on MAME's list 2910 (six rounds), core configuration
     (TEXLUT, LW8, PXK 0, MIPZ 3): the revolver is not drawn at all (the
     bullets' quad: 989 px, mean error 140.9 / 255; the face 33-40) and the
     ring's left half is missing. With only windows 2 and 4 in the list both
     draw: the polygons were hidden, not lost.
  4. AND A KEY OF 20 BITS NEEDS AN EVEN PASS COUNT. The radix sort moves the
     order between idx_a* and idx_b each pass and the replay reads idx_a*;
     at five passes (RADIX 4) the fifth pass's result was left in idx_b and
     the bench drew exactly what it drew at 16 bits.

*The fix (2A only, Model2.sv R3D_WINKEY = M2A):* m2_geo counts window_data
per walk (render_frame_start's cur_window = 0, saturating at 15) and
latches it with each object (obj_win; the walk already waits for the
geometry to drain before the next object). m2_geometry WINKEY puts
{15 - window, z} in q_z[19:0]; m2_raster3d KW 20 sorts on it (front to back:
the last window first, then z, ties LIFO as before). m2_quad_store: with an
odd pass count (ODDP) R_INIT writes the start order into idx_b and the first
pass runs b -> a, so the fifth lands in the bank. KW 16 builds exactly as
before (ODDP 0).

*Before / after (tb_m2_raster3d, the 2A raster configuration, MAME's lists;
mean max-channel error / 255 over every painted pixel):*

    VCop2 2300 (four rounds, the water)     5.10    4.21   4,356 (3,174 / 1,142)
    VF2 attract 400 (windows 1, 5, 6, 7)    7.36    7.37   121 (61 / 58)
    VF2 attract 2620                        4.20    4.20   2
    Sega Rally attract 1500 (one window)    7.17    7.17   0

**R894 -- "WAY TOO QUIET, SPEAKERS AT 150% AND STILL BARELY HEAR IT" (Ben,
2A board): TWO OSD SETTINGS, NOT A CHANGE TO THE MIX. VOLUME GOES TO 150 /
200 / 300 / 400% (CLAMPED, NEVER WRAPPED); "DIRECT BOOST" OFF / +6 / +12 dB
MULTIPLIES THE SCSP's DIRECT SENDS BEFORE THE DSP's RETURN JOINS THEM. BOTH
DEFAULTS ARE R886's MIX: VOLUME 80%, BOOST OFF = MAME's RAW SCSP OUTPUT.**
(Ben, through the coordinator. The first ask was a +12 dB boost by default;
then a per-game default with a VF2 trim so its music would not move; then,
superseding both, "we already have a volume option, why not allow it to go
up to 150 or 200": Volume past 100%, and Direct boost as a plain switch,
default Off.)

*Believed:* the core is quiet against MAME as players hear it. R886 showed
our mix is MAME 0.289's raw SCSP output to 0.1 dB; the capture's own
cfg/default.cfg lists a Filters / Compressor / Reverb / Equalizer chain that
MAME 0.289 runs after the mix. How much that chain lifts the level was not
measured here. Nothing in this entry says MAME's SCSP is wrong -- R886's
open question (a real board's recording) still stands.

*Built:*
  1. DIRECT BOOST (m2_scsp, sim/sound/scsp_uasm.py). The direct sends and
     the effect return ARE separable cheaply: the slots add their direct
     sends into SMPL / SMPR, then the effect-return loop (EFF) adds EFREG
     x EFSDL / EFPAN into the same registers. Four microinstructions after
     DSPGO / ICLR -- while the DSP runs, before the WAIT for it -- multiply
     SMPL / SMPR by MB_BST = 64 << boost on the existing 27 x 18 multiplier
     and take P[37:6] (PSL S6), so Off is SMPL x 64 >> 6 = SMPL exactly.
     The direct sum is bounded well inside the 27-bit multiplier operand
     (32 slots x 2^20 < 2^26) and x4 inside 32 bits; the DAC's existing
     clamp (18 bits, then >> 2) is the saturation. Microcode 119 -> 123 of
     256 words (no new ROM). MB's spare encoding 7 was free.
  2. VOLUME (rtl/sound/m2_volume.sv, 2A build only). R829's table, codes
     0-10 unchanged, plus 150 / 200 / 300 / 400% in the unused codes 11-14
     (15 = the default, 80%), so saved settings keep their meaning; gain to
     11 bits, a 16 x 12 multiply, the product's [23:8] clamped to
     [-32768, 32767]. The original core keeps R829's inline stage byte for
     byte (M2_NO_2A: the old CONF_STR line, the old stage, snd_boost tied 0).
  3. OSD (2A build): "Volume" gains the four entries after 70%; "Direct
     boost,Off,+6 dB,+12 dB" at O[65:64] -- status bits never used before
     (64-120 are free), so any saved config opens with it Off. Not under a
     menu mask: it applies to every game. Three flops into clk_sys, like
     the volume, to m2_2a_sound's new snd_boost port.

*Benches (all at the model2a tip + this change):*
  - tb_m2_scsp, new SCSP_BOOST: Off -- VF2 30 s 0 samples differ from the
    reference AND from MAME's mix, 9,421,266 slot samples 0 wrong; Sega
    Rally 30 s the same (0 / 0). Boosted, the reference becomes its direct
    sends x 2^boost plus its effect return: VF2 30 s x4, Rally 30 s x4,
    Zero Gunner 10 s x2 -- 0 differ from that, and 715,359 / 555,911 /
    234,912 of the non-zero samples differ from MAME's mix (the gain, and
    only the gain).
  - Engine time unchanged: the four instructions hide under the DSP's run.
    Zero Gunner 10 s mean 1,095 / max 2,252 clocks a sample, Rally 30 s
    262 / 767, identical to the model2a tip built and run the same way.
  - tb_m2_volume (make test_m2_volume, iverilog): every 16-bit input at
    all 16 codes, both channels -- equal to floor(x g / 256) clamped,
    never of the wrong sign, codes 0-10 equal to R829's 9-bit stage;
    147,456 of 1,048,576 clamp, 0 wrong. The same bench against the stage
    with the clamp removed: 404,132 wrong (it sees a wrap).
  - tb_m2_2a_sound VF2 6 s, boost Off (new SND_BOOST, default 0): PASS,
    98.9% of writes in MAME's order, 0 underruns, the RAM check 0 wrong,
    82.68 ms -- as R885 / R886.
  - lint_top: 2A, M2_NO_2A, M2_NO_DEBUG, M2_PROBE=1, M2_NO_2A_RALLY, and
    M2_NO_DEBUG + M2_PROBE=1 + M2_NO_2A_RALLY together: clean. lint_idx:
    no candidate in a changed line. quartus_map --analyze_file on
    m2_volume, m2_scsp, m2_2a_sound, Model2.sv: 0 errors (one "constant
    value overflow" warning, -16'sd32768, fixed to 16'sh8000).

*Area (quartus_map 17.0 of each unit alone, virtual pins; the whole design
was not mapped -- three fits were running on the machine):*
    m2_scsp (scsp_area_top, boost a live input)  1,965 -> 1,975 ALMs
                                                  (+8 ALUT, +1 register)
    the volume stage (R829 inline -> m2_volume)     44 ->    55 ALMs
                                                  (+32 ALUT; DSP blocks 2 -> 2)
    hps_io with the 2A CONF_STR (737 -> 796 bytes)  656 ->   666 ALMs
    boost synchroniser                             6 registers
  about +35 ALMs in all; block RAM bits and DSP blocks unchanged.

*Levels (MAME's own captures through scsp_ref.h / scsp_split, left
channel, in play: VF2 20-80 s, Rally and Zero Gunner 20-120 s; the DAC's
16-bit output, then the Volume stage):*
                  boost   RMS     peak     peak hits full scale at
  VF2             Off     2,681   25,353   129% (p99.9 at 285%)
                  +6 dB   3,402   30,993   106%
                  +12 dB  5,014   32,768   100% (the DAC clamps 0.001%)
  Sega Rally      Off       362    2,712   1,208%
                  +6 dB     724    5,425   604%

  What the boost does to VF2: +12 dB raises its effects +12.0 dB, its

**R892 -- MANX TT'S "ACTIVE MOTION SLIDER" SCREEN WAITS FOR THE DX CABINET'S
DRIVE BOARD ON THE 315-5649'S PORT D. THE CORE NOW ANSWERS AS A WORKING
BASE (0xCE / 0xCD FROM PORT E, GAME ID 0x19, M2_2A_MANX_MOTION): THE GAME
BOOTS TO ITS ATTRACT WITH NO KEY. ~3 ALM. PROVED IN MAME 0.289. NOT FITTED,
NOT ON A BOARD.**
(Ben, s1221: Manx TT stops at "DANGER! ACTIVE MOTION SLIDER NOW CHECKING
SYSTEM ... DO NOT TOUCH SLIDE BODY"; Test, Test gets past it but is "a faff
for users" -- "what is it waiting on?")

*Believed (R887, and MAME's TODO):* "no escape from the active motion slider
tutorial (needs analog inputs)"; every boot stops there, Test opens the test
menu, Test again and the game runs. WRONG ABOUT THE CAUSE: no analog channel
is involved. The game waits for a status byte from the cabinet's drive board.

*Found (MAME 0.289: read / write taps on 0x01c00000-0x01c0003f, the UART and
the comm board, with the IP; a debugger trace of a frame at 20 s; MAME's
disassembly of the program, which runs from ROM -- no RAM copy):*
  1. THE PORTS. Every frame the input routine (program 0x2308, the 2A path;
     0x21f8 is the 315-5296 one) sets the direction to 0x4e (B, C, D, G in),
     reads B, C (IN0, IN1), READS PORT D (0x01c00006) INTO RAM 0x514035 and
     WRITES RAM 0x514034 TO PORT E (0x01c00008); port F the lamps. MAME's
     manxtt binds port D to IN2 (all unused: 0xFF) and port E to the
     billboard. Nothing else is touched while the screen is up: no UART read,
     no comm-board access, no other serial channel; the eight analog
     channels are read but nothing waits on them.
  2. THE CHECK, main state 0 (0x5bba08 = 0, the handler at 0x5f530 from the
     table at 0x15c0), its sub-state in 0x5bba0c:
       first: if CABINET TYPE (0x51405a) is 1 (TWIN) -> main state 1, no check;
              if (status & 0xF0) == 0xB0 -> sub-state 3 (an error)
       0  0x5bba00 = 0x34e, -> 1 (port E holds 0x3D since boot, 0x5f878:
          0xFF - 0xC2; the commands are sent inverted)
       1  status == 0xCE: send the bike's centre, 0xFF - EEPROM 0x51406f
          (factory 0x80, so 0x7F), 0x5bba00 = 0x234, -> 2. Otherwise
          0x5bba00 -= 1 and -> 3 at 0 -- BUT 0x5bba00 IS ALSO A FRAME COUNTER
          (+1 a frame elsewhere: 564 -> 1131 over a warning screen), so in 1
          it never moves (845 / 846 for 17 s in run E2): the screen waits
          FOREVER, it never times out to an error
       2  status == 0xCD: -> main state 1 (the warning screen, then the
          attract, main state 3); otherwise the same never-expiring wait
       3  "Push TEST BUTTON to EXIT / But Motor Error" and, by the status,
          one of the strings above the handler (0xB0 Test Setting, 0xB1
          Motor Encoder, 0xB2 Motor OverCurrent, 0xB3 OverHeat/OverLoad, 0xB4
          Bank Volume, 0xB5 DriveBoard ROM, 0xB6 DriveBoard RAM, 0xB7
          Centering, else Not Respond); Test (0x514014 bit 2 / 4) leaves to
          main state 1
     With MAME's 0xFF the game sits in sub-state 1. Test sends it through
     the test menu (main state 12) and out to main state 1 -- the workaround.
  3. NOTHING ELSE READS THE STATUS in a race or the attract: 0x514035's only
     readers are this handler and the test menu's DriveBoard Test (0x71f24..,
     a network check: commands E0-EF expecting ~(1 << n), D2 / D3 expecting
     0xFF, then the status shown as the board's DIP switches). The game does
     send motion commands on port E all through the attract and the race
     (0x3d, 0x3f, 0xee, 0xab, 0xdf ...: R892's st.txt logs).
  4. WHAT A WORKING BASE RETURNS: no drive-board ROM for this cabinet is
     dumped (epr-18022 in the zip is the billboard's), so MAME has no model.
     From the game's own code: 0xCE in answer to the boot command, 0xCD once
     the centre is sent. INFERRED, the least that satisfies the code: status
     = 0xCE while port E holds 0x3D, else 0xCD.
  5. THE SETTING (option b): GAME ASSIGNMENTS' CABINET TYPE is 0x51405a
     (EEPROM word 5's high byte; the menu's order and 0x70fc4's copies:
     ADVERTISE SOUND 0x514058, COUNTRY 0x514059, CABINET TYPE 0x51405a
     DELUXE / TWIN, LINK TYPE 0x51405b, BIKE COLOR 0x51405c ...). The
     factory default (0x2ec0) is 0 = DELUXE, as is MAME's manxtt_dx_nvran.
     A blank 93C46 fails the game's test (word 1 must be 0x0038 and word 0
     the CRC of the next 54 bytes: the test at 0x3230) and the game writes its factory
     settings (0x2ff0) -- so the core boots DELUXE every time. TWIN skips the
     check but makes it the other cabinet (the game's Twin mode), and the
     core can neither preload an EEPROM nor keep one across a power cycle
     (R887: ~20 ALM for a load port). Not taken.
  6. MOTOR RAID: motoraid (Twin, 0x1A, R887's set) has no drive-board code
     (no DRIVEBOARD / slider strings; R887's 240 s sessions boot and race
     with no key) -- nothing to fix. motoraiddx (no game ID; 68 MB, does not
     load) has its own check (program 0xc54a8.., "NOW CABINET CHECKING",
     "DRIVEBOARD INITIALIZE OK", eight error strings) on the same ports with
     a different protocol, not analysed; R892's answer is gated on 0x19 and
     does not cover it.

*THE FIX (option a):* m2_315_5649 brings PE's latch out (pe); m2_2a_inputs
(MOTION, Model2.sv M2_2A_MANX_MOTION, on by default, M2_NO_2A_MANX_MOTION
leaves it out) answers IN2 for game ID 0x19 only: 0xCE while pe == 0x3D,
else 0xCD. Every other ID's IN2 is unchanged (the bench below). Before the
game writes port E (power-on 0xFF) the answer is 0xCD, which sub-state 1
ignores. A centre setting of 0xC2 (0xFF - 0x3D) would leave the answer at
0xCE and the check waiting as today -- Test still works.

*PROOF (MAME 0.289, sim/io/mame_m2_manx_motion.lua, sim/io/manx_motion_cmp.py;
EEPROM blank -- 128 bytes of 0xFF, as the core starts -- unless said; Tg the
attract's first frame; coins at Tg+10 and Tg+130, two credits, throttle,
lean, brake and shifts scripted from Tg; 240 s; a hash a second, snapshots
every 2 s, RAM dumps at 5 / 60 / 120 / 200 / 240 s):*
  E1  answered from power-on, no coins: passes at 1.13 s (frame 64-66), the
      warning screen, the attract at 11.0 s and cycling to 150 s. No key.
  E3  as E1 with MAME's default EEPROM (manxtt_dx_nvran): the same states,
      3 frames earlier (no factory write at boot), to 150 s; DELUXE either way.
  E2  MAME as it is (0xFF), no coins: on the DANGER screen until Test at 18
      s and 22 s, then the same states as E1, 21.87 s later.
  A   answered from power-on, coins: attract, both credits raced.
  T   0xFF, Test at 18 s and 22 s (the workaround), coins: the same.

(main_data 32 MB IN PLACE OF THE TEXTURE AND POLYGON SLOTS, THOSE TWO
LINEAR IN THE UPPER 64 MB), A THIRD LOADER REMAP, THE ENGINE CARRYING
MAME'S 23-BIT TEXTURE WORD; movre AND sqrtrl UNDER F2A; SIX MRAs. NOTHING
FITTED, NOTHING ON A BOARD.**
(Ben, through the coordinator: make Sky Target, Pilot Kids, Dynamite Cop,
Hanguk Pro Yagu 98, Motor Raid and Dead or Alive load and run, one overflow
scheme, released layouts unmoved, as little logic as possible; MRAs in the
2A style; benches against MAME. Limits: one MAME, one Verilator build,
quartus_map only, no board. A partial attempt on branch
worktree-agent-a5df2de13cf248fc3 (uncommitted: the a2_big decode, the
engine's 23-bit word, the bench mappings) was read and its approach kept.)

*Believed (R887, R891):* the five large sets need their own layouts with the
loader's remaps above 64 MB; Sky Target fits 64 MB with a third polygon remap
and a 1 MB data mask; the 4 MB-chip texture sets need R671's packing changed
to {a[22] | a[21], a[20:0]}; pltkidsa / dynamcop a 16 MB texture slot.

*THE SCHEME (Model2.sv a2_big: game IDs 0x13 0x14 0x15 0x16 0x18 0x1A; every
other ID reads exactly what it read before).* Every one of the six uses the
same image, Sega Rally's whole 0x32C0000-byte layout (R862) with one change,
and two regions appended:
  MRA 0x0000000  program 512 KB
      0x0080000  main_data 32 MB -- MAME's whole 0x02000000 window, ROM_COPY
                 mirrors written out (Sky Target's 1 MB pair sixteen times,
                 Motor Raid's eight, DOA's 4 MB twice; Pilot Kids' 8 MB then
                 zeros). It runs over the 2A texture (8 MB) and polygon
                 (12 MB) slots, which these games never read, so THE BRIDGE
                 NEEDS NOTHING: 0x02000000-0x03FFFFFF is already base_data +
                 a[24:1] and 0x06000000 base_data + 16 MB + a[23:1] (MAME's
                 main_data + 0x1000000) -- the windows R887 measured
                 hpyagu98, motoraid and skytargt reading land on their data.
      0x2080000  4 MB zeros (MAME's region 32-36 MB, unreachable)
      0x2480000  tables, 68000 program, samples (XTRA), program 512 KB-2 MB
                 and copro data (XTRA2): Sega Rally's slots, every one present
      0x32C0000  texture-coordinate ROM, MAME's 16 MB region linear (an 8 MB
                 region -- DOA -- written twice, as MAME's mask mirrors it;
                 the 8 MB-loaded 16 MB regions with their fill, 0 or 0xFF)
      0x42C0000  polygons, MAME's region to its last chip (16-32 MB)
  m2_rom_loader's THIRD REMAP, XTRA3_FROM / XTRA3_TO (default off; the
  original core passes all-ones): bytes from 0x32C0000 go to word 0x2000000
  + (byte - 0x32C0000) / 2 -- the textures at SDRAM byte 0x4000000, the
  polygons at 0x5000000 (GAME_TEX_BIG, GAME_POLY_BIG). 0x32C0000 has 18 low
  zero bits, so the subtract is 9 bits and the add one. Released images end
  at or before 0x32C0000 and never reach it. (The partial attempt used no
  subtract -- {1, a[25:0]} -- which needs 13.25 MB of padding in every MRA
  to reach 0x4000000; the subtract saves that download for ~10 LUTs.)
  The engine port (Model2.sv eng_base / eng_mem_idx): for a2_big the texture
  ROM base GAME_TEX_BIG with MAME's dword index whole (22 bits, 16 MB), the
  polygon base GAME_POLY_BIG with 23 bits (32 MB); otherwise R671's packing
  and 22 polygon bits, as before. m2_geo_engine's th_w / tp_w carry MAME's
  23-bit word (was R671's packed 22): the packing moved to the top level, so
  one register file serves both mappings. The only behavioural difference
  for a released game is a run of header / u/v words carrying out of a[20]:
  it now reaches a[21], which the packing drops (MAME's region reads its gap
  there; the old packing read the second pair) -- no list does it (below:
  the released walks identical).
  WHY ONE LAYOUT AND NOT R887's TWO: Sky Target (54 MB) would fit 64 MB with
  a polygon remap and a data mask, but that is two more decodes for one game;
  on the large layout it costs nothing more. It needs the 128 MB module like
  the other five. R887's "Sky Target program 0.5 MB" was wrong: its two
  EPROMs are 512 KB each, interleaved -- 1 MB (the image's 512 KB-2 MB slot
  has 128 non-zero 4 KB pages of 384).
  R887's {a[22] | a[21], a[20:0]} packing is NOT needed: on the linear slot
  a[21] and a[22] are simply address bits, for the 8 MB and 16 MB sets alike.
