*THE TWO TRAPS (R887), BUILT UNDER F2A (live for game IDs 0x10-0x1F, as
tanr; no new switch):*
  * SQRTRL (Motor Raid): VC's form -- its decode now (vc_on || ta_on), and
    T_RLLO starts the square root for (VC || F2A).
  * MOVRE (Dead or Alive), MAME's exactly. MAME copies three uint32_t
    through pointers: dst[0] = src[0]; dst[1] = src[1]; dst[2] = src[2] &
    0xffff, a pointer being a register triple at (n & 0x1e) or m_fp[k] -- a
    double's two words and then THE NEXT fp REGISTER'S LOW WORD, and after
    fp3 m_SAT, the member that follows m_fp[4] in i960.h. DOA's own code
    (program 0x7704-0x771c, 0x7860-0x7878, 0x7894.., 0x7928..; 16 movre in
    all): movre fp_k -> r4 then stt r4 to the frame, and ldt then movre r4 ->
    fp_k, k = 0..3 ascending -- so each restore's spill into fp k+1 is
    overwritten by the next, fp3's goes to the SAT (DOA's SAT is 0, program
    word 0, so MAME stores back what it read). Built: the decode (is_rl,
    fpmisc's move -- raw, as movrl), the third word read on ra2 (movre has
    no src2) or from fpr[k+1][15:0] / sat_reg[15:0]; a destination over the
    source's third word (a triple two above, fp k+1 from fp k) takes src[0],
    as MAME's write-then-read order gives; an fp destination writes fp k and
    spills into fpr[k+1][31:0] or the SAT in T_FP; a register destination
    writes its third register in a new state T_TRIP after T_PAIR. The
    silicon's fp registers are 80-bit and would spill nowhere; this core's
    are 64-bit doubles as MAME's are, and MAME is the reference.
  Reference (sim/i960/i960_cpu_ref.h): movre word for word as MAME, the
  SAT included; sqrtrl for ref_f2a. A literal source above fp3, a literal
  destination with bits 23:21 set (MAME's null pointers) and a triple at r30
  (m_r[32]) end the program, as does a subnormal left in fp0-fp3 (movrl's
  rule: the units flush it at its next use). tb_i960_top now compares the SAT
  every retire. +fx's mix: movre twice and sqrtrl added (a quarter of the
  movre with the destination over the third word); +nomvre for R887's mix.
  test_i960_top_fx, 20,000 programs each, seeds 1 / 2 / 3: 0 mismatches
  (25.97 M / 26.26 M / 26.08 M checks); movre retired 1,901 / 2,110 / 2,091
  (r->r, r->fp, fp->r, fp->fp all ~300-660; through the SAT 400 / 463 / 498;
  destination over the third word 330 / 321 / 398); sqrtrl 913 / 874 / 873.
  The first run failed once (seed 1, logbnr of fp2): a movre had left a
  subnormal double in fp2 -- the reference's missing end-of-program rule,
  not the RTL. PLANTED, each caught on seed 1: the fp spill dropped, the SAT
  write dropped, the alias ignored, T_TRIP skipped (FAIL, 1 mismatch each);
  movre's decode removed (MODULE TRAP); sqrtrl's start without F2A (FAIL).
  test_i960_top, _fr, _vc: PASS, 0 mismatches.

**R896 -- MANX TT AT 28.7 FPS IS NOT A SLOW STAGE: THE GAME READS THE
RENDER-MODE REGISTER BACK (MAME's render_mode_r) AND THIS CORE ANSWERED 0, SO
ITS OWN READ-MODIFY-WRITE PUT IT IN 30 Hz MODE. EVERY STAGE FITS ONE VBLANK
WITH ROOM. FIXED ON THE 2A BUILD: 0x10000000 READS BACK BITS 14 / 2 / 0.**
(Coordinator: s1230 runs Manx TT's attract race at 28.7 fps, 99% of frames
two vblanks; MAME 0.289 57.4 fps on the same race. Find the stage that misses
the deadline and make it fit.)

*What was believed.* A stage over the 17.39 ms vblank: the TGP (R888 left
Rally at 0.96x MAME's model), the geometry walk or the draw (Manx TT's
786-982 polygons, R893), or the i960's frame work (R854/R855: VF2's foreground
used ~81% of a vblank on the board, Manx TT's is longer).

*Each stage, measured against the 17.39 ms vblank (none is over):*
  * TGP -- `make tgp_capture_2a CAP2A_SET=manxtt CAP2A_GAME=bike
    CAP2A_COIN=30,200,330 CAP2A_START=1700 CAP2A_FR=2200` with
    PL_PRESS=18:test,22:test (the coordinator's MAME window): 2,203 frames,
    2,366,903 words in, 627,897 out. tb_tgp_replay TGP_PROG=4096 (R888's
    EARLY_ALU + BUFW_Q 32), --board-push --gap 60 --jitter 40, lat 6: PASS,
    bit-exact against MAME; 282.3 M cycles, CPI 5.88, 0.938x MAME's model.
    A frame's TGP work p50 1.78 ms, p90 2.89, p99 3.25, max 5.11; 0 frames
    over budget, 0 over half. The bench's i960 waits on the output FIFO
    ~1.5-1.8 ms a race frame (e.g. frame 2959: 2.81 ms busy, 1.77 ms i960
    wait). Manx TT stores little buffer RAM (1.02 M wait cycles in 282 M).
  * Walk -- geodiff_ra (the read-ahead, M2GD_LAT 12) built CRTC_Y 128 and
    WINKEY (R893) on MAME's walks of the race (R893's t3798 at 66 s and
    t4435 at 77 s): to the last quad 412,577 / 528,704 clk_sys = 5.16 /
    6.61 ms at 80 MHz (0.30 / 0.38 vblank); 943 / 1,143 quads, 40 / 60
    objects, 32,778 / 42,186 engine reads.
  * Draw -- tb_m2_raster3d in the 2A raster configuration (TEXLUT, KW 20,
    TXLW8, FB_DDR3; M2_R3D_TEXMEM, PXK 0, MIPZ 3, WINKEY) on MAME's race list
    2000 (R893's d2000): 764,391 cycles = 9.55 ms (0.55 vblank); colour
    against MAME mean 2.29 / 255 as R893. (R855's VF2 board/bench ratio,
    ~1.25x, puts the board's draw near 12 ms and the walk near 8 ms.)
  * The i960's frame work, MAME (traces with loops collapsed, frame marks
    and the flips; Manx TT's frame loop below): the coined race 38.3-39.1 k
    instructions from the vblank interrupt's entry (0xB70) to the flip;
    the attract race 28.6-31.3 k. 14.1 k of either is the vblank
    handler itself: a CRC-16 over 326 bytes of backup RAM, byte by byte
    (0x6b9d0), and a 5,804-byte copy of backup RAM to its mirror
    (0x1d00000 -> 0x1d016ac, 0x7b828) -- every frame. The rest of the frame
    (MAME's) is the vblank spin.
  * The i960's frame work, ours -- the whole-core bench below, the attract
    race (vblanks 1240-1347 after the fix, 108 of 108 flipped; TGP FIFO
    ~1,034 words a frame):
    0xB70 to the flip p50 343 k CPU cycles, p90 353 k, max 374 k of the
    bench's 417 k-cycle vblank (0.82 / 0.85 / 0.90), 28.3 k instructions
    (MAME 28.6-31.3 k); FP 30.0% of the cycles, T_MEM_W 24.0%, fetch wait
    15.5%, FRAME 12.8%; the TGP holds ~8.4 k cycles a frame. On the board's
    clocks the i960 has 695 k cycles a vblank: the bench's 342 k is 0.49 of
    it, ~0.70 with R854's board/bench factor of 1.42 (measured before
    R855, so an upper bound). INFERRED for the board; it fits either way.

*Manx TT's frame loop (MAME 0.289 trace, verified):* 0x3ed8 writes the flip
(0x803008), then 0x3f08 samples bit 2 of 0x98000c with `ldob` and spins at
0x3f1c-0x3f30 until it changes; 0x3f34 goes on with the next frame. Bit 2 is
videoctl_r's frame bit: m_framenum bit 0 in 60 Hz render mode, bit 1 in 30
Hz. A frame done inside its vblank therefore runs at 57.5 fps, and one that
is not waits a further vblank: two vblanks a frame is either a frame over
1.0 vblank, or the 30 Hz mode.

*The cause (MAME's taps, the trace, the bench; verified).* Manx TT writes
render mode 4 at boot (`stos` at 0x37cc) and then CHANGES it by
read-modify-write -- `ldos 0x10000000 / and 0xfeff / stos` at 0x24f80, and
the same at 0x6efec / 0x6f014, 0x1a08c and 0x1a40c (MAME's coined session:
reads at vblanks 1037, 1038, 1893, 2186, 2359; the attract with the motion
base answered reaches 0x24f80 at vblank 631).
MAME's render_mode_r returns `(unk << 14) | (mode << 2) | test`, so the
game writes 4 back (0x104 once, bit 8 dropped by render_mode_w). This
core's I/O read mux has no case for 0x10000000-0x101fffff and returned 0:
the first read-modify-write wrote 0, R765's 0x98000c then showed frame bit
1, and from there the game frames every other vblank -- with its work
nowhere near a vblank.
  The whole-core bench (test_m2_boot_2a's harness built A2X with a new
  MANX_MOTION parameter -- the DX motion base answered as m2_2a_inputs does,
  R892 -- and the image from rom_csum.py on Manx TT's MRA; M2_FRAMESTAT,
  M2_WORK_IPS=b70,3eec): vblanks 0-686 identical line for line before and
  after the fix. From vblank 687 (the first read-modify-write) the old RTL
  flips every SECOND vblank (687 0, 688 1, 689 0, ...) with the frame's work
  window (0xB70 to the flip) 58.2-58.7 k CPU cycles of the bench's 417 k
  (14%); with the fix one flip a vblank: 687-1224 all but one (885), then

  minute containing its race load has 58 flips in 60 vblanks too), and the
  attract race from 1240 on every vblank.
  make target: obj_boot_2ax with BOOT_2AX_G=-GMANX_MOTION=1 (Makefile note).
  MAME's taps over 4,000 vblanks of each 2A game: render-mode READS -- VF2

*The fix (Model2.sv, 2A only):* 0x10000000-0x101fffff reads

**R901 -- TO INVESTIGATE: THE i960'S WAIT STATES (0x00E00000).** Ben asked
whether the core runs the i960 with the board's wait states. It does not: the
game's writes to the system controller's CPU-control block (0x00E00000 -
0x00E00037, MAME: ".ram(); // CPU control (wait-states)") are dropped and the
block reads 0 (m2_cpu_bridge routes 0x00800000-0x00FFFFFF to T_IO; Model2.sv's
I/O read mux has no case). Our i960's per-access timing comes from its 40 MHz
clock, 8 KB I-cache and SDRAM latency instead -- faster than the board's 25 MHz
on cached code and fast registers, slower on SDRAM data misses under load.
MAME stores the values and ignores them; its notes suspect srallyc's start
grid depends on the CPU's pace. Future work, in order: the read-back (as MAME,
a few ALM, cheap insurance against an R896-style read-modify-write), the block's
format from what the games write, then per-region minimum access times where
we are faster than the board. Wait states only slow a CPU: they are not the
cause of Sega Rally's slowdowns (R888).

*ON THE BOARD (s1247 = model2a 38e66d3, built by accident from the main
checkout: clk_sys -0.044, clk_mem -0.123, hold +0.239), 2026-10-20: MANX TT
AT 57.5 fps -- tools/m2-fps.py, 1 vblank per 3D frame 100%, frame 15.0 /
17.5 / 19.6 ms, in the attract race, after booting to attract by itself
(R892). R896's render-mode read-back confirmed (was 28.7 fps). Virtua Cop 2
measured at 57.5 fps on s1240 (1 vblank per frame 100%).*
*Same build, Ben: Manx TT "mostly full speed, a few slowdowns"; Sega Rally
still has small slowdowns. Both are the occasional heavy frame now, not a
rate bug. Next to measure (R896's suggestion): the i960's frame work in the
whole-core bench on Rally's and Manx TT's heaviest frames -- R896 found
Manx TT's i960 spends 30% of its frame in floating point and 24% waiting on
data; R888's TGP speed-ups did not move Rally on the board.*

TEXTURES ARE R867's LUMA-ROW MAP, NOT THE LAYOUT. EACH GAME NOW HAS EIGHT ROW
RANGES OF ITS OWN (THEY USE 6-35 ROWS; EXACT FOR TWO, NEAREST BY CONTENT FOR
FOUR). PILOT KIDS RUNS ON UNCLEARED WORK RAM (MAME'S PATCH SKIPS THE GAME'S
OWN CLEAR): THE LARGE LAYOUT'S GAMES NOW START WITH WORK AND BOARD RAM ZEROED,
AS MAME'S. NOT FITTED, NOT ON A BOARD.**
(Ben, s1240 = baadcd5: Dynamite Cop, Sky Target and Dead or Alive run with
right geometry and 2D but "trippy", scrambled texels on every surface --
DOA's trousers striped, which they are not; Motor Raid "most textures black";

debug block: "0 / S = 0 / M = 0 / E-Rank = 14729 / F-Angle = 24 /

*Believed (the task):* either R867's colour path (the eight luma rows a game
uses, captured on chip) or the texel fetch for R897's layout (the texture

*THE TEXEL FETCH IS NOT INVOLVED (code; the bench below):* the rasteriser's
texels come from texture RAM (MAME's textureram0/1, written by the CPU at
0x12000000 / 0x12400000; Model2.sv GAME_TEXS0 / GAME_TEXS1, two 1 MB sheets
of 4-bit texels), which R897 did not move. R897's "texture ROM at 0x4000000"
is MAME's "textures" region -- the texture-COORDINATE ROM the geometry engine

differ). The raster bench below uses MAME's texture RAM and polygons: with

and sampling are not the fault. (Whether the CPU's texture upload on the
core equals MAME's is not benched here; nothing in R897 touched its path.)

*THE CAUSE, MEASURED (MAME 0.289 m2lod; sim/io/mame_m2_2a_play.lua sessions
of 160 s -- attract, two credits, play -- with a geometry-walk dump every
5 s through M2GEO_TRIG; a textured polygon's row = texheader[1] & 0xff):*
  game          rows  distinct  most used (polygons over 30 walks)
  dynamcop       17     17      96 7168, 7 6516, 6 5665, 100 2002, 76 1606;
                                106 and fades 131-144 (<1%)
  skytargt       35     32      96 21679, 76 7169, 6 6324, 107 1682 ...
                                (36=86, 42=92, 46=96 equal)
  motoraid       25     24      100 19435 (=101), 125 2446 ...
  pltkidsa       24      8      0-100 (17 rows, ALL EQUAL), 249-255
  doaab           6      6      98 25917, 100 14078, 72, 6, 89, 92
  hpyagu98       33     33      96 11081, 76 2766, 51 253 ...
  The luma RAM is written at boot and constant after it (every walk's dump
  equal), except Motor Raid's row 100, rewritten in a fade.
  R867's map captures rows 0-3 and 16-19 and colours any other row from the
  slot {row[4], row[1:0]} aliases. None of the four faulty games uses those

*THE FIX (rtl/video/m2_luma_map.sv, new; Model2.sv instantiates it in place
of the inline lslot):* for the large layout's games (a2_big) the eight slots
are eight RANGES of row numbers per game, s[0] < ... < s[7]: slot k takes
rows s[k] .. s[k+1]-1 (slot 0 everything below s[1]) and is filled from row
s[k] alone (the snoop writes only a range's first row). Rows with equal
contents in one range are exact (Pilot Kids' seventeen, Motor Raid's
100 / 101); the rest of a range takes its first row's table. The ranges were
chosen per game by a DP over the survey's rows, minimising the polygon-
weighted mean |difference| between a row and the table it gets (in luma
steps of 64), each range's first row being its table:
  game       starts s[0..7]                      error (luma steps a polygon)
  hpyagu98   47 51 52 54 76 92 96 100            0.451 (ideal 8 of 33: 0.124)
  dynamcop   6 7 76 96 100 132 138 142           0.024 (ideal 0.014)
  pltkidsa   0 249 250 251 252 253 254 255       0     (exact)
  doaab      6 72 89 92 98 100 254 255           0     (exact)
  skytargt   6 7 18 22 76 94 96 107              0.460 (ideal 0.224)
  motoraid   100 115 125 126 131 133 137 151     0.395 (ideal 0.182)
  ("ideal": any eight tables, every row to its nearest -- a general row map
  per game, a 256-entry lookup each. Ranges with a free table per range
  scored 0.376 / 0.296 / 0.364 for Sky Target / Motor Raid / Hanguk Pro Yagu
  98 but cost 56 more table bits and their registers -- the first cut, +158
  ALMs est., withdrawn for this one.) Every game outside a2_big keeps R867's
  function bit for bit (VF2, Virtua Cop 2, Sega Rally, Zero Gunner, Manx TT).
  MORE ROWS THAN SLOTS (four games): the exact answer is more slots. Each
  slot is 128 bytes of one M10K (lr_mem 1024 x 8, m2_span_tex); 16 slots is
  one more M10K and a fourth slot bit in the quad store's texture word, which
  R867 filled (att 30/30, uvt 195/195) -- a wider store word is more M10K.
  Sky Target needs 32 tables (~4 M10K). Neither fits 553 / 553; recorded for
  Ben. What is left is a few rows per game at < 0.5 luma step on average;
  the worst single rows (Sky Target 101, a descending ramp, 72 polygons in
  160 s; Hanguk Pro Yagu 98 101 / 103) stay visibly wrong on those polygons.

*PILOT KIDS (MAME 0.289 taps and disassembly; the whole-core bench):*
  1. THE DEBUG BLOCK IS THE GAME'S OWN. Its strings ("S = %d", "E-Rank =
     %d", "F-Angle = %d", "F-Length = %1.2f") are at program 0x59110-0x59160,
     printed by 0x5591c0 (the program runs from a RAM copy: ROM 0x50000-
     0xfffff at 0x550000), called from the frame routine at 0x558600 when
     the halfword 0x5092e6 is non-zero. 0x5092e6 is cleared at boot
     (0x551898) and toggled by an edge of 1P Start (0x509730 bit 8) at
     0x556f70 / 0x557124 / 0x55741c, each only while 0x5091b0 is non-zero
     (written at 0x55b370 from 0x50926a). In MAME 0x5091b0, 0x5092e4 and
     0x5092e6 stay 0 over a coined 90 s with Start every 2 s, and no single
     one of the 26 input fields sets the flag.
  2. THE BOOT (0x6d0-0x74c) copies the program to RAM, then runs a loop over
     work RAM 0x500000-0x54ffff that sums it into 0x5000d0 AND CLEARS it --
     the store at 0x730 (0x92f55000, st g14,(g5)). MAME's init_pltkids
     replaces that store with a branch (0x08000004), because the clear also
     wipes the PRCB copy at 0x500000 the interrupts vector through (R869's
     Zero Gunner case); the MRA carries the same patch. So the game RUNS ON
     UNCLEARED RAM, which in MAME is zero and on this core is whatever the
     SDRAM held.
  3. MEASURED: MAME with 0x500000-0x54ffff and 0x200000-0x23ffff filled
     0xFFFFFFFF (written, then a soft reset) stops at once: "I960: ffffffff:
     Unhandled 00". The whole-core bench (tb_m2_boot A2X on the MRA's image,
     its unwritten memory 0xFFFF): IP 0xffffffff, TRAPPED / HALTED after

     samples sit at 0x55cf3c-0x55cf4c). The board's debug block is a symptom
     of the same garbage; which word set 0x5091b0 there is not known (the
     bench's 0xFFFF RAM traps instead).
  THE FIX (Model2.sv, the boot sweep that already zeroes char RAM on the 2A
  board, R852): for a2_big it goes on to zero work RAM (GAME_WORK, 512 K
  words) and the 2A board RAM (GAME_BOARD, 128 K words) before the CPU
  leaves reset; every other game's sweep ends where it did. MAME's RAM is
  zero at start; the board's SRAM would be random, which the unpatched
  program cleared itself.
  NOT CHANGED, RECORDED: Zero Gunner's patch (0x700, R869) skips its own
  clear of 0x500000-0x53ffff the same way, so on this core it too runs on

**R904 -- THE i960'S WAIT STATES (R901), FOR SEGA RALLY ONLY, BEHIND A
SWITCH THAT IS OFF: WHAT EVERY GAME WRITES TO 0x00E00000 (MEASURED), THE
FORMAT AND REGION MAP (INFERRED), A MINIMUM ACCESS TIME PER REGION
(m2_waitst, M2_2A_WAITST). NOT FITTED, NOT ON A BOARD.**
(Ben: emulate the wait states for Sega Rally, game ID 0x10, behind a switch.
A Sega Rally hardware expert, through Ben: the registers hold EXTRA wait
cycles -- "if I set 10, the i960 read takes 1 cycle (address) + 10 wait
cycles + 1 cycle (data) = 12 cycles in total". Ben: count them in our own
clk_i960 cycles, not in real time -- the clock is already set so the core
runs at the board's speed.)

*What the games write (MEASURED, MAME 0.289, a write and read tap on
0x00e00000-0x00e00037 over sim/io/mame_m2_2a_play.lua; srallyc 100 s with a
coin at 20 s and the scripted race, vf2 / zeroguna / vcop2 / manxtt 60 s
each):* fourteen dword writes, mask 0xffffffff, one per word in order, in the
game's first ~10 us (vblank 0; IPs srallyc 0x440, vf2 0xd4, zeroguna 0x5ec,
vcop2 0x884, manxtt 0x45c) -- a copy loop from a table in the program ROM.
Never written again; NEVER READ (0 reads in 5,400 vblanks of Rally, 3,000
of each other game). The tables, found in each program image (the copy's
lda of the table, verified against the taps for the five games tapped; the
others statically only), words 0-13:

     srallyc   10 02 42 02 10 10 10 10 08 10 10 10 10 10
     zeroguna  10 02 42 02 04 04 10 10 20 10 10 10 10 10
     pltkidsa  10 02 42 02 04 04 10 10 20 10 10 10 10 10
     doaab     04 02 42 02 04 04 10 10 20 10 10 10 10 10
     vf2       04 02 42 02 01 02 10 10 20 10 10 10 10 10
     vcop2     04 02 42 02 01 02 10 10 20 10 10 10 10 10
     desert    04 02 42 02 01 02 10 10 20 10 10 10 10 10
     daytona   04 02 42 02 10 10 10 10 08 10 10 10 10 10
     vcopa     04 02 42 02 10 10 10 10 08 10 10 10 10 10
     manxtt    04 02 42 02 10 10 10 10 08 10 10 10 10 10
     skytargt  04 02 42 02 10 10 10 10 08 10 10 10 10 10
     dynamcop  04 02 42 02 10 10 10 10 08 10 10 10 10 10

(table terminated by 0xffffffff; the original board's Daytona, Virtua Cop
and Desert Tank program the same block the same way.) Words 1-3 are 02 42 02
on every game and both boards; words 6, 7 and 9-13 are 0x10 on all; word 0
is 0x04 or 0x10; words 4, 5 and 8 move together (10 10 / 08, 01 02 / 20,
04 04 / 20) with the game's generation, not its board.

*The format (INFERRED).* Every value has exactly ONE bit set in bits 5:0
(0x01, 0x02, 0x04, 0x08, 0x10, 0x20); word 2 adds bit 6 (0x42) on every
board. Read as binary counts (the expert's description), Rally would run its
program ROM, eleven other regions and the data ROM at 16 and 8 waits -- 18
and 10 bus cycles, 720 ns and 400 ns at 25 MHz, for 1990s EPROMs and mask
ROMs of ~100-150 ns -- and the 1 MB of work RAM the game hammers at 66 (or 2
with bit 6 a flag). Read as a ONE-HOT tap select (a shift-register wait
generator: bit n ends the cycle after n waits), the counts are ROM 4 (2 on
the 256-512 KB programs: 160-240 ns at 25 MHz), the three RAMs 1 (120 ns),
everything else 4 and word 8 3 or 5 -- plausible for the parts. One-hot is
the default here; binary is a parameter (ONEHOT=0, bit 6 dropped). Whether
0x01 is 0 waits or 1, and what bit 6 means, is unknown.

*The region map (INFERRED, nothing measured says which word governs which
address).* m2_waitst region_of(), MAME's 2A-CRX map in address order, with
words 1-3 the three RAMs because they are the words every board sets alike:
  0 program ROM 0x000000-0x1fffff     7 tile / char 0x01000000-0x017fffff
  1 board RAM   0x200000-0x3fffff     8 data ROM    0x02000000-0x03ffffff, 0x06000000
  2 work RAM    0x400000-0x7fffff     9 palette     0x01800000-0x019fffff
  3 buffer RAM  0x900000-0x97ffff    10 comm        0x01a00000-0x01bfffff
  4 geometrizer 0x800000-0x87ffff    11 I/O, UART, backup 0x01c00000-0x01ffffff
  5 copro       0x880000-0x8fffff, 0x980000-0xbfffff
  6 system      0xc00000-0xffffff (CPU control, interrupts, timers)
 12 renderer    0x10000000-0x11ffffff  13 texture / luma 0x12000000-0x13ffffff
For Rally only words 0 (4), 1-3 (1) and 8 (3) differ from the 0x10 (4) of
the rest, so the map's guesses matter only for which regions get 1 or 3
waits instead of 4.

*The semantics (DECIDED, R901's "per-region minimum access times").* On the
board the waits ARE the memory's access time; here the SDRAM behind the
bridge is, and a miss already takes far longer than 2 + N clk_i960 cycles
(R888: ~19 clk_sys idle, 25-40 typical). So the default (EXTRA=0) is a
MINIMUM: an access is never answered before cycle 2 + N of its own; an
answer the bridge has sooner (a line-buffer word, a data-cache hit, a
posted write) is latched and the bridge kept off the bus until then, and a
later answer passes as it was. Our accesses are never faster than the
board's and never slower than they are now. EXTRA=1 is the other reading
(N cycles on top of whatever the access takes: the request is shown to the
bridge from cycle N). BURST=1: an access back to back with the previous one,
same direction, same 16-byte line (the i-cache's line fill, ldl/ldq) is a
burst's next word -- 1 + N, the i960KB's one address cycle a burst; a fill
of four words at N=4 is 6 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 21 cycles, the bus's 1 + 4 x 5.
Instruction fetches the i-cache answers never reach the bus, as on the chip.

*The implementation.* rtl/io/m2_waitst.sv between i960_top and
m2_cpu_bridge on clk_i960 (Model2.sv g_waitst, built only with M2_2A_WAITST;
without it the bridge's nets are the CPU's own, assigned through). `en` is
is_srally through two flops: for every other game, and for Rally with the
switch off, every output is its input. With `en` it answers the block itself
(four byte-lane MLABs, 16 x 8, read back as MAME's RAM; the bridge never
sees a block access) and decodes each word's count as it is written (14 x 6
flops, cleared by the CPU's reset; the boot writes them in its first ~100
instructions); per access it counts cycles from the first shown (`cyc`),
registers the region's minimum in that first cycle (need_r -- the address
decode and the 14:1 count mux end at a flop, not in the acknowledge path),
and acknowledges when the bridge has answered and `cyc` has reached it.
c_ack is b_ack (or the held flag) AND a compare of two flops. Designed
against the bridge's registered acknowledge (FAST_ACK 0, what Model2.sv
builds), whose answer never comes in an access's first cycle.

*What is NOT known, and the questions for the expert (Ben is in contact):*
  1. Binary count or one-hot? Every value written has one bit set in 5:0;
     Rally writes 0x10 to word 0 and to nine others, 0x08 to word 8. Is 0x10
     sixteen waits or four?
  2. If one-hot: is bit 0 zero waits (bit n = n waits) or one?
  3. Word 2 is 0x42 on every board: what is bit 6 (burst / page mode for
     the work RAM? READY from the device?)
  4. Which word governs which address range? (Our guess above; words 1-3
     the three RAMs, word 0 the program ROM.) Words 4, 5 and 8 change with
     the game's generation (10 10 / 08; 01 02 / 20; 04 04 / 20): the TGP /
     geometrizer interface?
  5. Read and write the same count? Any recovery or idle cycle between
     accesses on top?
  6. Bursts (the i960KB's quad-word reads: i-cache fills, ldq): every data
     word 1 + N after one address cycle, or N only on the first?
  7. Where a device has its own READY (the TGP's FIFO full, the
     geometrizer busy): is the count a minimum before READY is sampled, or
     a fixed length?
  8. Do Model 2 (Daytona, Virtua Cop, Desert Tank write the same table
     layout), 2B and 2C use the same controller and format?

**R905 -- THE STRIPES ARE NOT THE TEXEL FETCH OR THE LAYOUT: TEXTURE SHEET
1's MIRROR (0x12600000-0x127FFFFF) WAS NOT A BURST REGION IN i960_memmap,
SO EVERY stq THE GAME SENT THROUGH IT WROTE ITS FOUR WORDS TO ONE ADDRESS.
THREE TEXEL WORDS IN FOUR OF SHEET 1 WERE NEVER WRITTEN. ONE CONSTANT
(rtl/cpu/i960/i960_memmap.sv: 0x12600000 -> 0x12800000). NOT FITTED, NOT
ON A BOARD.**
(Ben, s1253 = 71598a2, R900 on the board: Dynamite Cop, Dead or Alive, Sky
Target "no different" -- regular vertical stripes / bars across walls, a
ship's hull, floors, a cage; characters' faces and clothes much better;
Motor Raid's textures the same "trippy" (its long streaks are the 2D layer,
another run); Pilot Kids fine at 57.5 fps; Hanguk Pro Yagu 98 roughly right.)

*Believed (the task):* the texel fetch reads the texture ROM where the large
layout does not put it -- a dropped coordinate bit, a pitch, a bank, or the
data not where the fetch looks; R900's bench rendered from MAME's memory.

*THE PATH, TRACED.* The rasteriser's texels come from texture RAM only
(MAME's textureram0/1; m2_raster3d tex_base0/1 = GAME_TEXS0/1, words
0x1760000 / 0x17E0000, the same for every game), and texture RAM is written
only by the i960 (MAME: tex0_w / tex1_w at 0x12000000 / 0x12400000, each
.mirror(0x200000) with the BURST flag); no loader remap, no texture ROM and no
geometry command reaches it. MAME's "textures" region (R897's 0x4000000) is
the coordinate ROM -- headers and u/v, benched in R897. The large layout's
loader, MRA and bridge windows are as R897 left them: Dynamite Cop's sheet
words are contiguous halfwords of main_data (MAME's tex0 at f700: md+0xdb1e80
...), read through the bridge as every 2A game reads data. R900's bench
diverged from the board in the texture RAM's CONTENTS, not its address.

*THE CAUSE, MEASURED.*
  1. MAME 0.289 (mame-r869 m2lod, a write tap on 0x12000000-0x127FFFFF,
     dynamcop from power-on) against the whole-core bench (tb_m2_boot, A2X,
     the MRA's image built by tools/rom_csum.py, new hooks M2_TEXWLOG /
     M2_TEXDUMP): the first 349,568 texture stores are identical in address
     and data, in order. Store 349,569 is the first at IP 0x6ff90 into
     0x12600000: MAME writes 0x12600000, 04, 08, 0C; the core writes
     0x12600000 four times. Over the core's 1.82 M stores, IPs 0x6ff90 and
     0x6ffa0 (stq) wrote 227,136 runs of FOUR stores to one address in
     0x12600000-0x127FFFFF, and 489,216 single-address stores in sheet 0's
     mirror 0x12200000 (burst, correct).
  2. i960_memmap marked 0x12000000-0x125FFFFF ("texture RAM + mirrors"),
     which covers sheet 0, its mirror and sheet 1 but NOT sheet 1's mirror.
     i960_lsu advances a multi-word access's address only in a burst region
     (MAME: `if (pack.second & BURST) t1 += 4`), so the stq landed its words
     1-3 on word 0: in each group of four 16-bit texel words (16 texels in a
     row) the first holds the LAST word's data and the other three keep what
     was there -- regular vertical bars on every texture in sheet 1.
  3. Sheet 1 is where these games keep their scenery: Dynamite Cop's f700
     (the briefing room) draws the people from sheet 0 and walls, floor and
     desks from sheet 1 -- Ben's "characters better, surfaces striped".

*THE BENCH ON THE REAL PATH.* One MAME run of dynamcop with the tap on sheet
1 (0x12400000-0x127FFFFF, 3,075,200 stores to the frame dump) and the
M2DIFF dump of 3D list 700 in the same run. The stores replayed as MAME (and
the fixed core) handle them reproduce MAME's dumped tex1.bin EXACTLY (0 of
524,288 words differ); replayed with the old memmap (each stq at 0x6ff94 /
0x6ffa4 in the mirror onto its first address) 302,210 words differ. That
frame through tb_m2_raster3d (Model2.sv's 2A raster configuration, R900's
map, M2_R3D_GAME=0x14):
     sheet 1 as built (the board)   max-channel error 51.97 / 255, 40.63% of
                                    MAME's 3D pixels over 32: walls, floor
                                    and desks in vertical bars of 16 texels,
                                    the people untouched
     sheet 1 as MAME (the fix)      4.05 / 255, 0.47% over 32 -- R900's
                                    number for this frame
  (picture: r900/runs/bug_f700_dc_bug/side.png in the session scratchpad.)

*THE FIX:* rtl/cpu/i960/i960_memmap.sv, texture RAM's burst range to
0x12800000 (both sheets and both mirrors, as MAME's map). Nothing else.
lint_top (2A, -DM2_NO_2A, -DM2_NO_DEBUG -DM2_PROBE=1 -DM2_NO_2A_RALLY)
clean, lint_idx nothing new, quartus_map 17.0 --analyze_file 0 errors. Area:
one compare's constant (no map run; a decode of a[31:23] == 0x24 against the
old two-term range -- at most a LUT either way). No block RAM.

*FOUND ON THE WAY, NOT FIXED HERE: R828c's NO-MIP FLAG ASSUMES DAYTONA'S
lod AND coef.* R900's bench drove tex_mip_mode 0 (mip-mapping Off); the
board's OSD default is Sharp (mode 3). MAME's level is log2 z^2 -
log2(coef[attr >> 27] |dotp| lod) (model2_v.cpp; these games' log RAM is the
linear form, b[i] = i/256); R828c folded Daytona's lod 128 and coef 1.0 into
its constant. The large layout's games set their own (MAME walk dumps):
Dead or Alive lod 1000, coefs 11 / 351; Dynamite Cop and Sky Target 0.5 / 4
with coefs 1.94-351; Pilot Kids 4; Hanguk Pro Yagu 98 8; Motor Raid 0.25 --
the flag is up to eleven levels off. Dead or Alive never mips in MAME (100%
of its pixels at level 0 over 904 lists) and its sheets hold no mip levels;
at Sharp the core mips it by footprint. tb_m2_raster3d on doaab's list 700
(M2_R3D_MIPMODE=3; new MAME dumps carry L=/D=):
     Off (R900's bench)                      6.12 / 255, 1.67% over 32
     Sharp + R828c's flag (the board)       22.10 / 255, 17.36% over 32 --
                                            the far floor and the building
                                            behind go black
     Sharp + MAME's own level, B 0          6.12 / 255 (identical to Off)
  Dynamite Cop's list 700: 4.05 all three ways; Motor Raid's 5.45 / 5.93 /
  5.02. An RTL form (m2_geo streams each texture-parameter entry's coef and
  the 0x16 lod as twelve log bits; m2_geometry keeps a 32-entry table and,
  for a2_big, adds both to the flag's |dotp| term, B 0; released games keep
  R828c bit for bit) was written and linted, then held back: the table is
  384 more registers on a 98% part and was not mapped. Kept on local branch
  r905-mipz, one commit on this one. Until it lands, Mip-mapping Off on the OSD is the
  board's answer for Dead or Alive. (Landed as R911, its table in an MLAB.)

*VERIFIED / INFERRED:*
  * VERIFIED (MAME 0.289 and simulation): the core's texture store sequence
    against MAME's, the first divergence and its form; the replay of MAME's
    own stores reproducing its sheet 1 exactly, and the board's semantics
    reproducing the stripes on MAME's frame; i960_lsu's address rule for a
    non-burst region.
  * INFERRED: that Dead or Alive, Sky Target and Motor Raid stripe for the
    same reason (Dynamite Cop measured; the per-game survey of stq through
    0x12600000 follows); that the released games never send a multi-word
    store through that mirror (the survey), so they are unchanged.
  * What the board should show: Dynamite Cop's, Dead or Alive's, Sky
    Target's and Motor Raid's walls, floors, hulls and scenery as MAME's --
    no vertical bars; characters as now. Dead or Alive's far floor and
    background may still go dark with Mip-mapping on Sharp (above); Off
    shows MAME's picture. Pilot Kids, Hanguk Pro Yagu 98, VF2, Sega Rally,
    Virtua Cop 2, Zero Gunner and Manx TT unchanged.

FULL-SCREEN PICTURES SPLIT AT A COLUMN (WINDOW MODE 2), AND THE FETCH ENGINE
FETCHED BOTH MAPS ACROSS THE WHOLE LINE. NOT THE R897 LAYOUT, NOT TILE DATA.
FIX: A COLUMN WHOSE EVERY PIXEL IS MASKED IS NOT FETCHED (m2_tile_fetch
MASK_SKIP). PIXEL FOR PIXEL THE SAME PICTURE; +28 ALMs (standalone map), NO
BLOCK RAM. NOT FITTED, NOT ON A BOARD.**

*Fault (board, s1253 = 71598a2, Ben):* Motor Raid (motoraid, 0x1A, R897's
large layout) "MASSIVE OVERRUNS ON THE 2D" -- the background behind the
track streaks, long repeated lines, as R639's overrun. The released games do
not show it.

*Believed (going in), two candidates:* (a) bandwidth -- the glyph fetch
missing its line (R639 / R823); (b) addressing -- char RAM, tile RAM or the
scroll / line-scroll words misread on the new layout (GAME_CHAR under R897's
data, a mirror the bridge does not decode).

*Method (MAME 0.289; sim/video/mame_m2_ovrdump.lua unchanged, a scratch survey
script with write taps; the R823 bench, extended):*
  * Survey, 4,200 frames of motoraid's attract: per frame the eight scroll
    words, the H-scroll tables, the row-mask tables, and write taps on char
    RAM 0x01080000-0x010fffff, its mirror 0x01180000-, tile RAM
    0x01000000-0x0101ffff and its mirror 0x01100000- (MAME maps both mirrors;
    m2_cpu_bridge decodes neither).
  * 12 bursts of 6 consecutive frames (1400 / 1500 / 1800: the ranking
    screen over the 3D; 2100-3600: the race views -- sky and clouds behind
    the stands and track), each tile RAM, palette, char RAM.
  * Controls: Daytona (4 bursts), VF2 (3), Sega Rally (3), the same way.
  * tb_m2_video_ovr with r and d now both configurable (m2_video_ovr_top
    R_LBR / R_HSF / R_SIB, MSK): r = THE SHIPPED TILEMAP (LB_RING 1, the hscr
    read fixed as SCR_SYNC implies, SIBLING 0), d = the same + MASK_SKIP.
  * tb_m2_video_frame (LB_RING 1, HSCR_FIX 1) rendering MAME's own tile /
    char / palette images against MAME's snapshot.

*Now known -- VERIFIED:*
  1. NOT ADDRESSING. Zero writes to either mirror in 4,200 frames. Char RAM is
     written in 16 frames of 4,200, all at scene changes (largest 62,160 words
     at frame 1334, the ranking screen's load), so there is no per-frame
     invalidation storm on the glyph cache either. GAME_CHAR (byte 0x2D60000)
     is outside every region R897's MRA and its three remaps write (main_data
     ends 0x2480000; XTRA2 0x2600000-0x2B80000; samples 0x3400000-; XTRA3
     0x4000000-), and the char path is the same constants for every game. The
     2D renders MAME's image correctly (tb_m2_video_frame on f1500 and
     f2100: the clouds and the ranking text as MAME draws them, where the 3D
     does not cover them).
  2. TRUE OVERRUNS, AND HEAVY ONES. Shipped tilemap, native 24 kHz, visible
     lines late per frame (the ring's count), 6 frames a burst:

     | burst            | L 0 | L 20 | L 30 | L 45  | L 60  | L 90  | 14+U[0,30] | 14+U[0,50] | queue (mean 41) |
     |------------------|-----|------|------|-------|-------|-------|------------|------------|-----------------|
     | 1500 ranking     | 0   | 0    | 22.2 | 160.5 | 179.8 | 203.7 | 29.0       | 127.0      | 138.7           |
     | 2100 race        | 0   | 0    | 0    | 119.0 | 131.0 | 142.5 | 0          | 91.5       | 102.5           |
     | 3150 race        | 0   | 0    | 0    | 115.7 | 129.3 | 142.3 | --         | --         | --              |

     (1400 / 1800: 24 / 30 at L 30, 92 / 156 at L 45; the other race bursts
     64.7-100.8 at L 45.) Daytona's four bursts: 0 to L 45, 3-11.8 at L 60.
     VF2 and Rally: 0 everywhere to L 60. So Motor Raid's 2D is ~3-4x the
     load of the released games', and it falls over at ~35 cycles of port-3
     latency where Daytona holds to ~55.
  3. WHY. tile RAM 0x5006 (pair 2/3's ctrl, the even vscr) is 0x40xx in every
     dump: WINDOW MODE 2, the horizontal split at x = hscr & 0x1ff (0x1c5 ->
     453, 0x16d -> 365 ...), tilemap 2 one side, tilemap 3 the other, and
     both maps are full-screen distinct pictures -- 1,449 and 2,310 distinct
     tiles in the race views, 2,129 and 1,782 on the ranking screen (plus
     tilemap 1's 934 there, with 1,316 non-zero row-mask words). m2_tile_fetch
     masks the far side of a split PER PIXEL AT THE LINE BUFFER but fetched
     every column of both maps (as it does layer_off's map in mode 1 and
     row-masked columns -- tb_m2_tile_fetch's test 4 recorded it as "a real
     inefficiency ... recorded rather than made"). Two maps of distinct
     glyphs is ~126 columns of mostly-missing fetches a line where ~63 are
     shown; the 64 KB glyph cache cannot hold ~3,700 distinct tiles (116 KB),
     so the misses are steady, not R823's 4-line bursts, and the ring has
     nothing to borrow from.

*THE FIX (rtl/video/m2_tile_fetch.sv MASK_SKIP, through m2_video MASK_SKIP;
Model2.sv sets it 1 for every game):* F_CHECK registers f_col_masked -- the
column's first pixel fx and last pixel fx + ~f_off (= fx + f_step - 1; past
the line's end counts as masked) are all masked by layer_off, OR by the split
(split_right: last < h; else fx >= h), OR by the row mask at both of the at
most two 8-pixel mask columns the tile column touches -- and F_CADDR, a cycle
later, sends such a column straight to F_FULL with no tile-word use and no
glyph request. The emit side is untouched: it writes those pixels masked from
sx alone, as before, so the line buffer gets the same masked bits and every
unmasked pixel the same value. Conservative where sources mix (a column half
split, half row-masked is still fetched). Not taken: vscr bit 15 (a disabled
layer goes to the buffer as transparent, not masked, and an opaque pass
draws transparent pixels -- not provably invisible here).

*Benches:*
  * Motor Raid, all 12 bursts, shipped vs MASK_SKIP: MASK_SKIP 0 late lines
    to L 45 on every burst; L 60: 0 on the race views, 0.5 / 21.5 on two
    ranking bursts; L 90 native: race 0, ranking 126 (shipped 204). All six
    video modes and the jitter models (sweep / sweep2 on 1500, 2100, 3150):
    MASK_SKIP 0 at 14+U[0,30], 14+U[0,50], the queue model and 30+U[0,30] in
    every mode; first late lines at 45+U[0,30] native on the ranking (22).
  * EQUIVALENCE: MASK_SKIP at L 30 and L 45 against the shipped tilemap at

    Rally bursts (every frame compared; in the sweeps, badfr 0 in every mode
    and latency, and every differing line is a late line). Bad glyphs 0.
    The synthetic equivalence and mode-change tests: PASS.
  * Daytona / VF2 / Rally with MASK_SKIP: 0 late lines at every latency to
    60 (Daytona's 3-11.8 at L 60 gone: its mode-1 pair now fetches one map a
    line).
  * make test_m2_tile_fetch: the plain build PASS (12, unchanged); the
    MASK_SKIP build (tb -DTB_MASK_SKIP) 600 random lines -- layer_off, split
    at random h either side, random row masks, all three -- against the same
    DUT unmasked: every pixel's masked bit as MAME's sources give it, every
    unmasked pixel equal, every visible glyph fetched, no glyph the reference
    did not fetch, and (one source at a time) exactly the visible glyphs:
    609 checks, 0 fails; 18,479 fetches, 19,255 skipped. Planted: the last

  * make test_m2_video_ovr TEST_ARGS=+quick (defaults: R823's r and d) PASS,
    both builds.
  * lint_top clean on 2A, -DM2_NO_2A, -DM2_NO_DEBUG -DM2_PROBE=1
    -DM2_NO_2A_RALLY; Verilator -Wall on m2_video (MASK_SKIP 0 and 1): the
    same 9 warnings as HEAD; lint_idx: nothing new; quartus_map 17.0
    --analyze_file m2_tile_fetch.sv, m2_video.sv, Model2.sv: 0 errors.
  * AREA, quartus_map 17.0 standalone m2_tile_fetch: 801 -> 829 ALMs est.,
    736 -> 815 ALUT, 1,078 -> 1,079 registers, 0 block bits both. No
    whole-design map (another agent's map held the slot).

*INFERRED (what would settle it):*
  * The board's port-3 latency under Motor Raid is ~40 or more: the bench
    puts its race views clean at R823's board model (14+U[0,30]) and at
    L 30, and only the ranking screen late there, against Ben's "massive" on
    the race. Its heavier 3D / texel traffic (and R905's texel fault) would

  * Timing: f_col_masked is fx -> a 3-bit subtract -> a 10-bit add -> 9/10-
    bit compares and two 64:1 mask selects, into one register (acted on a

*What the board should show:* Motor Raid's sky, stands and ranking screen
without repeated lines; Daytona, VF2, Rally and the rest pixel-identical

**R902 -- SEGA RALLY'S REAR-VIEW MIRROR IS WINDOWS 3 AND 4: A BLACK BACKING
AT z 512, THEN THE SCENE BEHIND THROUGH A REFLECTED CAMERA IN ITS OWN
VIEWPORT. EVERY STAGE OF THIS CORE DRAWS IT FROM MAME's LISTS; BLACK IS
EXACTLY WHAT A z-ONLY SORT DRAWS. THE BOARD'S BLACK IS NOT REPRODUCED IN
SIMULATION -- NO RTL CHANGE.**
(Ben, s1240 = baadcd5: "the rear-view mirror is just black -- it should show
the scene behind the car". Not known whether it ever worked.)

*Believed:* backface culling flipped by a mirrored transform, the wrong
viewport rectangle, the backing in front in the sort, the near plane, or a
second camera dropped by the geometry.

*MAME 0.289 srallyc (build/mame289-mip, sim/io/mame_m2_2a_play.lua, coin
30 s; M2WIN, M2DIFF list 2000, M2GEO walks 3282 / 3457; verified):*
  1. The mirror is the bumper view's (VR from the near chase view; the far
     and near chase views have none). A race list there has FOUR windows
     (747 of 747 lists 1620-2366; the key's 15 is far off):
       W1 (0,128)-(496,512) centre (248,320): the world, 112-155 objects
       W2 same viewport: one HUD object (z bucket 0x5000)
       W3 (126,438)-(370,482) centre (248,460): ONE flat black quad, focal
          150, z bucket 512 -- the mirror's frame and backing
       W4 (128,440)-(368,480), same centre: the scene behind, 5-8 objects
          (terrain from polygon ROM, the cars from slow polygon RAM, count
          0), 29-96 polygons, z buckets 0x2383-0xf9a0; ONE camera matrix
          written twice, determinant -1 (a reflection), focal inherited
          from W3 (150); the list ends with focal 350 for the next frame.
     Screen rows 30-74 / 32-72 (MAME's 384 - vp_y + yoffs 128).
  2. MAME draws W4 before W3 (render_polygons, last window first, first
     write wins), so the scene covers the backing but its 2-px rim. The
     reverse bit of the object command is parsed and never used; the
     backface test is dot(normal, point) on transformed vectors, which a
     reflection does not change (and this core's engine does the same --
     there is no screen-space winding test anywhere in the path).
  3. The list is complete at the flip: snapshots of [rp, rp+0x900) at the
     read-pointer write and at the next vblank (where MAME walks) differ in
     0 words over 110 lists (flip 14.6 ms before the vblank). Lists are
     TRIPLE-buffered at dwords 0x0000 / 0x2000 / 0x4000 (Daytona double).
     The TGP writes only the matrices (opcode included) into the list; the
     i960 pushes the rest; the TGP's mirror matrices are followed by an
     output the i960 pops before it flips (rally_play capture, 1,724 of
     them), so a slow TGP cannot leave the slot unwritten at the walk.

*This core on MAME's lists (all 2A configuration; verified):*
  - geodiff (CRTC_Y 128, WINKEY) on walks 3282 / 3457: 1,221 / 1,688 of
    1,224 / 1,695 polygons match (the rest R643's edge-clip cases in W1),
    sort keys 1 / 4 off (W1), u/v and texture parameters as MAME; the mirror
    quads are there with window nibble 0xB, the backing 0xC.
  - tb_m2_raster3d (TEXLUT, KW 20, TXLW8, FB_DDR3, TEXMEM) on list 2000,
    mean max-channel error over each window's pixels:
        window      px     key on   key off (z alone)
        1       179,632     1.44      1.43
        2            96     2.75    202.83
        3         1,136     0.00      0.00
        4         9,600     5.07    158.44  <- black: the backing wins
  - THE WHOLE PATH, our geometry into our raster: tb_m2_raster3d's new
    M2_R3D_QUADS mode pushes geodiff's ours.txt as the clipper hands it
    over, coloured by quad index. The mirror rectangle (240 x 40 = 9,600
    px) is owned by W4 quads on 9,600 px with the key, by the W3 backing on
    9,600 px with the nibble cleared, on both walks. Draw 390,357 / 409,888
    core cycles (0.32-0.34 frame).
  - Tiny cull (R769/R776): no mirror quad is refused in the fine mode and 3
    of 50 in the coarse; the lists need 1,143-1,713 slots of 2,048.
  - The 2D (tb_m2_video_frame on MAME's tile/char/palette at 55 s): the
    mirror rectangle is all backdrop, category 0 -- nothing over the 3D.

*Our own list (m2_boot_harness A2X, the srallyc image, three coins, start,
VR twice; scratch tb with an input schedule and buffer dumps; ~2 h of
simulation):* after the second VR (frame 3,000) our i960 + TGP + push path
write MAME's structure exactly -- W3 at (126,438)-(370,482) with its one
object, W4 at (128,440)-(368,480) with 4 objects (200 polygons) and two
matrices of determinant -1. But every matrix's translation in that run is
NaN (the main view's too): the harness's analog inputs read 0xFF and its
sound board is a stub, so its camera is not the board's -- the harness
shows the mirror's commands are emitted, not that their values are right.

*Daytona (MAME, daytona, race with VR1-VR4 cycled, 125 s):* every window
is full-screen ((-1,128)-(496,512)); no view draws a mirror window. The
original core does not share this mechanism (main's key is off for Daytona,

*So:* black is exactly the z-only order (W3's backing at z 512 in front of
all of W4), and on the 2A build the key is on (R3D_WINKEY = M2A, confirmed
on the board for Manx TT and Virtua Cop 2). Nothing in simulation drops the
mirror. NOT ESTABLISHED, and the next board build should measure rather
than guess: per walk, the window count and the number of quads the store
took with each nibble (0xC and 0xB here: expect 1 and 29-96), on the
overlay. If 0xB is zero, the W4 objects die before the store (walk,
engine, clipper -- the camera's values); if it is there, the raster loses
them (then the draw, not the sort).

*Tools (scratch, ROM-derived output outside the tree):* M2_R3D_QUADS in

**R898 -- 15 kHz IS NOW A SCAN CONVERTER (RETROREPAIR'S), WITH HDMI KEPT AND
ALL THREE LINE RATES.** (Main, numbered clear of the Model 2A branch.) Ben,
2026-10-20: "on 15 kHz the implementation we have is flawed -- big black
borders at the top and bottom and it has sync issues. Retro Repair has looked
into this and has it working right, at least in size. The only issue is they
took out HDMI." Needed for Model 2 and 2A.

*Believed (R682, R701, R783, R799, R834, R840):* 15 kHz is the renderer
retimed -- the same 656-pixel line at a lower pixel clock, 192 of the 384
lines a field -- and its faults were timing faults to be tuned (vsync place,
line count, a narrow line for the shape).
*Now known (retrorepair, guncon-scan15):* the border is not a timing fault.
A field holds ~240 visible lines at the game's fixed 57.52 Hz and the 1:1
picture has 192 of them, so a fifth of the height is black whatever the
timing; only a vertical scale fills it. Their converter (m2_scan15): the
renderer stays on native 24 kHz timing, a ring of lines takes the finished
picture, and its own 15 kHz interlaced timing shows 240 lines a field, 480 a
frame, output row m from source row 4m/5 (an exact 4:5 bilinear blend). Two
output fields are exactly two native frames (3,476,800 clk_mem either way)
so it never drifts and adds no frame of delay; a 28.8 Hz game's two images
are kept in one output frame by watching show_tag. Their build was 262/263
lines only and had no HDMI (MISTER_DEBUG_NOHDMI) to fit.

*What this port changes, and why:*
  * HDMI KEPT; the 1:1 path retired instead (vid_il_c = 0 into m2_video,
    m2_raster3d and the crosshair, so synthesis removes the renderer's own
    interlace; ce_pix is a constant 16/100). quartus_map: m2_video -99 ALUT,
    m2_video_timing -32, m2_raster3d -23, its arbiter -10, fb_read -6.
  * ALL THREE LINE RATES KEPT (R840: most sets take only 15.7 kHz). The
    converter already carried nl/ml; its output enable is now per line count
    (547/5300, 537/5300, 861/8692 -- each exactly two native frames per two
    fields) and "15kHz lines" (O[61:60]) stays. Same 240 lines, 656-pixel
    line, 64-pixel hsync and 496 visible in every mode; the faster rates get
    more blank lines and a faster pixel clock.
  * TWO TAPS. Their four-row read served a vertical filter they built and
    rejected (tied off); the sharp table weights rows s-1 and s+2 with 0.
  * THE RING, SIZED BY THE DRIFT. A field reads 384 rows in 240 output lines,
    the renderer writes them in 384 native lines (41 us each), and those take
    different times: 15.1 kHz 15.89 ms against 15.74 (the read falls 3.6 rows
    behind), 15.4 kHz 15.54 (gains 5.0), 15.7 kHz 15.25 (gains 12.0). At 15.7
    the read must start ~12 rows behind and end just behind, so the ring holds
    those rows plus the two read and the one being written. A timing model
    (continuous rates, every read and write) and then the bench give the
    least ring per mode, two taps: 15.1 kHz 6 lines, 15.4 kHz 8, 15.7 kHz 15
    (14 places at no D_PX). Their 12 lines and four taps fit 15.1 only (the
    model reproduces their bench's 85.6 / 86.0 us margins exactly).
  * D_PX PER MODE (the delay from the native frame's first visible pixel to
    the first output line), each in the middle of its window: 5840 / 4310 /
    2490 output pixels at 15.7 / 15.4 / 15.1 kHz. One value cannot serve all
    three (at 15 lines: 15.7 needs 5430-5840, 15.1 4140 at most).
  * 24 BITS, NOT 16. 16-bit colour is not exact for this picture: the 3D is
    RGB565, but the 2D leaves the palette through the game's colour table and
    the gamma curve (m2_video, m2_palette), any 8 bits a channel. Storing the
    2D's 5-bit indices and colouring after the ring (17-18 bits) would need a
    second copy of the table and the curve: rejected as more logic.
  * 16 LINES, NOT 15. 15 x 512 x 24 bits packed as 20 bits in 512 x 20 blocks
    plus 4 in 8192 x 1 is 19 M10K, and quartus_map put a 115-ALUT read mux
    behind it (15:1, 20 bits); 16 lines in one array is 2048 x 5 blocks four
    deep, 20 M10K and a 28-ALUT mux, and doubles the margin (20 -> 40 us). At
    99% ALM the logic is the scarcer resource. 15 lines in one array is also
    20 M10K (2048 x 5 holds 6,144 a slice).
  * Not taken: the light-gun beacon (GunCon parked), the field-order switch.
  * READING THE 3D FROM DDR3 instead of storing it: no saving -- the ring
    holds the mixed picture, and the 2D half alone is 24 bits after gamma; a
    second scan-out of the framebuffer would add a DDR3 port and buffers.

*OSD:* "Video" (O[42]) unchanged, 15 kHz is now the converted picture;
"15kHz lines" (O[61:60]) kept; "15kHz width" (R834, O[55]) REMOVED -- it
lengthened the 1:1 picture's line; the converter has one 656-pixel line in
every mode (a narrow line there needs its own length, sync and alignment per
mode -- not built), so the ~4% shorter picture at 15.7 on a fixed-height set
is back. O[55] is reserved and must not be reused (a saved Narrow would turn
on whatever took it).

*Checked:* tb_m2_scan15 (ported from theirs; 140 native frames, every line
count, image cadence 2 in both phases, 3, 1 and none): every output pixel
against a first-principles blend of one native frame's rows; the two ring
words of each pixel are the rows asked for; the row fraction steps 4m mod 5;
hsync 64 px, 496 visible, 656 a line, 240 lines a field; every vsync interval
exactly one native frame and field 1's picture half a line (328 px) lower;
the re-alignment a no-op once locked (the pairing lock moves it once, at
native frame 17, in the phase that needs it); no output frame of two images
at cadence 2. 15 runs (3 line counts x cadence 2 phase 0 / 2 phase 1 / 3 /
1 / none), 140 native frames each: all PASS, 16,308,480 pixels a run, 0
blend, ring or row-step mismatches, 60 vsync intervals a run all exact.
Margins (written-before-read / read-before-overwritten): 15.7 kHz 40.6 /
41.4 us, 15.4 kHz 181.3 / 180.3, 15.1 kHz 210.4 / 210.3. At 15 lines (D_PX
5630) 20.3 / 20.7 us, PASS; at 14 lines it fails at D_PX 5430, 5630 and
5840 (rows overwritten before they are read). Mutations caught: row s+1 not
clamped on the last line (2,976 pixels), weights swapped (1,306,464), field 1
started on row 0's fraction (571,392). lint_top (and -DM2_NO_VCOP_GUN) clean;
lint_idx has no converter entries; Quartus parses m2_scan15.

*Cost (quartus_map, whole design, against s1142's map of the same RTL):*
"ALMs needed" 40,417 -> 40,537 (+120); ALUT 57,774 -> 57,879 (+105);
registers +101; DSP 88 -> 94 (+6: three x3277, three 8 x 5 products); block
memory bits +196,608 = the ring, 2048 x 5 four deep: 20 M10K, so 533 -> 553
of 553 expected (the fitter confirms). m2_scan15 is 205 ALUT / 129 registers
(28 of them the read mux); the retired path gives back ~170 ALUT; the i960
moved +71 ALUT with no RTL change (synthesis noise -- an earlier map of a
near-identical converter read +101 ALM in all).

*At risk, not verified:* THE FIT. s1142 placed 41,455 ALM from 40,417 in
map; the same ratio puts this near 41,580, where R848's s1144-s1146 needed
4,196-4,201 LABs of 4,191. M10K would be 100%. If it does not fit, the
levers in order of cost: a seed sweep; RING 15 with the 20 + 4 split (one
M10K back, ~+87 ALUT -- worse for the fit); dropping 268/269 (~-10 ALUT);
MISTER_DEBUG_NOHDMI (retrorepair's; Ben has ruled it out). The board and a
CRT: not seen.

*Consequences:*
  * R872 (the luma fix, ~9 M10K) can no longer be had from free M10K on main:
    with the converter main is at 553 / 553. It needs blocks freed elsewhere,
    or the converter limited to 15.1 / 15.4 kHz (8 lines: 2048 x 5 two deep,
    10 M10K) -- which R840 argues against.
  * MODEL 2A (0 M10K spare, ~98-99% ALM) needs the same 20 M10K and ~+120
    ALM net found there before this can merge in working order; the merge
    main -> model2a carries the RTL and the OSD unchanged (model2a's Model2.sv
    has the same 1:1 path, VGA_F1 = vid_field).

**R899 -- VIRTUA COP'S AMMO DISPLAY IS A 3D REVOLVER IN A LATER WINDOW, NOT A
TEXTURE; THIS CORE SORTED BY z ALONE AND HID IT UNDER THE SCENE. FIXED: THE
WINDOW IS THE TOP OF THE SORT KEY, FOR VIRTUA COP ONLY (the 2A branch's R889,
ported).** (Ben, Model2_20261016: "the bullets show but do not update when
you fire -- it always looks full"; R890.)

*Believed (R890, HANDOFF):* run-time texture updates -- the i960 rewriting
the bullets in texture RAM per shot -- not reaching what the renderer
samples (a stale texel cache or copy); the lead from model2a R889 was a
stale object pointer or polygon data in the walker.

*Measured (MAME 0.289 vcopa, build/mame289-mip; a scripted game -- coin 40 s,
start 41.5 s, a shot at 52 s picks the stage, play from ~54.3 s -- shots,
write taps on texture RAM, luma, tile / char RAM, palette, buffer RAM, the
geometrizer and the TGP FIFO; M2GEO walks 1728 / 1843 and 35 more at 1 s
spacing 55-89 s; M2DIFF frames 1172 / 1287 = walks 1728 / 1843):*
  1. THE AMMO DISPLAY IS A REVOLVER CYLINDER, bottom left: 13 polygons from
     POLYGON ROM, ONE OBJECT PER ROUND COUNT -- six rounds oba 0x80e588 /
     tha 0x5384 / tpa 0x5a47e, five 0x80e65b / 0x53d0 / 0x5a526, three
     0x80e801 / 0x5468 / 0x5a676 -- under a rotation matrix that turns a
     chamber a shot. Six side faces (h0 0x4009), six translucent chamber faces
     (0x6009, texture (0,0) sheet 1: the empty chambers) and ONE translucent
     quad for the loaded rounds whose texture position IS the count (h1/h2
     7001/1900 six, 0801/1980 five, 0401/1882 three -- (0,128), (0,192),
     (64,64)). It is the list's last object group, after its fifth
     window_data: WINDOW 5, z bucket 45,635. The scene is window 1, z buckets
     17,040-40,601 (lists 1172, 1287). It also flies in large and full at a
     stage's start (54.3-54.6 s), still at z 45,185-45,635.
  2. NOTHING ELSE CHANGES PER SHOT: no texture RAM write in play (the only
     writes are the stage load, 54.26-54.41 s), no luma, palette or tile write
     that tracks the shots; the i960 writes no buffer RAM (the list comes from
     the TGP, fed through the FIFO). Only the list's object addresses and the
     matrix change.
  3. OUR WALKER AND GEOMETRY ARE RIGHT. geodiff_ra (the core's walker,
     read-ahead and geometry) on walks 1728 / 1843: the bullets' quad comes
     out with tex 0x301113 (five: texy 6, texx 0, sheet 1) and 0x105113
     (three: texy 2, texx 2) -- MAME's headers -- at key 0xb243 = 45,635.
     No stale object, pointer, polygon datum or texture.
  4. THE RASTERISER HIDES IT. tb_m2_raster3d, the core configuration (FTB,
     PXC, FRB 2, M2COV, SPLIT_TRI, FB_DDR3 + wcomb, TXLATE 3, TXNS / TXRSP 4,
     TXK 16, TXLW8, MIP 1, MIPZ 3, PXK 0), MAME's lists: the revolver is NOT
     DRAWN AT ALL -- the ground (window 1, nearer by z) wins every pixel under
     it. Drawn alone, the same RTL draws it exactly, five and three rounds.
     Over the 35 sampled walks (25 with the revolver; MAME's counts six and
     five, auto-reload on), 0 of its ~2,500 pixels survive in any of them.
     MAME draws window by window, last first (render_polygons), first write
     winning, so window 5 is in front of window 1 whatever the z -- R889's
     finding on Virtua Cop 2, the same mechanism on Virtua Cop.

*So "shows but always full" is NOT reproduced:* on the bench this core never
shows the revolver in play, full or otherwise. INFERRED, not settled: Ben
saw it where the scene did not cover the bottom left (a scene, angle or
moment not sampled here -- the fly-in is full by definition), or saw
something else as the bullets. The board settles it; nothing found on the
path (walker, read-ahead, texel cache, texture RAM) holds a stale picture.

*The fix (R889's, ported; on main as the 2A branch has it, plus a run-time
gate):* m2_geo counts window_data per walk (cur_window = 0 at the walk's
start, saturating at 15) and latches it with each object (obj_win);
m2_geometry WINKEY puts {15 - window, z} in q_z[19:0]; m2_raster3d / the
quad store sort a 20-bit key (KW 20, five radix passes, the first started in
idx_b so the fifth lands in the bank -- R889's ODDP). SELECTED AT RUN TIME
FOR VIRTUA COP ONLY (Model2.sv wk_en = is_vcop, registered): for Daytona and
Desert Tank obj_win is held at 15 (the nibble is 0) and the store's new
key_hi input low runs the old four passes starting in the bank -- the 16-bit
sort exactly, in the same cycles. M2_NO_WINKEY builds KW 16 (the old core).

*Evidence:*

    MAME's pixels of that window (the scene's ~40-48 is R872's luma model,
    still open):
        list 1172 (five rounds): revolver 80.4 -> 51.9, scene 47.6 = 47.6
        list 1287 (three rounds): revolver 92.9 -> 45.3; the window-2
          overlay (42 flat polygons, z 17,322) 7.0 -> 0.6; scene and

      The revolver now shows five and three rounds, as MAME (bench crops).

      cycles): the revolver drawn, and the fifth pass.
  - geodiff (new geodiff_wk target) on walks 1728 / 1843: our quads

    5). geodiff_ra with the key off: ours.txt byte-identical to the old RTL.
  - Daytona and Desert Tank, the KW 20 bench with the key off (the core's

**R905 (main) -- THE SAME BURST-REGION FIX ON THE ORIGINAL MODEL 2 CORE.**
i960_memmap is shared, and main carried the same range: texture RAM + mirrors
ended at 0x12600000, so sheet 1's mirror 0x12600000-0x127FFFFF was not a burst
region and a multi-word store there wrote all its words to its first address.
The full finding (MAME write tap against the whole-core bench, Dynamite Cop)
is R905 on branch model2a, where the stripes were seen. Daytona, Desert Tank
and Virtua Cop show no stripes on the board, so they either do not upload
through that mirror or not with stq; the range is MAME's
(model2_tgp_mem: both sheets .mirror(0x200000) with BURST) either way, and
the core should match it. Not fitted on main at the time of writing.

**R907 (main) -- AREA FOR THE RELEASE: ~820 ALM BACK, NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED.**
main-next (2cebd70: scan15 R898 + Virtua Cop's window key R899 + R905) no
longer fitted reliably: s1254-s1256 needed 4,192-4,194 LABs of 4,191, and
s1249/s1250 fitted at 41,463 / 41,910 ALM with clk_sys -3.4 / -2.1 ns. The
worst clk_sys paths in s1249 (m2_geo_engine xhalf / m2_eng_ra data ->
poly_uv*, -3.29 ns) are ONE LUT deep with 10.8 ns of interconnect -- the
fitter's congestion at 100% LABs, not logic depth -- so the lever is
area, not a register on the path (R848: at 99% the area such fixes add costs
more than the margin they buy). Decisions rest on section 7 Tier 1 (no
accuracy loss) and section 5.6 (M10K is spent: 553/553, so nothing here may
take a block). Measured with quartus_map (17.0, same QSF), whole design,
"Estimate of Logic utilization (ALMs needed)":

    2cebd70 (main-next)                         40,579
    + viewport converter shared (4c0117a)       40,310   -269
    + xlat table in three MLABs (d741e1a)       39,761   -549
    total                                                 -818

  1. m2_geo_view: SIX int-to-float units in parallel (575 ALUT; 290.6 ALM
     placed in s1250) for six values that change once an object. One unit now
     visits the six slots in turn (one subtractor, one sign/magnitude, one
     encode); each output is rewritten every 6 cycles and right within 8 of
     its inputs changing (was 3). Values bit for bit the same. 140 ALUT.
     Verified: test_m2_geo_view PASS (window() now ticks 8, and FAILS at 7 --
     the bound is tight); geodiff_ra on four MAME walks (w1000, w2300, w5000,
     w8000; M2GD_POOLHASH, M2GD_STATE): pool hash (every FP operand on every
     unit, every cycle) and ours.txt identical to 2cebd70's. Margin: the same
     walks are still identical with the converter slowed to one slot per 64
     cycles (~390 cycles of latency), and differ only at one per 65,536 --
     the bench sees the view, and 8 cycles is far inside what the walk allows
     (R760: the walk waits for the geometry to go idle between objects).
  2. m2_video's colour translation table was NEVER A RAM. R564 described it
     as "an MLAB written on clk_sys, read asynchronously on clk_mem", and it
     was not: one 96-entry array read at three addresses at once, Quartus
     built it as 768 flip-flops and three 32:1 x 8 read muxes (no RAM-inference
     message at all; lint_idx flagged it every time as "pre-existing"). Split
     into one 32 x 8 array per channel (one read port each), tagged MLAB:
     three dual-clock altdpram LUTRAMs, written on clk_sys, read into the same
     x_r/x_g/x_b registers on clk_mem; the power-up pal5bit table is honoured
     (initialised from a MIF, checked: entry 31 = 0xFF). Quartus absorbs
     pal_data_q[4:0] as the read-address register, so the lookup's latency is
     unchanged. Addresses 96-127 wrote nothing before (outside the array) and
     write nothing now. Warning 276023 ("functionality differs") is the
     cross-clock read-during-write, old or new data -- what R564 already said
     of it. Cost: three LABs. Verified: new bench test_m2_video_xlat (the
     2cebd70 m2_video beside the new one, the same hashed tile/glyph/palette
     data, random table writes 0-127 on a second clock after a frame on the
     power-up table): 7.6 M cycles, 0 differences in pixel, syncs or palette
     address; two deliberate faults (channel 3 into blue, one wrong power-up
     entry) each fail it by over a million cycles. test_m2_video_timing,
     _ovr and _r826 pass. lint_top clean; lint_idx no longer lists m2_video.

Considered and not done:
  - poly_uv* path (-3.29 ns): a register after the half select would move
    the uv writes a cycle; not needed if the area relieves the congestion,
    and R848 says such registers lose at 99%. Re-measure after the fit.
  - m2_recip_rom to M10K (~150 ALM, its read is already registered) -- no
    free M10K; the candidates for freeing two (ioboard DPRAM as TDP, loader
    FIFO merged) touch paths with board-found bugs behind them (R65, the
    loader's byte lanes) for one or two blocks each.
  - i960_top's write-back mux (336:1, ~1,800 ALUT after restructuring) and
    the FPU units: real area, but CPU semantics; not without the lockstep.
  - debug counters (dbg_mtx_n, dbg_walk_objs, ...): present in the post-map
    netlist but marked "dangling" and swept by the fitter (s1250's emu has
    ~2,300 fewer registers than its map) -- nothing to gain.
  - sys/ (two OSDs ~930 ALM, pll_hdmi_adj ~436): the framework's; HDMI and
    the analog output (scan15) both need theirs.
Map numbers are estimates; the fit decides. Not fitted at the time of writing.

*THE BLOCKER, M10K.* The 2A core fitted at 553 / 553 RAM blocks (s1240,
4,467,189 bits). The ring is 16 lines x 512 x 24 = 2048 x 5 blocks four deep,
20 M10K, which R898 itself said the 2A core would need found before this
could work. A per-RAM count from the map's RAM summary (each array's best
M10K shape) gives 544 before and 564 after; it reads ~9 below the fitter's
553 on the same netlist, so the merged design needs ~573: the fitter will
refuse it. NOT FIXED HERE (Ben's rule: nothing but R898 and R907). The
levers, a study-level decision, cheapest first (estimates, unmeasured):
  1. Small arrays that occupy a whole M10K each, into MLAB, paid from the
     717 ALM above: m2_geo_clip's 20 x 163 (5 blocks, 3,260 bits),
     m2_raster3d's span queue 32 x 260 (7 blocks, 8,320 bits), and the 2A
     sound board's small arrays (128 x 1, two 16 x 32, two 64 x 11, 32 x 24,
     128 x 16, 128 x 24, the 128 x 27 ROM: 9 blocks, ~16 kbit). An MLAB is
     32 x 20 in one LAB (10 ALM): 9 + 13 + 34 LABs, ~560 ALM for 21 blocks
     -- most of what R907 gave back; a better-packed candidate list is the
     first thing to look for.
  2. RING 8 (15.1 and 15.4 kHz only): 10 M10K back, but R840 found most
     sets take only 15.7 kHz.
A fit of this merge is still worth one seed to confirm the count.

**R909 -- 27 M10K BACK ON THE 2A CORE, NOTHING IT COMPUTES CHANGED: THE
SCSP's LFO TABLE FACTORED (18 -> 4), NO SHIFT-REGISTER RAMs IN THE CORE (6),
THREE SMALL ARRAYS OUT OF M10K (7). ~573 -> ~546 OF 553 BLOCKS. NOT FITTED.**
(Branch m2a-scan15, on R908's merge f7437e2. Section 5.6 governs: M10K, not
ALM, binds this core once the 15 kHz ring is in. Ben's rule: every 2A fix
survives; the converter keeps its 16 lines, R840.)

*How it was counted.* The fitter's own per-RAM "M10K blocks" column, from the
last 2A fit with this RAM set (s1267, 553 / 553; s1240 has the same 4,467,189
bits), is the price of each array as the fitter really builds it -- which is
not the best shape: it takes 16,384 x 9 as 8192 x 1 slices (18 blocks, not
16) and 8192 x 64 as 64. Those columns sum to 569 on s1267, 16 above the 553
physical blocks, because the fitter packs some RAMs into shared blocks (15
shared locations: uce/ucf, lbe/lbo, uvt/vtx, ln_d/ln_t, the loader FIFOs);
none of the arrays below is among them, so each block here is a physical
block. The converter costs 20 (main's s1264). So the merge needs 573, and:

    array (2A build)                          s1267 blocks   now
    m2_scsp lfo_rom 16,384 x 9                       18       4 (4,096 x 9, max_depth 2048)
    mb86233_alu pop..pxd shift taps 3 x 115           3       0 (registers)
    emu status synchronizers 3 x 15 (texoff_s..)      1       0 (registers)
    m2_fp_pool fp_add p_exp.. 3 x 12                   1       0 (registers)
    m2_span_tex lp2..lp4 4 x 43 (+3 MLAB cells)        1       0 (registers)
    m2_scsp wq 4 x 29                                  1       0 (registers, ramstyle logic)
    m2_span_tex of_x 16 x 16                           1       0 (one MLAB)
    m2_geo_clip sk_mem 20 x 163                        5       0 (nine MLABs)
                                                      31       4   -> 27 freed, ~546 / 553

The map's own per-RAM estimate (each array at its best shape, from the RAM
summary) reads 564 -> 538, -26: it prices the old LFO ROM at 16 and the
lp2..lp4 taps at 2.

*quartus_map 17.0, the whole 2A design, each commit (ALMs needed / ALUT /
registers / block bits):*

    f7437e2 (R908 merge)      39,716  57,025  47,171  4,663,810
    365b088 LFO               39,718  57,022  47,170  4,553,218
    968ddd7 no shift taps     39,896  57,067  47,775  4,552,608
    4457cb2 small arrays      40,062  57,150  47,947  4,548,976
                                +346    +125    +776   -114,834

Still 371 ALM below model2a 75ee3a2 (40,433): R907 paid for it. (The map's
ALM figure is an estimate; the LFO alone read +42 in a run without
max_depth, +2 with it.)

*1. The LFO table (365b088).* R858 baked the four LFO waves into one ROM,
{sel, LFOS, LFOWS, phase >> 8} -> 9 bits, 16,384 words. The waves are MAME's
formulas (saw, square, triangle) and one 256-entry noise table, and the
table factors exactly into them and the two scale tables: entry =
PSCALES-flat[LFOS * 256 + wave + 128] for pitch -- read flat, as MAME's
pointer reads it, so the noise wave's 128 - 0 = 256 is the next row's first
and past PSCALES[7] is ASCALES[0][0] -- and ASCALES[LFOS][wave] for
amplitude. So m2_scsp_lfo (in m2_scsp.sv) computes the wave in logic from
tadr and reads a 4,096 x 9 ROM (scsp_lfoscale.hex, PSCALES then ASCALES);
the noise is a case function (scsp_lfonoise.svh). tadr is a register that
feeds nothing else, so the logic sits between it and the block's address
register and tbl_q keeps its latency. scsp_tables_gen.cpp writes both files
(with MAME's tables.bin, from the Rally capture: every other output it
writes is byte-identical to the committed files, and so was its old
scsp_lfo.hex, before the change); scsp_lfo.hex is gone. max_depth 2048
(MAXIMUM_DEPTH in the map's parameters) makes it two by two 2048 x 5 blocks
and a 9-bit 2:1 mux on tbl_q, where the fitter left free takes no-mux
shapes -- 4096 x 2 x 5, five, as it took 8192 x 1 slices for the old ROM.
  * test_m2_scsp_lfo (new): the module against f7437e2's scsp_lfo.hex (from
    git), every tadr in order then 4,000,000 random, each standing at one
    edge: 4,016,384 clocks, 0 fails; the old ROM against MAME's tables

*2. No shift-register RAMs in the core (968ddd7).* Quartus's shift-register
recognition (default Auto) had made altshift_taps M10K of four groups of
short register chains, merged across modules: the status synchronizers in
Model2.sv with m2_cab_inputs' (texoff_s, mip_s*, vol_s*, boost_s*, rsteer_s
...: 3 x 15, a synchronizer in block RAM), the TGP ALU's result pipeline with
its fp_add / fp_mul flags (3 x 115, 3 blocks), the geometry pool's fp_add
exponent / fp_mul flags (3 x 12) and m2_span_tex's lp2..lp4 stage (4 x 43).
`(* altera_attribute = "-name AUTO_SHIFT_REGISTER_RECOGNITION OFF" *)` on
module emu turns it off for the whole core (quartus_map: all four gone, 598
bits; sys/'s five stay, the framework keeps the default). An attribute: the
RTL and every simulation are untouched; the netlist holds the registers the
RTL describes. +178 ALM, +605 registers.

*3. Three small arrays (4457cb2).* of_x (16 x 16) MLAB, one LAB; wq (4 x
29, read asynchronously) ramstyle "logic" -- as MLAB Quartus uninfers it
anyway ("unsupported read-during-write"); sk_mem back to MLAB, which R332
had and R684 reversed for LABs when M10K was free -- on the 2A core with
the ring it is not. Attributes only; Quartus's uninferred-RAM list grows by
wq alone (a ramstyle "logic" note).

*REJECTED, MEASURED:*
  * rfa / rfb (the SCSP's 16 x 32 register file copies) and the DSP's mems
    (32 x 24) to MLAB, ~2 LABs a block, looked like the next cheapest. It
    took quartus_map from 39,881 to 44,310 ALM and +8,396 registers: an
    MLAB takes its read-address register into itself, rfa's is a field of
    uf (ucf's read register) and mems' is IRA in ins (mpro's), and ucf
    (256 x 41) and mpro (128 x 64) were "uninferred due to asynchronous
    read logic" -- both into logic. Both arrays stay M10K, with a comment
    saying why. A ramstyle change is NOT local: check the map's uninferred
    list for arrays you did not touch.
  * m2_char_cache's cdata (8192 x 64 at 64 blocks, 52 at 2048 x 5) by
    max_depth 2048: 12 blocks for a 64-bit 4:1 mux, but it is on clk_mem
    (100 MHz), which s1268 missed by 0.048 ns. Kept in reserve.
  * the TGP program store (4096 x 32, 16 -> 14 at max_depth 2048): a 2:1
    mux on the copro's fetch, clk_sys, which no 2A seed has met cleanly.
  * span_q (32 x 260, 7 blocks) to MLAB: 13 LABs; R684's reason (LABs) is
    the one that still holds. Not needed.
  * the ring at 8 lines (R908's lever 2): not needed, and R840.

**R911 -- DEAD OR ALIVE'S "WRONG TEXTURES ON SCENERY" (s1259) ARE THE
CORE'S MIP LEVELS, WHICH MAME NEVER DRAWS FOR THIS GAME: R828c's NO-MIP FLAG
ASSUMED DAYTONA'S lod AND coef. THE FLAG NOW TAKES THE GAME'S OWN
(coef_table[attr >> 27] AND THE 0x16 lod) FOR THE LARGE LAYOUT'S GAMES --
R905's HELD-BACK RTL (r905-mipz), ITS TABLE ONE MLAB INSTEAD OF 384
FLIP-FLOPS. NOT FITTED, NOT ON A BOARD.**
(Ben, s1259 = 485bd44, R905 on the board: Dynamite Cop, Sky Target and Motor
Raid's stripes gone, "all others seem fine"; Dead or Alive "still has a
couple of wrong textures on scenery" -- the courtyard stage's flagstone
floor with square patches unlike their neighbours (darker, blurred blobs,
another picture), the same on the buildings; the characters right. The OSD's
Mip-mapping setting for the picture is not known.)

*Believed (the task):* a texture-RAM write path R905 did not cover (another
mirror, another store width, a non-burst region), sheet selection, the mip
level, the luma / format path, or the large layout.

*THE WRITE PATH IS NOT IT (MAME 0.289 m2lod, a write tap on 0x12000000-
0x1281FFFF, doaab from power-on, 110 s of attract, 2,218,333 stores):* every
texture store Dead or Alive makes is an stq (IPs 0x7559c / 0x755ac, mask
0xffffffff) through the two sheets' MIRRORS -- 0x122/0x123 (sheet 0,
982,016) and 0x126/0x127 (sheet 1, 1,218,909) -- plus one luma clear at
0x132c (16,384, frame 59). Uploads at frames 1019-1200 and again at every
stage change (2100-6600). Both mirrors are burst regions since R905, which
is what the game needs; nothing else writes texture RAM. THE CORE'S OWN
(tb_m2_boot A2X, this model2a's RTL, the MRA's image from rom_csum.py,
M2_TEXWLOG / M2_TEXDUMP): its first 671,623 texture and luma stores -- the
luma clear and the whole first upload, bench frames 136-1300 -- equal MAME's
in order, word and data (0 differ), and its sheets at bench frame 1500 equal
MAME's stores replayed to the same point on every word MAME wrote (262,144
of sheet 0, 393,216 of sheet 1: 0 differ). The rest -- 262,144 words of sheet
0 and 131,072 of sheet 1 -- the game never writes; the bench reads them
0xFFFF, MAME 0, the board whatever its SDRAM held. With Mip-mapping Off the
board's texels are MAME's.

*THE MIP LEVEL IS IT (tb_m2_raster3d, Model2.sv's 2A raster configuration,
M2_R3D_GAME=0x16, on MAME's frame of Ben's scene -- the gate courtyard,
Jann Lee and Lei Fang, m2lod frame 1780, ~46 s into the attract; MAME

     Off                      6.65    2.49%
     Sharp (the default)     21.23   17.01%   R828c flag set on 1341 of 1660 quads
     Medium                  33.44   26.40%

  (Sharp is the default and the least affected); with Off the core already
  draws MAME's picture (6.65, the same as the fix).

*THE FIX (R905's held-back commit 4f08e67, reworked):* m2_geo streams each
texture-parameter entry's distance coefficient (the second word, MAME's
coef_table[index]) and the 0x16 lod operand as twelve log bits (exponent and
four mantissa bits); m2_geometry keeps the 32 coefs and, with mz_exact
(Model2.sv: a2_big), forms the flag as 2 log z_far + 4176 < log |dotp| + log
coef[attr >> 27] + log lod + 2160 in sixteenths of a level -- MAME's own
level <= 0 over the whole polygon (MIPZ_BX 0). Daytona's coef 1.0 and lod 128
sum to R828c's constant, so the rules agree there; without mz_exact the flag
is R828c's bit for bit (VF2, Rally, Virtua Cop 2, Zero Gunner, Manx TT).
THE CHANGE FROM 4f08e67: the table is `(* ramstyle = "MLAB" *)`, one write
port and an asynchronous read on the polygon's attr[31:27] latched with the
polygon (m2_xf_mat's pattern) -- one MLAB, 384 bits, instead of 384
registers. Polygons whose MAME level is > 0 keep the core's own footprint
rule (R828) under the OSD setting.

**R912 -- MIP-MAPPING, GAME BY GAME (Ben: "check mip mapping on other games.
If not used in MAME remove it in our cores"). MAME DOES MIP: A REAL
TRILINEAR SAMPLE OF THE LEVELS IN THE SHEETS, AND EVERY GAME BUT DEAD OR
ALIVE (AND, NEARLY, VIRTUA COP 2) USES IT. WHAT IS WRONG IS WHERE THE CORE
MIPS: R828c's NO-MIP FLAG FOLDS IN DAYTONA'S lod 128 / coef 1.0, AND NO 2A
GAME BUT RALLY IS CLOSE TO THAT. THE 2A CORE NOW TAKES R911's RULE (MAME's
OWN LEVEL, FROM THE GAME'S coef TABLE AND lod) FOR EVERY GAME, NOT ONLY THE
LARGE LAYOUT. THE ORIGINAL CORE (main) IS MEASURED, NOT CHANGED. NOT
FITTED, NOT ON A BOARD.**

(Section: §10, R828 / R828c / R911. Authority: MAME 0.289 for what the
level is and how it is sampled; Model 1 has no mip.)

*Believed (the task):* MAME may compute a level and not sample it; several
games may never mip in MAME, as Dead or Alive does (R911), and the core
should then not mip them at any OSD setting.

*HOW MAME USES THE LEVEL (0.289, unmodified source):*
  * model2_v.cpp: geo_texture_parameters (op 0x06) keeps each entry's second
    word as coef_table[index]; geo_lod (op 0x16) sets geo->lod; each
    textured polygon pushes distance = coef_table[attr >> 27] * |dotp| *
    geo->lod (lines 1105-1108, the same in the other three polygon parsers);
    model2_3d_process_triangle turns it into object.texlod = ((cb[10] >> 8)
    & 0x7f80) - 0x3f80 + log_ram[cb[10] & 0x7fff] (429-430), i.e. 128
    log2(coef |dotp| lod).
  * model2rd.ipp draw_scanline_tex, per pixel (303-324): mml = -texlod +
    fast_log2(z) (256 log2 z); level = clamp(mml >> 7, 0, max_level), max_level
    = 30 - clz(min(w, h)) (268, down to 2x2); fetch_bilinear_texel at that
    level, which reads sheet texsheet[L & 1] at ((x - 2048) >> L, (y - 1024)
    >> L), u, v >> L (132-138); and when mml > 0 and level < max_level it
    fetches level + 1 too and LERPs by (mml & 127) << 1 -- TRILINEAR. When
    mml < 0 and the polygon has a microtexture it blends that instead (up to
    ~50%). So a polygon with 0 < mml < 128 is "level 0" by MAME's integer
    but already up to 254/256 level 1.
  * The core (R828) does not do this: its level is the quad's edge
    footprint (nearest level, no blend), sharper or blurrier per the OSD,
    and R828c's flag forces level 0 where MAME's level, computed with
    Daytona's lod and coef, is at most -3 over the whole polygon.
