**R919 -- THE MODEL 2 FAMILY REVIEWED AGAIN, PART BY PART, AGAINST BOTH CORES:
docs/model2-family-hardware.md. R832 CORRECTED IN TEN PLACES; 2B AND 2C EACH
NEED ONE NEW PROCESSOR, NOT TWO; THE 2C GAP IS ~600-2,100 ALM, THE 2B GAP
~2,600-8,600. DOCUMENT ONLY, NO RTL.** (Ben: "Hardware of all models, review
again. Add a column in the tables with a green tick for done, otherwise add
what can be taken from the previous variants." Then: for 2B and 2C, what the
work done covers and what remains.)

*Method.* MAME 0.289's source (sm2-builds/mame-r869): model2.cpp machine
configs, memory maps and GAME() lines, model2_v.cpp, the devices (m2comm,
model1io, model1io2, 315_5649, 315-5881_crypt, 315-5838_317-0229_comp,
segabill, dsbz80, dsb2, shared/segam1audio) and the CPU cores (mb86233,
mb86235, sharc). The implementation by `git grep` / `git show` on main
(b0c1790) and model2a (8e40e35), nothing checked out over the open tree;
module sizes from s1248's fitter report (a 2A build). Every row of the
document names the module and the R entry, or what to take from where.

*Believed (R832), and what changed -- VERIFIED from the source unless marked:*
  1. COMMON PARTS. R832 listed the i960, tilemap, renderer, timers, video
     timing and comms as common. Also common, and missing there: 1 MB of work
     RAM at 0x00500000, the 128 KB geometry buffer RAM at 0x00900000, the
     16 KB battery-backed backup SRAM at 0x01d00000 (NVRAM, powers up 0xFF),
     the interrupt controller, the palette / colour tables. R832's "128 KB
     work RAM at 0x200000" (original) and "256 KB work RAM" (2A) are the BOARD
     RAM beside it.
  2. THE SOUND UART. Every board has the uPD71051 (i8251) the i960 talks to
     its sound board through: 0x01c80000 on the original, 2A and 2C;
     0x009c0000 on 2B (one byte per dword).
  3. THE ORIGINAL I/O BOARD also carries a 315-5338A and its own 93C45 EEPROM
     (model1io.cpp, 837-8950-01; Z80 at 32 / 8 MHz). Virtua Cop's type-2
     board (837-11130 + 837-11131) adds an FPGA for the guns, 4 KB backup RAM
     and a diagnostic LCD.
  4. MANX TT'S MODEL 1 SOUND BOARD. R832: "manxttdx also carries a Model 1
     sound board". MAME's `manxttdx` CONFIG holds both `manxtt` (Revision D,
     the parent, "defaults to DX mode") and `manxttdx`; only manxttc and
     Motor Raid use `manxtt`. So the set the 2A beta plays is, in MAME, the
     board WITH the extra sound board -- the release notes' "a few extra
     sounds are missing".
  5. THE GEOMETRIZER ON 2B AND 2C. R832 (cont.): "MAME uses a high-level C
     version of the geometrizer for original and 2A games". It uses it for
     EVERY board: geo_prg_w on 2B / 2C counts the uploaded geometrizer words
     and drops them, and model2_v.cpp's plan to run the real DSP for 2B / 2C
     is not done in 0.289. So "2x SHARC" / "2x TGPx4" is one coprocessor
     running the game's code plus a geometrizer m2_geometry already covers to
     MAME's degree. R832's "each a large new CPU core" stands, as ONE core per
     board. Exception, from model2_v.cpp's notes: Top Skater's geometry code
     has a second transformation matrix MAME's HLE lacks.
  6. 2B AND 2C MEMORY MAPS. Not in R832: texture RAM at 0x11000000 (sheet 0)
     and 0x11200000 (sheet 1) as plain 32-bit RAM (2B maps 1 MB twice, 2C
     2 MB) instead of 2A's 16-bits-per-dword windows at 0x12000000 /
     0x12400000 (tex0_w); luma RAM at 0x11400000 with umask16 0x00ff instead
     of 0x12800000 umask32 0x000000ff; copro status at 0x00980014 (Sonic the
     Fighters); 2B's SHARC IOP at 0x008c0000 and bank register 0x00980020;
     2B's FIFOs 16 deep with empty / full on the SHARC's FLAG0 / FLAG1 (8 on
     the TGP and TGPx4). The SHARC boots from the host: 16-bit words by
     external DMA. The TGPx4's program is 4 K x 64, uploaded as word pairs.
  7. GAME LISTS. 2B is missing INDY 500 (its own `indy500` config, three
     sets), Over Rev Model 2B (indy500 config) and Dynamite Cop / Deka 2
     Model 2B (model2b_5881). 2C is missing Sega Touring Car Championship
     (`stcc`, four sets, with the Z80 Digital Sound Board: MPEG-1 Layer II,
     8 MB) and Dynamite Cop USA Model 2C (model2c_5881); Top Skater carries
     the 68000 DSB2 (16 MB MPEG). The original's list omits the turbo hacks
     daytonat / daytonata (daytona config, not working).
  8. THE BILLBOARD is on 2A and 2B only: MAME's model2c has no SEGA_BILLBOARD.
     It is the Versus City board 837-11854 (Z80 at 8 MHz, 315-5338A, four
     7-segment digits).
  9. THE DRIVE BOARD. R832 has it on Daytona and Sega Rally (right). Not in
     R832: MAME runs its Z80 but leaves the motor output unconnected
     (driveio_port_w: "TODO: hook up"), so there is no reference for force
     feedback. Rail Chase 2 has its own Z80 + CXD1095 drive I/O board
     (837-11694), answered only far enough to pass its checks.
 10. "ROMs FIT" (R832: vf2 47.2 MB) held for VF2 only. Raw ROM by MAME's
     ROM_STARTs: 2A 26.5 (Air Walkers) to 90.5 MB (Dynamite Cop) -- six of
     the eleven beta games need the 128 MB module (R887, R891, R897); 2B 27.6
     to 90.5; 2C 33.6 to 90.5 (House of the Dead 84.5, Water Ski 90.5).
  Also recorded, not a correction: in MAME 0.289 every 2C set is
  MACHINE_NOT_WORKING, and on 2B only Virtua Striker, Gunblade NY, Rail
  Chase 2, DOA 2B, Zero Gunner 2B and Pilot Kids 2B are not. Why was not
  checked (R832's warning about the flag applies: five 2A sets MAME flags
  play on the 2A core).

*Implementation findings on the way (VERIFIED by reading the branches):*
  * The 2A core's 93C46 is never saved: m2_93c46's header says persistence
    "is not here yet", and the OSD save (upload index 2) is the backup SRAM
    alone. INFERRED: GitHub #15 (Sega Rally doesn't save its settings) is
    this. Not checked on a board.
  * Main's textured colour is still Daytona's fixed luma model (R872 open);
    the fix is 2A's m2_luma_map + TEXLUT (R867 / R900), ~9 M10K, against
    main's 553 / 553. GitHub #10's "inaccurate colors" fits it.
  * MAME 0.289's own TODO lists the Virtua Cop 2 stage-select tilemap
    priority fault -- the same screen as GitHub #16.
  * Neither core has the comm board; branch link-play (R916) has it for
    Daytona, not merged. Neither has the drive boards, the billboard, the
    lamps, or microtexture (Desert Tank, R912).

*THE 2B / 2C GAP (INFERRED estimates -- nothing written or mapped).* The 2A
core (s1278): 41,389 / 41,910 ALM (521 free), 547 / 553 M10K (6 free). The
TGP board it would give up (s1248: m2_copro with m2_tgp): 2,867 ALM, 24
M10K, 1 DSP; its MB86233 core 2,413 ALM. Scaled from that by each ISA's
breadth (MAME interpreter lines as a rough proxy: MB86233 1,231, MB86235
~1,840, SHARC ~6,300):
  * MB86235 (2C): ~4,000-5,500 ALM; program 4 K x 64 (~26-32 M10K) + RAM A /
    B 2 x 1 K x 32 (~8): ~34-40 M10K. Net +1,100-2,600 ALM, +10-16 M10K:
    over by ~600-2,100 ALM and ~4-10 M10K. R909's reserve (char cache 12,
    span_q 7 M10K) covers the blocks; the ALM needs R818's texel levers or
    the 15 kHz ring. At 20 MHz it has 4 clk_sys per instruction. Reusable:
    fp_add / fp_mul (SUBNORM), fp_div, m2_fifo_m10k, m2_copro's i960 side,
    m2_geo_rsqrt / m2_recip_rom for FRCP / FRSQ, the tgp_replay harness. New:
    decoder, sequencer (delay slots, 4-deep PC stack, repeat), address units,
    register files, the PR queue. Section 5.4.1 says nothing about the
    MB86235; it is not the MB86233.
  * ADSP-21062 (2B): ~6,000-12,000 ALM; its 2 Mbit RAM is 205 M10K and must
    go to SDRAM / DDR3 behind caches (R859's pattern); 32 M instructions/s
    with two data accesses each is 2.5 clk_sys per instruction, a pipelined
    design. Net +3,100-9,100 ALM: over by ~2,600-8,600. Only the no-HDMI
    build (R818 item 8, -3,861) is a lever that size, and it is not a release.
  * Oracles: MAME's SHARC (BSD-3, Ville Linde; also Konami Hornet / NWK-TR)
    is mature; MAME's MB86235 (BSD-3) has open TODOs (illegal delay slots,
    FIFO hookups in the opcodes) and computes FRCP / FRSQ / FLOG with host
    maths. No open-source FPGA SHARC or MB86235 was found (web search,
    2026-10-21; absence of evidence). Model 1's reference has neither.
  * NOT MEASURABLE HERE: no 2B or 2C ROM is in ~/roms/Model2, so the SHARC's
    upload size, the 2B / 2C i960 FPU forms (R869's method) and whether the
    HLE geometrizer is enough per game are unknown. They are the first item
    of each board's remaining-work list in the document.

*Decision unchanged:* 2B and 2C stay documented only (Ben, R832). The
document's last section lists the remaining work for 2B, 2C, the original
core and the 2A core, in order, with sizes and the games each would bring.

**R914 -- DEAD OR ALIVE'S "CONSTANT BASS RUMBLE, THERE EVEN WHEN NO OTHER
SOUND" (Ben, s1278) IS THE SCSP DSP RUNNING WITH EVERY MADRS = 0: MAME 0.289
MIRRORS 0x7C0-0x7FF ONTO MADRS, EVERY 2A SOUND DRIVER WRITES 32 ZERO WORDS
THERE RIGHT AFTER ITS MADRS TABLE, AND OUR RTL COPIED THE MIRROR. DOA's
REVERB THEN SELF-OSCILLATES: A 21.5 / 43 / 87 / 173 / 217 Hz DRONE AT
-24 dBFS ON THE BOARD IN SILENCE, ON A DC THAT CLIMBS TO 85% OF FULL SCALE.
THE MIRROR IS GONE (writes there dropped, reads 0, as Mednafen's SCSP);
MAME's IS A PARAMETER FOR THE BENCHES; THE DSP's CACHE GOES 64 -> 256 LINES
(SAME M10K) SO VIRTUA COP 2's REAL REVERB KEEPS UP. NOT R909, NOT THE LARGE LAYOUT, NOT
SOUND-RAM CONTENTS. NOT FITTED.**

*Believed (the task):* something of ours, not MAME's -- R909's factored LFO
(never run on DOA), the large layout's sound-ROM mapping, or unwritten
sound RAM (0xFFFF on the board, 0 in MAME) feeding the DSP's ring.

*Measured (MAME 0.289 + p16, doaab, 150 s: attract to 90 s, a coin at 90 s;
sm2-builds/doa-rumble/build/scsp/doaab; replayed through scsp_ref.h -- 0 of
6,615,361 samples differ from MAME's out.bin -- with the mix taken apart into
the direct sends, per slot, and the DSP's EFREG; left channel, mix units,
DAC = >> 2):*
  1. THE RUMBLE IS IN MAME TOO, AND IN OUR RTL BIT FOR BIT. In 13-16 s of
     the attract no slot sounds (direct sends 0.4 RMS) and the mix is the
     DSP's EFREG 0 alone: a mean of +73,262 and 10,828 RMS of AC, all below
     300 Hz (bands 0-20 / 20-50 / 50-150 / 150-300 Hz: 1,239 / 5,667 /
     5,105 / 7,404; lines at 21.5, 43, 87.5, 173.5, 217 Hz -- 21.5 Hz =
     44,100 / 2,048). The DC on EFREG 0 climbs from 15,224 (3 s) to ~28,000
     (60 s on) of the register's +-32,768; the mix's mean from 46,701 to
     ~111,000 of the DAC's 131,072, where 0.13% of in-play samples clip.
     Through the board's path (DAC, Volume 80%, MiSTer's DC blocker): 2,154
     RMS 16-bit in that silence, -23.6 dBFS -- louder than the music's
     direct sends. MAME's listener hears less of it: its default Filters
     effect is a 20 Hz high-pass (emu/audio_effects/filter.cpp, fh 20),
     MiSTer's DC blocker a one-pole ~7 Hz one.
  2. NOT OURS ALONE: tb_m2_scsp on the DOA capture, model2a f4d6b53 (R909
     in): the whole 150 s, 0 differ from the reference and from MAME's mix
     (81,797,765 slot samples, 1,563,235 reads 0 wrong); pre-R909 75ee3a2:
     20 s, 0 / 0. R909 is not involved, and
     every 2A build (s1253 .. s1278) has the rumble.
  3. NOT SOUND-RAM CONTENTS: the reference with sound RAM filled 0xFFFF
     before the first write (the board's unwritten SDRAM): 0 samples differ
     over 150 s, with the mirror and without it (DOA 40 s, VF2 and Virtua
     Cop 2 60 s without it). The drivers write their rings before the DSP
     reads them -- and m2_2a_sound zeroes all 256 K words before the 68000
     starts (V_ZR) anyway.
  4. NOT THE LARGE LAYOUT: DOA's MRA places epr-19328 at 0x24C0000 and
     mpr-19329..19332 at 0x2540000 (moved by XTRA to byte 0x3400000), as
     VF2's (R882's sums); the sound RAM (byte 0x2580000) sits in the hole no
     layout loads; the large layout's extra regions start at MRA 0x32C0000.
  5. THE CAUSE. The DSP program (dsp.txt, START at n 143,499: 58 steps,
     RBP 0x38, RBL 32 K words) is a reverb: 12 memory reads and 4 writes at
     MADRS 1..12, comb / all-pass loops of gain 0.87-0.9998. At its START
     all 32 MADRS read 0. regs.bin: the 68000 writes COEF 0x700-0x77E, the
     MADRS table 0x780-0x7BE (0x0000 0x3007 0x2bff 0x52c0 0x33c0 0x43dc
     0x55e3 0x3e16 0x3ce1 0x3ce4 0x4c96 0x4bba 0x4b6f, 0 ...), then 32 zero
     words 0x7C0-0x7FE, then MPRO. MAME's scsp.cpp maps 0x7C0-0x7FF onto
     MADRS again ("MADRS is mirrored twice"), so the zeros overwrite the
     table; m2_scsp_dsp did the same (w_madrs to 0x400). Every tap then
     reads and writes the same ring word (DEC alone): the loops close on
     themselves and the program becomes an oscillator with a DC integrator.
     THE OTHER 2A DRIVERS DO THE SAME: VF2 (writes 0x7C0-0x7FF 64 times,
     after its table), Virtua Cop 2 (32), Zero Gunner (864, its 0x7C2 zero
     later than its 0x782 = 0x2ffe), Sega Rally (128; it runs no DSP
     program). All five games' DSPs run with MADRS 0 in MAME and in s1278.
  6. THE MIRROR IS MAME's GUESS, NOT THE SILICON'S. It came in with MAME
     0caa890cca (R. Belmont, 2014-02-26, "Array bounds patrol (nw)"): MADRS
     was u16[32] written for 0x780-0x7FF, so 0x7C0-0x7FF ran past it into
     the struct's next field (MPRO, which the driver then rewrites) -- the
     table survived. The bounds fix chose a mirror; nothing says it was
     measured. Mednafen's SCSP (ss/scsp.inc; read for the fact, no code
     taken) decodes MADRS at 0x780-0x7BF only: writes to 0x7C0-0x7FF fall
     through and are dropped, reads give 0. MASA is 5 bits, so 32 MADRS
     are all a program can name (not checked here: what the Saturn manual
     says of 0x7C0). And a mirror would make Sega's own
     driver -- shipped on every 2A board -- erase its own reverb table.
     REFERENCE ORDER (the project rules): Model 1 has no SCSP; MAME wins for what
     the silicon computes, but this line is a 2014 bounds fix, not a model
     of the silicon, and two independent facts contradict it. This entry
     departs from MAME on that one decode and says so.
  7. WITHOUT THE MIRROR (the reference, NOMIRROR), DOA's DSP is a reverb:
     13-16 s silent (8 RMS, mean -3); in play EFREG 0 mean ~0, 200-450 RMS.
     Levels, 16-bit at 100% Volume, in play (the DAC clamp, left):
                       direct  MAME-mirror: return(mean / AC)  out   R914: return  out
       DOA 20-140 s     4,371     108,881 / 9,917         2,804      16 / 1,467  1,151
       VF2 20-80 s      3,567        -290 / 8,375         2,678    -156 / 1,518    957
       Virtua Cop 2     1,275      10,867 /   175           357      -9 /   240    359
       Zero Gunner      2,074          15 /   885           598      71 /   973    606
       Sega Rally         --  (no DSP program: identical)
     (direct / return in mix units, out = the DAC's 16-bit RMS.) VF2's
     "music loud through the return" (R886) was the collapsed reverb: its
     return falls from 2.3x its direct sends to 0.43x, the whole mix -8.9 dB,
     and its effects come up against the music. Virtua Cop 2's constant DC
     (R886's +2,717) is gone. R886's "Rally / VF2 = 17%" becomes 38%.
     Clips (mono, ROM-derived, git-ignored): build/scsp/clips/
     doa_8-30s_{MAME_mirror,R914}.wav, vf2_20-50s_{MAME_mirror,R914}.wav.

*The change (rtl/sound/scsp/m2_scsp_dsp.sv, m2_scsp.sv, sim/sound/scsp_ref.h):*
  1. m2_scsp_dsp parameter MADRS_MIRROR (default 0; m2_scsp passes it down):
     w_madrs only for 0x780-0x7BF; the 68000's read of 0x7C0-0x7FF gives 0
     (Zero Gunner reads it -- CLR's read cycle -- and only ever writes 0
     there). MADRS_MIRROR = 1 is the old RTL. scsp_ref.h: madrs_mirror, from
     SCSP_MIRROR in the environment (default off), so every replay tool
     keeps MAME's mirror one variable away.
  2. THE DSP's READ CACHE 64 -> 256 LINES (u_rcache IDX 6 -> 8), because
     item 1 alone made Virtua Cop 2 underrun on the board bench (below).
     With every MADRS 0 all of a program's taps read one ring line and hit;
     with real MADRS each tap is its own line, and 64 direct-mapped lines
     miss 44.6% of VC2's DSP reads (scsp_replay's cache model, 30 s: 10.1
     line fetches a sample; 128 lines 27.2%, 256 lines 18.5% = 4.2; with
     the mirror 1.1%). M10K UNCHANGED: quartus_map 17.0 of scsp_area_top
     (virtual pins) puts the 64 x 64 data array and the two 64 x 11 tag
     arrays in the same three 256-deep M10K blocks it now fills 256 x 64 /
     2 x 256 x 9 (the slot cache's exact shape); block bits 163,072 ->
     178,560, registers 1,720 -> 1,718.

**R922 -- VIRTUA COP 2'S "SHOOT TO SELECT" BEHIND THE CITY (GitHub #16) IS
MAME'S TILEMAP ORDER, AND MAME'S OWN TODO SAYS SO. A FRONT CATEGORY-0
PIXEL NOW HIDES A BACK CATEGORY-1 PIXEL.** 2026-10-21, branch vc2-layer.

*What was believed.* m2_tile_mixer (and Model 1's m1_tile_mixer, which it
copies) is model2_v.cpp's screen_update: every tilemap's category-1 tiles
over the 3D over every category-0 tile, i.e. front to back tm0.cat1,
tm1.cat1, tm2.cat1, tm3.cat1, [3D], tm0.cat0 ... (R213). So the order of
the two tilemap PAIRS (0/1 over 2/3) reverses wherever the back pair's tile
has the category bit and the front pair's does not.

*What is now known (VERIFIED in MAME 0.289 and our RTL; the board rule is
INFERRED).* Stage select, vcop2 frame 2520 (coin 2300, start 2500), all
scroll and window registers 0: SHOOT TO SELECT and the red arrows are
tilemap 0 category 0; the city map is tilemap 2, every tile category 1
(17,580 opaque pixels); the BEGINNER / MEDIUM / EXPERT boxes are the 3D.
The text overlaps the city in 2,637 pixels, none of them under a 3D pixel.
MAME draws the city over the text -- exactly the user's photo -- and MAME's
model2.cpp TODO names it: "vcop2: stage select has tilemap priority issue,
tilemap B (city model) has priority bit set, yet it should appear
underneath tilemap A ('shoot to select') which does not". Our core before
the change = MAME pixel for pixel (frame bench + MAME's 3D buffer, Model2.sv's
mix: 0 of 190,464 differ). A second screen settles which rule: Zero Gunner's
SCORE RANKING (zeroguna, frames 8880-9210 of the survey run) is a
full-screen tilemap-2 category-1 background with GUNSHIP / COBRA / APACHE
helicopter icons on tilemap 0 category 0, one per rank in the empty gap
between the rank number and the name -- never visible in MAME (6,411
pixels). No strict layer order can put the text over the city, the city
over the 3D and the 3D over category-0 text; the order that fits both
screens and every other is the one a tile chip with a single output would
give: the 2D layers resolve in their own order (pair 0/1 over pair 2/3),
and the WINNING pixel's category decides it against the 3D. Model 1's RTL
has MAME's rule too, so it does not answer this; no Model 1 screen tested
there has the case.

*The fix.* m2_tile_mixer: `front_cat0 = hit_cat0[0] || hit_cat0[1]` (a
non-transparent category-0 pixel of tilemap 0 or 1) suppresses hit_cat1[2]
and hit_cat1[3]; the pixel falls to the category-0 chain, so vid_cat1 is 0
and a 3D pixel there still wins (Model2.sv unchanged). Shared by both cores
(main's file is identical).

*How it was established -- and what else moves (nothing).* A survey Lua
(tile RAM every 20 frames, char RAM when written; coin at 1500, start and
fire pulsed, pedals held) over 6,000 frames of all 15 sets with MRAs
(daytona, daytona93, desert, vcopa, vcop2, srallyc, vf2, zeroguna,
manxtt, dynamcop, doaab, motoraid, pltkidsa, skytargt, hpyagu98) and
14,000 frames (every 30) of the eight that use tilemap-2/3 category-1
tiles (vcop2, dynamcop, hpyagu98, zeroguna, vf2, doaab, skytargt, vcopa),
with a Python System 24 decoder (window modes and line scroll; checked
against MAME's snapshots: 0 pixels differ on the two frames composed):
the case occurs in exactly two screens -- the vcop2 stage select and the
Zero Gunner ranking. RTL, tb_m2_video_frame (now also writes vid_cat1 as
<out>.cat) on old and new mixer over 79 dumped frames (five from each set,
1200-6000, plus four of the two screens): 75 frames identical in RGB and
vid_cat1; the four others change in exactly the overlap pixels (2,637 /
6,411 / 6,411 / 657), no pixel outside it. Area: the mixer standalone 31 -> 31 ALMs, 46 ->
47 ALUTs. lint_top 2A and M2_NO_2A clean, lint_idx nothing in the changed
file, analyze_file 0 errors, test_m2_video_ovr PASS.

*Not settled.* The rule where the overlap also has a 3D pixel (this change
shows the 3D, MAME the back tile): no screen found has it. Whether the
board's ranking really shows the icons: INFERRED from the layout, check it
on the board.

**R926 -- SEGA RALLY'S BLINKING, CLIPPING, SIDEWAYS AND FLYING OPPONENTS
(GitHub #19) ARE THE GAME'S OWN DETAIL BUDGET: EACH FRAME IT TIMES ITS FIRST
PIECE OF WORK AGAINST THE VBLANK AND, IF IT RAN LATE, DROPS THE CARS NEAREST
THE PLAYER FROM THEIR PHYSICS TO THE COURSE LINE. THIS CORE'S i960 RUNS THAT
CODE SEVERAL TIMES SLOWER THAN MAME'S, SO THE BUDGET FALLS AND THE CARS
FLICKER BETWEEN THE TWO. THE i960 AND THE TGP COMPUTE IT BIT FOR BIT. NO RTL
CHANGED; A TEST MRA FORCES THE BUDGET FOR A BOARD CHECK; THE BENCH'S R902 NaN
WAS ITS OWN DATA ROM.** 2026-10-22, branch rally-ai (from model2a 1526562).
(GitHub #19, mike911ok, Model2A_20261021d and earlier: "AI opponent glitches.
1- Cars blink. While they are blinking they can be clipped (no collision
detection) and will sometimes show the car sideways like it had crashed for a
few frames, but the next frame the car is straight. Can be spotted as soon as
you catch the first opponent in the first track. 2- Cars actually fly
upwards." Photos: a purple opponent rolled on its side beside the player at
222 km/h, 0'21"98; two cars upside down high over the track.)

*Believed:* a value the game computes for the opponents comes out wrong on
this core -- an i960 FP form or operand edge case, the TGP (R876 / R888 / R923),
the buffer RAM's posted writes, the data ROM -- or uninitialised RAM.

*THE GAME'S MECHANISM (MAME 0.289's disassembly of the work-RAM code,
0x580000-0x5effff, and write / read taps; VERIFIED in MAME):*
  1. The object table at 0x500000, stride 0x100: +4 the handler (0x5cacf0 an
     opponent, 0x5d3f40 the player), +0x10 flags (bits 31:16 the wheels'
     state: 0000 while the car runs on the course line, 2222 / 3333 / 4343
     with its physics), +0x14 x y z, +0x2c velocity a frame, +0x88 the course
     segment, +0x8c its render record, +0x9c the heading. The handler's mode
     (+0xe8) follows the record's byte 0x51 bits 7:6.
  2. 0x5bb320 (ROM 0x1c320) fills byte 0x51 for each car each frame: a
     detail by distance (< 50, < 100, < 200, beyond) granted only while the
     frame's row of a table at 0x5bb200 has a slot left -- row 8 allows 3 / 2
     / 2 cars the three nearest details, row 7 2 / 1 / 1, rows 3-5 one car
     the nearest, rows 0-2 none. The row is (m / 10000 - 21) >> 1, clamped 0-8,
     from m = [0x20aac0].
  3. m is TIME: the vblank interrupt (0x5a0490) loads timer 2 with 0x5e9ac
     (15.5 ms at 25 MHz); at 0x5bade0, after the frame's first work, the game
     reads it back (ldl 0xf00008), adds 90,000, and subtracts 400,000 if a
     vblank has already come ([0x202000] no longer 1). Row 8 needs the read
     within 4.3 ms of the interrupt; the nearest car keeps its physics
     only within 8.3 ms.
  4. MAME at 25 MHz (five frames sampled at 36 s): the read 2.06-2.14 ms
     after the interrupt (112-136 TGP
     result reads before it, ~1,050 after; the frame's work done at
     6.7-7.4 ms); m 376,523-434,083 -- ROW 8 IN ALL 1,852 RACE FRAMES, rows
     5-7 in 89 frames of the start's fly-over. MAME's own TODO ("srallyc:
     initial enemy car placement seems to be slightly incorrect for a few
     cars, seems to be affected by i960 clock speed") is this budget.
  5. MAME with the i960's clock set (new sim/io/mame_m2_clock.patch,
     M2_I960_CLK), the same scripted race: 14 and 25 MHz row 8 throughout
     (16-40 MHz: no unexplained step either); 10 MHz
     rows 6-8, and the third car (180 units ahead) flips 0000 / 2222 with the
     row frame by frame (34 changes against 9); 8 MHz rows 0-8; 7 MHz rows
     3-8. The cars' modes follow the row exactly, a frame late.
  So a slow frame start demotes the nearest opponents for that frame, and
  the demotion lightens the next frame, which promotes them again: a car that
  alternates between its physics (collision with the player, its own body
  attitude and height) and the course line (no collision, the line's
  attitude) -- blinking, clipped, sideways one frame and straight the next,
  and launched when it comes back into physics from a stale state.

*WHAT THIS CORE COMPUTES (all VERIFIED, nothing differs):*
  * A scripted race that catches the opponents (new sim/io/mame_m2_rally_ap.lua:
    an autopilot that follows the AI cars' own trails; PL_COIN=8: the first
    opponent within 15 units at 36.8 s, within 3 at 41.8 s). MAME: 21,861 AI
    steps, none the velocity does not explain (> 2 units); the same at i960
    16 / 25 / 33 / 40 MHz and TGP 12.5 / 25 / 100 MHz.
  * The TGP: that session's near-car window captured (frames 2033-2767,
    1,502,835 words in, 511,377 out, 1,343,136 io reads) and replayed through
    m2_copro (TGP_PROG 4096, R888's posted writes and early ALU), plain and
    --board-push --gap 60 --jitter 40: BIT-EXACT both, 0 dropped.
  * The i960's forms in that session (R921's census, m2lod): 148 forms, 431
    variants, 0 trap on the 2A core; atanr 16,261 / remr 1,066 / sinr 1 /
    cvtzril 8,180 / cpysre 6,350 distinct tuples, 0 differ from MAME. New
    against R921's Rally session: cvtir g0,fp1 at 0x5e2db4 / 0x5e2e1c (a
    random angle) and cmprl fp1,fp0 at 0x5da0e4 (the automatic gearbox).
  * Uninitialised RAM: work RAM, buffer RAM and backup RAM filled 0xFFFFFFFF
    before the boot -- work RAM identical to the plain run at every 5 s for
    100 s (the game clears it). One byte the game reads unwritten: 0x2139d8
    (board RAM; the AI car creation ORs it << 7 into +0x10; MAME 0, the
    bench 0xFF, the board whatever the SDRAM held -- Rally is not a2_big, so
    R900's sweep does not clear board RAM). Set to 1 in MAME: the flags
    carry bit 7 and nothing else moves (92 near-car frames pixel-identical,
    every mode change on the same frame). Recorded, not the cause.
  * THE WHOLE CORE (tb_m2_boot A2X, the srallyc image; new: M2_INSCHED,
    MAME's own port values frame by frame; M2_RALLY_AP, the autopilot in
    C++; M2_CARLOG, the AI log in the Lua's format): every state of the
    three opponents furthest from the player is one of MAME's, bit for bit
    (slots 5-7, ~1,280 states each, the 1,300 race frames the bench ran); the cars
    nearer the player leave MAME's sequence where their mode changes -- the
    third car at frame 2189 at the very state MAME's 10 MHz run leaves it.
    The bench's budget (M2_BUSLOG on 0x20aac0, with the frame now): m
    213,993-370,531 in the race, rows 0-2 in 263 of 552 frames, 3-7 in 284,
    8 in 5 (MAME: 8 in all). Its interrupt-to-read window (M2_FRAMESTAT,
    M2_WORK_IPS=5a0490,5bade8): 251,255 i960 cycles for 21,969 instructions,
    CPI 11.4 (MAME's 2.1 ms is ~52 k cycles at 25 MHz: CPI ~2.4); T_FRAME
    30.7% (call / return, the register cache's spills and fills), T_MEM_W
    29.9%, instruction fetch waits ~28% (Rally runs from its work-RAM copy,
    which R728's code cache, program ROM only, does not cover), the TGP's
    hold 3.4%. The bench's clocks are not the board's (24 MHz i960, a
    6-cycle memory, 417 k i960 cycles a vblank against the board's 40 MHz
    and 695 k), so its rows are not the board's; the board's are NOT
    MEASURED. Inferred from R888 / R897 / R901 (Rally's "small slowdowns"
    on every 2A build, unexplained by the TGP) and from the report itself:
    the board's frame start is slow enough, near opponents, for rows 0-2.

*THE BENCH'S OWN FAULT, FIXED (sim only):* tb_m2_boot answered every 2A
data-ROM read 0 (R852: "no copro data ROM on 2A"), which R862's Rally
broke: the TGP's course lookups found nothing and the player's height was
NaN from the grid. R902's "every matrix's translation NaN ... the analog
inputs read 0xFF and its sound board is a stub" was this; with the ROM at
word 0x13C0000 (Model2.sv's GAME_COPRO_2A) the grid matches MAME's and the
race runs. The harness also gains the 315-5649's analog channels (cab_an0-2).

*NOT A FIX, A BOARD CHECK:* "Sega Rally Championship - Twin-DX (Revision C)
[AI detail test].mra" -- one word, ROM 0x1c334 (work RAM 0x5bb334) cmpible
0,g0 -> b +0x10, so the row is always 8, as MAME's is in every race frame.
MAME 0.289 with it: a 440 s session plays normally (three races, game over,
attract); at 25 MHz the far opponents' states are the plain run's, the grid
cars settle differently during the fly-over (MAME's plain run uses rows 5-7
there); at 10 MHz the cars' mode changes drop to the 25 MHz pattern (slots
1-4: 3 / 8 / 9 / 12 against 102 / 19 / 34 / 4). Its cost is frame rate where
the CPU is short: 57.5 -> 57.0 fps at 10 MHz, 55.5 -> 45.3 at 7 MHz (the
budget was the game's way of keeping its rate). Not for release: on the
board it would show whether the opponents stop blinking (the mechanism
confirmed there) and how much slower the near-opponent frames get.

*THE FIX THE GAME ASKS FOR:* the i960 as fast as the board in Rally's race
code -- MAME's ~2.1 ms from the vblank to the read, the board's 4.3 ms
at most. Where this core loses it (the bench's split, above): the register
cache's memory spills and fills on deep call chains (MAME and the chip
keep four frames on chip, as this core does; the cost is ours, 16 words
through the bridge each way), data waits, and instruction fetch from the
work-RAM copy. Each is an area and timing change (Model2A_20261021d:
41,244 ALMs, 547 / 553 M10K) and needs the board to judge; not attempted.

*Tools (committed):* sim/io/mame_m2_rally_ap.lua (the autopilot, APLOG,
INREC); sim/io/rally_ai_check.py (glitch / align / modes / budget);
sim/io/mame_m2_clock.patch; tb_m2_boot M2_INSCHED, M2_RALLY_AP, M2_CARLOG,

**R927 -- THE 2A i960's SPEED IN SEGA RALLY'S FRAME START (R926's AI
BUDGET): WHERE ITS CYCLES GO, MEASURED; THE REGISTER CACHE AS THE CHIP KEEPS
IT (A RING OF EIGHT FRAMES, NOT MAME'S DEPTH RULE) TAKES 30% OF THE WINDOW
OUT AND A 1 KB DATA CACHE ON THE CPU'S SIDE ANOTHER 3%. ON THE BOARD'S CLOCK
RATIOS THE RACE START MOVES FROM ROWS 0-3 TO 3-8; ROW 8 EVERYWHERE NEEDS THE
MEMORY PATH ITSELF. BOTH CHANGES 2A-ONLY, SWITCHED, ON. NOT FITTED, NOT ON A
BOARD.** 2026-10-22, branch i960-speed (model2a 1526562 + rally-ai 7558f98).

*Believed (R926):* the frame start's time splits ~31% register spills and
fills on call / return, ~30% data waits, ~28% instruction fetch "from the
work-RAM copy, which R728's code cache (program ROM only) does not cover".

*THE INSTRUMENT (sim only).* tb_m2_boot M2_FRAMESTAT now writes a 'P' line
after each M2_WORK_IPS window: bus cycles and transactions by master (load /
store unit, register-frame spill / fill, instruction fetch, the interrupt
path) and region (program ROM, board RAM, work RAM, buffer RAM, I/O, data ROM,
other); calls, returns, the depth at each call, and the frame traffic MAME's
rule and the chip's ring would make at 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 32 frames; the
i-cache's requests and fills by region; models of a CPU-side data cache (1-8
KB, line or word allocation, direct and 2-way) and of the i-cache (8 / 16 /
32 KB direct, 2-way, 4-way). sim/io/i960_prof.py sums them. M2_BOARDCLK=1
(with the harness's TMR_BOARD) runs the bench at the BOARD's ratios -- clk_mem
80 : clk_vid 32 : clk_cpu 40 MHz, the vblank and the 2A timers to match --
where the plain bench is a 24 MHz i960 against a 25 MHz timer (R926: its rows
are not the board's). Harness parameters RC_RING / RC_FRAMES / DC_LINES /
DC_LANES build the changes below. (A window opened by the vblank IRQ and not
closed before the next one is now reset, not accumulated.)

*THE BREAKDOWN (MEASURED, the whole-core bench as R926 ran it -- srallyc,
MAME's inputs, the autopilot from frame 2070, LAT 6; window 0x5a0490 ->
0x5bade8, vblanks 1207-1347, 109 windows):* 276 k cycles a window for 26.9 k
instructions, CPI 10.27:
    T_MEM_W 3.27 CPI (31.8%)   T_FRAME 2.88 (28.0%)   T_FETCH + T_EXEC 2.00
    T_FETCH_W 0.96 (9.4%)      T_FETCH2_W 0.84 (8.2%)  FP + MULDIV 0.25
  * CALL / RETURN: 250 calls a window, 98% of them at depth >= 4 (5: 69%,
    6: 19%): under MAME's rule 97.6% of calls spill and every matching
    return fills -- 487 frame transfers of 16 words a window. A spill word
    costs 10.4 cycles (two 16-bit SDRAM writes through the bridge each), a
    fill word 7.0 (the spill's own writes invalidated those lines in the
    bridge's data cache, so every fill misses it): ~280 cycles a call /
    return pair, 24.6% of the window in bus time. The chip's ring at the same
    depths (modelled on the same call stream): 4 frames 9 transfers a window,
    8 frames 0.02.
  * DATA (load / store unit): board RAM reads 7.4 cycles each (3.1 k a
    window), work RAM reads 7.6 (2.1 k), I/O reads 38.8 (0.26 k: the TGP's
    output FIFO holding the read), I/O writes 3.2 (3.0 k: the FIFO pushes,
    posted), board RAM writes 3.9, "other" (0x1xxxxxxx tile / palette /
    backup) 5.0-5.1. A dcache hit is ~5 CPU cycles of crossing (R729's
    toggle across, S_DCK, the toggle back, the registered answer); a store is
    posted in 3 but the next access waits for its two SDRAM words.
  * FETCH: CORRECTION TO R926 -- the i-cache in i960_top (8 KB, 512 x 16 B,
    R815) caches EVERY fetch address, work RAM included; R728's bridge code
    cache (program ROM only) is a different block and has been off since
    R733. Rally's race code misses it on 4.7% of requests (1.7 k fills a
    window, ~25 cycles each through the bridge's line buffer: 15.5% of the
    window). The rest of T_FETCH_W / T_FETCH2_W is the front end's own shape:
    a taken branch costs two cycles of T_FETCH_W on a hit, and a two-word
    instruction (MEMB with a displacement, ~a quarter of Rally's) two of
    T_FETCH2_W.

*THE REAL CHIP (what is documented, what is inferred).* MAME's i960 charges
fixed cycles (call 9, ret 7, ld 4, st 2, ldl 5, ldq 7, stq 5) and models no
cache, no wait state and no spill cost; its register cache is 4 saved frames
by depth since the last flushreg (I960_RCACHE_SIZE). The i960KB's own (Intel's
KA/KB documentation, from memory -- NOT re-checked in this session): a
512-byte on-chip instruction cache, four on-chip local register sets, and the
architecture's rule that a frame is written to its save area only when a call
finds the register cache full and read back only when a return finds it gone
-- the save area is undefined until flushreg. The board's work RAM (R904,
inferred one-hot reading of Rally's wait-state table): 1 wait, 3 bus cycles
an access at 25 MHz (120 ns), a burst's later words 2. So on the chip a
spill of 16 words is four quad bursts, ~36 cycles at 25 MHz (1.4 us), and
the ring makes it rare; this core paid ~166 cycles at 40 MHz (4.2 us) for
every call at depth >= 4.

*THE CHANGES (R927, 2A only).*
  1. i960_regs RING = 1, CACHE_FRAMES = 8 (i960_top RC_RING / RC_FRAMES;
     Model2.sv M2_2A_I960_RING, default 1): eight saved frames in a ring; a
     call that finds it full writes the OLDEST frame to its own address
     (through the flush path) and takes its slot; a return takes the newest,
     or reads memory when the ring is empty; flushreg writes all of them,
     oldest first. 8 frames because the MLAB is 32 rows deep anyway (4 frames
     used 16 of them): the array is the same 7 MLABs. The frame addresses are
     now [31:6] (a frame is 64-byte aligned), a concatenation instead of an
     adder, which more than pays for the ring's control. RING = 0 is MAME's
     rule exactly (every MAME-mode bench below unchanged).
     WHY THIS IS ALLOWED: only the 16-word register save areas see a
     difference, and those are undefined until flushreg on the chip itself;
     software cannot depend on MAME's stream without depending on something
     the silicon does not do. Checked in the games that switch contexts: VF2's
     background coroutine (0x4add0-0x4aeac, MAME's dasm) saves g1-g14 and
     r3-r15 with ordinary stores and returns normally; Sega Rally and Zero
     Gunner flushreg once at boot (R865).
  2. i960_dcache (i960_top DC_LINES = 64, DC_LANES = 0; M2_2A_I960_DC,
     default 1): 1 KB, direct-mapped, 16-byte lines with a valid bit a word,
     ONE WORD ALLOCATED PER MISS (no line fill: the bus sees what it saw
     before, less the hits), board RAM 0x200000-0x23ffff and work RAM
     0x500000-0x5fffff only, write-through; a full-word write that lands in a
     held line updates it, a partial write drops its word (one 32-bit array,
     one M10K -- byte lanes would be four). Hits are answered the cycle after
     the request and kept off the bridge; every CPU write to those regions,
     from any master (loads / stores, frame spills, the interrupt path's
     saves), passes it. Coherent for the reason the bridge's own data cache
     is: board and work RAM are written by the CPU alone once it runs, and
     the R900 RAM sweeps run with the CPU in reset (the valid bits sweep at
     reset). Buffer RAM and everything else is never cached.

**R923 -- VIRTUA FIGHTER 2 "CRASHES AT RANDOM" (GitHub #17): NO DEADLOCK IN
THE TGP / COPRO HANDSHAKE THAT SIMULATION CAN REACH. VF2's TGP IS BIT-EXACT
AGAINST MAME OVER A NEW 60 s CAPTURE WITH FIGHTS AND UNDER EVERY BOARD-LIKE
TIMING TRIED (LATENCY, JITTER AND i960 PACING TO 30x R876's); NO FIFO WORD IS
LOST OR DUPLICATED; s1278's FAILING clk_sys PATHS ARE NOT IN THE TGP. A PROBE
BUILD (M2_PROBE_TGP) THAT NAMES WHAT EACH SIDE WAITS ON AT THE HANG, AND HOLDS
THE LAST 256 i960 TRANSFERS BEFORE IT. NO BEHAVIOUR CHANGED. NOT FITTED.**
(GitHub #17, Model2A_20261021b = s1278, users: VF2 "crashes at random ...
even in the attract mode. Sometimes as soon as the match starts, sometimes in
round one, or after a second fight, after a credit is inserted". The symptom
-- freeze, reset, garbage -- is not stated.)

*Believed (R871, R876, R921):* the one recorded VF2 lockup (s1203, before
R876 and R888) held the i960 at 0x7dc4 -- three ldq from the TGP's output
FIFO -- with the TGP never answering; the probe of the day could not say where
the TGP was. R876 cleared VF2's TGP under board-like timing on three windows
(attract only); R921 cleared every i960 form. Open: a handshake deadlock the
replays do not reach, a lost or duplicated FIFO word, a marginal timing path,
or a TGP divergence on data the captures never held.

     in, 272,424 out) through tb_tgp_replay, 16 runs: --board-push with

     stay far under 128 words, as R876).
  3. The other 2A TGP programs on this RTL: Zero Gunner's play and Sega
     Rally's race windows (board-push, R876's settings), and a NEW Virtua
     Cop 2 window (make tgp_capture_2a CAP2A_SET=vcop2 CAP2A_GAME=vcop2,
     frames 1300-2500: 1,556,551 in, 439,627 out; --board-push --gap 60
     --jitter 40): PASS (VC2: 8 outputs differ in NaN encoding only, as
     Daytona's). Daytona race5400 on the original core's TGP: PASS as R876
     (15 / 5 NaN encoding) and IDENTICAL to the stored RTL baseline.
  4. tb_m2_fifo_fuzz (new): m2_fifo_m10k -- the queue behind both copro FIFOs
     and the TGP's posted writes -- against a reference queue every cycle,
     20 M cycles each at DEPTH 128 and 32, in phases that fill it and sit
     full, drain it and sit empty, push into it full while the head is
     popped (1.8 M such cycles) and pop the last word as it lands: 0
     failures. Three planted faults (write while full, a second read in
     flight, full one late) each FAIL by thousands; a fourth is equivalent.
  5. The i960 side, read rather than simulated: m2_cpu_bridge holds an I/O
     access in S_IOW with io_sel re-asserted while io_stall, and completes it
     in the cycle stall falls, sampling a combinational copro_rdata --
     exactly one push or pop per access (no registered read on the path, so
     no stale word). MAME's VF2 writes copro_ctl1 twice (the boot's upload)
     and reads fifo_control once in 260 s with fights: no re-upload, no
     polling -- the replay's push / blocking-pop i960 is the game's
     protocol. MAME's i960 defers interrupts during a burst-stalled ldq, as
     ours (it is blocked in the bus cycle), so 0x7dc4's wait cannot need an
     IRQ handler's words.
  6. ALIASES, ruled out for VF2: Model2.sv decodes the copro ports from
     cpu_io_addr[23:0] only, so any T_IO access at 0x1X88xxxx or above
     would push into the TGP's FIFO. A MAME tap on every i960 access at or
     above 0x10000000 (230 s, attract and fights): VF2 writes only
     0x10000000 (once), the texture mirrors 0x122-0x127xxxxx and luma
     0x128xxxxx -- all decoded to SDRAM before T_IO; no read at all.
  7. MODEL 1 (tools/model1-ref 0b5d04f, current with its local repository):
     m1_tgp's fifo_ack for a write is `!fifo_out_full || pushed` -- a full
     output FIFO stalls its TGP (MAME halts it). Ours acknowledges and drops
     (R146-era: the board froze at 0x1166C when the i960 stopped draining),
     with 129 places against MAME's 8; nothing counted it (`fifo_out_push`
     is gated, so u_fout's `dropped` cannot move). Kept -- VF2's protocol
     never has more than a command's results outstanding -- but now counted
     (m2_tgp dbg_out_refused) and the replay FAILS on any: 0 in every run.
  8. TIMING. quartus_sta on a copy of s1278's database (80 MHz clk_sys,
     slow corner): the failing clk_sys endpoints are gp_outr -> PhaseInc
     (-0.328), -> shadowmask_data (-0.210), -> vs_line (-0.070): hps_io's
     GPO into the video / scan-converter configuration. The worst TGP path
     is mb86233_core state.S_DST -> maddr_q[15] at +0.484; none of the 60
     worst paths ends in m2_copro's FIFOs, the bridge's I/O state or the
     SDRAM crossings' slow side. A marginal-path hang in the copro is not
     what STA shows for s1278 (it cannot see the asynchronous crossings,
     which are false-pathed; m2_sdram_cdc's toggles are synchronised).

*What would tell a deadlock from a timing fault on the board:* a logic
deadlock is reproducible in state -- the same TGP pc and sequencer state, a
consistent pair of FIFO counts (the i960 waiting on an empty output FIFO and
the TGP in S_SRC on an empty input FIFO: the two disagree on a command's
length) -- and the ring shows a normal command stream up to the hang. A
corrupted crossing or path shows as an inconsistent state: a req with no
ack for ever (tbl / dat / bufw), the TGP's popped count ahead of the i960's
pushed count, fin_valid with a zero count, or a command code in the ring
that the program never dispatches. A livelock moves the TGP's retire count.

*THE PROBE (M2_PROBE_TGP, rtl/dbg/m2_tgp_probe.sv; decoder
tools/decode_tgp.py).* VERILOG_MACRO "M2_PROBE=1" and "M2_PROBE_TGP=1" (with
M2_NO_DEBUG as every probe build; add "M2_NO_2A_RALLY=1" for the area below).
The sound and memory-test records give their place (SND_CHKSUM off); M2_PROBE's
stream, slot rate (2.46 ms) and UART. A state record and a ring record in
turn: C (i960 IP | copro_stall, unimplemented, frozen, TGP pc), h (m2_copro
dbg_fifo: halted, uploading, both FIFOs' flags and counts, the i960's access
| m2_tgp dbg_hs: the sequencer's state and every req / ack), j (pushed /
popped counts both ways), p / x (the last words each way; output words lost on
a full FIFO; input words dropped), i (TGP io address, retires, program word),
a (the i960's I/O access, trap / halted, the TGP's bank, the longest
copro_stall), and r -- THE LAST 256 i960 TRANSFERS (push, function-port
command, pop, copro_ctl1), with a 6-bit vblank count, in one M10K, which
FREEZES once copro_stall has held 2^23 cycles (105 ms). New debug ports, all
open in the release build: mb86233_core dbg_state, m2_tgp dbg_hs /
dbg_out_refused, m2_copro dbg_fifo / dbg_tgp_hs / dbg_tgp_out_refused /
dbg_xfer*.

    UART (DIVISOR 8, FREEZE_BIT 12): 700 transfers with short stalls, the

**R931 (board) -- VF2's FREEZE IS GONE WITH THE TGP HOLDING ON A FULL OUTPUT
FIFO.** s1340 (vf2-skip 909251d: the R931 fix on model2a 35210cb), Ben,
2026-10-22: Pai's backflip skipped with Start repeatedly (the board capture's
trigger, ~1 in 10 before) -- "I have not been able to get a crash"; every 2A
game runs. GitHub #17's cause, as captured on the board (s1336): a 190-word
TGP command, 129-word output FIFO, 18 words dropped, the i960 waiting at
0x7dcc for the rest.
*(2) VIRTUA COP AT 57.5 fps (an OSD hack, off by default).* Virtua Cop
runs in the video board's 30 Hz mode (render_mode bit 2 = 0; model2.cpp
lists skytargt, desert, vstriker and vcop), so its 3D updates every other
vblank (28.75 fps). Forcing 60 Hz in the core is NOT the hack:
  - the display list is built across two frames in 30 Hz mode, and the
    walk runs on alternate frames as the reference does (R256) -- walking
    every frame reads a half-built list, which is R256's scenery dropout;
  - if the game's loop did run every vblank, its per-frame logic (enemy
    movement, timers) would most likely run at double speed.
A real hack is a GAME CODE patch (an MRA patch, as Dead or Alive's
MRA patches its protection routines) that sets 60 Hz mode and halves the logic's per-frame
step, or runs the logic every other vblank while the 3D list is rebuilt
every vblank. First step: a MAME experiment -- vcopa with render_mode
forced to 60 Hz (a Lua write tap), watching game speed and the picture --
then find the frame loop in the program. Desert Tank and Sky Target are the
same 30 Hz family; whatever is learned applies to them.

**R937 (main, from model2c) -- THE BRIDGE READ TILE RAM AND THE PALETTE ONE
WORD LATE, ON EVERY CORE.** Found on branch stcc-title (model2c) from
Sega Touring Car Championship's title and rankings, whose loops read tile
RAM back (ldos / xor / stos over every tile at 0x779a0; a column copy at
0x13774) and drew each 8-pixel column twice. m2_cpu_bridge presented an
on-chip read's low word with `half` still set from the previous access
(cleared in S_IDLE, a cycle late for the M10K's one-cycle read), so an
aligned halfword read of tile RAM or the palette returned the NEXT word and
a 32-bit read came back halves swapped; a read at +2 was right by accident.
Writes never saw it. The unit bench missed it because its RAM model
answered in the same cycle. Fix (cherry-picked as is): `half` cleared when
an access completes, a read moves to the high word when accepted, reads
fetch the whole dword. Bench: 1,009 / 1,009 checks here (the old bridge
fails the corrected bench with 46 mismatches). On model2c the whole-core
bench then matched MAME's tile RAM in all 32,768 words and the frame on
0 / 190,464 pixels (30,766 before).
WHO IT TOUCHES (MAME 0.289, 120 s attract, reads of tile RAM / the 2D
palette -- every one wrong before): on this core VIRTUA COP (tile and
palette); Daytona reads none; Desert Tank not measured. On 2A: Zero Gunner
(~23,000), VF2 (~19,000, scroll registers read back), Pilot Kids, Hanguk
Pro Yagu 98 (the whole palette), Motor Raid, Sky Target and Virtua Cop 2 (a
few). What each game did with the wrong values was not traced: a board look
at Virtua Cop's 2D (and on 2A VF2, Zero Gunner) before release. Open
question worth re-asking with this in: R929's "why the tile-path flash is
lost on the board".
*BOARD (Ben, 2026-10-23, s1386 = model2a + R937, clk_mem -0.004):* Manx
TT's leaderboard no longer flickers (its broken thin strokes are texture
minification -- the panel is 3D -- not R937; the coloured dots at its grid
crossings are the R938 seams). ZERO GUNNER "looks better -- some 2D was
missing before", so R937 restored 2D the game builds from read-backs. (Its
ranking-screen helicopter icons were already there before R937 -- they came
with R922, Model2A_20261021d.)
*BOARD (Ben, s1386, continued):* Hanguk Pro Yagu 98, Pilot Kids, Motor Raid,
Virtua Cop 2 and Sky Target all "look good"; VF2 good (the sky / hill dots
of #27 are in VF2's 2D layer, consistent with R937; the green pixel ~4

**R939 (main) -- 15 kHz: THE CONVERTER'S PAIRING MOVED THE LINE TIMING HALF A
LINE AT EVERY RE-PAIR, ~27 TIMES A MINUTE IN VIRTUA COP. NOW IT SWAPS THE
FIELD LABELS AND THE LINES NEVER MOVE; "15kHz pairing" (Auto / Off) ADDED.**
(GitHub #24, madstalker80, a 15 kHz CRT at 15.4 kHz: on the [15kHz CRT] MRAs
Virtua Cop and Desert Tank "lose sync for a short time", often, all through
the game; a top band of torn, displaced lines; every other game fine. The set
is picky: at 15.7 kHz the OSD is wrong, at 15.1 the top third loses sync.)

*Believed (R898, the converter's header):* pairing locks once -- "a cadence
that changes by a frame now and then never gets eight in a row, and is left
alone" -- and the re-alignment that makes it "moves the output once, by a
field". The bench drove only a steady two-frame cadence, so it saw one move,
early, and skipped its timing checks around it.

*Now known (tb_m2_scan15, before / after, every line count):*
  1. WHAT A RE-PAIR DID. It reloaded the output counters as if the odd native
     frame were the even one. A native frame is N0 - 1/2 output lines
     (273.5 / 268.5 / 262.5), so the reload stepped the line timing by HALF A
     LINE: one line of 984 px (1.5 lines) at 15.7 and 15.1 kHz, 328 px (0.5)
     at 15.4 kHz, against 656. The vsync intervals did NOT change (every one
     still exactly one native frame) -- the fault is horizontal: the CRT's
     line oscillator re-locks, and the step falls DL lines (4-9) before the
     first visible line, so the re-lock tears the top of the picture. That
     is the capture.
  2. HOW OFTEN. After a re-pair the cadence must slip again before the next
     one, and Virtua Cop's does: on the board (s1381) 95% of 3D frames at 2
     vblanks, 2% at 3 -- every odd-length image flips the parity, and the
     next eight images on the new parity re-pair. A frame-level model of the
     pairing logic (sim/video/scan15_pair_model.py, the bench's LCG), checked against
     the RTL bench run for run (9, 5 and 15 re-pairs in 1,200 native frames
     on three seeds -- the model's counts exactly):
         2 frames 96%, 3 2%, 4 2%       26.5 half-line steps a minute
         2 frames 95%, 3 2%, 1 3%       46.8 (catch-up frames flip it too)
         steady 2                        0 after the first lock
     60 Hz games change image every frame, so a "good" change resets the
     count and they never re-pair: why only Virtua Cop and Desert Tank.
  3. THERE IS NO ORACLE. The board's own output is 24 kHz; Model 1 has no
     15 kHz path (VGA_F1 = 0). The requirement is Ben's: stable sync on a
     picky CRT first, least combing second, no added latency.

*What pairing is for:* a CRT draws fields one after another and does not
weave them; an image shown in (field 0, field 1) or (field 1, field 0) looks
the same on it. Pairing matters to a deinterlacer that weaves field 0 then
field 1 -- MiSTer's scaler does (ascal ends a frame after field 1,
i_endframe on i_flm) -- and a capture device or flat panel.

*The fix (option a, chosen):* the output's line grid is fixed at the first
lock and never moves. Fields still start D_PX after an even native frame
and D_PX +- HT/2 after an odd one; what a re-pair changes is which LABEL
(field 0 = even rows, its vsync half a line nearer; field 1) each native
frame carries -- `s` in m2_scan15. A swap repeats one label (two field 0s or
two field 1s), so ONE vsync interval is half a line short or long (273 or
274 lines for 273.5) -- the same event as a console switching 240p / 480i --
and the odd frame's field moves a whole line (D_PX - HT/2 when it is field
0). The swap is made at an odd frame's start, before the odd field begins
and before the vsync that places the next even field; evidence completed on
an even frame waits one frame. The align (every second native frame) loads
the label state as well (field = ~s_e, nxt = s), so it stays a no-op.
PAIR_N stays 8 (retrorepair's): fewer changes running re-pair sooner but
more often, for no sync gain.
OSD "15kHz pairing" Auto / Off, O[67] (free on main, model2a, model2c: main
has O[64] / O[66], the others O[65:64]); Auto = 0, so saved configs open as
before. Off never swaps: the output timing then never changes at all.

*Options weighed (model, 60 min, 96/2/2 cadence; "combed" = output frames of
two images, i.e. what a weaving deinterlacer shows):*
                                  line jumps/min  1/2-line vsync steps/min  combed
  retrorepair's re-align              26.5             0                    11.7%
  field swap, PAIR_N 8 (Auto)          0              26.5                  13.2%
  field swap, PAIR_N 4                 0              30.6                   7.4%
  field swap, PAIR_N 16                0              19.8                  21.7%
  swap at most every 10 s / 30 s       0              5.4 / 1.9          41.7 / 46.9%
  pairing Off                          0               0                    48.3%
(b) A gradual slew of the line phase instead of a step (half a line over a
few hundred lines, the line rate ~0.15% off meanwhile) is feasible in the
ring's window at 15.7 kHz (+-410 px) but buys nothing: the swap above needs
no change of line phase at all -- the odd field moves a whole line instead --
so a slew would only add a line-rate excursion a picky set could see. (c)
Rate limits trade combing for fewer vsync steps almost one for one -- at 10 s
apart the pairing is barely better than Off; not taken. (d) Taken as the
Off switch: for a set that minds even a half-line vsync step, Off costs a
CRT nothing.
BEN'S VARIANT -- hold the renderer's flip a frame so the image starts on the
even frame -- was weighed and NOT built. In steady running a slip PERSISTS:
after a 3-frame image every following on-time image lands on the odd frame.
Holding only the late image (Ben's limit: no latency in steady running, at
most one frame, only on a frame the game delivered late) leaves every image
after it mis-paired: 17-34 holds a minute and 46-50% combed, the same as Off.
Keeping the pairing that way needs every image held until the next slip --
+17.4 ms on about half the images -- which the limit rules out. Beside the
swap it would save at most the one combed frame per slip (~1%), for a change
to m2_raster3d's publish (clk_sys, shared with 2A/2C), the frame parity
crossed from clk_mem, and a held image dropped when a one-frame catch-up
arrives behind it (0.5 a minute on the catch-up mix). (Nothing else waits on
the publish: the walk waits on the swap, fb_busy clears on fb_complete.)

*Checked (tb_m2_scan15, extended: a slipping cadence from an LCG, the line
period checked through every event, vsync intervals measured in pixels
against N0 - 1/2 lines, label repeats, an output hash from reset):*
  * 60 Hz and every cadence that never re-pairs is BIT-IDENTICAL: the output
    hash old = new for cadence none / 1 / 3 / 2 in the locked phase, at all
    three line counts (626eb962... 273/274, 4e435dce... 268/269, 9700b83c...
    262/263; 12 pairs, 140 native frames, 24.9 M output samples each).
    Pairing Off with the other phase gives the same hash too.
  * Cadence 2, the phase that needs the swap, all three line counts: PASS --
    0 line period faults, 0 re-alignments that move the output, one vsync
    interval half a line short followed by the repeated label, 0 output
    frames of two images after it, 16.3 M pixels against the blend, 0 ring
    mismatches. Retrorepair's RTL on the same run: one 984-px line.
  * Slipping cadence, 1,200 native frames (20.8 s), 142.5 M pixels a run, all
    PASS: 273/274, 268/269, 262/263 seed 1 -- 9 swaps, 9 vsync intervals
    +-1/2 line (5 short, 4 long), each followed by its repeated label, 0 line
    faults, 13.3% combed; seed 2 -- 5 swaps, 4.5%; catch-up mix -- 15, 24.7%;
    Off -- 0 events, 43.6% / 63.8%. Retrorepair's RTL on the same inputs: 9 /
    5 / 9 half-line line steps (984 px at 15.7 and 15.1 kHz, 328 px at 15.4),
    11.0% / 3.6% combed.
  * Ring margins (written-before-read / read-before-overwritten): the odd
    field at D_PX - HT/2 is the new tight case -- 15.7 kHz 8.9 / 41.4 us (was
    40.6 / 41.4), 15.4 kHz 148.9 / 180.3, 15.1 kHz 177.3 / 210.3. The bench
    sees the edge: at D_PX_I 5740 the swapped phase fails (1,525 ring
    mismatches), 5780 passes at 3.1 us. D_PX is NOT re-centred (6009 would
    give ~24 us both ways) because that would move every game's output phase
    and break bit-identity for 60 Hz; the margin is exact (both enables are
    rationals of clk_mem), not a tolerance.
  * lint_top clean on main, and on model2a's and model2c's Model2.sv with this
    converter and the same three Model2.sv hunks (patch applies; offsets
    only); lint_idx: no converter entries (104 findings, none new).
  * quartus_map 17.0, whole design, 0aa5905 -> this: ALMs needed 40,361 ->
    40,365 (+4); ALUT 57,224 -> 57,227; registers 49,776 -> 49,786; block
    memory bits 4,670,992 unchanged (no M10K); DSP 98 unchanged. m2_scan15
    207 -> 215 ALUT, 129 -> 134 registers.

*Not verified:* a CRT. Whether this set minds the one half-line vsync step a
swap makes is for the tester; Off removes it. If the tear persists with Off,
the cause is not the pairing.

*Carrying to model2a / model2c:* m2_scan15.sv is identical on all three
branches; the change is the file, its bench, and three Model2.sv hunks (OSD
line, the vpr_s synchroniser, .pair_en on the instance).
*Ben (s1386):* Sega Rally good. Its car-shadow white line (#26) looks like a

*Ben (s1386):* Dead or Alive and Dynamite Cop good. The 2A board pass for

**R940 -- DYNAMITE COP'S "HORIZONTAL LIGHT LINES" ON THE DARK SEA ARE THE CORE,
NOT THE GAME: THE SEA IS ONE POLYGON 2,890 TEXELS ACROSS, AND R609 STILL
CLAMPED A QUAD WIDER THAN 2,048. NOW SUCH A QUAD IS SHIFTED DOWN BY 2^s
(s = 1..2) AND SHIFTED BACK AFTER THE DIVIDE (UVSH, 2A BUILD). +2 M10K; ALM
AT MAP NOISE (-10).** (Ben, s1386 = model2a + R937: in the attract's cruise-ship
shot the dark sea beside the hull shows regular thin horizontal light lines,
spaced wider toward the bottom; the open sea further out is normal sparkly
water; Mip-mapping Off the same.)

*What MAME draws (0.289, sm2-builds/mame-r869, dynamcop attract, 3D frames
90 and 100 dumped with M2DIFF):* normal water everywhere beside the ship --
no lines. So it is the core.

*What was believed (R609):* moving the four vertices by a multiple of twice
the texture's size fixes every polygon that fits 2,048 texels; "only a
polygon that itself spans more than 2,048 texels still clamps", taken as
rare.

*NOW KNOWN (MEASURED):* the sea is ONE polygon (texture 128 x 128, header
40d2) over the whole screen, five vertices after MAME's clip, u up to
23,128 and v up to 22,028 raw (2,890 x 2,753 texels): 66,102 of the frame's
188,460 3D pixels at frame 90, 75,782 at frame 100. Through this core's own
geometry (geodiff_2abig on the walk that follows frame 100, walk 699) it
comes out as two quads -- 918 (the left and bottom) and 919 (the right
triangle) -- whose u, v after R609's move reach 10,644 quarter-texels; the
clamp put three of 918's four corners at u = 8,191, so across the near-left
sea u hardly moves and each row reads one texel column of a dark texture:
horizontal light lines on black. 919 keeps one clamped corner of three and
still looks like water -- Ben's picture exactly (the whole path rendered
textured from our quads: the clamp reproduces his lines, the fix draws
water). Two other quads in the frame clamp (header 60c0, 107 px).
Model 1 has no texture mapping, so the oracle for this is MAME
(model2rd.ipp reads u as float * 256 and only ever (u >> 8) & (w - 1)).

*THE FIX (a study-level choice, R609 / §5 budget):* widening u, v to 15
bits through the store, the fill and the span walk would cost +16 bits a
quad in the store (195 -> 211 bits a bank: +8 M10K, past the 2A core's 548
/ 553) and two more bits in every u/z path (span_u no longer fits 32
bits). Instead, per quad: m2_geometry UVSH registers the eight differences
after the move (15 bits) and shifts the quad -- u and v together -- right
by the least s in 0..2 that fits 13 bits (truncated: a rounding adder a
coordinate is 16 adders), handing s over as q_uvs; m2_raster3d stores it
beside the texture word (197 bits a bank, one M10K a bank more) and carries
it through the fill (span_uvs, latched with the quad) and the span queue
(262 of its 280 bits, no block more) to m2_span_tex, whose un-normalising
shift is one shift less s ((pu >> 16) >> (2 + sr - s); with s = 0 exactly
the old two shifts); m2_raster_fill adds 4s quarter levels to the quad's
mip bias (lq of a value 2^s larger is exactly 4s more). A quad that fits
has s = 0 and is drawn bit for bit as before. One geometry stage more
(c_age 4 -> 5). Model2.sv R3D_UVSH = M2A: main keeps the clamp (its store
has two spare bits there -- 193 of 195 -- so it could take this at no M10K
if wanted).
*VERIFIED:*
  * tb_m2_raster3d in the 2A raster configuration (TEXLUT, KW 20, window
    key, REALCOL, game 0x14) on MAME's frame 100: colour vs MAME mean 15.77
    -> 12.81 (>32: 10.47% -> 8.10%); the sea polygon alone 15.31 -> 8.22;
    its texel coordinates against MAME's own (owners.txt tu/tv, every
    fetch): more than 8 texels off 92.3% -> 3.4%, mean u 18.5 -> 1.6, v
    30.2 -> 1.3 texels. Frame 90 the same way: 14.45 -> 11.55; sea
    85.7% -> 3.0% of fetches > 8 texels off. With mip-mapping on (MIPMODE 3,
    MIPZX 0) frame 100: 12.56 -> 10.26.
  * s forced on EVERY quad of frame 100 (bench M2_R3D_UVSHMIN, ~1,100
    polygons), mip on: s = 1 moves the level of 59 of 55,307 fetches and
    the colour error 13.33 -> 13.36; s = 2: 207 levels, 13.93. The shift and
    the mip compensation are right over a whole frame, at both shifts, and
    cost a quad that fits almost nothing even if it were shifted.
  * NOTHING ELSE MOVES. The same RTL with UVSH 0: frame 90's pixel hash
    equal to the old RTL's (568c370cef941f38); Daytona frame 2000 in the
    main configuration (TEXLUT 0, KW 16) equal (f5eb78853a18b2ef). UVSH 1
    on games with no quad past 2,048 texels: VF2 frames 600 and 3480, Sega
    Rally 960, Daytona 2000 -- pixel hashes equal to the old RTL's, mip off
    and (VF2, Rally) mip on. Sky Target frame 1080 changes: ten horizon-
    strip quads (header 40db) are exactly 8,192 quarter-texels wide, one
    past the clamp, and now shift by one; 2,844 px differ, the strip's error
    vs MAME 35.23 -> 34.96, the frame's 12.23 -> 12.26. Not R938's sky lines
    (those are in the sky above, not this strip).
  * test_m2_geometry, test_m2_geo, test_m2_quad_store, test_m2_raster3d,
    test_m2_span_tex (+ftb, mip), test_m2_raster_fill (+mip),
    test_m2_raster_band PASS; lint_top clean on 2A and M2_NO_2A, -Wall
    warnings for the five files unchanged (one unused q_uvs on M2_NO_2A,
    waived); lint_idx: the same 114 findings as before; quartus_map
    --analyze_file on the four modules and Model2.sv: 0 errors.
*AREA (quartus_map 17.0, whole design, 2A, cc9510d -> this):* ALMs needed
40,120 -> 40,110 (-10, noise); combinational ALUTs 57,178 -> 57,190;
registers 48,097 -> 48,250; block memory bits 4,572,656 -> 4,580,912 (+8,256: the two
store banks 2048 x 197, the span queue 32 x 262); DSP 96 unchanged; no new
"uninferred" RAM. M10K: 548 -> 550 of 553 expected (the store's two banks
go from 39 to 40 blocks; the fitter confirms).
*BENCH NOTE:* a 2A-configuration tb_m2_raster3d run needs M2_R3D_WINKEY=1
beside -GKW=20, or polygons of a later window sort by z alone -- Sky Target
frame 1080 then shows its horizon strip covered by the sea (a bench
artefact, not the core).
*LEFT / OPEN:* the hull's window rows look brighter and more aliased in the
bench than in MAME, before and after (MAME blends two levels; this core
takes the nearest) -- not part of Ben's report, not chased. On the board:
the sea beside the ship should be water like the open sea.

**R938 -- THE "SEAMS" (GitHub #26 / #27, Sky Target's sky lines) ARE NOT
COVERAGE GAPS: A SPAN'S CUT-SHORT LAST TEXEL GROUP WAS SAMPLED UP TO 1.5 PX
PAST THE SPAN'S END. Fixed in m2_span_tex (all three cores), +35 ALM (map).**
(Reports, mike911ok on Model2A_20261022: #26 Sega Rally -- a thin white line
across the car's shadow while racing, a row of white dots across the attract's
sky; #27 VF2 -- dots in the sky near the distant hills on stage 1, a white
dotted line where the floor meets the wall on Jacky vs Sarah's stage. Ben on
s1386 (model2a + R937): VF2's towered stage shows a single green pixel ~4 px
ABOVE a conifer's tip, flickering, unchanged by the filter and mip settings;
Sky Target's title sky has darker 1-px vertical lines at ~0.21 and ~0.60 of
the width; Rally's shadow line looks like a texture seam to him.)

*What was believed:* polygon seams -- a fill rule, vertex snapping or
clipper T-junction leaving pixels that neither polygon of a shared edge
covers ("polygon alignment").

*NOW KNOWN (MEASURED, MAME 0.289 m2lod dumps; tb_m2_raster3d in Model2.sv's
2A raster configuration; ROM-derived scratch outside the tree):*
  * COVERAGE IS WATERTIGHT. (a) MAME's own post-clip polygons through this
    core's fill (NOTEX, owner = polygon): pixels where the core shows a
    polygon behind every polygon MAME shows in the 3x3 around it -- Rally
    attract frames 960 / 1500 / 2040: 10 / 47 / 5, VF2 600 / 3480: 8 / 16,
    all in tiny far objects (the distant cars). (b) The whole path -- this
    core's geometry (geodiff_2a, CRTC_Y 128 for Rally) on MAME's walks, then
    this fill -- against MAME's polygons through the same fill: Rally walks
    1920 and 3000, VF2 walk 1200: 0 pixels where the core's depth is behind
    the MAME-vertex picture's 3x3; every vertex MAME shares bitwise between
    polygons (1,074 / 1,672 / 811 on screen) lands on ONE quarter-pixel
    position in all of the core's quads (0 disagreements); of MAME's
    clipper-made near-coincident pairs (< 0.02 px, 125 / 82 / 58), one lands
    a quarter apart. The fill rule (R658's MAME poly.h rule on quarter-pixel
    vertices) shares edges exactly: both polygons walk a shared edge from the
    same top vertex with the same slope.
  * VF2's SKY AND DISTANT HILLS ARE THE 2D LAYER: MAME's 3D buffer covers
    39% of rows 0-47 and 46% of rows 48-95 over 154 attract frames (Rally:
    100% everywhere -- its sky is 3D, polygons at z ~62,000). So #27's sky
    dots are not 3D seams unless they are the tree-tip dot below.
  * THE CAUSE. Texel step 4 (the OSD's default, pxk 2) gives a group of four
    pixels one texel, sampled at the group's centre (R616, (2^pxk - 1)/2 px
    in). A span's last group is cut short at x1 -- 1 to 3 pixels -- and a span
    shorter than a group is all one cut-short group; both were still sampled
    1.5 px in: up to 1.5 px PAST the span's last pixel, outside the polygon,
    where u/v are extrapolated beyond the polygon's own range.
    Sky Target (MAME frame 1080): sky panels 17 and 14 meet at x ~110; panel
    17's u at the joint is 2047/8 = 255.875 of a 256-texel, wrapping texture.
    Row 70: the group at x 109 (pixels 109-110, the span's end) was sampled
    at x 110.5+: u 255.78 (fetch 65480/256) where MAME's exact u at 109 is
    255.03 and at 110 255.66 -- the bilinear tap past 255.5 is texel 0 of the
    wrapped edge, darker: a dashed dark column at every panel joint. MAME
    shows the joint faintly (its own bilinear wraps there too, by less); the
    same bench at texel step 1 (pxk 0) matches MAME's picture.
    VF2 towered stage (scripted play, MAME frame 3360): the conifer's top is
    a translucent billboard; its narrow apex rows end in cut-short groups
    sampled past the end into the leaves' texels -- three detached green
    pixels at (272,19), (281,23), (282,23), 3-5 px above the visible tip,
    where MAME paints no 3D at all: Ben's dot, reproduced.
  * NOT THE FILTER, NOT MIP: Point sampling takes the nearest of the same
    taps, so the extrapolated coordinate picks the wrong texel there too
    (Ben's filter/mip test agrees). The texel step IS the knob: on the
    released core, OSD texel step 1 should remove both (an A/B for the board
    without a build).

*THE FIX (m2_span_tex, GC builds -- PXC 1, every core):* a cut-short group
is sampled at its FIRST pixel, without the centre offset -- inside the span,
never further from any of its pixels than R616's centre is from a whole
group's. A span shorter than a group loads without the offset (ld_short); the
issue pointer steps to a cut-short last group by the group step less the
span's offset (iss_half; the offsets gc_ur/gc_vr/gc_or latched with the
span). Whole groups are unchanged. (A first version stepped the last group by
half a group -- 0.5 px left of its first pixel; it removed the seam but its
interior error was larger, so it was replaced before commit.)

old RTL fails it (planted: u, level and texture-word mismatches).

**R945 -- THE 93C46 IN THE NVRAM FILE: THE GAMES' SETTINGS SURVIVE A POWER
CYCLE (GitHub #15 Sega Rally, #21 Manx TT; House of the Dead on 2C). Benched,
NOT FITTED, NOT ON A BOARD.**

*Believed:* R919 (implementation findings): "The 2A core's 93C46 is never
saved ... INFERRED: GitHub #15 is this." m2_93c46's header: persistence "not
here yet". Hanguk Pro Yagu 98's MRA: "The EEPROM is not saved". The plan:
append the EEPROM to the backup RAM's <nvram> region (16 KB + 128 B = 16512)
-- MiSTer sends the .nvm after the ROMs, so a saved file overrides the MRA's
default, and with no file the default stays.

*Which games (VERIFIED, MAME 0.289 model2.cpp):* EEPROM_93C46_16BIT "eeprom"
is in model2a (l.2716), model2b (2854) and model2c (2995): every 2A, 2B and 2C
set keeps its settings there (eeprom_w / in0_r on the 315-5649's port A / B).
So all eleven 2A MRAs (VF2, Sega Rally, Virtua Cop 2, Sky Target, Manx TT,
Motor Raid, DOA, Zero Gunner, Dynamite Cop, Pilot Kids, Hanguk Pro Yagu 98)
and the three 2C ones (House of the Dead, Over Rev, STCC). MAME ships a default
image for hpyagu98 (hpyagu98_nvram, already MRA index 5, R897), manxtt
(manxtt_dx_nvran) and manxttc; only hpyagu98's is loaded -- Manx TT boots
blank, fails its CRC test and writes its factory settings (R892 item 5), and
now keeps whatever the test menu sets after that.
The original board (model2o: Daytona, Desert Tank, Virtua Cop) has no 93C46
on the main board; its settings are the backup RAM ("backup1"), already in the
.nvm. Its I/O board's 93C45 (model1io.cpp) is the I/O firmware's own: MAME's
daytona93 nvram from three separate sessions here (~/.m2-mame-play, ~/roms,
nvram/) has three different backup1 files and one identical ioboard_eeprom
("SEGA" and the firmware's defaults, written to a virgin part at boot).
INFERRED: nothing a Daytona test menu sets lives there (not tested by changing
one in MAME). main is unchanged; m2_ioz80's EEPROM stays volatile.

*Main_MiSTer, what it actually does (VERIFIED, mra_loader.cpp / file_io.cpp
at 915ca33, 2026-08-29):*
  1. ONE <nvram> per MRA: nvram_idx and nvram_size are single statics, a
     second element replaces the first. A second index is not possible; the
     EEPROM has to be in index 2's region.
  2. arcade_nvm_load runs when the parser closes the <nvram> element -- after
     the <rom>s before it, before those after it (every Model 2 MRA has it
     before index 0, so the game is in reset). Only if the file opens; then it
     allocates the MRA's size, memsets it to ZERO, reads min(file, size) over
     it and sends ALL of it. A 16 KB file under a 16512 MRA arrives as 16 KB
     and 128 zero bytes: the plan's layout would load 64 zero words over the
     MRA's default (Hanguk Pro Yagu 98: "Error #1", R897), and a plain-sum
     checksum passes on zeros. So the tail starts with a tag and the core
     takes the EEPROM only after it.
  3. arcade_nvm_save runs on the OSD's close only when UIO_CHK_UPLOAD (0x3C)
     answers -- the core's ioctl_upload_req, the "Save settings (NVRAM)" line.
     Unchanged: the user saves as for backup RAM today.
  4. THE OLD CORE'S BACKUP WRITE WAS UNBOUNDED (hps_word = ioctl_addr[13:2]):
     a longer file wraps onto backup words 0-33. Shown in the bench (the
     "nobound" mutation: backup word 0 reads 00000000 after a zero-padded 16 KB
     file). A 16520 MRA must never run on a pre-R945 Model2A rbf -- the MRAs
     and the rbf ship together.

*The design (rtl/io/m2_nv_port.sv, Model2.sv M2_2A_EE_SAVE, on by default):*
  index 2, 16520 bytes:
    0x0000-0x3fff  backup RAM, as before
    0x4000-0x4007  "M2EEPROM" (4 words, all must match, in order)
    0x4008-0x4087  the 93C46, word n = bytes 2n / 2n+1 (MAME's .nv, as index 5)
  The tag comes first so the words go straight into the EEPROM's load port as
  they arrive (a tag after them would need a 64-word staging copy). No tag, a
  damaged tag or a 16 KB file: the EEPROM stays as the MRA and power-on left
  it. The save reads the EEPROM through a second registered read port on
  m2_93c46 (DUMP), a second 64 x 16 MLAB copy, while the game runs. Every load
  write is registered (R593's pattern); the backup write is bounded to
  0x0000-0x3fff. The NVRAM path moved out of Model2.sv into m2_nv_port so the
  bench runs the code that is built; the save request (status[17]) and the
  upload pipeline (3 cycles, address to ioctl_din) are as they were.
  MRAs: every Model2A / Model2C <nvram> 16384 -> 16520 (mra/, releases/mra/);
  the Model2 (original) MRAs stay 16384.

*Bench (test_m2_nv_save, new):* Main's SPI words (FIO_FILE_INDEX / TX / TX_DAT,
UIO_CHK_UPLOAD; the zero-padded buffer of arcade_nvm_load) through the real
sys/hps_io.sv, m2_nv_port, m2_backup and the 315-5649's 93C46; the i960 side
bit-bangs the EEPROM as eeprom_w / in0_r and reads all 64 words back
serially (the game's own view). Each round, with a random default image
(index 5) or none, 1-64 random settings, random backup RAM words and an SPI
strobe spacing log-uniform 4-400 clk_sys a word:
  boot 1  no .nvm -> the MRA's default; settings written; OSD save: the
          16520-byte file checked byte for byte (backup, tag, 64 words)
  boot 2  that file -> the saved settings and backup RAM; saving again gives
          the identical file
  boot 3  no file -> the default        boot 4  a 16 KB file -> the default,
  boot 5  one tag bit flipped -> the default         the file's backup RAM
  boot 6  the file under a 16384 MRA -> the default
240 rounds (seed 7): 1,440 simulated power-ons, 107,520 EEPROM words read
back serially, 7.9 MB uploaded, 1.01 billion simulated clk_sys cycles, a few minutes on
this PC: PASS. 24 rounds is the make default. Controls: +spacing=3 (inside
the 3-cycle upload pipeline) FAILS (110 mismatches); five mutations of
m2_nv_port each FAIL -- no tag check (boots 4, 5), no tail write (boot 2), the
backup write unbounded (backup word 0 overwritten), the dump address off by
four words (the saved file), the tag's first-word restart removed (boot 5).
test_m2_315_5649 now also reads all 64 words through the dump port and
compares them with the MAME-transcribed reference: 75,818 dumps, 4.85 million
words over its 2 million random accesses (one module, one instance): PASS.
test_m2_vcop2_guns PASS (its harness and m2_boot_harness tie the new port).

*Checks:* lint_top clean on 2A (default), -DM2_NO_2A, and on model2c's
-DM2_2C=1 -DM2_NO_2A_MANX_MOTION=1; lint_idx: the same 113 candidates before
and after, none in the changed code; quartus_map --analyze_file m2_nv_port,
m2_93c46, m2_315_5649: 0 errors.

*AREA (quartus_map 17.0, 2A, release macros, whole design):*
  (ee-save 028aaa0 against model2a 65f10ac, mapped side by side here)
                       ALMs needed  regs    block bits  MLAB bits  M10K RAMs
     model2a 65f10ac   40,039       48,093  4,572,656   47,068     86
     ee-save           40,096       48,145  4,572,656   48,092     86
     difference        +57          +52     0           +1,024     0
  m2_nv_port 63 ALUT / 67 registers (Model2.sv's own share fell 699 -> 656
  ALUT: the old path moved into it); m2_93c46 146 -> 163 ALUT, 106 -> 128
  registers, and its array is two 64 x 16 MLABs (ee_rtl_0 / ee_rtl_1, both
  "MLAB, Simple Dual Port"), not flip-flops. No M10K, no DSP.

*Not done / open:* not fitted, not on a board. The board check: change a
setting in Sega Rally's or Manx TT's test menu, Save settings, power off and

index 5 (not done: the game builds its own). 2B is not built. The 2C HOTD CRT
