**R944 -- SEGA RALLY'S CAR-SHADOW DOTS ARE T-JUNCTION CRACKS: QUARTER-PIXEL
VERTICES ON ONE QUAD'S LONG EDGE AND THREE QUADS' SHORT ONES. REPRODUCED IN
THE BENCH THROUGH THE CORE'S OWN PATH, THEN CLOSED BY MOVING EACH EDGE OF A
FLAT QUAD OUT BY (1 + |dx/dy|) / 8 PX (m2_raster_fill DIL). Branch
rally-crack (off bridge-r937-2a 5ffd438), not pushed, not fitted.**
(Board, s1415: Rally attract, the CHAMPIONSHIP TOP 16 screen over the
Celica's rear: two rows of evenly spaced single-pixel holes in the black
shadow along two long, shallow lines -- R938's board verdict. Measured on
Ben's grab: one hole per scanline, ~39 px apart on the upper row, ~27 px on
the lower. GitHub #26's line while racing is the same shadow.)

*What was believed (R938):* the shadow is "a mesh sharing exact vertices,
and the fill covers it without a gap" -- not reproduced, because none of
R938's frames had this shadow at this angle. And R938's whole-path test
counted a pixel as a hole only where the core's geometry was worse than
MAME's vertices through the SAME fill, so a crack the fill makes on both
was invisible to it by construction.

*NOW KNOWN (MEASURED; MAME 0.289 m2lod dumps of srallyc, ROM-derived
scratch outside the tree):*
  * THE SCENE. A 200 s attract survey (thumbnails every 30 3D frames, no
    inputs) puts the Top 16 rear close-up at 3D frames ~7230-7330. Dumped
    frames 7290, 7292 .. 7300 (M2DIFF) and, by a file trigger on every walk
    while the frame count was 7294-7300, walks 8894-8899; frame F's list is
    walk F + 1598 here (matched by vertex values -- R938's "walk = 2 x
    frame" does not hold this far in). Frame 7300 in the bench is Ben's
    picture within a few frames of camera.
  * REPRODUCED, BOTH WAYS, IN Model2.sv's 2A RASTER CONFIGURATION
    (tb_m2_raster3d: PIXSTEP 4, FB, FRB 2, M2COV, SPLIT_TRI, TEXLUT, KW 20
    with M2_R3D_WINKEY=1, UVSH, TEXMEM for the textured picture). Holes =
    pixels MAME gives to the shadow (its flat black polygons, h 00c0 ..
    0000) that the core paints with something else while both neighbours
    across are shadow:
      MAME's post-clip vertices, frames 7290..7300:  6 17 19 22 25 22
      the core's geometry (geodiff, CRTC_Y 128, WINKEY, MZX, UVSH) on
      walks 8894..8899, its quads through the same raster bench:
                                                     22 14 25 20 22 17
      MAME's own frames:                             0
    On the matched pairs (7296/8894, 7298/8896, 7300/8898) the two lists
    are the same pixels: the geometry is not involved. The rows lie where
    the board's do: y 259-266 every ~40 px and y 290-304 every ~28 px.
  * THE TWO EDGES (frame 7300, MAME floats). Polygon 0's lower edge
    (422.24,259.98)-(103.75,268.36), 38 px a row; on the other side of it
    polygons 9, 10, 11, whose upper edges split it at (252.61,264.44) and
    (287.93,263.51). Polygon 4's upper edge (80.48,306.08)-(496,290.89),
    27 px a row; polygons 9-11's lower edges split it at (278.57,298.84)
    and (324.76,297.15). The split points are on the long edges to 0.001 px
    in floats -- T-junctions -- and MAME, filling floats, has no gap. The
    geometry rounds every vertex to the nearest quarter, independently: a
    split point and the long edge's ends each move up to 1/8 px in x and
    in y, so the two sides of the edge part by up to (1 + |dx/dy|) / 4 px
    in a row -- several pixels on a 38-px-a-row edge, once a row, where the
    edge crosses the row centre. A Python model of R658's rule on the
    quarter vertices gives the bench's 22 holes of frame 7300 exactly.
  * NOT the fill's edge rule: both sides walk R658's rule on the same edge
    direction; the two "edges" are different lines. More vertex precision
    shrinks it but does not close it (model, frame 7300: 1/8 px 9 holes,
    1/16 5, 1/64 1) and costs the store's width (M10K, 550 of 553).
  * MODEL 1 (the oracle for shared edges): m1_raster_fill covers
    [floor(xl), floor(xr)] -- both ends inclusive, a pixel of overlap on
    every shared edge, never a gap. Model 2's R658 rule (MAME poly.h) is
    exactly abutting, which is watertight only on exact vertices.

*THE FIX (m2_raster_fill, parameter DIL; Model2.sv sets it, every build):*
R658's rule with each walked edge of a FLAT quad moved outward by
(1 + |dx/dy|) / 8 px -- half the widest gap quarter vertices can open, so
the two sides together close any T-junction -- and each edge's x clamped to
its own vertices' extent +/- 1/8 (without it a shallow edge moved out runs
past its end vertex: 18-91 whisker pixels a frame, modelled). The move is
made once per reloaded edge, in the rounding copy (xah / xbh) only, in a new
state S_FS_DIL (code 9, unused S_DIVBW); the clamp is applied as a span
leaves stage 1, off R739's emit path, and a span it empties is dropped.
The overlap on a true shared edge is at most 1/4 px across it, where the
quad drawn later wins. TEXTURED QUADS ARE NOT MOVED: m2_span_tex walks a
span's texel groups from its first pixel, so a textured span start moved out
by a pixel re-phases every group of the span -- measured with textured quads
included: Rally attract 960, 38,863 pixels changed for ~2,000 that change
polygon, whole-frame error vs MAME 9.148 -> 9.294; VF2 3480 6.137 ->
6.356. Rejected; textured T-junctions keep R658's edges (open, below).

    flagged pixel on walk 8895, (405,259), is the car's quad 178, sorted
    between the shadow quads, correctly in front).

**R944, SMALLER (the same pixels, half the area).** The first version spent
+147 ALMs (2A map): the move held in two 32-bit registers (dga / dgb) with
their own |slope| adders, two clamps per edge in registers (lb / ub) formed
in S_OFF, a per-row select of them beside the emit sort, two more registers
carrying them through stage 1, and a separate add for the move. Now:
  * the move has no register and no adder of its own: S_FS_DIL feeds the
    walk's adder (xah_nx = xah + sla in S_FS_WALK) with the move's operands,
    xah + (t or ~t) + (C or 1 - C), t = sl >>> 3, C = 1/8 + 2^-16 -- the
    same value as before bit for bit (|sl| >> 3 by ones' complement);
  * the clamps are two registers per SEGMENT (lbq: the left edge's least
    vertex x - 1/8, ubq: the right edge's greatest + 1/8, chosen by swapf
    and a one-bit "which vertex is lesser" per edge taken from S_DIVA's
    existing subtract), formed in S_FS_DIL, which waits for stage 1 to
    empty so a span keeps its own segment's clamps; the output stage reads
    them directly. Nothing in the emit path (R739) changed.
Measured (module alone, map): the move ~34 ALMs, the clamp ~109 -- the clamp
is still needed (without it 18-91 whisker pixels a frame) and a per-quad
bounding-box clamp instead leaves 1-17 of them (modelled), so it stays per
edge. 11-bit compares and dropping the empty-span test saved < 20 ALMs and
were not taken (the clamp CAN empty a span: x = 10.0, round(x - 1/8) = 10,
round(x + 1/8) - 1 = 9).

*4. THE SCSP AGAINST srg320's (MiSTer-devel/Saturn_MiSTer c072434,
rtl/Saturn/SCSP/SCSP.sv + SCSP_pkg.sv, read-only clone sm2-builds/saturn-ref;
NO LICENCE FILE in that repository -- used as a reference only, nothing
copied, nothing in THIRD_PARTY.md):*
  same as ours and MAME's (no level difference):
    * TL: 10-bit attenuation, TL << 2 on the EG level, 6 dB per 64 steps --
      MAME's 0.375 dB a TL step.
    * DISDL / EFSDL / IMXL: an arithmetic shift by ~SDL (0, -6 ... -36 dB, 0 =
      off) -- MAME's SDL table. The pan: -3 dB a step, the far side 0 dB.
    * The direct sum: each slot's 16-bit send at 1x in an 18-bit accumulator;
      the effect returns (EFREG x EFSDL / EFPAN for slots 0-15) added to it.
    * MIXS: {slot level, 4'h0} >>> ~IMXL summed in 20 bits; the DSP's INPUTS
      MIXS << 4 (24 bits) -- MAME's (x16 then << 4).
    * EFREG = SHFT[23:8], written (not accumulated -- MAME's "+=" after a
      clear is the same here: every program in these captures writes each
      EWA once a sample).
    * The DSP's multiply (24 x 13 >> 12), shifter saturation (SHFT 0 / 1),
      ring addressing (MADRS + DEC + NXADR, masked by RBL, + RBP << 12), and
      its float format: DSPItoF / DSPFtoI against scsp_ref.h's PACK / UNPACK,
      all 2^24 values and all 65,536 words -- 0 differ (scratch fl.cpp).
    * MEMORY ACCESS ON ODD STEPS ONLY: every program here has MRD / MWT on odd
      steps only (none on even), so MAME's rule changes nothing.
    * MADRS IS DECODED AT 0x780-0x7BF ONLY (MADRS_SEL = REG_A[11:6] == 011110)
      -- 0x7C0-0x7FF is not a mirror: R914's decode, independently. The
      Saturn core is the second working implementation (after Mednafen) to
      say MAME's mirror is wrong; R914 stands.
  different:
    * EG key scaling: srg320 adds clamp(KRS + OCT, 0, 15) to the 5-bit rate;
      MAME adds OCT + 2 KRS + FNS[9] to the 6-bit one, so a negative octave
      slows MAME's (and our) envelopes (OCT -2: 1.2x, -3: 1.5x longer decays)
      where srg320's do not. Measured in scsp_ref.h (scratch option):
      HOTD chapter 2 every category within 0.1 dB, Dynamite Cop 0.0 dB. Not
      a level cause; not changed (MAME's formula is the one the reference
      order trusts for what the chip computes).
    * DAC18B: srg320's 16-bit output is the sum << 2 saturated when DAC18B is
      set (MVolCalc), MAME's and ours the sum (the 18-bit DAC's scale). The
      Model 2 drivers set DAC18B (0x400 = 0x0F0F); a uniform 12 dB with
      clipping, no balance change, and nothing on a Saturn exercises it.
      Not taken.
    * FM depth (MDCalc): the same offset as MAME's for MDL 13 within the
      sample (both s/4 samples for X = Y = s); srg320 wraps the offset at
      2,048 samples. No level change.
  Which comparison found what: srg320's MADRS decode confirmed R914; nothing
  in srg320's mix arithmetic differs from ours. The fault this entry fixes
  (5.) was found by following the output past the SCSP into sys/, not by the
  SCSP comparison.

*5. THE TINNY SOUND: THE OUTPUT PATH, ALL GAMES, SINCE R788.* sys/audio_out.sv
samples AUDIO_L / AUDIO_R in its own clock at 48 kHz (sample_ce); its IIR
filter, which low-passes the core's output at a high rate before that, is
not built here (R788, MISTER_DISABLE_AUDIO_FILTER, for 430 ALM). So each 48 kHz
tick takes the 44.1 kHz staircase as it stands: content at f also comes out
at f + 3.9 kHz, and everything above ~16 kHz folds into 4-16 kHz,
inharmonically. MAME resamples properly and the arcade has an analog
reconstruction filter; neither shows this. Measured (pure tones through the
hold-and-48 kHz model): 500 Hz spurs at -34 dB, 2 kHz -22, 4 kHz -16, 8 kHz
-9 dB. On the games (R914 reference audio):
    aliasing products below the signal      as built   linear interpolation
    HOTD chapter 2, whole mix                23.2 dB     32.8 dB
    HOTD chapter 2, the FM voice alone        8.5 dB     15.9 dB
    HOTD chapter 2, everything else          24.9 dB     40.4 dB
    Dynamite Cop 30-38 s                     28.5 dB     40.6 dB
  HOTD's FM voice (sample 0x028C0: PCM16, MDL 13 with MDXSL = MDYSL = 0, a
  triangle pitch LFO) has half its energy at 16-24 kHz (spectral centroid
  10 kHz); as built, 8-12 kHz comes out +9.7 dB and 12-16 kHz +11.1 dB over
  the ideal -- the high-pitched tinny layer, and it plays through the
  chapter-1 boss and all of chapter 2 (1,580 slot-seconds in ch2 against 50
  in the whole attract): Ben's "starts in chapter 2". It does not change
  loudness: A-weighted, 50 ms windows above the median, as built vs ideal
  +0.00 dB median, +0.08 dB max (Dynamite Cop and HOTD alike).
  THE FIX (rtl/sound/m2_snd_lerp.sv, new; in m2_2a_sound behind LERP;
  Model2.sv M2_2A_SND_LERP, default 1 on 2A and 2C): the output moves along
  the line from the previous sample to the current one, one sample late,
  re-evaluated every 64 clocks (1.25 MHz) and held between, so audio_out's
  two-flop equality check takes it cleanly; the phase is the clocks since the
  sample changed x round(2^19 x 441 / T44_DEN) >> 11 (80 MHz: x 289 >> 11).
  tb_m2_snd_lerp (sim/sound, new): the module at 80 MHz on the drain's
  441 / 800,000 accumulator, read as audio_out reads it (two flops at
  24.576 MHz, taken when equal, 48 kHz): full-scale steps and a sweep, 3 s --
  0 of 239,992,744 outputs outside their bracketing samples, 0 reads of a
  value the RTL never held; HOTD's FM voice and the rest (20 s each) through
  the RTL, band energy vs ideal (dB of the ideal total):
                     FM voice: ideal  as built  LERP   | the rest: ideal  as built  LERP
      4-8 kHz              -28.4    -22.5   -28.8   |          -17.7    -17.8   -18.2
      8-12 kHz             -31.8    -22.1   -32.9   |          -25.6    -25.3   -26.9
      12-16 kHz            -31.0    -19.9   -32.6   |          -29.9    -29.6   -32.7
  (the bench model's numbers to the 0.1 dB). tb_m2_2a_sound with LERP on,
  Dynamite Cop 6 s: PASS, 99.5% of writes in order, levels second by second

  lint_idx: no candidate in a changed line (m2_2a_sound's two, line 437's

  * THE CAUSE. The band's top edge is a long shallow line (core quad 418 on
    walk 4076: (0,39.75) to (357.25,54.0), 0.04 px a pixel) along which v is
    exactly texel 128 -- the band uses rows 128-255 of a 256-high texture,
    rows 0-127 hold something else, opaque white at row 127. Once a scanline
    the edge passes within ~0.01 px of a pixel centre; there exact v is
    128.005 or so, and the core's v came out 127.98 (fetch log: 32764 and
    32766 of 32768 /256-texel units). Measured along that edge, the core's v
    is low by 2.1-6.6 /256 texel (mean 4.4) on walk 4076 and -0.2 +- 0.75 on
    walk 4080 (no dots there): the plane fit's quantisation, per quad and
    per frame (R338's 0.02-0.59 texel; MAME's polygons through the same
    raster: +1.2 +- 1.4, no dots). Under 128.0 the bilinear (m2_texel_bl,
    MAME's rule) gives row 127 over half the weight, the alpha test (alpha
    >= 1/2) passes, and the pixel is row 127's white; point sampling takes
    the nearest row, 127, the same way. MAME has exactly the same rule and
    the same knife edge -- its floats are just ~5x less often on the wrong
    side of it.
  * R944'S DIL ON TEXTURED QUADS MAKES IT WORSE: built and measured (both
    `!tex_r[0]` gates off, the plane at the clamped start): every frame a
    dashed white line, 26-34 px, three-pixel dashes at every crossing --
    edges moved out by 1/8 px cover more pixels whose v is under 128. A
    textured T-junction fix would need to keep the samples inside anyway.

*THE FIX (UVCL; m2_raster_fill, m2_raster3d, m2_span_tex; Model2.sv sets it,
every build):* every pixel the fill covers lies inside its quad, so in exact
arithmetic its u and v lie inside the box of the quad's corners. The fill
takes that box per textured quad -- floor of the least u, v and ceil of the
greatest less one, whole texels at level 0, one vertex a cycle beside S_OZ's
normaliser from the raw u, v it already reads (four running compares; a quad
stored >> uvs, R940, gets no box). The box goes beside the span queue: one
45-bit word per textured quad in a 32 x 45 MLAB read asynchronously (no
output register), pushed with the quad's first span (a spare bit of the span
queue, 278 -> 279 of 280); its head stays the quad now leaving until the next
quad's first span reaches the queue's head, and a full queue (31 words: the
word before the head may still be read) holds the fill back. m2_span_tex keeps
a 5-bit word index per span slot and reads the box back at the divided
coordinate's stage; at level 0 it clamps ONLY A NEAR MISS: a coordinate in the
texel just under the floor, or exactly on it, becomes floor + 1/256; one in the
texel just over the top becomes top - 1/256. The alpha test then sees what an
exact coordinate a hair inside sees (under half), and point sampling the
polygon's own texel. Further out is left alone: a first version clamped every
out-of-box coordinate and, where a divide had saturated at a quad's far edge
(VF2 frame 1304, a conifer quad at (385,188)), it painted a tree texel where
MAME shows the stone behind. Level > 0 is not clamped (the box would need the
bounds shifted per group); every dot measured is at level 0.

**R952 -- MORE ROOM BY MAKING THINGS SMALLER, NOTHING SWITCHED OFF: PARALLEL
CONVERTERS TIME-SHARED WHERE THE SCHEDULE HAS IDLE CYCLES, EXCLUSIVE
OPERATORS MERGED, ONE ARITHMETIC IDENTITY. quartus_map 17.0: 2A 40,225 ->
38,718 ALMs needed (-1,507), 2C 40,133 -> 38,774 / 38,842 (-1,359 / -1,291,
two maps of the same logic). M10K 2A -1 (R948's cache merge), 2C =; one MLAB
more on both. Every change checked old against new, cycle for cycle.
BRANCHES room2-2a (off bridge-r937-2a 77a4689) AND room2-2c (off room-2c
c9ee859), LOCAL, NOT FITTED.**

*Believed (R948's helpers, measured again here):* a register removed is room
gained. *Found:* registers alone buy ~0 ALMs on this part -- pipeline copies
already share ALMs with logic (the TGP ALU's 160-register lane: standalone fit
1,788 -> 1,787 ALMs). The ALMs follow the LUTs. And Quartus already merges
two copies of the SAME expression (the engine's pointer steps written twice:
an identical netlist; the divider's two negates: -1 ALUT) and some exclusive
operators inside one register's mux. What it cannot see is a SCHEDULE: N
converters run in one cycle whose results are read on N different cycles, or
in a state that comes cycles later. That is where the room was.

*Method:* every RTL change measured by quartus_map 17.0 on the full design
(2A: Model2.qsf; 2C: + M2_2C=1, M2_NO_2A_MANX_MOTION=1, M2_RECIP_LOGIC=1),
and, because untouched units swing +-70..90 ALUTs between maps (i960_fpadd,
unchanged RTL: 1,032 / 1,075 / 1,106 / 1,123), by a standalone map + FIT of
the changed module at the core's parameters (virtual pins, the project's
synthesis settings). Timing: near-critical registers (within 0.6 ns) dumped
from copies of s1446 / s1447 (2A) and s1449 / s1462 (2C) with quartus_sta;
nothing on that list was given logic. Identity: NEW sim/miter/miter.py builds
an old-against-new miter -- the module (and changed submodules, renamed) twice
from the same inputs, every output compared on every cycle -- run under the
module's existing benches (sim/miter/fill.sh, sim/miter/geo.sh).

*TAKEN -- geometry and fill (this session):*
  1. m2_geometry / m2_geo_clip: THE u/v CONVERSIONS SHARED. The quad
     projector ran eight u2f (16-bit integer to float) in Q_IDLE's cycle;
     the clipper reads them only on clip_in_valid, eight cycles later at the
     earliest (Q_MM, Q_MM2, Q_CHK, four granted Q_ISS, an answer). Now the
     pairs are latched raw (puv) and two u2f convert a vertex a cycle
     (puv -> uvsel -> hu/hv, done four cycles after the take). And the eight
     f2uvw that ran on the clipper's output EVERY cycle (cu -> wu) are gone:
     the clipper keeps qwu / qwv = f2uvw(qu / qv) beside qu / qv, written
     wherever they are -- K_IDLE from the raw pairs (f2uvw(u2f(n)) = n for
     every 16-bit n), K_POPR through two f2uvw on the stack word. wu reads
     it. m2_geometry own 2,327 -> 1,537 ALUTs, m2_geo_clip 1,398 -> 1,545,
     +294 registers; standalone fit 6,617 -> 6,284 ALMs; 2A map -301.
     TIMING: s1449's poly_uv3 -> hu[3][15] (0.669 ns) is gone (hu now from
     local registers); cu -> f2uvw -> wu (R614's path) is now cwu -> wu.
  2. m2_raster_fill: ONE NORMALISER FOR THE PLANE FIT'S SIX NUMERATORS.
     S_PF_NRM negated six numerators at once, counted twelve halves, joined
     six. They are read one a state (R742: wait 3, wait 4, Q1, Q1W, Q2, Q2W);
     one pipeline (select, magnitude, halves, join) started on S_PF_N's
     second cycle finishes each the cycle before it is read (nxu_z exactly
     when it was). Fill 5,626 -> 5,247 ALUTs, 4,119 -> 3,969 ALMs (fit).
  3. m2_geo_project: one mag8 for both coordinates -- x's in S_A1 while the
     adder returns y (sx_f landed), y's in S_RND, a 2:1 select in front.
     Projector 473 -> 376 ALUTs (fitted 386 -> 321 ALMs). A first version
     ran mag8 on the adder's result as each landed: -122 ALUTs, but the new
     path fp_add|result -> mx_r became the standalone worst (2.43 ns at
     12.5) next to s1462's project sst -> clip kst (0.199 ns) -- not taken.
  4. m2_geo_engine: the texture header's three word addresses (th_w + 1 /
     + 2 / + 3 in F_TH0..2) from one adder: engine -42 ALUTs.
  5. m2_raster_fill: one adder per edge accumulator. xa / xb took three sums
     in three states (S_OFF, S_FS_MULA / MULB, S_FS_WALK), xah / xbh two
     outside the walk's own (S_OFF, MULA); now one each, the operand picked
     by the state. xbh -> s1_valid (0.525 ns, s1446) is the emit path, not
     touched; xah / xbh's D mux loses a source. Fill 5,247 -> 5,112 ALUTs,
     3,969 -> 3,856 ALMs.
  6. m2_raster_fill: each plane's two corner products summed once: base_u =
     A - (bp_ux << k) - (bp_uy << k) + D is A - ((bp_ux + bp_uy) << k) + D in
     32 bits, and bp_ux + bp_uy = 32'(dudx * x + dudy * y). One subtract
     fewer per plane, 82 registers fewer, DSPs unchanged (38). Fill 5,112 ->
     5,027 ALUTs, 3,856 -> 3,814 ALMs.

**R957 -- R944'S EDGE DILATION BEHIND AN OSD SWITCH, "SEAM FILL", OFF BY
DEFAULT: EVERY CAR IN SEGA RALLY GOT WHITE DOTS FROM IT.** Ben, on the board,
2026-10-24, on the released Model2A_20261024 (s1468): dotted white lines along
the polygon edges of the player's Lancia (and every car), absent on
Model2A_20261022 and in MAME. Board bisect: s1447 (R944 + R940, no R951, no
R952) has them; the room-only build (R952, DIL 0, UVSH 0) does not. Bench
(R955's agent, MAME srallyc 3D frame 4940, 252 polygons at the board's
settings): int-2a 605 isolated wrong pixels, 309 pure white; DIL 0 408 and
pixel-identical to the 20261022 RTL; UVSH 0 and UVCL 0 change nothing. The
cause: the cars' bodies are FLAT white panels with the livery as textured
decals drawn over them in painter's order; R944 moves each flat edge out by
(1+|dx/dy|)/8 px, so a white panel's widened edge paints over the decal of
the panel beside it, one pixel where the moved band crosses a row centre.
Any dilation overlaps a neighbour, so R944 cannot keep the shadow fix and
be free of this in general; MAME's polygons abut exactly. What was believed
(R944: a flat-quad-only dilation is safe because it only closes gaps) was
wrong: it also overlaps.
  Fix: the DIL hardware stays (parameter DIL 1 on 2A), gated per quad by a
run-time input dil_on, latched at S_IDLE with the quad (the stages behind it
are empty then): dil_e = DIL && dil_q replaces DIL in the four places it
selects (S_FS_DIL, s1_dc, the empty-span drop, the walk entry). OSD
"O[68],Seam fill,Off,On" (a bit never used, so saved configs open Off),
three flops into clk_sys. Off is the DIL 0 fill exactly. Rally's car-shadow
cracks (R944's target) return with it Off. main and model2c never had R944.
  Checks: lint_top clean; test_m2_fill_dil (dil_on 1) checks 3,007 fails 0;
test_m2_raster_fill_mip 1,989,828 / 0; test_m2_raster3d, quad_store,
span_tex_uvcl PASS. LEFT: a narrower rule that fills only real gaps (any
widening overlaps), measured before it is offered.
  R957, SHADOWS: Ben asked for the black-only rule to test (R955's agent
measured it as a parameter DILK, not committed: Rally shadow frame 7300 holes
DIL 0 22 / DIL 1 0 / black-only 0; Lancia frame 4940 no white dots, 156 px
change against DIL 0, all black flat trim overlapping by the same 1/8 px,
error vs MAME 2.980 -> 3.031 against DIL 1's 3.303). Built as the switch's
middle setting: "O[69:68],Seam fill,Off,Shadows,All" (3 reads as Off);
dil_on is 2 bits, and the fill latches dil_q = On || (Black only && the quad's
colour is 0) with the quad -- one 24-bit zero compare, no new state.
test_m2_fill_dil (On) 3,007 / 0, raster_fill_mip and raster3d PASS.

*THE MECHANISM.* R652's hold: a finished list waits for the draw in progress
and, while it waits, the vblank interrupt and the next walk are withheld
(Model2.sv r3d_game_hold; 3D pacing tied to Hold game by R831). VCop2's frame
loop waits for the vblank counter, so every list drawn in over a vblank costs
the game a whole vblank: 28.75 game frames a second while the train is busy,
the game's own clock at half speed -- "the game slows a lot". The 2D (HUD)
holds with it by design.

**R955 -- THE "TREE PIXELS": A NEGATIVE DIVIDED COORDINATE WAS SATURATED TO
THE FAR EDGE OF THE TEXTURE, NOT CLAMPED TO 0 AS to_tx SAYS, AND R951'S
NEAR-MISS CLAMP NEVER SAW IT. FIXED (m2_span_tex NEGZ). DOA's SEAMS ARE
TEXTURED T-JUNCTION CRACKS; DIL ON TEXTURED QUADS CLOSES THEM AND IS
REJECTED. Branch tree-px (off int-2a b4250d8), not pushed, not fitted.**
(Board, s1468 = int-2a: Sega Rally, a stray pixel near the trees; VF2,
Lau's stage, the conifer dot "much better" since R951 but still there; Pilot
Kids, a green pixel a few pixels from the tree seen through the bedroom
window; DOA and VF2 Jacky / Sarah, seams showing the 2D layer.)

*What was believed (R951):* a near miss outside a quad's u / v box is
caught by the box clamp. Anything further out is "a fit gone wrong" and is
left alone.

*NOW KNOWN (MEASURED; MAME 0.289 m2lod dumps, ROM-derived scratch in
sm2-builds/tree-px-data; the core's geometry (geodiff 2A) on MAME's walks;
tb_m2_raster3d at the board's settings, benchbd):*
  * THE FAULT. Stage 4a of the divide forms u/z x 1/z as a 64-bit UNSIGNED
    product (d3_r1 is unsigned). A negative u/z -- a pixel a hair inside an
    edge where u is 0, pushed a few 1/256 texel under 0 by the plane fit's
    quantisation, R951's knife edge -- gives a two's-complement pattern that
    the logical shift and sat32 turn into 0x7FFFFFFF, i.e. texel 4095.996.
    to_tx's own comment says negative coordinates clamp to 0. They never
    did once the product went 64-bit (R468 / R718). At a no-wrap edge
    4095.996 is the texture's LAST column (MAME's rule for u just under 0,
    model2rd fetch_bilinear_texel, applied to a far bigger miss). And
    R951's clamp compares 4095 with the box floor 0: "not the texel under
    0", so it is left alone. R951 is blind exactly where most boxes start.
  * SEEN IN THE FETCH LOGS: 2-32 saturated coordinates a frame in every
    game looked at (VF2 1304 walks, Rally 2724 walks, Pilot Kids 9000
    walks, Rally 4940). Rally's canyon start (walks 4074-4082): 10-32 a
    frame, mostly the roadside trees and bushes and the car beside them
    (textures c319a5 / c399a5). VF2's conifers: u 0 at each plane's top,
    the trunk in columns 254-255 (v 56-71). A top-edge pixel over the
    tree's axis that goes negative paints a trunk texel above the canopy,
    the class of Ben's dot.
  * THE FIX (NEGZ, Model2.sv sets it, every build): the sign of u/z (and
    v/z) is registered beside the product, and a negative one gives d4 = 0.
    to_tx gives 0, and R951's clamp ("exactly on the floor") makes it
    floor + 1/256, where MAME's exact coordinate is. Two flops, and the
    sign folded into sat32's existing select.
*VERIFIED:*
  * Rally walks 4074-4082 (the core's geometry, board settings): 13 pixels
    change in the 9 frames (0 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 1 / 3 / 4). Every one
    was a near-black stray (0x1082 or 0x0000) among the trees' and car's
    greens and greys and now takes its neighbours' colour. On the walk
    matched to MAME's frame 2724 (walk 4080) the one changed pixel's error
    vs MAME is 58 -> 12. R951's sky dots on the same walks: 0 before and
    after. The images are tp/img/rally_4076_negz.png (scratchpad).
  * VF2 1304 walks 2110-2119: 2 pixels change in 10 frames, neither on a
    conifer. Pilot Kids 9000 walks 9309-9315: 3 pixels (the umbrella's
    fringe). MAME's polygons, Rally 4940: 2 px, 3.303 -> 3.302. Rally 7300
    (R944's shadow frame): unchanged. NEGZ 0 is pixel-identical to int-2a
    (Rally 4940 hash 466f11933cfcf722).
  * Unit: new test_m2_span_tex_negz (in `make test`): R951's coordinate
    test with one span in four starting at a negative u/z and crossing 0;
    8,930 negative fetches, each must be 0 then clamped. PASS, 7,226
    checks. The old RTL against it FAILS (got fffff, want 00001).
    test_m2_span_tex_uvcl unchanged (7,225 checks, PASS).
  * lint_top clean (2A and M2_NO_2A). lint_idx 111, the base's count.
*NOT REPRODUCED:* the conifer dot itself and the Pilot Kids window-tree
pixel. In 10 VF2 walks only one conifer top-edge pixel saturated (179,152),
at v 36.9, transparent in column 255. In 54 tiled copies of that tree (scaled
0.94-1.06, moved in quarter pixels) none did. The window tree in Pilot Kids
is three screen-parallel quads (constant 1/z), whose left edge u = 0 sits
on a pixel boundary: no knife edge. NEGZ removes the one mechanism found
that puts a texel from outside the polygon's top edge above a tree. Whether
it is Ben's dot is for the board to say; a photo of the dot with Texture
filter Point would pin it down.

*(B) SEAMS.* Coverage-only bench (NOTEX, every quad flat so DIL applies):
  * DOA frame 7290 (the temple, the ceiling's edge over the frieze), MAME's
    polygons: 20 see-through pixels with DIL off, one every ~21 px along one

    textured picture DIL leaves textured quads alone, and the same 22 pixels

  * VF2 5310 (the stage under the bridge, from the attract): 1-3

**R958 -- "ANALOG CONTROL": TWO WHEEL LAYOUTS (WHEEL A / WHEEL B) BESIDE THE
PAD'S, FOR EVERY DRIVING AND RIDING GAME ON ALL THREE CORES (GitHub #12).**

(Section: §10. Authority: the request itself -- a wheel owner's description of
what MiSTer Main reports for two kinds of wheel, after Jotego's OutRun core's
"Analog control" option. No MAME question: the game-side values are the
existing ADC ranges, 0x20..0xE0 (R835/R837, R862/R887, R928/R933). Model 1
has no wheel layout to follow.)

*What was there.* R816 / R831: the pedals share the right stick's Y (split by
sign, O[28] "Pedals" swaps the halves), steering is the paddle, else the left
stick's X past a dead zone of +-12, else (O[54] "Right stick: Pedals+steer")
the right stick's X past the same dead zone, else the d-pad's ramp. That fits
a wheel only if MiSTer maps it onto the right stick. The reporter's wheels
(the cathoderayblog guide's setup; and newer direct-drive pedal sets such as
the Logitech RS50) put the wheel on the left stick's X and each pedal on its
own axis, so neither pedal worked.

*What is added.* O[71:70] "Analog control: Standard / Wheel A / Wheel B".
O[71:70] is free on main, model2a, model2c, dilk-2a / dil-off-2a (Seam fill,
O[69:68] / O[68]) and every other local branch (searched: no O[] or status[]
use above 69 bar hps_io's own status words and O[122:121]); 0 is today's
behaviour, so a saved config opens on Standard, and 3 (unreachable from the
OSD) reads as Standard. All of it is in m2_cab_inputs, the one block every
analog game goes through (main's Daytona / Desert Tank directly; the 2A / 2C
games through m2_2a_inputs' cab_steer / accel / brake), so it lands once:
  steering   Wheel A and B: the left stick's X, always, with NO dead zone (a
             wheel's first degrees are steering, not noise); the right stick
             never steers (Wheel B's brake is its X; "Right stick" is
             ignored); the paddle still comes first; the d-pad steers while
             its left / right is held. "Steering" (O[30:29]) and "Steering
             smoothing" (O[51:50]) apply unchanged -- same scale, same
             limiter downstream.
  Wheel A    accelerator = the left stick's Y, brake = the right stick's Y,
             each centre released .. full up (-127) fully pressed; the lower
             half reads released.
  Wheel B    accelerator = the left stick's Y over the whole axis, -127 (up)
             released .. +127 (down) fully pressed; brake = the right
             stick's X, -127 (left) released .. +127 (right) fully pressed.
             Seven-bit pedal = (v + 127) / 2; -128 reads released.
  both       a pedal p (0..127) reads 0x20 + p + p/2: the right-stick pedals'
             own 3/2 scaling (0x20 released, 0xDE full -- the same top a pad
             reaches today; the 0xE0 rail is the buttons'). "Pedals: Swapped"
             exchanges the two pedals. The Accel / Brake buttons still give
             0xE0. The pedal values are registered once (one clk_sys) so the
             new arithmetic is off the stick -> ADC paths R842 / R934 timed.
Per game:
  Daytona USA (both sets), Sega Rally: steering / accelerator / brake as
             above, nothing else.
  Desert Tank (R837's one drive pedal and the lever): Wheel A / B count as a
             wheel, as "Pedals+steer" does -- the further-pressed pedal past
             the dead zone (12) drives, the accelerator forward and the
             brake in reverse, setting the lever; the cannon is the
             d-pad's. Its pedals ARE the cabinet's (HANDLE + ACCEL; the
             third channel is the turret).
  Manx TT, Motor Raid (manxtt ports: THROTTLE, BRAKE, BANK): the wheel banks
             the bike (AN2 = 0xFF - steering, as before), the accelerator
             pedal is the throttle grip and the brake pedal the brake lever.
             No special case: the profile already takes the block's three
             values in those roles.
  Sky Target (0x18): a flight stick. m2_2a_inputs hands the block Standard
             for it whatever the OSD says (p_sky), so its STICKX / STICKY are
             byte for byte as before.
  Over Rev, STCC (2C, R928 / R933): the block's values through the existing
             0x20..0xE0 -> 0x00..0xFF widening and Over Rev's PORT_REVERSE.
             Virtua Cop / VC2 / HOTD (guns) and the digital games: untouched.

*Verified.* tb_m2_cab_inputs (all three branches, identical): Part A, the
DUT at Standard against the 0f3cbc4 block, 30,000,000 checks, 0
mismatches; Part B (Desert Tank, R837 model) 320,000,000 / 0; Part D,
random inputs with Analog control random (Standard / 3 against the 0f3cbc4
block, Wheel A / B against a model written from the request), 145,662,741
checks / 0 (5.35 M Wheel A and 5.22 M Wheel B Daytona cycles, 10.8 M
wheel-model steering checks, 3,980 Desert Tank lever sets to reverse);
Part E, every axis swept -128..+127 in each wheel mode x Pedals Normal /
Swapped x every Steering, 50,202 checks / 0, including the request's
endpoints (released 0x20, full 0xDE, full lock 0x21 / 0xE0 -- -127 gives
0x21 at 3/4 exactly as Standard does), monotonic pedals, the unused axes
inert, buttons, d-pad and paddle precedence; Standard and 3 swept over every
axis x 16 OSD combinations against the 0f3cbc4 block, 327,680 checks, 0
differences (the default unchanged byte for byte); smoothing (Wheel) on the
wheel's X slews 10 counts in 10 steps and settles at 0xE0; Desert Tank's
pedals in A and B. Two mutations (Wheel B's brake read from the right Y; the
mode decode leaking into Standard) each FAIL it. tb_m2_2a_inputs (2A, 2C):
Analog control random, every analog profile against the block with the same
setting, Sky Target against a second block held at Standard; 0 mismatches
(removing the Sky Target exception: 711,768 mismatches). Quartus 17.0
analyze_file clean on both RTL files; the new functions constant-folded by
quartus_map to the bench's values (up(-128) 127, full(-127) 0, full(+127)
127, full(0) 63, an(127) 0xDE). lint_top clean (2C: -DM2_2C
-DM2_NO_2A_MANX_MOTION); lint_idx unchanged but for hps_io's CONF_STR
width (2A's CONF_STR now passes 1,024 bytes, so byte_cnt is a bit wider).
Not fitted; not on a wheel.

*Open.* Whether MiSTer Main reports the RS50-class pedals exactly as the
request says (whole axis, -127 released) is the reporter's account, not
measured here; if a pedal set rests at +127 instead, "Pedals: Swapped" does
not help (it exchanges pedals, not directions) and a Wheel C would be the
fix. Wheel B with a pad and no pedals reads half accelerator and half
brake -- it is for pedal sets only (README says so).

  The data arrival of s1479's DSP path: 2.46 ns of M10K clock-to-out, then

*1. m2_scsp_dsp.* (a) ins, MPRO's output a clock later in a register, for
everything a step decides in ph 2-4; the RAMs' read addresses (TEMP's TRA,
MEMS's / MIXS's IRA -- both banks with OVERLAP --, COEF, MADRS, EFREG's EWA,
which ef_q shows) keep MPRO's output itself, as before. The row is read in
ph 0 and holds from ph 1 until k moves in ph 4, so ins == mp_q in ph 2-4 --
given no MPRO write lands in a run, which m2_scsp guarantees (op_ok holds the
68000's DSP-region accesses off while dsp_busy, and with OVERLAP dsp_pend);
the standalone bench writes only when !busy too. (b) a_off, (TABLE ? 0 : DEC)
+ (ADREB ? ADRS : 0) + NXADR in a register: addr_w is read in ph 3 and 4
only, and none of its terms moves from ph 2 to ph 4 (DEC in D_FIN, ADRS at
ph 4's edge or a go); 16 bits, the mask keeps at most bits 15..0.
  Proof, sim/miter/scsp_dsp.sh (R952's miter.py, old against new, all 11
outputs every clock -- 13 with OVERLAP -- plus two invariants of the new
copy: ins == mp_q in a run's ph 2-4, addr_w == the old copy's in ph 3-4).

*2. m2_sdram.* rr_mask, inflight, nxt_total and nxt_is_write are written
from arb_sel (one-hot whenever rr_valid: rr_sel is the lowest bit of a
non-zero mask, low_pri of one when use_pri), not through rr_grant: rr_mask
<= bit i set iff a bit of arb_sel below i is (all ones when arb_sel[NP-1]) ==
ones << (rr_grant + 1); inflight bit by bit; blen() OR-ed over arb_sel's bits;
we_gr (R421 wrote it and nothing used it). rr_grant stays for nxt_grant. No

0.66 equiv_make / equiv_simple / equiv_induct over the two netlists,
registers and outputs matched by name -- the same command stream, data and

(2,493 equivalence cells), the Model 2 build's (2,373), 2A with AGE (2,524)
and the defaults NP = 5 (1,293). A mutation (the mask one bit off) leaves 16
cells unproven -- the check sees it. The file is the same on dilk-2a,
model2c and int-2c; main's differs (not touched). lint_idx 3 fewer
(inflight[rr_grant], we_p[rr_grant] x 2 gone).

command case). A registered pre_ok would have to equal the live counters'

else the lowest, else the pointer, its masks a decode of the pointer
register beside the requests -- encoded into the same index (one level); the

**R961 -- VIRTUA COP'S OFF-SCREEN BORDER: 2 PX AT EACH EDGE, NOT MAME'S 5%
(R960'S RULE), AND VIRTUA COP 2'S THE SAME ON THE 2A BUILD. BRANCHES
gun-edge-main (OFF main) AND gun-edge-2a (OFF model2a), NOT FITTED.**

*2A (gun-edge-2a):* R960 (branch hotd-gun, off model2c; its entry is there)
found on the board that MAME's lightgun_offscreen_r border -- int(span *
0.05f), X 24 / Y 19 units = 24 / 19 px on Virtua Cop 2's ranges -- hides the
crosshair and turns the trigger into a reload 19-24 px short of every edge,
and changed Virtua Cop 2 and HOTD to the 2-px rule below. This branch
carries that rule to the 2A build's Virtua Cop 2 (M2_2A_VCOP2_GUN, V2 = 1)
with hotd-gun's module (plus the Virtua Cop change below): its HD (House of the Dead) mapping comes along as a parameter that
is off here (Model2.sv leaves HD = 0: every HD term is a constant), and
test_m2_hotd_guns comes with it. Virtua Cop 2's units are unchanged.

*What was believed (R846):* the off-screen bit is MAME model1io2 fpga_r's
rule -- any coordinate within int(span * 0.05) of its range's end: X 24
units, Y 19 (P1_X <= 0x09b or >= 0x25e, P1_Y <= 0x037 or >= 0x196; P2 the
same on its ranges). The core maps a pixel ~1:1 to a unit, so that is 24 px
at each side and 19 px top / bottom where the crosshair is hidden (c_on)
and the trigger reloads: nothing near an edge can be shot. R960 (branch
hotd-gun) found the same on the board for HOTD and Virtua Cop 2 and fixed
those; Virtua Cop was left as it was.

*Does the game itself reject coordinates near the edge? No* (MAME 0.289,
vcopa, fresh NVRAM -- its default calibration, MAME's ranges; the I/O
board's FPGA reads forced through a Z80 read tap, sim/io/mame_m2_vcop_edge.lua;
the revolver counted in snapshots every 0.25 s): in play, three shots at
P1 (0x086, 0x0e6) -- the core's unit for x pixel 2 -- with the off bit
clear: 6 -> 3 rounds; one shot at (0x083, 0x024) with the bit set: reloaded
to 6; two at (0x273, 0x0e6) (x pixel 493): 6 -> 4; one at (0x17c, 0x027) (y
pixel 2): 3; one at (0x17c, 0x1a6) (y pixel 381): 2. Every on-screen edge
value is a shot; the reload is the off bit alone, as R960 found for HOTD.

*The fix (m2_vcop_guns):* off-screen = a reload, or the crosshair pixel
within 2 of an edge (x <= 1 or >= 494, y <= 1 or >= 382 on the 496 x 384
screen) -- edge_q, now for every game; the 5% compares and their constants
(O1XL / O2XL / O2YL) are gone. The units are unchanged. Game units at the
edge: P1 x px 0-1 = 0x083-0x085, px 2 = 0x086 (on), px 493 = 0x273 (on), px
494-495 = 0x274-0x275 (off); P1 y px 2 = 0x027, px 381 = 0x1a6 (on); P2 x px
2 = 0x083, 493 = 0x270; P2 y px 2 = 0x02a, 381 = 0x1a6. A MiSTer-calibrated
gun or stick at +-127 lands on pixel 1 / 494 (x) and 1 / 382 (y): off, so
shooting off the screen reloads; +-126 is on (3 / 492, 3 / 381). The mouse
clamps to 0..495 / 0..383: its every edge reloads. Kept at 2 px, not wider
(Ben): a USB light gun reports absolute positions, so a wider zone would
reload a gun aimed at a target near the edge. The file is now hotd-gun's
m2_vcop_guns.sv (R960, its V2 / HD parameters off here) with this one
change; main and model2a carry the same file, and hotd-gun needs only this
change to match.

*Proof (2A):* test_m2_vcop2_guns (hotd-gun's bench: the off byte through
the 315-5649 and c_on by the 2-px rule, units as before) 223,916 checks, 0
failures; test_m2_hotd_guns 191,757, 0 failures (mark within 0.542 px);
test_m2_vcop_guns and test_m2_vcop_xhair as below. lint_top clean (the 2A
default build); quartus_map --analyze_file 0 errors.
*Proof (both):* tb_m2_vcop_guns, extended: the off bit and c_on against the 2-px
rule at every stick sample (each value of each axis against the edges and
centre), every one of the 200,000 random mouse packets, the mouse's every
pixel walk, a walk across the middle of the screen both ways for both guns
(off exactly at x 0-1 / 494-495, y 0-1 / 382-383), ten screens past each
edge with the mouse, each axis alone at -128 / -127 / +127 (off) and +-126
(on); units, buttons and reload checked as before. 828,113 checks, 0
failures (main's old module: 20,512 failures, all the off bit / c_on;
its units pass the same checks). test_m2_vcop_xhair PASS. lint_top clean;
verilator -Wall on the module clean for (V2, HD) = 00 / 10 / 11; quartus_map
17.0 --analyze_file 0 errors.

*LEFT:* the fit and the board (Ben). Virtua Cop 2's in-game reload at the
2-px edge is benched in the core, not run in MAME (as R960).

    the car scene just before). This core's geometry (geodiff 2A: CRTC_Y
    127, WINKEY, MZX, UVSH, TEXLUT, M2GD_LAT 12) on walks 4510-4602: 2,243-
    2,249 quads (culled 932, clip in 2,484). Walk time 1,313,880 clk_sys =
    16.4 ms (bench).

    2A raster build), walk 4576: "quads 2048 dropped 198". Quads 2048-2247
    all lie at x 321-449, y 295-331 -- rank 5's score -- and the bench's

    own 2,219 polygons through the same bench (textured): dropped 188, the
    same hole; colour error vs MAME mean 3.55, > 32 on 1.88% of pixels.
  * Not tiny: 10 of the 2,246 are under 4 px both ways, 9 have zero area. No
    threshold can make room; the list needs the slots.

*THE CHANGE (m2_quad_store NX, m2_raster3d QNX; Model2.sv .QNX(M2A ? 512 :
0); FB_DDR3 only).* The two banks are 4,096 slots, and with the framebuffer
the bank on display is dead once its draw is whole (fb_complete). A list now
numbers its quads by POSITION; positions 2,048.. live in the OTHER bank,
counted down from its top. The index arrays hold SLOT CODES {s, address}
(s: the other bank), so the replay's RAM-to-RAM path gains no arithmetic,
only a bank select. The sorted order is two-ended the same way; the sort's
scratch for positions past 2,048 is the other bank's index array from the
bottom (NX <= NQ/2 keeps the two apart). Only the spilled keys need new
storage: key_x, 512 x 20.
  * When the other list is not yet drawn whole, the collecting list stops
    below that list's spill (2,048 - its excess) and is HELD (q_ready low,
    registered two quads early), not refused; the hold ends at its
    fb_complete. Only a swap lowers ofree, and a swap ends the collection.
  * Past 2,560 the excess is refused as before.
  * NX = 0 is the store as it was (the Model 2 build: lint -DM2_NO_2A clean).

*CHECKS (benches, all at the board's run-time settings):*
  * Walk 4576 (owner colours): before dropped 198, the score gone; after
    2,246 stored, "80000" whole. PIXEL- AND CYCLE-IDENTICAL to the old store
    rebuilt with NQ 4,096 (PX md5 c66bc8cc..., draw 633,586 cycles both).
    MAME's polygons textured: 2,236 stored, colour error 3.55 -> 1.53 mean,
    > 32 1.88% -> 0.56%; the picture matches MAME's.
  * The hold: list A (2,246, spilled 198) swapped in, list B (the same
    shifted 7 px) collected at once behind it: B held once for 616,933
    cycles (A's draw), 0 refused; B's picture equals B drawn alone; A's
    shown frame equals A drawn alone (PX md5).
  * An order of magnitude past: a 4,496-quad list alone stores 2,560,
    refuses 1,932; behind a spilled list it is held, then the same; A intact.
  * NX 0 and lists under 2,048 with NX 512: identical to the old RTL (PX md5
    and draw cycles: walk 4576 at NX 0, car scene walk 4462 at NX 512).
  * test_m2_quad_store (also at NX 512, ofree 0), test_m2_raster3d PASS;
    lint_top clean (2A and -DM2_NO_2A); lint_idx 112 lines, as before.
  * quartus_map 17.0 of m2_quad_store alone at the 2A parameters: old 2,252
    ALMs needed; NX 512 2,208; NX 0 2,104 (noise of the map's estimate,
    not a saving to bank). RAMs: as before plus key_x (512 x 20, one M10K);
    the index arrays at 12 bits stay three 2048x5 blocks each. 550 -> 551
    of 553 M10K expected.
  * FOUND ON THE WAY: written as one `x <= sel ? ramA[a] : ramB[b]` with a
    select that depends on the address, Quartus left the index and att
    arrays as flip-flops ("uninferred due to asynchronous read logic",
    60,818 / 84,933 ALMs standalone). Each array is now read into its own
    register and selected after. Verilator cannot see this; only the map.

*COST IN TIME.* The ranking draws in ~1.10 M cycles textured (bench) and the
walk reaches quad 1,850 (where a list behind a spilled one is held) at
971,645 cycles; a hold of up to ~0.13 M cycles (~1.6 ms) on such frames,
INFERRED. The walk is already 1.13 vblanks on the board (x1.2), two vblanks a
list with or without it. Lists under 1,850 never wait.

**R963 -- A FRAMEBUFFER GRAB FROM THE BOARD (READ-ONLY), AND THE TREE PIXELS
SPLIT IN TWO: VF2'S CONIFER DOT IS R955'S FAR-EDGE CLASS (NEGZ, NOT YET IN A
RELEASE); PILOT KIDS' WINDOW SPECKS ARE THE GAME'S OWN SPARSE TEXELS UNDER
MAME'S ALPHA TEST, WHICH NO THRESHOLD CHANGE REMOVES.** Branch wheel-2a
(tools only; no RTL change), not fitted.
(Board, Model2A_20261024b = s1483, which does NOT carry R955's NEGZ: a green
dot ~4-8 px above a VF2 conifer's tip on Lau's stage, flickering; a green
pixel a few px from Pilot Kids' window tree; strays near Rally's trees. Ben
later: stock MAME 0.289 pltkidsa shows the Pilot Kids specks too, and real
Model 2A hardware shows none of them, "one bug shared by MAME and the core".)

*The tool.* tools/m2-fbgrab.py runs on the MiSTer and only reads /dev/mem
(O_RDONLY, PROT_READ): both buffers at 0x30000000 / +1 MB (Model2.sv fb_base
0x06000000 words), 384 lines of 512 32-bit words, {7'd0, painted, RGB888}.
Nothing the HPS can read says which buffer is on show, so it is inferred:
a buffer that changes between two copies is being drawn and the other is on
screen (m2_raster3d fb_draw / fb_show); with neither changing, the last to
change is the newest frame. A copy is kept only if a second copy read
straight after it is identical; a burst (-n N) keeps each distinct complete
frame once, so a flickering pixel shows as a frame with it next to one
without. -r y0:y1 narrows the lines when a full copy is too slow for a
60 fps game. tools/m2-fb2png.py decodes exactly as the scanout shows
(R[23:19] G[15:10] B[7:3] widened as Model2.sv r3d_r8/g8/b8; unpainted in
a key colour), plus the painted mask, frame-to-frame diffs and word dumps
(--px). The raster bench writes the same files (M2_R3D_FBRAW). VERIFIED:
Pilot Kids frame 9000 (MAME's polygons, board settings): the converted
buffer against the bench's scanout, 160,075 painted pixels, 0 painted-flag
and 0 colour mismatches; the grab logic run against a file (--mem) with the
buffers planted in it, both buffers and a 20-line burst returned exact.
NOT run on the board (Ben runs it).

*The tree pixels, measured (MAME 0.289 m2lod M2MIP dumps -- every textured
pixel's 1/z, u/z, v/z, level and texel -- replayed through a transcription
of model2rd.ipp's fetch_bilinear_texel<true> and the mip blend: 12,388
translucent textured pixels of Pilot Kids frame 9000, 0 colour mismatches
against MAME's own):*
  * PILOT KIDS: every detached green pixel of the window tree (texture
    448,192 in sheet 0, 128 x 128, wrap on both axes) in frames 8995-9004
    takes ALL its opaque texels from inside the polygon's own texel box. None
    comes from a wrap, a clamp, a mirror or a far edge. They are texels the
    texture holds: 9 opaque texels with no opaque 8-neighbour, e.g. (92,25)
    = 5 drawn at (110,76)-(110,77) of frame 9000 with ONE of its four taps
    opaque (alpha 0.67 >= 1/2), and dozens with one or two. MAME's 4bpp
    nibble order is the right one (of the 24 orders of a 16-bit word's four
    texels, MAME's gives the smoothest texture and the fewest lone texels: 9,
    the next 12). Under ANY of four alpha rules -- MAME's (>= 1/2), > 3/4,
    two or more of the four taps opaque, all four opaque -- the tree layer of
    frames 8996 / 9000 / 9003 keeps 0-8 pixels with no painted neighbour
    (all four: 4-8, more than MAME's 2-6, because eroding a sparse fringe
    leaves new fragments). A stricter test is not "the hardware rule that
    removes them"; it removes nothing reliably and erodes 1-14% of the tree.
    If real hardware draws none, the difference is elsewhere (its filter, or
    the texture's luma on a CRT) and needs a real-hardware picture of the
    same moment to find -- not settled here.
  * VF2: THE DOT IS WHERE THE PLANE'S TOP EDGE IS. The conifer planes
    (h0 6013 / 6293, 256 x 128, wrap off) run u 0 to 228.6 from the top;
    the canopy's tip is at u ~22 (texture rows 54-72) and the trunk is in
    columns 240-255, rows 56-71 -- i.e. ON THE TREE'S AXIS. On MAME's Lau
    frames (R955's 1304 / 2704 / 4104) the u = 0 edge lies 8-19 px above the
    tip on screen (8-12 px for the distant trees). A top-edge pixel whose u
    goes a hair negative takes column 255 at its v -- the trunk when v is
    56-71, so the dot lands centred above the tip, green because the texture
    is luma on a green polygon, and flickers because u's sign there is a
    knife edge. That is R955's fault (a negative u/z saturated to 4095.996),
    fixed by NEGZ on branch tree-px -- not in 20261024b. MAME has the same
    edge in its own maths (fetch_bilinear_texel's !wrap clamp takes column
    w-1 for any raw u in [-0.5, 0)) but s32() truncates toward zero and its
    floats stay on the right side: on R955's MAME Lau frame 1304 there is no
    dot above any tip (zoomed), and none of its detached green pixels takes
    its point texel from outside its polygon's box (60 replayed temple-stage
    frames: 0-1 pixels a frame drawn only by a texel outside the box, none
    at a far edge). MAME does not show the VF2 dot.
  * The two do not share a mechanism: the VF2 dot is the core's own coordinate
    fault (and R951's / R955's family: a texel from outside the polygon); the
    Pilot Kids specks are drawn the same way by MAME and the core from texels
    inside the polygon.
*How established:* MAME pltkidsa frames 8995-9004 (M2MIP, r943 build) and
vf2 (R955's M2DIFF dumps, r869 build -- attract runs are not repeatable:
r943 and a second r869 run both landed on the temple stage, frames
1200-1399 with no conifer). Scripts in the scratchpad (tp2/mipan.py,
rules2.py, m2det.py); data in sm2-builds/tree-px2-data.
*Left:* fit NEGZ (tree-px) and look again at VF2 Lau and Rally with it --
then use m2-fbgrab.py on the board with the dot on screen: a grab says
whether the pixel is in the 3D layer, its exact colour, and with the bench
which polygon and texel painted it. For Pilot Kids, a real-hardware picture
of the window tree is the only thing that can say what the hardware does
with a lone opaque texel.

**R965 -- GUN FLASH OFF FOR VIRTUA COP 2 (2A) AND THE HOUSE OF THE DEAD (2C):
BOTH GAMES FLASH AS VIRTUA COP DOES, AND MODEL 2's OFF PATH PORTS AS IT IS.
OSD "Gun flash" Arcade (default) / Off, O[66] as on Model 2 (R929).**
R936 (1) and R942 (2), built. Branches gunflash-2a (off combo-2a 3e883c2) and
gunflash-2c (off combo-2c 1b67488), the same change on each.

*Believed:* R929 6 -- Virtua Cop 2 flashes with the window table (7 shots,
7 white frames); House of the Dead "has the same table written by 0x18650 in
its attract", its play not reached, "not measured".

*Measured (MAME 0.289 /usr/bin/mame; sim/io/mame_m2_gunflash_wt.lua, every
write to tile RAM words 0x6000-0x67FF logged per frame with the ip;
House of the Dead driven by sim/io/mame_m2_hotd_play.lua, seed 1, beside it):*
  1. VIRTUA COP 2 (vcop2): an accepted shot -> 0xFFFFFFFF over CPU
     0x0100C000-0x0100CBFF (words 0x6000-0x65FF) from 0x6000 up, ip 0x19f08,
     in the vblank after the shot; zeros the same at each of the next FOUR
     vblanks (0x19f98) -- Virtua Cop's countdown. The frame after it is
     (255,255,255) on all 190,464 pixels. Coverage: 85 s with shots every
     1.3 s (12 requests), 400 s with shots every 0.7 s through play, game
     over and attract (20), 400 s attract with no input (0): NOTHING else
     writes the table at all -- the boot's clear (0x74c8) apart.
  2. HOUSE OF THE DEAD (hotd): the same request, ip 0x18620 (same range,
     from 0x6000 up), cleared at the NEXT vblank only (0x18650): one flash
     frame, one flat colour, (228,228,228) on all 190,464 pixels (its
     palette, not pure white). 300 s of play: 1,984 requests, every one from
     0x18620; 720 s of attract with no input: no request (0x18650's zero
     runs only -- R929's "attract" writes were these). The only other
     writers: 0x185f0 (zeros, rows 256-383) and 0x183f0 / 0x184f8 -- a band
     of mixed masks over rows 336-367, ONLY while a request stands on the
     chapter card (below).
  3. A SHOT DURING HOUSE OF THE DEAD's WHITE CHAPTER CARD ("The First
     Chapter", 25.17 s): the request (one grey flash frame), then the table
     is NOT cleared for 61 frames (0x18650 does not run while the card is
     up) while 0x183f0 / 0x184f8 rewrite the rows 336-367 band every frame;
     MAME shows the card streaked (tilemap 1's columns) with "HOLD YOUR
     FIRE!" hidden, then the whole table cleared (26.25 s). With the table
     writes forced to zero (WT_NOFLASH) the card is clean, "HOLD YOUR FIRE!"
     blinking, white on 174,176 pixels -- the card's white is NOT the table's.
  4. With every table write forced to zero, the game runs on identically
     (the game never reads the table): vcop2 691 frames 29.5-41.5 s, only
     the 9 flash frames differ (they become the scene); hotd 190 frames,
     only the 13 flash frames and the 62 card frames of 3 differ.

*So the request is a fact about the game, not about the picture:* word
0x6000 written 0xFFFF is the flash routine's first store (0x19f08 / 0x18620)
and nothing else in either game writes it. Off does not look at brightness:
it takes out the table's effect -- the renderer reads words 0x6000-0x67FF as
zero while the request stands and up to the frame start after it goes -- so
a white explosion, a white card or any bright 3D is untouched (it is not the
table), and the table's other uses (VCop's stage band, HOTD's band without a
request) pass through. The one place Off changes more than the flash frame
is 3: the card shows clean for the ~1 s the game leaves its flash standing,
exactly as MAME does with the flash writes removed.

*Built (Model2.sv, M2_2A_GUN_FLASH; on by default with M2_2A_VCOP2_GUN,
VERILOG_MACRO "M2_NO_2A_GUN_FLASH=1" builds the core before R965, CONF_STR
included):* rtl/video/m2_gun_flash.sv copied unchanged from main 5a192f5
(R929); en = v2_gun (is_vcop2 on 2A, is_vcop2 | is_hotd on a 2C build),
mode {status[66], 0} (no CRT gun mode), trig_n tied high, trig_game_n and
white unconnected; its kill gates tram_q_vid into tram_data. OSD
"h1O[66],Gun flash,Arcade,Off;" after the Crosshair / Mouse lines (menumask
bit 1: the gun games only). O[66] was never used on model2a / model2c
(git log -S), so every saved config opens on Arcade. ARCADE ADDS NOTHING --
unlike Model 2's Arcade (R929 board: its tile path lost the flash, so
Model 2 whites the output) the 2A / 2C picture is the game's own; R929's
board note says House of the Dead flashes on its core without help. Whether
Virtua Cop 2's own flash shows on the 2A board is NOT checked here.

*Evidence:* sim/video/run_gunflash2a.sh (make test_m2_gunflash2a with
GF2A_DUMPS = vcop2 f1726, hotd f1716, hotd f1470 the card; dumps from
MAME, out of the tree), tb_m2_gunflash2a: m2_video with the 2A parameters
(MASK_SKIP on), the kill on the tile-RAM read, a stand-in 3D, the output

Not caught, and harmless here: the frame start on the vblank's rising edge

**R967 -- R953 REPRODUCED AND FOUND: QUARTUS 17.0 BUILDS THE SCSP DSP's MPRO
WITH AN 8-BIT WRITE PORT, SO A WORD WRITE STORES ITS HIGH BYTE ONLY. EVERY
MPRO LOW BYTE IS 0 ON THE BOARD (MASA, IWT / IWA, TWT / TWA, IRA[1:0], ADREB,
NXADR, YRL, FRCL, ADRL, SHFT, NEGB, ZERO, BSEL). VERILATOR RUNS THE CODE AS
WRITTEN; THE POST-SYNTHESIS NETLIST, SIMULATED, IS THE BOARD: DYNAMITE COP's
HITS -4.8 / -3.3 dB AND BREAK +8.1 .. +8.4 dB AGAINST THE MUSIC (BOARD -5.0 /
-3.4, +7.8 .. +8.4), THE MUSIC WITHIN 0.53 dB OF THE BOARD's (R914's RTL:
2.38). FIX: MPRO AS TWO ARRAYS, ONE PER BYTE LANE; ITS NETLIST EQUALS THE
REFERENCE. NOT FITTED.** Branch snd-silicon (off model2a 91c2bf9), LOCAL.

*Believed (R953):* the board's mix is not the bench's, the framework, SDRAM
latency and clipping ruled out; the bench (tb_m2_2a_sound, tb_m2_scsp) gives
R914's mix exactly. Left: the board's i960 MIDI, or the sound board's silicon
doing what its simulation does not. The candidates checked here, in order:

*1. INFERRED RAMS (s1447's own Model2.map.rpt, bridge-r937-2a build/seeds/
s1447, rbf md5 2ce93917 = the recording's):* every M10K of the sound board
(sreg x 2, st, rfa / rfb, mpro, mems, temp, both caches' dram / tram, lram,
the 68000's line cache ln_d / ln_t / ln_v) is single-clock simple dual port
with mixed-port read-during-write OLD_DATA -- the RTL's `q <= mem[ra]` beside
`mem[wa] <= d` exactly; the ROMs (ucf, uce, eg, rate, lvl, lfo) unregistered
outputs. Their MIFs equal the .hex files bit for bit (all six; the 44 -> 41,
68 -> 66, 16 -> 13, 28 -> 27, 12 -> 9 truncation warnings keep the low bits,
as Verilator). The MLABs (ud, mfifo, mo_fifo, ring, coef_h / l, madrs_h / l,
mixs, efreg, the output fifo) are altdpram, mixed-port DONT_CARE, read
address unregistered and output registered: a read at the edge of a write
sees the old word in the RTL and in the part alike (the write lands after
the edge). No pass-through logic added (no 276020 on the sound board), no
dual-clock RAM. THE ONE SHAPE THAT IS WRONG: mpro, Simple Dual Port,
port A 1024 x 8, port B 128 x 64. The RTL writes two byte lanes a clock,
    if (w_be[0]) mpro[row][{word, 1'b0}] <= w_data[7:0];
    if (w_be[1]) mpro[row][{word, 1'b1}] <= w_data[15:8];
and Quartus folded the lane into the address of ONE 8-bit write port (its
own netlist equations): address {w_addr[9:1], w_be[1]}, data w_be[1] ?
w_data[15:8] : w_data[7:0], enable w_mpro && (w_be[0] || w_be[1]). The
68000 writes MPRO with word moves (be 11): the high byte is stored and the
low byte never. No warning (map.log names mpro only in the inference info).
sreg, written the same way but with constant lane indices, was built right
(16 bits, two byte enables) -- confirmed by the netlist below.
*2. RESET / INITIAL VALUES:* every sound RAM powers up 0 on the part as in
Verilator; nothing in rtl/sound/scsp has an initial block but the ROMs.
*3. TIMING:* quartus_sta on s1447's database (a copy; the report had no
paths): the sound board's worst setup slack +0.236 ns (madrs_l -> mul_b,

has no exception on u_snd2a (R743's fx68k multicycle names u_sndboard, the
Model 1 board, absent on 2A). The SDRAM ports cross on m2_sdram_cdc (toggle

*4. LINT:* Verilator -Wall on the SCSP: unused bits only; on m2_2a_sound:
pin-empty, unused, VARHIDDEN (scsp_uc.svh's OP_ADD / OP_SUB shadow fx68kAlu's
$unit ones -- local wins in both tools). Quartus: the hex truncations, unused

CHKSUM = 0: a constant, harmless).
*5. THE NETLIST, SIMULATED (sim/netsim, new):* quartus_map of the module alone

UNCHANGED benches (the netlist's top has the RTL's ports). s1447's RTL:
    tb_m2_scsp_dsp DSP_RANDOM 20 (40,000 runs): RTL 0 / 0 wrong; NETLIST
      130,647 EFREG values and 265,809 RAM words wrong, from sample 0
    the RTL with Quartus's MPRO write ("board model", scratch): wrong in the

    tb_m2_scsp, the whole SCSP netlist on dcop_att: equal to the board model

      non-zero; stopped there -- the netlist runs ~40x slower than RTL), both away from the RTL
      from the first key-on (n 172,628) on
So the DSP's MPRO write is the only synthesis divergence these benches see
in the SCSP; the rest of the netlist is the RTL.
*REPRODUCED -- R953's three numbers.* sim r953.py (scratch): 100 ms windows,
board 0 s = MAME 38.34 s (envelope correlation re-found at 38.34), each
source against MAME's out.bin, music = 8-17 and 20-22 s, numbers relative to
the music's mean (the board's own method gives R953's to ~0.3 dB but for the
18.2 s hit, -3.4 here against -5.3 there: window placement):
                              hits 11.0 / 18.2 s   break 18.8 / 18.9 / 19.0 s
    board (HDMI, s1447)          -5.0 / -3.4         +8.2 / +8.4 / +7.8
    netlist / board model        -4.8 / -3.3         +8.1 / +8.4 / +8.2
    RTL as written (R914)        -2.0 / -1.4         -2.3 / -2.3 / -2.3
  and against the board directly, the music windows' sd: board model 0.53 dB,
  R914's RTL 2.38 dB (R953: MAME's mirror 0.89). The "no taps" is MASA = 0:

*Every 2A / 2C build is affected* (model2a, model2c and the release share the
code since R856), every game with a DSP program: VF2, DOA, Virtua Cop 2,
Zero Gunner, Dynamite Cop, House of the Dead -- Ben's "each game a different
issue" is each driver's own program mangled differently. R914's board

x 128, one write statement each (w_be[0] / w_be[1]), read together into the
same 64-bit mp_q. quartus_map: two Simple Dual Port M10Ks, port A 512 x 8,
port B 128 x 32 (4,096 bits each; the old one 8,192 bits in two blocks, so the
block count should not move -- the fit decides). SCSP alone (model2a's RTL):
2,047 -> 2,043 ALMs, registers 1,942 both, block bits 178,560 both, 3 DSP;
no new warning.
  Checks: fixed RTL tb_m2_scsp_dsp DSP_RANDOM 100: PASS; its NETLIST
  DSP_RANDOM 100 (200,000 runs) PASS, at latency 1-2 (50) PASS, 60-400 (50)
  PASS; model2a's unfixed netlist DSP_RANDOM 100: 881,509 / 1,250,729 wrong

  300,000 samples: 0 differ from the reference, 420,139 slot samples right;
  the fixed RTL on all of dcop_att (62 s, 2,734,658 samples): 0 differ

*WHY NO BENCH SAW IT:* every bench simulates the RTL, and the RTL is right;
the error exists only in Quartus's netlist. R909 / R914 / R959 read mpro's
RAM summary (1024 x 8 / 128 x 64) for M10K counts, not as a write width.
Rule taken: a RAM whose one write port is narrower than the widest write the
RTL makes in a clock is a mis-synthesis -- check the summary's port A width
against the code, and when in doubt, sim/netsim.
